candidate.description_text: The Austrian research institution is one of the leading application-oriented universities in the Alpine region, conducting more than 150 research and innovation projects annually in close cooperation with industry and public-sector stakeholders. Its multidisciplinary research capabilities cover electronics and data analytics, energy and process technologies, fluids and mechanics, biotechnology, health technologies and smart production systems. Together with an experienced Italian filtration technology company, the consortium is developing next-generation filtration solutions adapted to demanding industrial and environmental operating conditions. The objective is to identify organizations facing filtration-related challenges and work together to define technical requirements, evaluate operating conditions and develop optimized filtration concepts that can be validated under real-world conditions. The consortium provides: - Expertise in filtration technologies, process engineering, biotechnology, chemical analysis and fluid mechanics - Scientific and technical support throughout the development process - On-site testing and validation activities - Measurement campaigns and operational data acquisition - Engineering analysis and performance evaluation - Access to laboratory and pilot-scale infrastructure - Development of customized solutions based on partner-specific requirements Previous application areas have included: Waste management facilities, biomass and district heating plants, hydropower facilities, water treatment and process water systems. The consortium is now looking to expand into additional sectors where advanced filtration technologies can improve efficiency, sustainability, reliability and operational performance.
candidate.technical_problem_evidence_text: The consortium is currently looking for complex fields of application to further develop, implement and validate advanced filtration systems. Examples include usecases from construction, maritime, and municipal contexts, but usecase proposals from other sectors are also welcomed.
candidate.title: Industrial and Infrastructure Operators Sought for Joint Development and Validation of Advanced Customized Filtration Solutions

candidate.description_text: Weather forecasting, particularly at global scale and high resolution, is one of the most computationally demanding application domains. As forecasting systems continue to increase in complexity, Quantum Computing is widely expected to become a key enabling technology for future advances in forecasting performance, efficiency and scalability. An Austrian SME with extensive experience in weather forecasting, extreme weather events and publicly funded R&D projects is seeking to form or join a consortium for a Eureka project dedicated to the application of Quantum Computing in weather, climate and environmental modelling. The company aims to become an early adopter of quantum technologies and contribute to bridging the gap between today's forecasting systems and future quantum-enabled forecasting architectures. The envisioned project should develop a hybrid Quantum–HPC framework in which a selected component of the weather forecasting model chain is implemented using a quantum computing approach, while the remaining workflow continues to run on classical high-performance computing (HPC) infrastructure. The project pursues two complementary objectives: (i) preparing a first operational forecasting workflow for future quantum computing infrastructures; and (ii) exploring how concepts derived from quantum algorithms and quantum-inspired approaches can already be leveraged on today's classical HPC systems to improve forecasting workflows. To develop a competitive Eureka proposal and define a concrete implementation strategy, the SME is looking for companies eligible for Eureka funding with expertise in one or more of the following areas: • Development and implementation of quantum algorithms for real-world applications; • Hybrid Quantum–HPC architectures and integration frameworks; • Quantum hardware and access to quantum computing platforms. Universities and research institutes are also welcome, provided they are eligible for participation and willing to join the consortium as full project partners. The Eureka proposal submission deadline is 1 February 2027. The SME is seeking interested partners by latest mid-October 2026 to allow sufficient time for bilateral discussions, consortium building and the joint development of a strong project concept and proposal.
candidate.technical_problem_evidence_text: The SME is seeking industrial and research partners with proven expertise in Quantum Computing and its application to real-world computational challenges. Relevant expertise includes: • Development, adaptation and optimization of quantum algorithms for complex scientific and engineering applications; • Assessment of suitable quantum computing approaches for computationally intensive components of numerical weather forecasting workflows; • Design and implementation of hybrid Quantum–HPC architectures and orchestration frameworks; • Experience with quantum software development environments and quantum programming frameworks; • Access to and experience with current quantum computing hardware platforms and/or quantum simulators; • Expertise in quantum-inspired algorithms and their implementation on classical HPC systems; • Experience in benchmarking, performance evaluation and validation of quantum and hybrid computing approaches. Partners should be interested in jointly defining the specific forecasting component to be addressed, evaluating suitable quantum approaches and contributing to the development of a competitive Eureka project proposal.
candidate.title: Quantum computing expertise sought for a Eureka project addressing weather forecasts

candidate.description_text: A Bulgarian company is exploring the development of a software toolkit that supports compliance of high-risk AI systems with the requirements of the European AI Act. The AI Act introduces strict obligations for AI systems that may affect fundamental rights, safety, or wellbeing of citizens. These high-risk systems span sectors such as healthcare, finance, employment services, infrastructure, security, transportation and other areas where automated decision-making could have significant societal impact. Organisations developing or deploying such systems are required to implement safeguards including bias monitoring, human oversight, transparency and risk management. However, practical tools enabling companies to operationalise these compliance requirements are still largely unavailable, as the regulatory framework is new and most regulatory sandboxes are not yet operational. To address this gap, the Bulgarian company proposes the development of a modular AI compliance toolkit supporting organisations in implementing technical and organisational safeguards required by the AI Act. The planned toolkit will include several components: AI Bias Detection and Mitigation Tool Supports compliance with Article 14(2) of the AI Act by enabling systematic testing of AI outputs through modification of key dataset attributes. This allows identification and mitigation of potential biases that may affect fairness or decision outcomes. AI Over-Reliance Mitigation Tool Addresses risks related to excessive reliance on AI outputs, as described in Article 14(4)(b). The tool introduces deliberately incorrect outputs in controlled scenarios in order to ensure that human overseers remain vigilant and critically evaluate AI recommendations. AI Training and Confidence-Building Tool Supports compliance with Article 14(4)(c) and (d) by providing training tools that help human operators better understand AI limitations, detect inconsistencies, and intervene when necessary. The project is currently at concept stage, and no comparable commercial solutions addressing AI Act compliance requirements are widely available on the market.

candidate.description_text: The company operates at the intersection of product innovation and applied research in digital health. Its R&D pillar supports the continuous development of AI, interoperability and clinical data science solutions, while its product pillar translates these results into deployable healthcare technologies through the Alasia Health ecosystem. This dual structure gives the company the capacity to participate in collaborative research while also validating outcomes in practical healthcare environments. Its research profile is supported by 20+ years of digital health expertise, participation in 40+ projects, 130+ scientific publications, and more than €1.2M in research funding. The company materials also show active engagement in multiple national and European projects spanning AI in medical image and clinical data analysis, hospital transformation through AI, precision medicine, secondary use of health data and digital community health interventions. Indicative project involvement includes PROTECT (AI-supported surgical planning for prostate cancer brachytherapy), PRECIOUS (AI-based precision tracheostomy), HOSPAITAL (hospital transformation through artificial intelligence), VELES (smart health regional excellence and innovation), ArguMammoNet (AI-based breast cancer detection, classification and prediction using sequential mammograms), and ALTHEA (postpartum health behaviour change through social connection). These activities demonstrate experience in both clinical AI and broader digital health innovation ecosystems. The company is particularly interested in collaborative opportunities linked to EHDS implementation, interoperable EHRs, primary and secondary use of health data, AI-ready digital infrastructures, remote monitoring, decision support, and patient-centred mobile health tools. Because its solutions are already being tested in real environments with rehabilitation centres, elderly care providers, hospitals and public health stakeholders, the company can contribute both technical development and real-world piloting capacity.

candidate.description_text: A Czech company specializing in innovative electric watercraft has developed a patented electric kayak technology featuring a fully integrated electric propulsion system. Unlike conventional electric kayaks that rely on externally mounted motors, the company's solution integrates the propulsion unit directly into the kayak hull, improving weight distribution, stability, hydrodynamic efficiency, and user comfort. The electric drive is operated through wireless controls integrated into the paddle, allowing users to adjust speed without interrupting paddling. The modular design enables manufacturers to adapt the technology to different kayak models, materials, and customer requirements while maintaining the advantages of the patented propulsion system. The technology is suitable for a wide range of recreational and professional applications, including: - recreational kayaking - tourism and water sports - kayak rental fleets - fishing and angling - guided outdoor activities - rescue and emergency response - environmental monitoring, - inland waterway operations The company is seeking manufacturing partners interested in incorporating the patented propulsion technology into their own kayak production or establishing licensed manufacturing operations. Cooperation may include technology transfer, product adaptation, joint manufacturing, and commercialisation in new markets.
candidate.technical_problem_evidence_text: The company is seeking manufacturers with experience in the design and production of kayaks, canoes, small boats, or other composite watercraft. Partners should have capabilities in composite manufacturing, plastic moulding, rotational moulding, thermoforming, or similar production technologies applicable to kayak manufacturing. Experience in one or more of the following areas would be considered an advantage: production of recreational or professional watercraft, integration of electric propulsion systems, composite materials, fiberglass, carbon fibre, or polyethylene manufacturing, product assembly and quality assurance, marine equipment manufacturing, international sales and distribution of water sports products. The ideal partner should be interested in licensing and manufacturing the patented integrated electric propulsion technology, adapting it to their product portfolio where appropriate, and supporting commercialisation in regional or international markets.
candidate.title: Czech company offering patented integrated electric kayak technology seeks manufacturing and licensing partners across Europe

candidate.description_text: A German research institute specialized in manufacturing technology is backed by an almost complete consortium of European partners. The consortium includes companies of different sizes with expertise in powder technology and experience in Europe wide collaborative projects. The initiative is an EU funded defence R&D project (European Defence Fund) targeting new technologies with high innovative potential; specific end use applications will be defined with project partners. The project aims to evaluate the Freeform Metal Injection Molding (Freeform MIM). The method uses soluble resins for 3D printing to produce cavity inserts that are applied in the injection molding step of the MIM workflow. After molding, the part undergoes the usual debinding and sintering steps. Freeform technology enables processing of metals, ceramics and polymer base. In the best case, completely new parts can be created and showcased as new applications. The project will have partners from several countries in Europe and a new network will be created that will include multiple companies with their own specialities which creates a possibility for completely new products in the future.  The desired outcomes are validated process chains, qualified prototype parts, pilot production runs, and defined routes to serial production or technology transfer.
candidate.technical_problem_evidence_text: The institute is seeking product or system manufacturers (defence and adjacent sectors) interested in applying Freeform MIM either to existing or new parts. Preferred characteristics include the authority to make decisions on part design/qualification, access to in-house or contracted test/qualification facilities, and the willingness to engage in joint development work. Prior experience with metal/ceramic components or powder processes is beneficial but not mandatory.
candidate.title: German research institute, backed by a consortium, is seeking European product or system manufacturers for an EDF-funded research and development project on Metal Injection Molding combined with Additive Manufacturing Technology.

candidate.description_text: Electric vehicles increasingly rely on software defined control architectures. While power electronics based on wide bandgap semiconductors enable higher efficiency and power density, transistor ageing caused by thermal and electrical stress remains a limiting factor for lifetime, reliability and total cost of ownership. Current vehicle control strategies optimise energy consumption but do not actively consider semiconductor degradation mechanisms or remaining useful lifetime of power electronic components. The proposed project aims to develop an intelligent inverter system with an integrated digital twin capable of modelling transistor ageing in real time. The approach links junction temperature monitoring with physics based and data driven degradation models to estimate the remaining useful lifetime of power semiconductor devices during vehicle operation. The inverter is connected to a driving simulator environment that enables evaluation of mission profiles under realistic traffic conditions. Based on this framework, innovative control strategies will be developed. These include route optimisation algorithms selecting driving paths with reduced semiconductor stress, as well as active control interventions that smooth junction temperature fluctuations in order to slow degradation. The objective is to demonstrate how software defined vehicle architectures can directly contribute to improved power electronic lifetime, enhanced reliability and increased overall energy efficiency. The project will be submitted under Horizon Europe Cluster 5 in response to HORIZON-CL5-2026-05-D5-02. Consortium building is ongoing. Expression of interest from potential partners is requested at the earliest opportunity in order to prepare a competitive proposal. The expected call deadline follows the official Horizon Europe timetable. The anticipated project duration is 36 to 48 months. Partners are sought with expertise in one or more of the following areas: vehicle system integration, electric drivetrain development, wide bandgap semiconductor devices, embedded systems and software architecture, digital twin development, data analytics, reliability modelling, thermal management, or advanced control algorithms. Industrial partners are expected to contribute vehicle platforms, real world mission profiles or semiconductor components. Research partners may contribute modelling methods, material characterisation or complementary testing infrastructure. The consortium aims to jointly develop and validate a demonstrator vehicle powertrain with integrated lifetime aware control functionality and to establish new design methodologies for ageing aware electric mobility systems.
candidate.technical_problem_evidence_text: The institute seeks partners with complementary expertise to develop and validate a lifetime aware inverter system for software defined electric vehicles. Industrial partners are sought with experience in electric vehicle powertrains, traction inverter integration or vehicle control units. Access to vehicle platforms, real world driving data and representative mission profiles is highly desirable. Expertise in automotive functional safety, embedded control implementation and vehicle communication architectures is relevant for system integration. Semiconductor partners with knowledge in wide bandgap device technology, packaging, thermal characterisation or degradation mechanisms are invited to contribute devices, electrothermal models or reliability data for digital twin calibration and validation. Research organisations with expertise in physics based degradation modelling, remaining useful lifetime estimation, electrothermal simulation or data driven modelling methods are sought to support development of the digital twin framework. Additional expertise is welcome in advanced control strategies, model predictive control, intelligent energy management, route optimisation algorithms and software defined vehicle architectures. Experience with hardware in the loop testing, driving simulators or co simulation environments is particularly valuable for validating the interaction between inverter ageing and vehicle level decision making. Partners should be willing to actively contribute to proposal preparation, definition of work packages and joint development of demonstrators within a Horizon Europe collaborative framework.
candidate.title: German Research Institute seeks Consortium Partners for HORIZON-CL5-2026-05-D5-02 on Energy-efficient software-defined EVs with Expertise in Power Electronics Design and Reliability Testing

candidate.description_text: A German university with strong expertise in materials engineering and the mechanical characterization of metallic materials is seeking partners to jointly form a research consortium for a proposal under the call HORIZON-CL4-2027-01-MAT-PROD-22 within the Horizon Europe programme. The university intends to actively participate as a project partner within a collaborative European consortium. The objective of the call is the development of innovative advanced materials (IAMs) and production technologies that reduce or substitute critical and strategic raw materials while maintaining high levels of performance, safety and sustainability. The research team contributes expertise in the experimental investigation of fatigue behaviour and fracture mechanics of metallic materials. A particular focus lies on determining crack resistance parameters and analysing crack propagation behaviour, including for highly alloyed steels that may contain strategic alloying elements. Mechanical testing capabilities range from room temperature down to approximately –60 °C, enabling the assessment of materials under demanding service conditions. The resulting fracture mechanics data support safety assessments and structural integrity evaluations of newly developed materials and components. The research activities also address the relationship between manufacturing processes, resulting microstructures and material properties. This enables the evaluation of innovative materials as well as components produced by advanced manufacturing processes that may contain internal or surface defects. The research group has access to extensive laboratory infrastructure for mechanical testing, microstructural characterization and non-destructive testing, enabling comprehensive experimental analysis of materials and components. The university is looking to join a European consortium and is therefore seeking partners with complementary expertise in advanced metallic materials, innovative manufacturing processes, substitution or reduction of critical raw materials, material testing and characterization, or structural integrity assessment. Potential collaborators include universities, research institutes, industrial companies, as well as testing and certification organisations. The team is primarily targeting the HORIZON-CL4-2027-01-MAT-PROD-22 call but remains open to collaboration within other relevant Horizon Europe calls.

candidate.description_text: A German SME develops and produces electric cargo bikes for a wide range of applications – from urban logistics and postal delivery to family transportation and municipal services. With a team of dedicated engineers, mechanics, and designers, the company focuses on local manufacturing, durable design, and social responsibility. They have delivered over 2.500 bikes to customers in more than 20 countries. For their current range of two- and three-wheeled electric cargo bikes, the company offers a wide variety of box types and attachments, including refrigerated boxes, passenger modules, and waste containers. Further to this, they develop customized solutions for fleet operators. Sustainability, reparability, and long-term product value are core to the company’s design philosophy. The SME is working on developing a new Light Electric Vehicle (LEV) in the European vehicle class L2e - i.e. a three-wheeled light vehicle for up to 2 people with a maximum top speed of 45 km/h and the maximum rated power is limited to 4 kW.  The new LEV is aimed at going beyond the performance of the current cargo bikes. It is a vehicle with a more powerful motor, regenerative braking, increased load capacity and a more comprehensive usability – e.g. for rural areas or longer distances. The cargo bikes with Pedelec drive are designed to address the future of urban mobility, which requires scalable, flexible, and climate-friendly solutions. Current regulatory and technical limitations as e.g. the 250 W / 25 km/h cap for pedelecs restrict the application of cargo bikes in certain scenarios, especially in rural or hilly regions. The project targets a joint research and development initiative under the bilateral SME collaboration programme between Germany and Sweden, coordinated by Vinnova on the Swedish side. The submission deadline for grant proposals is on 13. October 2026. Expressions of Interest are required by 15. September 2026. The German SME aims to co-develop the LEV by collaborating with a Swedish technology provider, municipality or research body. Ideally, the partner is a vehicle manufacturer, automotive supplier, manufacturer of forklift trucks or a university with expertise in electric engines, brakes or fuel cell technologies. The collaboration will focus on the engine with an increased performance and / or the regenerative braking. The aim is to jointly push the boundaries of what LEVs can do in terms of technology but however, within the existing legal framework. The project will result in tested prototypes and pilot use cases. The company is convinced that co-creating new vehicle categories and sharing real data from pilot use cases will enable better products, smarter policies, and new business opportunities. The R&D-project would allow them to combine deep field expertise with cutting-edge innovation.
candidate.technical_problem_evidence_text: The SME is looking for •	drive system manufacturers (motors, batteries, controllers) •	municipal or commercial pilot users •	research institutions or test labs for LEV classification •	hydrogen and fuel cells technology providers with an interest in co-developing an electric engine or regenerative brakes for cargo bikes. The partner should have expertise in electric drive systems, battery technologies, braking systems or hydrogen and fuel cell technology for light electric vehicles (especially in the L2e or L3e category). A strong understanding of urban mobility challenges and commitment to ecological innovation is essential.
candidate.title: Seeking Swedish partner with expertise in electric drives, regenerative braking or fuel cell technologies for joint Swedish-German R&D project call 2026

candidate.description_text: Conventional oil-based lubricants exhibit significant drawbacks: they readily attract and retain dirt, dust, and metallic debris, thereby promoting wear and increasing frictional losses. In both bicycle chains and industrial applications, this results in higher maintenance demands, reduced efficiency, and potential impairment of product quality and process reliability. Wax-based lubricants, by contrast, form a clean, dry protective film with low affinity for contaminants. This reduces friction and wear, enhances energy efficiency, and extends the service life of technical systems. The German startup with academic backgrounds in nanochemistry has even further improved wax-based lubricants: - The one-step solution completely removes oil whilst simultaneously applying a high-performance wax that bonds perfectly to the metal parts, making the process quick, simple and efficient. Following successful market launch of a first product range of wax-based lubricants for bicycle chains, now the company aims to expand into further industrial sectors. Diverse applications are possible: - Manufacturers of agricultural machinery could benefit from waxed-based lubricants as their food-related applications require high sustainability standards and high durability. For food applications, HSF N1 certification would be part of the development project. - Conveyor Belt Manufacturers could benefit from reduced downtime and longer maintenance intervals thanks to less adhesion of dust and dirt - Motorbikes could benefit from longer running times and more driving pleasure - Outboard motors would be less susceptible to corrosion - Bearings and sliding rails could gain long lasting high performance free of grease and dirt Together with a German research partner in tribology and a partner (to be found) from one of the promising application areas as mentioned above, the company would like to apply for funding in EUROSTARS 3 programme (https://www.eurekanetwork.org/programmes-and-calls/eurostars/) with deadline either 10 September 2026 or 4 March 2027. Funding conditions are different for each country, please check according to your location. The partner sought: - Must be an SME - Must be located in one of the eligible countries except for Germany, which are: Austria, Belgium, Canada, Bulgaria, Croatia, Cyprus, Czech Republic, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Greece, Hungary, Iceland, Ireland, Israel, Italy, Latvia, Lithuania, Luxembourg, Malta, Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Singapore, Slovakia, Slovenia, South Africa, South Korea, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, Turkey, UK - Must be a manufacturer of machinery or components that could benefit from a transition to wax-based lubricants both in terms of reduced environmental impact and increased performance and efficiency. The partners is expected to provide information about specific requirements within their application, test the innovative wax-based lubricants and provide feedback and data to prove performance.
candidate.technical_problem_evidence_text: SME that manufactures machinery or components that wax-based lubricants could be applied to.

candidate.description_text: The project EX2BUILD addresses one of Europe's largest waste streams: urban excavation material. The objective is to transform this underutilised resource into circular, building-regulation-compliant construction materials, enabling large-scale market adoption of a proven environmental innovation. After successful demonstrators and low volume production, the upscaling for industrial use is now in focus. The project will establish an industrial, scalable production system along the value chain: •	material sourcing and preparation •	industrial pressing and drying processes improvements •	quality assurance and certification •	business model development and replication A demonstration plant in Berlin (Urban Tech Republic TXL) will serve as a real-world lab to validate the system under industrial conditions and achieve TRL 8 and even 9. Production with small scale resources already active and running. The project is structured into 8 work packages, including: •	industrial product and process development •	engineering of tailored machinery and related components for high automation •	proof of significant upscaling of production •	certification and standardisation (DIN 18940) •	life cycle assessment and environmental impact monitoring •	replication and exploitation strategy The consortium is looking for an experienced organisation to act as project coordinator with expertise in EU-funded programmes (e.g. LIFE, Innovation Fund, Horizon Europe). Key responsibilities •	Overall project management and governance •	Coordination of partners and work packages •	Financial and administrative management •	Risk and quality management •	Interface with CINEA / European Commission •	Contribution to dissemination, exploitation and replication strategy Consortium The core consortium already includes partners covering: •	material and product development (cleantech company) •	demonstration site (Berlin TXL) •	testing and certification (independent institute) Additional partners (engineering, construction, LCA) are being integrated.
candidate.technical_problem_evidence_text: The consortium is seeking an experienced organisation with expertise in at least two of the following sectors: •	construction technologies •	construction materials •	industrial process engineering •	system integration Experience in coordinating EU-funded projects (e.g. LIFE, Horizon Europe, Innovation Fund) is strongly required. Suitable organisations include applied research institutes, engineering centres or universities with strong industrial collaboration and demonstration experience.

candidate.description_text: We want to join an EIC Pathfinder consortium (Biotechnology for Healthy Ageing) as a partner contributing the functional immune-ageing biomarker work package. The scientific gap we address: immunosenescence and inflammaging are established drivers of age-related morbidity, yet routine biomarker panels remain static — they quantify molecular or omics signatures without capturing how immune cells functionally cope with lysosomal and autophagic load. Lysosomal/autophagic competence is a candidate functional hallmark of biological ageing that current diagnostics do not measure. Our contribution is a functional assay performed on peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) — a minimally invasive, scalable, patient-accessible sample type — designed to read out lysosomal stress-handling and autophagic capacity in a standardised, reproducible format suitable for clinical cohorts and interventional endpoints. candidate.description_text: A public-law institution with a statutory mandate to support agriculture and the professionals working within the sector, intends to participate in a Horizon Europe consortium under topic HORIZON-CL6-2027-03-GOVERNANCE-04. They are offering a project idea focussing on the further development and piloting of an AI-powered assistance system designed to support agricultural advisors, farmers, and forestry enterprises by providing reliable, context-aware, and impartial assistance for technical, operational, and procedural decision-making. The objective is to deliver a practical, high-maturity solution that strengthens competitiveness, sustainability, and resilience. The solution is intended to support, not replace, human advisors and decision-makers. The relevance of the initiative is reflected in the scale of the sector. Within the remit of this organisation, approximately 33,570 farms manage around 1.49 million hectares of agricultural land, including about 1.07 million hectares of arable land. The sector employs approximately 117,200 workers and includes specialized production systems such as 4,470 dairy farms and 6,630 pig farms. This scale requires scalable, data-driven governance and advisory solutions capable of addressing a very large number of operational queries and decision-making processes each year. The organisation does not intend to assume the role of project coordinator. Instead, it seeks to contribute as a practice, testing, validation, and knowledge transfer partner. As a public-law institution with statutory responsibilities and direct links to advisory services and agricultural practice, they bring real-world requirements from farming operations, professional advisory services, and administrative procedures into the project. The proposed project could build on a conceptualized AI assistance system that could be further developed into a proactive, data-driven, and conversational support platform. The system would capture farm-level data, integrate domain-specific applications and procedures, analyze documents, perform plausibility checks, and recommend appropriate actions. Multimodal inputs, geospatial data, curated expert knowledge, and human-in-the-loop approaches could be combined to create an assistance system supporting advisory services, application processes, and decision-making. A particular emphasis for the organisation belongs to transparent, neutral, and trustworthy advice. Quality and reliability needs to be ensured through curated knowledge repositories, editorial quality assurance processes, and clearly defined escalation mechanisms. Any data obtained by the German organisation through its statutory administrative and regulatory functions may only be used for advisory purposes with the explicit consent of the respective client or data subject. The project will strengthen sustainability, competitiveness, and resilience by improving the basis for decision-making, reducing complexity, and streamlining operational and administrative processes. The solution is designed with scalability and transferability to European agricultural systems in mind. The German organisation can contribute real-world use cases, access to target groups, and established advisory and procedural structures. To ensure broad European relevance, partners from additional Member States and from the forestry sector are sought. The project will also include training and capacity-building activities aimed at enhancing AI literacy and competencies among relevant stakeholders. The consortium is seeking an experienced project coordinator, as well as partners with expertise in AI development, data engineering, interoperability, forestry, social sciences, evaluation, and pilot implementation. The German large public agricultural advisory and regulatory organisation will contribute to co-creation, field testing, validation, impact assessment, dissemination, and knowledge transfer activities.

candidate.description_text: A German university is coordinating the proposal for a project in “Advancing the European bio-based innovation enabled by biotechnology and biomanufacturing concepts.” HORIZON-CL6-2026-01-CIRCBIO-07. The project aims to establish an integrated value chain for biotechnology-enabled, bio-based, functional, and circular automotive interior materials. The project brings together expertise in biotechnology and protein/peptide engineering, bio-based polymers, PEF textiles, bio-based polyurethane systems, material formulation and processing, pilot-scale upscaling, biotechnology-enabled recycling, circular material recovery and reintegration, automotive interior manufacturing, OEM validation, and sustainability and circularity assessment. The current consortium comprises 10 partners from Germany, France, Italy, Spain, the Netherlands, Türkiye and UK, and covers most of the required scientific, technological and industrial value chain. The  Call topic explicitly encourages international cooperation. Against this background and the project is interested in identifying a suitable international cooperation partner from a country not yet covered by the consortium, e.g. from Canada, North Macedonia, Japan, Norway, Switzerland, Ukraine, Columbia, Vietnam, Philippines, Albania, Bosnia Herzegovina Suitable partner profile: It would preferably an industrial company, SME, research or technology organization, or applied research institute with expertise and existing technologies in one or more of the following areas: - bio-based, renewable, waste-derived or circular flexible materials for automotive interiors; - sustainable artificial leather or leather-alternative materials; - flexible materials produced from agricultural residues, food-processing side streams, biomass or other renewable resources; - bio-based or circular PVC and related polymer materials derived partly or fully from renewable, waste or other non-fossil feedstocks; - bio-based or circular polymer films, sheets and surface materials; - sustainable coated textiles and upholstery materials; - processing and manufacturing of flexible surface materials for automotive seats, door panels, instrument panels or other interior applications. The objective is not simply to expand the consortium. The consortium is seeking a partner that can simultaneously strengthen the project’s international cooperation dimension and fill a clearly identified technological gap in the project value chain. An example of the type of material concept they consider relevant is the production of leather-alternative or flexible surface materials from agricultural or food-industry residues, such as olive-processing waste. However, they are open to other innovative technologies based on renewable resources, biological feedstocks, industrial side streams, recycled materials or circular material concepts. The Call is a RIA targeting TRL 4-5. The consortium is therefore particularly interested in organizations possessing an existing and sufficiently mature material technology that could be advanced, biotechnology-enabled and validated within an integrated automotive material value chain.

candidate.description_text: Cardiovascular disease and cancer remain the two leading causes of death in Europe, together accounting for over half of all mortality, with cancer cases projected to grow 18% by 2040 and cardiovascular disease prevalence potentially rising 90% by 2050 due to population ageing. AI-assisted early screening is a key lever to improve survival rates and support overburdened healthcare systems. A German digital innovation company, specialised in AI/ML (machine learning), cloud architectures, IoT and healthcare interoperability (EHR (Electronic Health Records) / PACS (Picture Archiving and Communication Systems) / RIS (Radiology Information Systems) integration) is looking for partners to respond to the Horizon call in order to provide an AI-powered digital screening solution for medical imaging services as an analytical tool. For this call, the SME will act as the industrial technology partner, providing a scalable cloud-based AI platform to collect, process and analyse medical imaging data (X-ray, CT, MRI, ultrasound, PET) submitted by radiology and screening centres, covering both cancer and cardiovascular disease areas, with seamless integration into clinical workflows. A consortium is already being set up, bringing together clinical and technological partners from several European Union countries. The consortium is currently seeking medical centres for piloting and validation, expertise in cardiovascular imaging and artificial intelligence-based medical image analysis, a regulatory and compliance partner, a communication and dissemination partner, and an experienced project coordinator. Altogether, the consortium is looking to set up several AI and medical imaging teams under medical supervision and a coordinator.

candidate.description_text: The German research institute specializing in manufacturing technology shall be backed within the project scope by a consortium comprising European stakeholders. The consortium should encompass enterprises of varying scales possessing expertise in powder technology and demonstrated experience from transnational collaborative initiatives. The initiative constitutes an EU-funded research endeavor aiming at breakthrough technologies exhibiting high innovation potential; specific target applications shall be defined jointly with the project partners. The project targets the assessment and advancement of metal powder recycling processes from waste streams. The process chain encompasses collection, sorting, mechanical preprocessing, classification, and purification of pulverulent waste fractions, as well as thermal or chemical treatments for the recovery of high-purity secondary feedstock. candidate.description_text: Winter wheat production faces dual threats from climate change: severe biotic pressure from Fusarium head blight and abiotic stress from extreme heat and drought during early growth phases. The OPTI-ALG project introduces a closed-loop solution for climate-resilient seed processing combining dual-action botanical protection with instant optical diagnostics. The automated high-speed system integrates: 1. Innovative Microalgae-Based Seed Coating (Bio-Coat): Developed by Algae-Farm, this coating is designed to provide botanical antifungal activity against Fusarium while enhancing heat and drought tolerance during seed germination and early growth. 2. Inline Laser Speckle Photometry (Inline-LSP) Monitoring Module: Developed by Fraunhofer, this non-destructive optical system measures real-time seed surface micro-dynamics. It evaluates wetting coverage and film drying kinetics within seconds to verify uniform coating coverage and identify coating irregularities, while simultaneously assessing baseline seed vitality and indications of mold infection under simulated heat stress. Project Duration: 36 Months. Call Framework: Eurostars Call 11 (Open until September 2026). Target Market Launch: Within 2 years post-project (approx. 2031-2032). To meet the international collaboration requirements of Eurostars and to maximize regional synergies, the institute is particularly seeking project partners from Central and Eastern Europe, with a strong preference for Czechia and Poland due to their proximity to Saxony. Partners from Slovakia, Hungary and Austria with suitable seed-processing, phytopathology or pilot-testing capabilities are also of particular interest. Role Profile A (Research/Validation Partner): Agri-SME, optionally collaborating with an Agricultural University or RTO, to cultivate regional Fusarium strains, conduct artificial inoculation, and validate germination tests against LSP laser data. Role Profile B (Industrial/Pilot Partner): Agri-SME (certified seed producer, cleaner, or wholesaler; or SME + RTO/University) to provide real-world wheat batches, serve as a live pilot testing site for the Inline-LSP sensor, and perform field tests under CEE climatic conditions.
candidate.technical_problem_evidence_text: Partner Profile A: Phytopathology, laboratory seed testing, cultivation of local/regional Fusarium strains, artificial seed inoculation, and expertise in correlating traditional germination protocols with fast-track optical data. Partner Profile B: Seed processing capabilities (sorting, cleaning, coating, distribution), access to real-world winter wheat batches, facilities for live pilot testing of inline sensor equipment, and capacity for field trial validation under Central/Eastern European climate conditions.

candidate.description_text: Traditional tolerancing methods are unsuitable for assembling large, flexible structures made from anisotropic materials, leading to high quality costs and inefficiencies for SMEs. This problem is especially critical for structures combining large dimensions, material-related compliance, strong directional dependence of mechanical properties, such as in shipbuilding, aerospace, special-purpose machinery or wind energy. It makes it difficult for SMEs to remain competitive. Two German university institutes and a German SME aim to develop a digital, uncertainty-aware tolerance management approach for the assembly of large compliant structures made from anisotropic materials within a bilateral research programme with France or Sweden. The project will combine a functional tolerance ontology, real-time surrogate models for deformation prediction, physics-based digital twins, metrology and uncertainty-aware conformity assessment. The central innovation is a closed-loop approach in which measurement data continuously update the digital twin and process parameters, enabling tolerances to be managed dynamically throughout assembly rather than as static geometric requirements. This is expected to reduce excessive safety margins, manual adjustments, rework and scrap. Consortium: The consortium is currently in formation. Two German research facilities, a leading research institute in the fields of metrology, quality sensing, digital twins, and intelligent production systems and a leading research institute in mechatronics, automation, and industrial production technologies are looking for an industrial partner in France or Sweden. The German expertise covers digital twins, surrogate modelling, metrology and uncertainty-aware quality assessment. The German side intends to coordinate the scientific development. A French or a Swedish SME from a relevant sector (possibly together with research institute) with an industrial use case, is sought to submit a proposal either via: Franco-German Call for Proposals for Joint Research and Development Projects between SMEs (Deadline for proposal submission: 18 November 2026) or Swedish-German Call for Proposals for Joint Research and Development Projects by young, small and medium-sized enterprises (Deadline for proposal submission: 13th October 2026) Deadline for EOI : 01.10.2026

candidate.description_text: The company seeks to establish a Danish-German consortium to finalize a proposal for the Food & Bio Cluster Denmark "Pathways to Net-Zero" programme. The proposed project will demonstrate how continuous soil nitrate monitoring can contribute primarily to the Call's inflection point 3: [Nutrient-rich crop production per hectare of agricultural land reaches its highest sustainable yield, while greenhouse gas emissions are significantly reduced, and nitrogen leaching and other environmental contaminants are minimized or eliminated.] The German company has developed a patented soil monitoring solution that combines automated in-field sensors with a secure cloud-based analytics platform. The system continuously measures nitrate concentration, soil moisture, and temperature and transforms these data into actionable nutrient management recommendations. The technology has already been validated under commercial farming conditions in several European countries, but not yet in Danish soils as a relevant environment. Predictions and data analysis require local adaptation, demanding further R&D effort. Potential project activities may include, among others: - Multi-site farm demonstration trials in Denmark - Integration of sensor data into farm management systems - Development of decision-support tools for nutrient optimization - Quantification of environmental and climate benefits - Assessment of nitrogen leaching reductions - Measurement of greenhouse gas mitigation potential - Economic impact and business case analysis The company has already made significant progress on the proposal, but is naturally open to adapting the project scope and jointly defining work packages with consortium partners.

candidate.description_text: European agriculture faces increasing pressure to reduce herbicide dependency, minimise environmental impact, and maintain productivity—particularly in high‑value crop systems. Conventional weed-control approaches still rely heavily on blanket chemical application or labour-intensive manual methods, both of which are costly and increasingly restricted by regulation. The Danish SME coordinator is developing an AI-enabled precision agriculture solution that combines high-resolution sensing, advanced computer vision, and selective laser-based intervention. The objective of the Eurostars project is to achieve reliable, crop-safe weed targeting at sub-millimeter scale under real-world operating conditions. The project focuses on improving small-object weed detection accuracy, precise localisation, and predictive targeting under motion, latency, and varying light, soil, and crop conditions. Strong emphasis is placed on real-time performance, deployment on moving platforms, and robustness in field environments. The consortium is formed with a clear applied and market-oriented ambition, aligned with Eurostars principles. Expected results include reduced herbicide use, lower labour requirements for weed management, improved crop safety, and enhanced sustainability and regulatory compliance. The solution has a clear route to commercialisation, particularly for high-value and sensitive crop segments.
candidate.technical_problem_evidence_text: Partners are invited to contribute expertise in one or more of the following areas: High-precision computer vision and small-object detection Object localisation, keypoint estimation, and spatial prediction under dynamic conditions Predictive modelling for real-time systems affected by motion and delay Deployment and optimisation of AI on embedded, robotic, or field-based platforms Validation of AI systems in agricultural, robotic, or outdoor environments Experience from precision agriculture, field robotics, or comparable applied AI systems is considered a strong advantage.

candidate.description_text: A Danish SME is developing a new autonomous robot for non-chemical weed control in private lawns. The company has worked on the concept for several years and has previously developed and tested a functioning prototype based on mechanical weed removal. This earlier work demonstrated that automated weed control in lawns is technically feasible, but the mechanical approach is not considered optimal for the next product generation. The company is therefore developing a new concept based on laser technology combined with artificial intelligence and computer vision. The intended solution is a stand-alone consumer-oriented garden robot that can distinguish grass from unwanted plants and target the weed at root level using a compact laser module. Laser-based weed control is already known from larger agricultural machinery, but existing solutions are too large and unsuitable for private garden robots. The main research and development challenge is to miniaturise the laser module and adapt it to a mobile consumer robot while meeting relevant safety, regulatory, power-output and system-integration requirements. The company is looking for an SME partner to join a Eurostars project. The project would focus on the research, design, development and testing of a compact laser-based weed-control module. The partner is expected to contribute with specialist know-how in laser technology, optical engineering, thermal design, electronics, safety design and testing. The Danish SME will contribute the overall product concept, market insight, user requirements, previous prototype experience and knowledge of the intended robotic application. Both parties are expected to jointly define the technical requirements, build and test a prototype module and prepare the basis for further integration into an autonomous garden robot.
candidate.technical_problem_evidence_text: The company is looking for an SME with strong technical expertise in laser technology and applied product development. The preferred partner should be able to act as an active R&D partner rather than a standard supplier. The partner should be willing to participate in a joint Eurostars application and contribute to defining, developing, testing and validating the compact laser module. Partners from EU and Eurostars countries are relevant. There is particular interest in partners from Poland, Germany, Eastern Europe, the Baltic countries and the Netherlands, but suitable partners from other eligible countries are also welcome.

candidate.description_text: A Danish biotechnology SME working at the intersection of industrial biotechnology and the circular economy is developing a novel approach to recovering critical raw materials (CRMs) from industrial waste streams. The technology is based on proprietary bio-derived metal-binding molecules capable of selectively capturing valuable metals from complex feedstocks, including lithium-ion battery waste, waste electrical and electronic equipment (WEEE), and mining brines. Current CRM recovery processes are largely based on hydrometallurgical methods that require significant chemical inputs, energy consumption and pre-treatment steps. The proposed technology aims to provide a more selective and resource-efficient alternative by enabling targeted metal capture under challenging process conditions. The Eurostars project will focus on converting the laboratory-scale technology (TRL 3–4) into an industrially relevant recovery platform. The main objective is to develop reusable recovery cartridges in which the bio-based metal-capture molecules are immobilised on inorganic support materials. Such cartridges could enable modular deployment close to waste generation sources, reducing transport needs and improving resource recovery efficiency. The consortium already includes academic partners with expertise in inorganic material synthesis and characterisation, as well as biological macromolecule analysis. Additional partners are sought to strengthen industrial development and validation activities. The project will be submitted to Eurostars and is expected to run for approximately three years. The consortium aims to advance the technology from proof of concept to a validated prototype with demonstrated industrial relevance. Two partner profiles are of particular interest: Materials engineering partner (preferably SME) An organisation with expertise in inorganic materials, adsorption systems, filtration technologies, membrane engineering or column design. The partner will contribute to support material development, cartridge design, prototype optimisation, performance testing and scale-up activities. Industrial validation partner (SME or research organisation) An organisation active in battery recycling, electronic waste processing, mining brines or other metal-containing industrial waste streams. The partner will provide representative feedstocks, support pilot-scale testing, benchmark performance against existing recovery processes and assess industrial implementation potential.
candidate.technical_problem_evidence_text: Materials engineering partner Expertise in inorganic support materials for adsorption, separation or filtration applications. Experience with membrane technologies, column packing, filter systems and performance testing. Knowledge of support material manufacturing and scale-up. Industrial validation partner Access to relevant CRM-containing waste streams. Experience in battery recycling, electronic waste processing, mining brines or industrial metal recovery. Capability to participate in pilot validation and industrial assessment activities. Previous participation in collaborative R&D projects is advantageous but not essential.

candidate.description_text: The company is a deep-tech startup developing advanced environmental sensing and artificial intelligence solutions for real-time monitoring, predictive analytics and decision support in complex operational environments. The company combines proprietary multi-sensor hardware (AGO micro-stations) with its AI platform AURA to transform heterogeneous environmental data into actionable intelligence, supporting health, safety, efficiency and sustainability objectives. Company’s technologies are currently applied in agro-industrial and livestock contexts, with proven capabilities in monitoring air quality, gas emissions, temperature, humidity and environmental risks under real operational conditions. The basque company is interested in participating in the EU-RAIL Joint Undertaking Call Proposals 2025-02 (HORIZON-JU-ER-2025-02), and is currently seeking partners to join or integrate into a consortium addressing this call. The official deadline for the call is 11th February 2026. candidate.description_text: The aim of the Project Proposal is the development, integration and demonstration of an Emergency Geospatial Platform aimed at improving the prevention, anticipation and operational management of critical situations, as well as post-event assessment, analysis and mitigation, with a particular focus on wildfires and environmental risks, while maintaining a clearly cross-sectoral approach. Currently, emergency management relies largely on reactive models, activated once an event has already occurred. This approach limits anticipatory capacity and forces critical decisions to be taken with incomplete or delayed information. The project addresses this challenge by introducing a paradigm shift towards prevention, based on the availability of useful information in (near) real time, combining space technologies, advanced analytics and artificial intelligence. The solution integrates and fuses data from Earth Observation (Copernicus), meteorology, terrain and operational sources, transforming them into actionable information for decision-making. On this basis, AI-based spatio-temporal predictive models are developed to estimate ignition probability, event evolution and severity, enabling scenario anticipation and optimisation of resource deployment before an emergency materialises. The project incorporates a resilient SATCOM-based communications architecture, ensuring service continuity even when terrestrial infrastructures are degraded or unavailable. In addition, the platform includes embarkable capabilities on UAVs and High-Altitude Platform Systems (HAPS), enabling persistent observation, edge computing and communication relay functions in remote or highly critical areas. Interaction with end users is supported through collaborative web interfaces and Augmented Reality (AR) and Virtual Reality (VR) technologies, which enhance first responders’ situational awareness, facilitate multi-agency coordination, and enable advanced simulations for demonstration, training and operational preparedness. The project will be developed to reach TRL 9, through large-scale demonstrations in real operational environments, with the direct participation of first responders (fire services, civil protection and emergency services), who will validate the technology from a functional, operational and impact perspective. The Emergency Geospatial Platform is designed with a cross-sectoral and cyber-resilient approach, allowing its reuse across domains such as emergency management, security, environmental protection and critical infrastructures. The project contributes to increasing the uptake of data and services from the European Space Programme (Galileo, EGNOS, Copernicus). Call: HORIZON-EUSPA-2026-SPACE-02-52 Call Deadline: 24 February 2026 at 17:00 CET. Type of Action: Innovation Actions (IA). Indicative Budget: Expected contributions range between EUR 1.5 and 1.8 million per project Type and role of the partner: Entities acting as first responders in Crisis and Emergency Management. Role: to validate the technologies in real operational environments; firefighters, civil protection, etc
candidate.technical_problem_evidence_text: The partners sought will act as system end users and first responders in emergency management, providing a real operational perspective and validating the solution under actual conditions of use. Their role within the project will include the following key functions: •	Definition of operational requirements: contributing expert knowledge of real emergency response procedures, identifying operational needs, constraints and priorities from a field perspective. •	Functional co-design: working with the technical team to validate workflows, interfaces and functionalities, ensuring alignment with real intervention and coordination processes. •	Validation in operational environments: participating in field trials, exercises and demonstrations to assess system performance in realistic emergency scenarios. •	Usability and operational value assessment: evaluating ease of use, relevance of the information provided, improvement of situational awareness and support to decision-making under pressure. •	Impact assessment: contributing to the evaluation of benefits such as reduced decision-making time, improved multi-agency coordination and more efficient resource deployment. •	Support to adoption and exploitation: providing recommendations for integration into existing procedures and for future scaling and adoption by other operational entities. Overall, the partners will play a key role as technology validators and operational reference users, ensuring that the developed solution is effective, usable and aligned with the real needs of emergency management operations.

candidate.description_text: The organisation is a private Spanish company with over 30 years of experience in Defence, security and emergency training, operating across both public and private security domains. It has demonstrated international activity, including acting as a training provider for United Nations personnel assigned to special missions. It has served as a partner on projects funded under the European Defence Fund (EDF), ensuring familiarity with EU defence research frameworks and with collaborative project implementation. European Defence and civil security R&D projects increasingly face a structural challenge: technologies may be technically sound, but they often fail to fully reflect operational realities. A recurrent gap exists between laboratory-based developments and real operational deployment, particularly in areas such as usability, robustness, interoperability, human–machine interaction and performance under stress conditions. Within this context, the organisation contributes as a realistic operational validation partner capable of bridging technology developers and real operational environments. A key added value of the organisation lies in its capacity to provide controlled yet operationally credible environments that closely mirror real conflict, crisis and emergency scenarios. Validation activities are informed by direct advisory input from defence and security professionals with first-line operational experience, including personnel recently deployed in high-intensity conflict environments. This ensures that threat models, operational constraints and testing scenarios reflect contemporary realities rather than theoretical assumptions. The organisation’s capabilities allow for: ●	Field testing and demonstration of technologies in urban, semi-urban and confined environments. ●	Evaluation of systems under realistic conditions of mobility, limited visibility, noise and operational stress. ●	Validation of equipment, procedures, decision-support tools and training systems involving individual operators as well as coordinated units. ●	Integration of live, virtual and constructive components, supporting hybrid testing and simulation methodologies increasingly required in EU defence and security projects. In parallel, the organisation maintains professional and structured relationships with military, police and emergency units, including commanding officers and operational decision-makers responsible for requirement definition and system validation. This enables structured professional feedback not only on system performance but also on operational requirements and concepts of operation. Such engagement contributes to higher Technology Readiness Levels (TRLs), strengthens the operational credibility of project outcomes, and increases their likelihood of real-world adoption. The Spanish company is ready to join EDF and HE Cluster 3 R&D project proposals that require an industry validation partner. They will support Defence and Security R&D consortia as an early-stage operational requirement and validation partner, will bridge the gap between technology developers and real military and security end-users, translating operational needs into structured requirements and validating solutions in realistic environments, thus reducing the project’s risks, strengthening the alignment with end-user expectations, and enhancing the chances of real-world adoption. Some current matching EDF open calls for proposals include: ●	AI-based tactical situational awareness using swarms of small robots and drones – participation in a technological challenge: EDF-2026-LS-RA-CHALLENGE-DIGIT-AISAP-STEP ●	New abilities in over-the-horizon sensing: EDF-2026-LS-DA-DIS-OTHR ●	Non-thematic development actions by SMEs: EDF-2026-LS-DA-SME-NT ●	AI-based tactical situational awareness using swarms of small robots and drones – organisation of a technological challenge: EDF-2026-LS-RA-CHALLENGE-DIGIT-AISAO

candidate.description_text: The Spanish company, with strong experience in European projects, is building a consortium for the topic: HORIZON-MISS2026-05-SOIL-02- Living Labs to enhance soil health in managed forests and in natural/semi-natural lands. The consortium has already covered the required Living Labs in Southern and Central Europe and is currently looking for an experienced partner to lead the Central-Northern Europe Living Lab. The selected organisation will coordinate the establishment and implementation of a Living Lab addressing shared soil health challenges in managed forests under Temperate or Nordic/Boreal conditions The role includes leading baseline soil assessment, facilitating stakeholder co-creation processes, implementing and monitoring innovative management solutions, and contributing to harmonized impact assessment across the consortium. The coordinator is particularly interested in institutions with demonstrated expertise in forest soil management, field-based experimentation, stakeholder engagement, and regional coordination. Experience in soil monitoring, ecosystem services assessment, and participation in European research projects will be considered an asset. The Central-Northern Living Lab is expected to play a strategic role within a consortium comprising four to five Living Labs located in different EU Member States and/or Associated Countries. There is exclusive interest in partners from Germany, Poland, Sweden and Finland.

candidate.description_text: The project addresses the need for advanced recycled asphalt binders capable of restoring aged bitumen by adjusting its maltene/asphaltene balance through innovative rejuvenators derived from waste streams and chemical by‑products. The results will allow for the optimization of the design of recycled binders with high RAP (Recycled Asphalt Padding) rates, adjusting the waste-rejuvenator dosage to restore workability, fatigue resistance, and durability against rutting, while simultaneously reducing virgin bitumen consumption and associated emissions. Understanding the diffusion coefficients and induced rheological changes will enable the modeling of the long-term behavior of the aged bitumen-rejuvenator system and the establishment of formulation and quality control criteria applicable to specifications and regulations. The typical duration of an R&D project focused on new binders and recycling technologies is around three years, which is compatible with the time required for formulation synthesis, advanced characterization (FTIR-ATR, rheological tests, fatigue testing), and validation at the experimental section scale. From a scientific/technological point of view, the project is based on the mixing thermodynamics of asphalt colloidal systems and on the diffusion kinetics of the rejuvenator in aged matrices, applying FTIR-ATR spectroscopy and Arrhenius-type diffusion models to correlate microstructural parameters (asphaltene/maltene ratio, degree of oxidation) with the macroscopic response of the binder and the mixture
candidate.technical_problem_evidence_text: A SME with proven experience in the design and manufacture of conventional and modified asphalt emulsions, preferably oriented toward recycling processes and sustainable surface treatments. The ideal partner should demonstrate: -Capability to formulate project‑specific emulsions, including binders incorporating rejuvenating agents, low‑emission formulations, and full compatibility with high RAP contents. -Pilot‑scale and industrial‑scale production capacity for customized emulsions and binders. -Comprehensive in‑house laboratory facilities for quality control and technical support, including testing of stability, breaking behaviour, adhesion, and in‑service performance. -Experience working with public road agencies and construction companies, providing on‑site technical assistance and optimizing solutions for real‑world pavement applications.

Understanding the diffusion coefficients and induced rheological changes will enable the modeling of the long-term behavior of the aged bitumen-rejuvenator system and the establishment of formulation and quality control criteria applicable to specifications and regulations. The typical duration of an R&D project focused on new binders and recycling technologies is around three years, which is compatible with the time required for formulation synthesis, advanced characterization (FTIR-ATR, rheological tests, fatigue testing), and validation at the experimental section scale. From a scientific/technological point of view, the project is based on the mixing thermodynamics of asphalt colloidal systems and on the diffusion kinetics of the rejuvenator in aged matrices, applying FTIR-ATR spectroscopy and Arrhenius-type diffusion models to correlate microstructural parameters (asphaltene/maltene ratio, degree of oxidation) with the macroscopic response of the binder and the mixture
technical_problem_evidence_text: A SME with proven experience in the design and manufacture of conventional and modified asphalt emulsions, preferably oriented toward recycling processes and sustainable surface treatments. The ideal partner should demonstrate: -Capability to formulate project‑specific emulsions, including binders incorporating rejuvenating agents, low‑emission formulations, and full compatibility with high RAP contents. -Pilot‑scale and industrial‑scale production capacity for customized emulsions and binders. -Comprehensive in‑house laboratory facilities for quality control and technical support, including testing of stability, breaking behaviour, adhesion, and in‑service performance. -Experience working with public road agencies and construction companies, providing on‑site technical assistance and optimizing solutions for real‑world pavement applications.
title: Seeking SME Expert in Asphalt Emulsions and Rejuvenators for Collaborative R&D Project under Horizon Europe/Eurostars

candidate.description_text: The Spanish research group specializes in the development and biological validation of human-relevant in vitro models that mimic the complexity of the tumour microenvironment. Key areas for VHT parameterization include: • Cellular Models: Expertise in isolation and culture of primary epithelial, tumoral cells and stromal cells (fibroblasts or inflammatory cells, from tumoral or non-tumoral tissue), to provide real-world kinetic data for multiscale simulations. Extensive experience with human mesenchymal stem cells (MSC) and their secretome and derived extracellular vesicles analysis to model therapeutic responses. • Inflammatory Signalling & Mechanistic Biomarkers: Expertise in identifying molecular signatures and signalling pathways essential for training predictive AI models. • Clinical Integration: Being embedded in a hospital setting allows the access to well-characterized primary human samples for the incorporation of human biological variability into digital twin architectures. • Standardization & Reproducibility: The research group implements strict protocols for cell isolation and characterization, defining quantitative molecular endpoints, ensuring that biological data for VHT training is robust and reproducible.
candidate.technical_problem_evidence_text: The research group offers expertise in: • Isolation and standardized culture of primary human cells (epithelial, tumoral, fibroblasts, inflammatory, MSC). • Design of co-culture systems (tumor-stroma-inflammatory signals). • Access to clinically characterized human tissues and primary cell derivation for model validation. Seeking: A coordinator developing Virtual Human Twin platforms that require a robust biological validation pillar to ensure clinical and mechanistic accuracy. They would also be open to enter an already existing consortium addressing this.
candidate.title: Horizon Europe: Expertise in primary human biological validation and stromal-tumor crosstalk sought for Virtual Human Twin (VHT) oncology consortia.

candidate.description_text: The project focuses on transforming the tourism experience in rural areas and walking routes through an AI-based platform that generates real-time dynamic itineraries by seamlessly integrating local services such as accommodation, gastronomy, and activities. This technological solution aims to mitigate critical sector challenges, including low digitalization, fragmented service offerings, and the strong seasonality that affects SMEs in these territories. By directly connecting travelers with rural hosts, the business model eliminates intermediaries and unfair commissions, ensuring that economic benefits remain entirely with those who live and work in the region. The core technology and business management model have already been developed by the Spanish SME acting as the coordinator, so partners are not required to participate in the creation of the software or the base tourism product. The primary goal is to strengthen the resilience and competitiveness of local ecosystems through a tool that adapts offerings to current events, real-time availability, and user preferences. Under the DETOUR financial support scheme (SMP-COSME-2023-TOURSME), the consortium will implement a pilot phase lasting between 6 and 9 months to validate and adapt the platform to the specific reality of selected routes in eligible countries such as Italy, Greece, Bulgaria, or Türkiye. This approach not only drives digital transformation but also promotes a sustainable and "slow" tourism model that protects the authenticity of rural heritage.
candidate.technical_problem_evidence_text: The company is seeking a strategic local partner in Italy, Greece, Bulgaria, or Türkiye to act as a territorial bridge for the project implementation. The ideal partner should not be a technology developer, as the AI platform and core business model are already fully developed by the Spanish coordinator. Instead, the company is looking for an entity—such as a local tourism association, an innovation hub, a regional development agency, or a specialized SME—with deep roots and established connections within rural areas and walking route ecosystems.
candidate.title: AI-powered real-time itinerary platform for sustainable walking routes: seeking local partners in Italy, Greece, Bulgaria, or Türkiye for DETOUR Programme.
