candidate.description_text: An Andalusian engineering company is preparing a project addressing road safety and resilience in rural areas through an integrated approach inspired by the Safe System framework. The project recognises that safety in rural networks depends on the interaction of infrastructure, road users, vehicle technologies and the effectiveness of emergency response systems. The project is structured around five innovation pillars: - Infrastructure & environment assessment: development of advanced data‑driven methods and digital tools to assess rural road infrastructure safety and environmental risk factors, building on the Network‑Wide Road Safety Assessment (NRWSA) framework. - Road users in rural contexts: analysis of rural user behaviour, risk exposure and targeted interventions supported by data analytics. - Vehicles for rural conditions: exploration of vehicle technologies, intelligent safety systems and vehicle‑to‑infrastructure communication adapted to rural road characteristics. - Post‑crash resilience & response optimisation: new solutions for accident detection, communication and emergency response coordination in rural territories. - Road safety and resilience DSS: development of an integrated Decision Support System enabling authorities to identify risks, prioritise interventions and plan safer and more resilient rural road networks. The project will progress towards TRL 6–7, with demonstrations in operational environments across different European regions. Rural road authorities participating as partners will validate tools and methodologies from functional, operational and impact perspectives. Expected outcomes: Project results are expected to contribute to all of the following expected outcomes: - Implementation of the NWRSA methodology for secondary rural roads; - Innovative and effective enforcement strategies, incentive mechanisms and measures raising risk awareness for fostering safer behaviour; - Prevention strategies for reducing road fatalities and serious road traffic injuries on rural roads along with the respective implementation guidelines and policy measures tailored to the responsible stakeholders (regional authorities, police, healthcare professionals, national governments, etc.); - GIS-based application to assist local and regional authorities in identifying and mapping the impact of extreme weather phenomena and other natural disasters (such as floods, fires, storms, heavy snowfall etc.) on the safety and resilience of the road network in their jurisdiction. Main Conditions and Characteristics: HORIZON-CL5-2026-10-D6-09 Submission Deadline: 08 October 2026 EOI deadline: 17 April 2026 Type of Action: Innovation Action (IA) Indicative budget: Expected contribution 6.00 M€ per project. Technology Readiness Level (TRL): projects are expected to reach TRL6-7 by the end of the action. Project duration: 42 months. Type and role of the partner: rural road authority willing to participate as demonstration partner and operational reference user.
candidate.technical_problem_evidence_text: a rural road authority (at any level: national, regional, or local) responsible for planning, managing, and/or maintaining rural roads networks. The partner will act as an operational reference user and technology validator, providing real-world perspective and access to road safety data. Key functions will include: - Requirements definition: providing expert knowledge of rural road operations, infrastructure constraints, and safety priorities. - Co-design and validation: collaborating with the project team to review workflows, tools, and interfaces for field applicability. - Supporting demonstrations in actual rural environments. - Providing data and insights to evaluate system performance, usability, and impact. - Impact evaluation: contributing to the assessment of safety improvements, enhanced decision-making, and integration into existing operational procedures
candidate.title: HORIZON-CL5-2026-10-D6-09: Rural road authorities sought for road safety and resilience project

candidate.description_text: The Spanish SME specialised in the design and development of gamified, self-guided cultural routes, currently implemented in more than 200 destinations across Spain. The company focuses on enhancing visitor engagement and promoting cultural heritage through interactive storytelling and digital experiences. The proposed project aims to develop an innovative digital platform for the valorisation of cultural heritage through immersive, narrative-driven and gamified experiences. The solution will combine advanced digital technologies, including gamification, storytelling, conversational Artificial Intelligence (AI), and data analytics, to transform how visitors interact with cultural heritage assets in both urban and rural environments. The platform will enable users to explore destinations through interactive challenges, missions and stories connected to local heritage, traditions and history. Through a conversational AI assistant, users will receive personalised guidance, contextual information and adaptive narratives based on their preferences, behaviour and profile. This approach will enhance accessibility, engagement and learning, making cultural heritage more attractive, especially for families and younger audiences. In addition, the platform will integrate a data analytics system providing destination managers and public authorities with insights on visitor behaviour, engagement levels, routes followed, time spent and interaction with heritage elements. This will support evidence-based decision-making, improve heritage management strategies and contribute to more sustainable and balanced tourism models. The project directly contributes to the Cultural Heritage Value Chain by strengthening the interpretation, accessibility and valorisation of both tangible and intangible heritage. It supports the digital transition of cultural destinations and addresses current challenges such as low visitor engagement, limited interaction with heritage, and lack of innovative tools for cultural storytelling. A key focus of the project is on rural and low-density territories, which often face difficulties in attracting visitors and providing engaging cultural experiences. By offering a scalable and cost-efficient digital solution, the project will help these areas increase their visibility, diversify their cultural offer and promote local identity and traditions. The solution will be tested and validated in real pilot destinations through collaboration with rural destination networks, local authorities and cultural stakeholders. This will ensure that the platform is adaptable to different contexts and can be replicated across European regions. The project is fully aligned with European priorities related to digitalisation, sustainability and cultural heritage valorisation. It contributes to strengthening the competitiveness of SMEs within the cultural heritage ecosystem and fosters cross-sector collaboration between technology providers, cultural content creators and territorial actors. Ultimately, the project aims to deliver a scalable, innovative and market-ready solution that enhances the value of cultural heritage, improves visitor experiences and supports the sustainable development of European destinations.
candidate.technical_problem_evidence_text: We are looking for complementary partners to build a strong and balanced European consortium covering the full Cultural Heritage Value Chain. First, we seek a cultural heritage SME with expertise in cultural content creation, storytelling, heritage interpretation, museography or related fields. This partner will play a key role in developing and adapting cultural narratives to different territories, ensuring historical accuracy, cultural relevance and educational value. The partner will contribute to the design of engaging, meaningful and accessible heritage experiences, integrating intangible and tangible cultural elements into the digital solution. Second, we are looking for a rural destinations association, network or cluster representing municipalities or cultural territories. This partner will provide access to pilot destinations where the solution will be tested and validated in real conditions. It will facilitate collaboration with local stakeholders, support user testing activities and contribute to the assessment of the impact on visitor engagement and heritage valorisation. This partner may participate as an associated partner without receiving funding. The consortium aims to combine technological innovation, cultural expertise and territorial implementation capacity, ensuring a strong, scalable and impact-driven project at European level.
candidate.title: AI-driven Gamified Cultural Heritage Experiences Platform for Rural Destinations

candidate.description_text: The company, in collaboration with a R&D Center, is preparing a R&D project aimed at converting wastewater from vineyard irrigation and/or wine-growing activities into a safe and traceable water resource for organic agriculture. The problem to be addressed is the growing water vulnerability of the wine sector, exacerbated by the reduced availability of conventional irrigation resources and by more frequent and intense droughts. Reusing reclaimed water is a strategic opportunity, but it requires controlling risks associated with emerging contaminants, recalcitrant organic matter, color, colloidal solids, and other trace compounds that can affect water, soil, crops, the final product, and brand perception. The project will develop and validate an advanced, decentralized, and modular solution that combines: (i) intensified pretreatment, with options such as electrocoagulation and advanced flotation; (ii) advanced oxidation, with technologies such as ozonation, electro-oxidation, or photocatalysis; (iii) MBBR/MBR biological treatment; and (iv) refinement stages using adsorption and/or membranes. The system will adapt to the variability of the incoming water and prioritize meeting the quality required for safe reuse. The digital architecture will integrate sensors, SCADA/IoT, data acquisition and governance, data-driven and/or hybrid predictive models, early anomaly detection, and AI-based autonomous control. The control agent will recommend or implement real-time operational adjustments to optimize quality, energy consumption, costs, and maintenance. The planned work schedule covers 28 months: study and selection of the treatment train at laboratory scale (M1-M6), design and instrumentation of the pilot plant and SCADA/IoT system (M1-M8), development of the predictive model and autonomous control (M8-M20), comprehensive validation on a pilot farm during a representative season (M20-M28), and management, dissemination, and operation throughout the project. Planned consortium: the company will lead the design, assembly, and commissioning of the pilot prototype, the sensor/data acquisition system, field validation, operational evaluation, and exploitation strategy. Whereas the R&D center will contribute analytical characterization, definition of target contaminants, technological assessment, predictive modeling, AI, validation, and scientific-technical transfer. Funding: This project is geared towards a proposal under Horizon Europe or other funding programs. The specific call for proposals, identifier, official deadline, and link must be confirmed before submission. Sought Partners: Wineries, cooperatives, or vineyards, preferably with organic production and located in the EU or countries associated with Horizon Europe, that can act as end users, provide real-world data, facilitate a pilot farm, and participate in agronomic and market validation.
candidate.technical_problem_evidence_text: The company is primarily seeking an end-user partner in the organic wine sector, such as a winery, cooperative, vineyard, or agri-food group, with the capacity to facilitate a real-world validation case study. Expected responsibilities: Provide samples and real-world wastewater flows from vineyards/wineries, as well as operational information on seasonal variability, flow rates, irrigation practices, and reuse requirements. Provide a representative pilot farm or demonstration plot for the installation, commissioning, and operation of the system during the field validation phase. Collaborate in defining the experimental protocol, acceptance criteria, reclaimed water quality requirements, irrigation conditions, and monitoring of water, soil, crop, and final product. Allow sampling, access to operational data, and participation in the assessment of agronomic safety, compatibility with organic farming, and regulatory compliance, including the applicable water reuse framework. Participate in operational trials in recommendation, supervised, and automated modes, providing end-user feedback on ease of use, maintainability, costs, adoption barriers, and scaling needs. Support the technical, economic, environmental, operational, and market evaluation, as well as the definition of the business case, deployment model, and commercial exploitation roadmap. Partners located in the EU or countries associated with Horizon Europe will be valued, provided they demonstrate a commitment to validation under real-world conditions, organic production or ecological transition, sector-specific communication skills, and availability to participate in dissemination, technology transfer, and commercialization. Complementary partners such as water treatment integrators, sensor/SCADA manufacturers, certification bodies, or research centers with additional analytical/agronomic capabilities may also be considered.
candidate.title: VITI-REGENIA: intelligent hybrid system for safe water regeneration and reuse in the wine or agri-food industry

candidate.description_text: The company is leading AquaTexIA, a collaborative R&D project to develop and validate a modular, digitized, and reconfigurable infrastructure capable of regenerating complex textile wastewater and transforming it into a safe, traceable, and reusable water resource. The company will contribute its expertise in process engineering, integration of treatment technologies, design and assembly of pilot plants, automation, sensor technology, SCADA/IoT, real-world operation, and operational strategy. The challenge addressed is critical for the textile industry: high water demand, increasing pressure on water sources and discharges, the need to reduce water footprint, and the difficulty of reusing effluents from dyeing, spinning, finishing, washing, textile finishing, industrial laundry, or other wet processes. These effluents may contain COD/TOC, color, turbidity, salts/conductivity, ammonia nitrogen, surfactants, dyes, microfibers, microplastics, PFAS, metals, and other emerging or recalcitrant contaminants that limit the effectiveness of conventional treatments. AquaTexIA does not require industrial users to be water treatment experts: their value lies in providing a real-world case study, outlining their reuse needs and operating conditions. The solution will combine advanced grey technologies such as electrocoagulation, MBR/MABR, advanced oxidation with O3, O3/H2O2, or O3/UV, adsorption, and UF/NF membranes, with a final green barrier based on natural solutions, such as wetlands, biofilters, or naturalized ponds. The system will adapt to effluent variability, maximize water recovery, and aim for a quality compatible with internal industrial uses, auxiliary services, cleaning, non-critical processes, or controlled environmental return where applicable. The smart layer will integrate real-time monitoring, data acquisition and governance, a SCADA web application, actuators, cybersecurity criteria, hybrid predictive models, and an AI-based autonomous control agent. This agent will recommend or adjust operating parameters to optimize reclaimed water quality, energy consumption, reagent usage, membrane fouling, maintenance, and operational continuity. 3-4 m³/h prototype in a relevant industrial environment, with an approximate evolution from TRL 4 to TRL 7. The technical objectives include overall recovery >=90-92%, turbidity <=1 NTU, COD <=10 mg/L, TOC <=0.5 mg/L, NH₄-N <=0.1 mg/L, conductivity adjusted to use, sum of metals <=50 micrograms/L, removal of emerging micro-contaminants >=90%, availability >90% and a 15-30% reduction in specific energy consumption through digital optimization. The planned consortium: The company will lead the architecture, engineering, integration, piloting, instrumentation, validation, and operation. The participation of technology centers and partners specializing in secure digitization, AI, cyber resilience, membranes, advanced characterization, analytics, and environmental validation is also anticipated. Funding: The proposal is primarily aimed at Horizon Europe, as well as other European R&D&I programs related to water resilience, zero pollution, the circular economy, industrial symbiosis, digitalization, and environmental innovation. The specific call for proposals, identifier, link, and deadline will be confirmed before submission. Partners sought: (1) an end-user industrial textile user, preferably in Spain or Portugal, capable of providing real effluents, operational data, and a validation site/case study; and (2) a consultancy, cluster, industry association, or facilitating entity to lead on KPIs, impact, scalability, replicability, transfer, and dissemination. The consortium is open to other EU or associated countries if there is a solid industrial case study that can add value to the proposal.
candidate.technical_problem_evidence_text: Two clearly complementary partner profiles are being sought. 1) End-user industrial user in the textile sector. This could be a dyeing, finishing, washing, or fine textile company, an industrial laundry, a garment manufacturer using wet processes, an integrated textile producer, or an industrial group with representative effluents. Their main contribution will be to transform AquaTexIA into a real-world demonstrator, not just a laboratory test. They are expected to provide real samples and/or flow rates of textile wastewater, water consumption data, production variability, campaigns, discharges, current costs, regulatory limits, and potential internal uses of reclaimed water. The industrial user will participate in defining the use case, test protocol, acceptance criteria, quality requirements, installation conditions, connection to auxiliary services, safety, and internal permits. They will also collaborate on sampling, KPI validation, testing in recommendation/supervised/autonomous modes, process compatibility assessment, identification of adoption barriers, CAPEX/OPEX estimation at scale, and defining the business case for future commercial implementation. 2) Consulting firm, cluster, sector association, or facilitating entity. Its role will be to strengthen the impact, scalability, and sector transfer. It is expected to lead or support the framework of technical, environmental, economic, and social indicators; the LCA/LCC/LCSA assessment; the scalability and replicability analysis; the identification of regulatory and market barriers; the deployment roadmap; the connection with textile companies, government agencies, utilities, and other stakeholders; and the communication, dissemination, and exploitation activities. Partners from Spain and Portugal will be prioritized due to their relevance to water stress and their potential to build an Iberian demonstration case. Partners from other EU countries or those associated with Horizon Europe will also be considered if they contribute industrial capacity, operational commitment, sector visibility, or access to textile ecosystems with a high need for water reuse.
candidate.title: AquaTexIA: intelligent and circular regeneration of wastewater from the textile sector

description_text: The company is leading AquaTexIA, a collaborative R&D project to develop and validate a modular, digitized, and reconfigurable infrastructure capable of regenerating complex textile wastewater and transforming it into a safe, traceable, and reusable water resource. The company will contribute its expertise in process engineering, integration of treatment technologies, design and assembly of pilot plants, automation, sensor technology, SCADA/IoT, real-world operation, and operational strategy. The challenge addressed is critical for the textile industry: high water demand, increasing pressure on water sources and discharges, the need to reduce water footprint, and the difficulty of reusing effluents from dyeing, spinning, finishing, washing, textile finishing, industrial laundry, or other wet processes. These effluents may contain COD/TOC, color, turbidity, salts/conductivity, ammonia nitrogen, surfactants, dyes, microfibers, microplastics, PFAS, metals, and other emerging or recalcitrant contaminants that limit the effectiveness of conventional treatments. AquaTexIA does not require industrial users to be water treatment experts: their value lies in providing a real-world case study, outlining their reuse needs and operating conditions. The solution will combine advanced grey technologies such as electrocoagulation, MBR/MABR, advanced oxidation with O3, O3/H2O2, or O3/UV, adsorption, and UF/NF membranes, with a final green barrier based on natural solutions, such as wetlands, biofilters, or naturalized ponds. The system will adapt to effluent variability, maximize water recovery, and aim for a quality compatible with internal industrial uses, auxiliary services, cleaning, non-critical processes, or controlled environmental return where applicable. The smart layer will integrate real-time monitoring, data acquisition and governance, a SCADA web application, actuators, cybersecurity criteria, hybrid predictive models, and an AI-based autonomous control agent. This agent will recommend or adjust operating parameters to optimize reclaimed water quality, energy consumption, reagent usage, membrane fouling, maintenance, and operational continuity. 3-4 m³/h prototype in a relevant industrial environment, with an approximate evolution from TRL 4 to TRL 7. The technical objectives include overall recovery >=90-92%, turbidity <=1 NTU, COD <=10 mg/L, TOC <=0.5 mg/L, NH₄-N <=0.1 mg/L, conductivity adjusted to use, sum of metals <=50 micrograms/L, removal of emerging micro-contaminants >=90%, availability >90% and a 15-30% reduction in specific energy consumption through digital optimization. The planned consortium: The company will lead the architecture, engineering, integration, piloting, instrumentation, validation, and operation. The participation of technology centers and partners specializing in secure digitization, AI, cyber resilience, membranes, advanced characterization, analytics, and environmental validation is also anticipated. Funding: The proposal is primarily aimed at Horizon Europe, as well as other European R&D&I programs related to water resilience, zero pollution, the circular economy, industrial symbiosis, digitalization, and environmental innovation. The specific call for proposals, identifier, link, and deadline will be confirmed before submission. Partners sought: (1) an end-user industrial textile user, preferably in Spain or Portugal, capable of providing real effluents, operational data, and a validation site/case study; and (2) a consultancy, cluster, industry association, or facilitating entity to lead on KPIs, impact, scalability, replicability, transfer, and dissemination. The consortium is open to other EU or associated countries if there is a solid industrial case study that can add value to the proposal.

candidate.description_text: A Spanish industrial SME specialized in the manufacturing of precision metal components (promoter of the project) together with European industrial and technological partners in the defence sector, prepares a proposal aimed to develop a secure and federated digital manufacturing-as-a-service platform geared towards defence, to improve the resilience of the European supply chain, enabling the sharing of certified production capabilities, production reallocation, and rapid response to disruptions or demand spikes. This project addresses a key problem in the defence sector: the difficulty in reacting quickly to supply chain disruptions (e.g., supplier failures or sudden increases in demand). It proposes to develop a secure digital platform that will allow European companies to share information about their production capacity (in a controlled manner) and coordinate to redistribute manufacturing when necessary. The goal is to improve Europe's industrial resilience by reducing delays and external dependencies. The project will be developed in a European consortium with industrial companies, technology centres, and cybersecurity and logistics experts. This project falls under the European Defence Fund, which finances collaborative research and innovation projects aimed at improving European industrial and technological capabilities in defence. This type of call for proposals requires: Participation of European entities (especially SMEs and research centres). Strict compliance with security, confidentiality, and data sovereignty requirements is needed along the project and a focus on the European impact (cooperation between countries, reduction of strategic dependencies). The proposal is going to be submitted to the European Defence Fund program, within the call for proposals aimed at SMEs and technology centres (EDF 2026 LSRA SMERO). Timelines (based on available information): •	Call deadline: end of September 2026. •	EOI (Expression of Interest): 21st of September 2026. Project duration: 3-4 years. The partners sought are technology centers or companies with experience in cybersecurity, resilience modelling, and industrial digital platforms, and their role will be focused on technological development, validation, interoperability, and compliance with defence requirements.
candidate.technical_problem_evidence_text: Partners with relevant technical expertise are sought, especially in: • Industrial cybersecurity and data protection • Industrial digital platforms and integration systems (e.g., connection to factory systems) • Resilience modelling and supply chain management
candidate.title: EDF-2026-LS-DIS-RA-SMERO – Project for the defence supply logistics resilience

candidate.description_text: Autonomous robotic systems face critical challenges in real-world applications: heavy battery consumption due to AI processing and operation under variable lighting. The Spanish researcher (Dept. of Informatics, University of Oviedo) has successfully developed a lab-tested prototype: a 1/14 scale autonomous vehicle driven by Computer Vision. Currently, the car can autonomously navigate closed circuits, successfully handling curves, roundabouts, line-following, and automated parking maneuvers. This proposed project aims to scale their AI-driven software layer into larger robotic platforms (e.g., AGVs, UGVs, drones) for diverse real-world applications requiring robust, long-range, and efficient autonomous navigation, and disaster response, among others. The core objectives of the joint project are: 1.	Green Computing / Energy-Aware Robotics: The project aims to research and develop algorithms that dynamically adjust AI computing demands based on the robot real-time battery status and speed. 2.	Robust Environmental Perception: Instead of relying on a single sensor type, the project will explore adaptable multi-sensor integration to train Machine Learning models capable of robust path detection under highly variable real-world conditions (indoor/outdoor, day/night). They are proposing this as a Coordinator but are fully open to integrating their software, data science, and IoT expertise into another consortium as a partner.
candidate.technical_problem_evidence_text: Expertise in robotic hardware manufacturing/integration (platforms like AGVs/UGVs/Drones), software development (cloud, backend, specific AI integration), or end-users offering real-world testing environments (e.g., smart factories, logistics, emergency services).
candidate.title: EIG CONCERT-Japan: AI-Powered, Energy-Aware Autonomous Navigation for Real-World Robotics

candidate.description_text: A Spanish technology centre with a wide expertise in European projects is preparing a project proposal that aims to optimise needs of process heat, to improve energy efficiency and to reduce the GHG (Greenhouse Gases) emissions in process industries by upgrading excess/waste heat from the process itself. The project is intended to integrate technology development, process digitalization and implementation in one demo-site and comprises: - Upgrading excess/waste heat - Energy efficiency optimisation - Integration with neighbouring industries and/or communities - Low GHG and other pollutant emissions - Technology development and demonstration - Digitalisation of solutions The proposal will be submitted to the Horizon Europe call: HORIZON-CL5-2026-09-D4-08 due on 15th September 2026. The technology centre is looking for several partners: 1)	at least one industrial partner (SME or large company) that can participate as the demo-site industrial partners, where the innovations will be integrated at TRL 7-8. It might be established and located in Europe. The industrial partner should work in the food and beverage sector, for instance: •	Sugar processing & refining •	Dairy & milk processing •	Wineries & distilleries •	Meat, poultry, & seafood processing The role of this industrial partner might be: i)	Provide operational data (temperature, pressure…) ii)	Validate use of innovative solutions into their manufactured products (at lab scale) 2)	One company to act as the system integrator (SI). It should lead the design and implementation of the overall thermal energy system architecture, ensuring the seamless integration of heat recovery units, upgrading technologies (e.g. heat pumps, thermal storage), and related control systems into a coherent solution. It will be in charge of the detailed P&ID (Piping and Instrumentation Diagram) diagrams and Balance of Plant (BoP) designs. The SI will be responsible for integration of advanced control and monitoring strategies, and alignment with relevant standards to enable efficient heat recovery, temperature upgrading, and flexible operation under real-life conditions.UPDATED: THIS PARTNER IS ALREADY FOUND! The technology centre is only looking for non-Spanish partners. Deadline for expressions of interest is on 30th June 2026. Anticipated duration of the project: 4 years.
candidate.technical_problem_evidence_text: The interested companies should be located in UE, outside Spain. They should work in the food and beverage production sector.

candidate.description_text: FOODSERVICE TALENT 4.0 is a European project focused on modernising vocational education and training (VET) in the hospitality and foodservice sector through digital technologies, gamification, and work-based learning. The project will develop a digital platform that combines training with real workplace experience, offering flexible, engaging, and mobile-friendly learning opportunities. Its key innovation is the integration of learning directly into hospitality companies, where participants can apply and validate their skills in real working environments. Bringing together VET providers, hospitality businesses, and technology partners across Europe, the project aims to better align training with labour market needs. The expected impact includes improved employability, a more skilled workforce, reduced staff turnover, and stronger digitalisation of VET systems across Europe.
candidate.technical_problem_evidence_text: FOODSERVICE TALENT 4.0 is seeking partners with expertise in one or more of the following areas: Vocational Education and Training (VET), particularly in hospitality, foodservice, tourism or related sectors. Digital learning and e-learning solutions, including LMS platforms, microlearning and mobile learning environments. Gamification methodologies applied to education, training and skills development. Work-based learning (WBL), apprenticeships and skills validation systems. Hospitality and foodservice businesses, clusters or sectoral organisations able to support pilot testing and industry validation. Digital Innovation Hubs, technology providers or EdTech organisations with experience in platform development, data analytics and digital transformation. Skills assessment, certification and competency-based training methodologies. European project management and dissemination, especially within Erasmus+ VET projects. They are particularly interested in organisations that can contribute to the design, testing, implementation and scaling of innovative training solutions that strengthen the connection between education and labour market needs.

candidate.description_text: The construction sector faces increasing pressure to reduce its environmental footprint, particularly in road infrastructure, where large quantities of virgin aggregates and fossil-based bitumen are traditionally required. In this context, circular economy approaches offer significant opportunities to reuse waste materials while maintaining high technical performance. This project aims to develop and validate innovative asphalt mixtures incorporating recycled aggregates and rejuvenated binders obtained from industrial waste and organic by-products. The main objective is to restore the maltene/asphaltene balance in aged bitumen, improving ductility and reducing stiffness caused by oxidation processes. To achieve this, the project will investigate the incorporation of oils, chemical process by-products and metallic oxides into the binder. A scientific and technological approach will be followed, including advanced characterisation techniques such as FTIR-ATR to model the diffusion of rejuvenators and optimise formulations for high recycling rates. The project also includes the use of high-friction recycled aggregates to ensure safety and durability in medium and high traffic conditions. The expected results will contribute to optimising recycled aggregate design and establishing formulation and quality control criteria applicable to future technical specifications and standards. The typical duration of the project is estimated at around three years, covering formulation development, laboratory validation, pilot production and field testing. The profile is published by a Spanish SME construction company.
candidate.technical_problem_evidence_text: The consortium is seeking a company, preferably based in Spain, specialised in construction and demolition waste (CDW) management and the production of recycled aggregates, aligned with circular economy principles. The partner is expected to have strong expertise in the development of recycled aggregates with enhanced friction performance. This includes experience in working with different types of industrial by-products and waste materials such as blast furnace slag, steel slag, alumina residues and other similar materials with proven skid resistance properties (e.g. Accelerated Polishing Value – PSV/CPA). Specifically, the partner should be able to: Produce recycled aggregates with particle size below 5 mm Apply washing processes to remove fines and filler content below 0.063 mm Study and supply aggregates with improved skid resistance properties suitable for asphalt mixtures Work with different waste sources (e.g. slags, industrial residues) ensuring adequate mechanical and functional performance Develop and supply high-performance recycled aggregates adapted to medium and heavy traffic conditions Contribute to process optimisation and quality control of recycled materials Participate in laboratory validation, pilot-scale testing and demonstration activities The selected partner will play a key role in ensuring the quality, durability and performance of the recycled materials used in the proposed asphalt mixtures.
candidate.title: Spanish SME is seeking a partner specialised in recycled aggregates for a LIFE programme consortium on circular asphalt solutions

candidate.description_text: TECHNOLOGY: The Blue Box® is a point-of-care medical device that detects early-stage breast cancer from a non-invasive urine test. The device analyses volatile organic compound (VOC) biomarkers using a proprietary electrochemical sensor array combined with an AI classification model. Published in Nature Scientific Reports (2022), it achieved 88.42% sensitivity and 98.6% specificity — significantly outperforming mammography (73% overall; as low as 40–65% for women with dense breast tissue). The device is at TRL 7, with a pivotal CE mark clinical trial (TBB-BC-RK) launching July 2026 at 7 Spanish hospital partners. PROJECT: BlueScan-EU is a 24-month interregional project submitted to the PRECISEU Open Call (Horizon Europe Regional Innovation Valley), coordinated by The Blue Box Biomedical Solutions, S.L. (Catalonia), with technology development partners and 3 clinical partners. The project advances The Blue Box® from TRL 7 to TRL 8 through multi-site clinical validation (≥600 patient samples, ≥200/site), AI model validation across diverse EU populations, and preparation of a full CE IVD regulatory submission package.
candidate.technical_problem_evidence_text: • Active breast cancer screening unit or gynaecology department with access to a mammography screening programme • Capacity to recruit ≥100 female participants from screening populations per year • Access to histopathology confirmation for biopsy-indicated cases • Willingness to execute a non-invasive urine sample collection protocol alongside standard screening workflow • Biobanking capability is advantageous but not required
candidate.title: Partner Hospital Sought for Multi-Site Clinical Validation of a Urine-Based VOC Breast Cancer Screening Device (BlueScan-EU / PRECISEU Open Call 2026)

candidate.description_text: TColors is an award-winning Spanish manufacturer of paints, creative materials and DIY solutions for the educational, arts & crafts, hobby and retail markets. Owned by Grup Cooperatiu TEB, a non-profit social enterprise with more than 60 years of experience, TColors combines industrial expertise, product innovation and social impact in a unique business model. Every product is manufactured in Barcelona by a highly skilled team that includes people with intellectual disabilities, creating sustainable employment and promoting social inclusion through industry. Our portfolio includes children's paints, tempera, acrylic paints, sensory products, decorative finishes, chalk paints, textile paints, adhesives, glitters and the innovative Fly&Flot 3D creative system. All products are developed with a strong commitment to quality, safety and sustainability, complying with European regulations including EN 71-3 standards for toy safety. Beyond our own brands, TColors is a trusted manufacturing partner for distributors, retailers and international brands seeking private label and OEM solutions. Thanks to our in-house laboratory, flexible production capabilities and product development expertise, we support customers from concept creation to formulation, manufacturing, packaging and regulatory compliance.

candidate.description_text: Professional drivers’ (trucks, vans, buses, taxis) performance degrades differently for each driver, and therefore fatigue ADAS do not reliably catch it. Moreover, each car manufacturer develops different fatigue ADAS and focus on advanced stages of fatigue. An EU Horizon project proved an AI per-driver baseline can detect the onset of fatigue, before the driver even notices getting tired, using vehicle data plus a simple non-invasive wearable; calibrated against EEG enriched with other biophysiological data. It continuously learns, achieving 83.9% accuracy after only 30 days of unsupervised on-road training. The system learns continuously and keeps improving its detection, and reached TRL6. The project to be proposed will fuse this detection with an in-cabin LLM agent to negotiate rest, route or shift with dispatch, to a complete system covering from reliable fatigue onset detection to actively helping the driver, and take it to TRL8: prepared for market take-up. The interested company should add a (generic) OBD-II data reader to feed the system with data from the CAN bus. The goal of the proposal is to prepare the system for exploitation; the company has interest in commercialising it and can lead the necessary fine-tuning to own needs. The project will not include technological development, it just connects OBD-II with the fatigue-onset detection and the mitigation agent. The company must be based in one of these 5 regions: Bavaria/Bayern, Germany – Northwest, Rumania – Tuzla Canton, Bosnia and Herzegovina – Norte, Portugal – Castilla y León, Spain. The call closes in October. Project duration will be 18 months, €1.1M project funding.
candidate.technical_problem_evidence_text: Looking for OBD-II (On-Board Diagnostics) vehicle signal integrator to adapt the TRL6 personalised driver fatigue detection & mitigation system in a Transport Management System (TMS). We need the read-out of CANbus vehicle signals like acceleration, pedal position, engine load, rpm, etc.: normally over the OBD-II port of the vehicle. Not any OBD-II reader is able to do this for many car brands as often OEM-specific protocols are needed; experience with this is required. Stage of development. TRL 6: subsystem prototype demonstration in a relevant end-to-end environment.

candidate.description_text: This organisation is a think tank with nearly three decades of continuous work in democratic policy, public engagement and institutional research. Its publication record spans democratic governance, social policy, cultural industries and territorial politics. It convenes an annual cultural industries forum — fourteen editions since 2010 — that brings institutional stakeholders, including cultural organisations from Spain's minority language territories, into structured policy dialogue. It maintains active working relationships with members of the European Parliament across committees, regularly providing research inputs, briefings and co-authored policy analyses to MEPs and political groups. Engagement with linguistic diversity runs across several strands of the organisation's work. The 2022 Democracy Report included a dedicated chapter that mapped language policy conflicts across fifteen years and four territories through a structured comparative analysis. The same Observatorio that produces the annual cultural industries forum has also published on cultural rights as a framework — specifically the connection between participation in cultural life, linguistic identity and social wellbeing. That published work provides the analytical scaffolding for the non-linguistic benefits dimension the call explicitly requires: the case that language preservation matters for identity, cohesion and individual wellbeing, not only for linguistic heritage as such. On the deliberative side, the organisation has applied structured citizen engagement methodologies in bilingual territories. A citizen assembly on climate, conducted in Gipuzkoa — a Basque-speaking territory — used participatory formats adaptable to multilingual settings, demonstrating the operational capacity to run facilitated dialogue across linguistic communities without imposing a dominant language framework. The organisation participated in Chanmin — Changing Minds, Improving Citizens — a Europe for Citizens programme examining immigration perceptions among young people, including Roma communities in partner countries. That project reinforced cross-border dissemination capacity and experience working with ethnolinguistic minority populations in a comparative European frame. At the European Parliament, the organisation has co-authored policy analyses with sitting MEPs (including the President of the LIBE Committee and members of the Committee on Culture and Education) and has presented research on digital strategic autonomy, social participation and gender policy in parliamentary settings. This institutional access is a direct asset for a project requiring sustained policy engagement at EU level. We are looking for an academic institution — a university faculty, research centre or interdisciplinary institute — to take the lead research coordination role. Our preference is for a partner with demonstrated expertise in minority language research, ideally with connections to language communities beyond the Iberian Peninsula covered by the call: Celtic, Finno-Ugric, Slavic minority or sign language communities. We are prepared to co-coordinate the policy and dissemination work packages while the academic partner.
candidate.technical_problem_evidence_text: Spain offers one of Europe's most developed legal frameworks for linguistic pluralism: four co-official languages recognised under the 1978 Constitution and shaped through distinct normalisation legislation and statutory arrangements across autonomous communities, each with its own governance model and documented policy outcomes. The think tank brings nearly three decades of published analysis on how those frameworks operate in practice — the governance of co-official languages, linguistic conflict management in education and public space, and the translation of constitutional mandates into regional policy — making it a substantive reference point for the comparative study of language governance in multilingual democracies. It complements this research capacity with direct, working relationships with European Parliament groups and members, and experience producing policy analysis jointly with sitting MEPs on European legislative dossiers. To complete a competitive consortium, the think tank seeks partners who bring the scientific and technical dimensions the topic explicitly requires. Linguists and sociolinguists with field experience among minority language communities — corpus analysis, oral tradition documentation, language maintenance and transmission — provide the research backbone. Researchers able to document and communicate the non-linguistic benefits of language preservation — wellbeing, identity, health and social cohesion — address a dimension the call treats as a distinct deliverable. Experts in language technologies address the call's demand to map digital language presence and bridge the digital language gap. Specialists in linguistic cartography deliver the visual mapping dimension the topic specifically requires. Institutions from territories with comparable experiences of linguistic pluralism are especially welcome: Belgium, Ireland, Wales, Italy — including South Tyrol, home to one of Europe's leading minority language research centres — the Netherlands, France and other regions where co-official or minority languages coexist under diverse institutional frameworks. Partners working alongside Roma, Romani-speaking and other itinerant or dispersed communities, for whom oral transmission is the primary vehicle of language preservation, respond directly to one of the call's stated priorities. Connections to European language data infrastructures such as CLARIN or ELRA add further reach.
candidate.title: Think tank with nearly three decades of minority language and cultural policy expertise in Spain's four co-official language territories seeks academic coordinator for Horizon Europe RIA/ HORIZON-CL2-2026-01-HERITAGE-06 linguistic diversity

candidate.description_text: A small artisan dairy from northern Spain, specialised in lactic-curd (acid-coagulated) cheeses, is preparing an application to the Eurostars-3 programme (Call 11, deadline 10 September 2026). The project will develop an integrated, economically viable process to valorise acid cheese whey (pH 4.2–4.6) — a low-value, high-COD by-product that is technically difficult to process. The process will (a) recover the residual fat fraction to produce a fermented whey butter with extended shelf life, (b) concentrate the whey proteins into a high-value liquid protein concentrate, and (c) recover clean process water for reuse in CIP/cleaning. The SME, who will coordinate, is seeking an R&D cooperation agreement with two international partners and offers a real, replicable circular-economy solution for small and medium dairies across Europe. Description of the project and the offer Cheese whey represents 85–90 % of processed milk volume and retains roughly half of milk’s nutrients, yet it is largely treated as a polluting effluent. While sweet whey (enzymatic coagulation, pH 6.5–6.8) is well valorised industrially, acid whey from lactic-curd cheeses (pH < 4.6, low protein, high minerals and lactic acid) presents strong technical barriers and has been little studied. The coordinator is an innovative artisan dairy that generates this acid whey as a direct by-product of its core production and wants to turn it into marketable products. The project will move the technology from laboratory/early evidence to a validated pilot, structured around three valorisation routes that share a common separation front-end: •	Separation / clarification: high-speed centrifugal separation and/or membrane microfiltration to recover the cream (fat) fraction and remove casein/protein fines that would otherwise impair fat separation and foul downstream membranes. •	Fermented whey butter, using bioprotective cultures / starter ferments to extend the fat's shelf life: controlled lactic fermentation of the recovered whey cream, followed by churning and malaxing, to obtain a high-quality fermented butter with extended shelf life. •	Liquid protein concentrate: ultrafiltration (UF) of the de-fatted whey to concentrate the high-biological-value whey proteins for food/nutraceutical use. •	Water recovery: reverse osmosis (RO) of the UF permeate to recover clean water for CIP and cleaning operations, closing the water loop. The lead SME already works with Spanish subcontractors for sensory/shelf-life testing and engineering of prototype equipment. International partners are sought as full Eurostars consortium members (not subcontractors).

candidate.description_text: A Spanish non-profit organisation specialised in cultural rights, cognitive accessibility and participatory work with autistic people, persons with disabilities and families is preparing CHARTERABLE, a 24-month cooperation project under the Citizens, Equality, Rights and Values programme. The project addresses the gap between the formal recognition of rights in the EU Charter of Fundamental Rights and their practical application in institutional settings. It will focus on Articles 21 (non-discrimination) and 26 (integration of persons with disabilities), with Article 51 considered where relevant to the scope and applicability of the Charter. Museums and cultural institutions will be used as the main implementation environment. Culture is not treated as an isolated end, but as a concrete field in which Charter principles can be translated into institutional procedures, professional competences, participation mechanisms, monitoring indicators and measurable commitments. The planned activities include: legal and policy analysis; comparative identification of legal and institutional gaps; participatory co-design with rights-holders; institutional assessment; capacity building; practical implementation cases in cultural organisations; monitoring of organisational change; European policy dialogue; and transfer of results through disability and cultural networks. Expected results include a European legal and policy framework, a comparative gap analysis, a Charter-based institutional assessment and monitoring framework, a multilingual toolkit, institutional improvement plans, documented implementation cases, a rights-holder validation report, a policy brief and a European replication roadmap. The current core consortium includes the Spanish coordinator, a Cypriot university law school with expertise in EU public law and the Charter, and a Spanish foundation specialised in cultural law and cultural policy. The consortium is now seeking a limited number of non-Spanish partners with clearly complementary functions.
candidate.technical_problem_evidence_text: 1. European or National level expertise in autism, disability or neurodiversity network with a strong membership base, rights-based advocacy experience, access to national organisations and capacity to involve rights-holders in consultation and validation. 2. European or National level expertise in cultural, museum or heritage network able to mobilise cultural institutions in several countries, support implementation cases, validate the usability of project tools and promote sector-wide adoption. 3. European or National level expertise in EU policy, monitoring or fundamental-rights implementation organisation with experience in EU Charter application, policy analysis, rights-impact assessment, institutional monitoring, advocacy, equality bodies, national human rights institutions or public administration. Applicants should demonstrate operational capacity, relevant stakeholder access, experience in European cooperation and willingness to lead or co-lead clearly defined tasks and deliverables.
candidate.title: CHARTERABLE -  Making the EU Charter Actionable for Persons with Disabilities (European partners search for CERV Proposal)

candidate.description_text: This R&D project aims to replicate the SMART ERA methodology in a rural area facing structural socio-economic challenges within the Danube Macro-Regional Strategy (EUSDR). Rural communities frequently suffer from demographic decline, isolation, and fragmented data or low access to basic services. To solve this, the project will co-design and validate a Smart Innovation Package (SIP). The technological core of the SIP will be based on 'vAMOS Rural', an established digital platform designed to revitalize rural ecosystems. However, tech alone is insufficient; it must be bundled with social innovation, local governance models, and a sustainable business plan co-created with the community. Role of the Technology Provider (Coordinator): The Spanish partner will act as the 'Pilot Orchestrator'. They provide the platform (starting at TRL 4) and will handle technical adaptation, API and data integration following the SMART ERA Interoperability Methodology (NGSI/NGSI-LD standards), and technical mentoring during deployment to achieve TRL 6. Role of the Partner Sought (Community Activator): The Spanish entity is looking for a key regional stakeholder (e.g., Local Public Administration, Local Action Group - GAL, University, or regional NGO) with strong deep-rooted ties to a rural community in the Danube region. The partner must have the motivation to mobilize local citizens, coordinate participatory co-design workshops, and implement the SMART ERA Smartness Assessment (regional data screening and indicator collection). Priority is given to regions lacking previous experience in multi-actor approach projects.
candidate.technical_problem_evidence_text: The entity seeks an entity capable of acting as a Community Activator in an eligible rural region under the EUSDR (Danube Region). Eligible countries include Austria, Bulgaria, Croatia, Czechia, Germany (Bavaria/Baden-Württemberg), Hungary, Romania, Slovakia, Slovenia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Montenegro, Serbia, Ukraine, and Moldova. The partner must possess proven capabilities to organize public stakeholder processes, engage local citizens/SMEs, and collaborate with municipal authorities. Expertise in rural development schemes, sociology, or public governance is highly valued. No high-level technical expertise is required from this partner, but a strong institutional commitment to data-driven smart development is mandatory.
candidate.title: Spanish technology provider seeks rural Community Activator in the Danube Region for SMART ERA 2nd Open Call.

title: Spanish technology provider seeks rural Community Activator in the Danube Region for SMART ERA 2nd Open Call.

candidate.description_text: A Spanish agri-tech SME is looking for a Community Activator to join a consortium applying to the SMART ERA 2nd Open Call. The project will implement the SMART ERA community-led innovation methodology in one of the programme's Follower Regions*, supporting rural areas where large-scale, high-value crops (such as vineyards, olive groves, pistachio or almond orchards) face common challenges including ageing farmers, labour shortages, depopulation, climate change and the gradual loss of agricultural know-how. The project will co-design, pilot and validate a Smart Innovation Package (SIP) that combines an autonomous drone-in-a-box platform with AI-assisted analysis to provide continuous, high-resolution crop monitoring. Rather than serving individual farms, the system will operate as a shared community resource, generating objective information on crop conditions to help farmers and advisors identify priority areas for field inspection, improve decision-making, optimise input use and strengthen the resilience and sustainability of local farming systems. As Pilot Orchestrator, the Spanish SME will provide and adapt the technology, increase its maturity from TRL 5 to TRL 7, integrate monitoring data following the SMART ERA interoperability framework (NGSI-LD, FIWARE and Smart Data Models), ensure GDPR-compliant and FAIR data management, and provide technical support throughout the project. The partner sought will act as Community Activator. Suitable organisations include growers' cooperatives or associations, Local Action Groups (LEADER/LAGs), municipalities, rural development organisations, agricultural universities or research centres with strong links to farming communities in an eligible SMART ERA Follower Region. The partner will engage local stakeholders, identify regional needs, organise participatory co-design activities, contribute to the Smartness Assessment and support the validation of the solution under real conditions. Technical expertise in drone technologies is not required; strong local networks, stakeholder engagement capacity and commitment to rural innovation are the key assets sought. *SMART ERA Follower Regions are: EUSALP (Alpine Region), EUSBSR (Baltic Sea Region), EUSAIR (Adriatic-Ionian Region), EUSDR (Danube Region).

The ideal partner should have proven experience in stakeholder engagement, community mobilisation and participatory innovation processes. Experience in rural development, agriculture, regional policy or sustainability projects is an asset. Technical expertise in drones or AI is not required.

candidate.description_text: A Spanish technology small and medium-sized enterprise is preparing a Eurostars research and development project for the September 2026 call. The company develops cloud software for smart mobility, including shared and on-demand transport services such as demand-responsive transport, ridepooling, carpooling, flexible shuttles and first and last mile transport. The problem addressed is that many transport operators and bus companies already use software for fleet supervision, vehicle location, dispatching, ticketing, planning or passenger information, but these platforms often lack a real-time module to orchestrate shared and on-demand mobility. As a result, operators may need separate tools to manage flexible services, which creates integration costs, fragmented data and limited scalability. The project will research, develop and validate an interoperable prototype that connects an artificial intelligence-based shared mobility orchestration module with an existing transport technology platform. The objective is not to replace the partner's platform, but to add a new module able to receive travel requests, read available transport supply, apply service rules, group compatible passengers, propose the most suitable transport option and return operational decisions to the partner platform. The expected technical work includes: definition of use cases and data models; application programming interfaces for bidirectional integration; connection with vehicle availability, routes, stops, booking and passenger information; development of a multimodal decision engine; simulation and sandbox testing with real or realistic data; and validation with a transport operator or operator users connected to the partner's platform. The preferred partner is a technology small and medium-sized enterprise from a Eurostars country with an existing software platform for public transport, bus operators, shared mobility operators or mobility authorities. Relevant platforms may include vehicle operation support systems, computer-aided dispatch and vehicle location systems, ticketing, mobility as a service, journey planning, fleet management, scheduling or intelligent transport systems. The targeted framework is Eurostars Call 11, September 2026. The call opens on 9 July 2026 and closes on 10 September 2026 at 14:00 Central European Summer Time. The intended expression of interest deadline for partner discussions is 14 August 2026. The indicative project duration is 24 months and the indicative total budget is around EUR 1.5 million. The project will focus exclusively on civil applications.
candidate.technical_problem_evidence_text: The partner sought should preferably be a technology small and medium-sized enterprise from a Eurostars country, compliant with the European definition of a small and medium-sized enterprise. The partner should have fewer than 250 employees and its own software product or platform in the mobility sector. Relevant expertise includes one or more of the following: software for bus or public transport operators; vehicle operation support systems; computer-aided dispatch and automatic vehicle location; fleet management; scheduling and dispatching; ticketing and account-based payment; journey planning; mobility as a service platforms; intelligent transport systems; data platforms for mobility authorities; or platforms used by taxi, bus, shuttle or shared mobility operators. The partner should be able to provide access to technical documentation, application programming interfaces, a sandbox or test environment, anonymised or synthetic operational data, and staff able to work on software integration. Access to at least one operator client or operational validation environment would be highly valuable, but it is not mandatory if the partner can provide realistic data and user validation. The partner is expected to co-develop and test the integration prototype, define data exchange requirements, validate interoperability with its existing platform, contribute to the technical architecture, participate in testing and support the commercial exploitation plan after the Eurostars project.
candidate.title: Spanish SME looks for partners to collaborate on a EUROSTARS  - ORBIT project to provide a platform integration expertise, programming interfaces, test data and validation with operator users in the field of  transport and mobility.

candidate.description_text: A consortium with high expertise in advanced composite materials and manufacturing is preparing a proposal for the European Defence Fund call EDF-SMERO-NT, aimed at developing innovative low-signature composite materials and related manufacturing approaches for military aerial applications. The project addresses the need for new material solutions that combine structural functionality, low observability and more sustainable processing routes for future platforms operating in demanding defence environments. The technical work is focused on the development of an advanced manufacturing process for low-signature composite material solutions for military platforms in the X-band. Planned activities include the study and synthesis of nanostructures, their integration into manufacturing routes, and the manufacture and validation of material coupons. The proposed strategy includes multilayer composite concepts based on recycled carbon fibre scrap, electronic printing based on recycled carbon fibre materials, and combined approaches integrating both strategies into a single material concept. The consortium is specifically looking for an end user active in unmanned aerial vehicles or other aerial platforms. This partner is expected to define operational needs and technical requirements for the new material in airborne defence environments, including performance expectations, integration constraints, use-case conditions and relevant validation scenarios. The participation of such an end user will help ensure that the material development is aligned from the outset with realistic platform needs and future application pathways. The proposal is being prepared under the European Defence Fund framework.
candidate.technical_problem_evidence_text: The consortium seeks an end user from the field of unmanned aerial vehicles or other aerial platforms for defence-related applications. The partner should be able to contribute to requirements definition for a new low-signature composite material, including operational conditions, platform integration constraints, expected material behaviour and relevant validation scenarios in airborne environments. The ideal partner would have experience in one or more of the following: •	Operation, integration or development of unmanned aerial vehicles or other aerial platforms •	Definition of platform-level technical requirements for materials or structures •	Knowledge of defence-related airborne mission conditions and environmental constraints relevant to material use •	Capacity to support use-case definition, relevance assessment and future validation planning
candidate.title: Ongoing consortium seeks UAV or air platform end user for European Defence Fund EDF-SMERO-NT project SILENCE on low-signature composite materials

candidate.description_text: A Spanish technology center is preparing a proposal for Horizon Europe RIVCircular, Topic 4-Circular economy in the textile industry. The project aims to establish a new circular and bio-based textile value chain by transforming agricultural residues into high-performance textile fibres and textile products. The consortium seeks a fibre technology partner, a textile manufacturer and an LCA expert partner in Norway and France to complete the consortium. FULL DESCRIPTION (Description of the company and its expertise, project description, call, needed partners, role of the partners they look for. 4.000 characters max) (COMPULSORY) The Spanish private technology center, with large experience in European projects, is building a consortium for the topic 4-Circular economy in the textile industry of the Horizon Europe RIVCircular call. The project aims to establish a new circular, regional and bio-based textile value chain by transforming agricultural residues into high-performance textile fibres and textile products. Rather than cultivating crops specifically for fibre production, the project focuses on valorizing agricultural by-products and residues generated from sustainable crop production systems, contributing simultaneously to waste reduction, rural development and industrial decarbonization. The project will integrate the complete value chain, from sustainable biomass production and feedstock characterisation to fibre extraction, fibre modification, spinning, textile manufacturing, product validation and circularity assessment. Environmental assessment methodologies will demonstrate the reduction of environmental impacts compared to synthetic textile materials. In order to complete the consortium, the coordinator is looking for a fibre technology partner, a textile manufacturer, an LCA expert partner and a potential end user in Norway (Innlandet region) and France (Hauts de France region) to complete the consortium.

candidate.description_text: An internationally recognised reference organisation in the creative economy, based in the Basque Country (Spain), with a track record in the European Union and in Latin America. It has developed a methodology and a digital tool for the mapping, interpretation and analysis of cultural and creative ecosystems (CCE), based on a proprietary taxonomy that classifies sectors, sub-sectors, value-chain links, agent typologies and impacts. The tool combines a map and a directory of public profiles — which makes it possible to find and connect spaces, agents and initiatives through geographic, typological and sectoral filters — with the collection of primary data that feeds reports and recommendations for the design of cultural and territorial policies. Its outlook is international, and its methodology has already been adapted to Latin American contexts. Description (technical) The organisation brings proven expertise in: ●	Taxonomic methodology for mapping the CCE: a system of matrices that categorises agents, sub-sectors, value-chain links and impacts, adaptable and contextualisable to different territories and regions. ●	Collection and analysis of primary data on the cultural and creative industries, handled anonymously and in aggregate form, to generate reports, statistics and recommendations for decision-making and policy design. ●	Digital platform for visibility and connection: a directory of public profiles, an advanced search engine and a map that can be embedded on institutional or association websites, reducing the digital divide that leaves many cultural agents invisible. ●	Participatory processes for the collection of qualitative and quantitative data, and for training and fostering relationships among ecosystem agents. It proposes putting this methodology and this data infrastructure at the service of an interregional pilot that maps, compares and connects the cultural and creative ecosystems of Europe and partner regions (Latin America, Africa, South-East Asia, the Far East), generating the knowledge base and the connections on which to build balanced cooperation. General objective To demonstrate, through interregional pilots, how a shared methodology for mapping and analysing cultural and creative ecosystems — together with the accompanying data and connection infrastructure — can strengthen creative-industries innovation beyond borders, fostering knowledge exchange, mutual learning and resilient, balanced partnerships between European and non-European agents (Focus 1, with synergies with Focus 2). Particular objectives 1. Adapt and apply a shared CCE-mapping taxonomy to different regional contexts, enabling coherent comparison of ecosystems across regions. 2. Generate primary data and a body of knowledge on the cultural and creative industries in partner regions, currently insufficiently documented. 3. Give visibility to and connect cultural agents through a shared directory and filters, creating real channels for cross-regional cooperation. 4. Analyse unequal access to global markets and asymmetries in sectoral partnerships, with explicit attention to gender and other intersectional dimensions, using the mapping data. 5. Produce reports and recommendations with policy relevance for the cultural sector, transferable to European institutions and to those of the partner regions. 6. Establish collaboration mechanisms and a data infrastructure that endure beyond the project's lifetime.
candidate.technical_problem_evidence_text: Tasks to be done / Specific cooperation sought The organisation would contribute the work package(s) on ecosystem mapping, data and analysis, and on agent visibility/connection, and would lead the implementation of the methodology on that side. It is looking for: ●	A coordinating entity with experience in Horizon Europe / Cluster 2 (or an already-formed consortium looking for this profile as a partner). ●	Research organisations and think-tanks in cultural policy and creative industries, for the analysis and recommendations work. ●	Cultural organisations, agent networks and creative-industries representatives from Latin America, Africa, South-East Asia and/or the Far East, for the interregional mapping and connection pilot. ●	Partners with experience in international cultural relations / cultural diplomacy (synergy with Focus 2), in gender and inclusion, and in green and digital transition. Role sought: partner and WP contributor; open to co-leading a mapping/data or dissemination work package.
candidate.title: Partners sought for a HORIZON project (Cluster 2): with experience in cultural-policy think-tanks, and cultural organisations from Latin America, Africa, South-East Asia or the Far East for the interregional piloting.

candidate.description_text: An internationally recognised reference organisation in the creative economy, based in the Basque Country (Spain). It has developed a methodology, a proprietary taxonomy and a digital tool for the mapping, diagnosis and analysis of cultural and creative ecosystems, which already incorporates artificial intelligence systems in its mapping and diagnostic processes. candidate.description_text: European agriculture is under increasing pressure to reduce greenhouse gas emissions, improve resource efficiency and adapt to increasingly demanding environmental regulations, while facing labour shortages and rising production costs. Permanent crops such as orchards, vineyards, olive groves and nut plantations continue to rely heavily on diesel-powered machinery, creatingsignificant environmental impacts through greenhouse gas emissions, air pollution, soil compaction and fossil fuel consumption. A European SME specialised in autonomous agricultural robotics is preparing a LIFE Programmedemonstration project aimed at validating a new generation of autonomous zero-emission robotic platforms for permanent crops under real farming conditions. The project will demonstrate how autonomous electric machinery can reduce environmental impacts while maintaining or improving operational efficiency and farm productivity. The consortium is currently seeking end users willing to participate as demonstration sites. Farms, cooperatives, producer organisations and agricultural companies managing permanent crops will have the opportunity to validate the technology during real production campaigns and contribute directly to the development of future sustainable agricultural machinery. Demonstration partners will participate in field trials carried out under normal farming conditions, allowing the project consortium to assess technical performance, environmental benefits and operational suitability across different crops, climatic conditions and farming practices. The project will quantify indicators such as greenhouse gas emissions, energy consumption, air pollutant emissions, soil compaction, noise reduction and optimisation of agricultural inputs through standardised monitoring and Life Cycle Assessment methodologies. The consortium welcomes end users operating orchards, vineyards, olive groves, citrus plantations and other permanent crops across Europe. Demonstration sites representing different environmental conditions, farming systems and geographical regions are particularly sought in order to maximise the project's environmental impact, replicability and long-term adoption throughout Europe.
candidate.technical_problem_evidence_text: The consortium is seeking end users and demonstration partners with experience in the management of permanent crops, willing to participate in the validation of innovative autonomous agricultural technologies under real farming conditions. Relevant expertise and capabilities include: • Commercial orchards, vineyards, olive groves, citrus or other permanent crop plantations suitable for demonstration activities. • Experience in sustainable farming practices and precision agriculture. • Capacity to host field demonstrations throughout complete agricultural campaigns. • Availability to support operational testing, environmental monitoring and data collection. • Interest in evaluating innovative technologies that contribute to reducing emissions, improving resource efficiency and increasing farm sustainability. • Willingness to collaborate with research organisations, technology developers and other industrial partners within a European innovation project. • Ability to provide technical feedback and operational requirements to support the validation and future deployment of autonomous agricultural machinery Preference will be given to organisations representing different climatic regions, crop types and farming systems across Europe in order to maximise the project's demonstration value and replication potential.
candidate.title: LIFE Call Partner Search: End Users for the Demonstration and Validation of Autonomous Agricultural Technologies
