candidate.description_text: A Spanish Research and Technology Organisation (RTO) is coordinating the preparation of a Horizon Europe Circular Bio-based Europe Joint Undertaking (CBE JU) proposal under call HORIZON-JU-CBE-2026-RIA-02 – SSbD bio-based polymers from alternative sources. Problem addressed: conventional plastic packaging relies heavily on fossil-based polymers and struggles to meet tightening EU circularity and chemical-safety requirements (Packaging and Packaging Waste Regulation, REACH). There is a lack of aromatic, biodegradable, bio-based polymer platforms that are simultaneously cost-competitive, safe by design and validated under real industrial packaging conditions. The project, Biobased4Pack, aims to develop next-generation aromatic and biodegradable bio-based polymer platforms using alternative agro-food residue streams generated through industrial operations and supermarket reverse logistics. The project combines biomass valorisation, renewable monomer production, bio-based polymer synthesis, packaging development, circularity assessment (LCA) and Safe and Sustainable by Design (SSbD) methodologies, targeting TRL progression from lab to pilot/demonstrator scale. The consortium currently includes technology centres, universities, industrial technology providers, circularity and regulatory specialists, feedstock owners and retail actors from Spain, Germany and France, and is now completing its industrial validation base ahead of submission. The project will develop and validate innovative packaging solutions for different market sectors through the production and validation of representative demonstrators. To strengthen the market validation activities, the consortium is seeking additional industrial end-users, packaging converters and brand owners interested in testing, validating and assessing novel bio-based packaging solutions under real operational conditions, including their recyclability and end-of-life performance. Partners sought should be willing to: •	Define application requirements and acceptance criteria for packaging demonstrators. •	Support demonstrator validation under real industrial conditions. •	Provide feedback regarding functionality, usability, recyclability and market requirements. •	Contribute to exploitation, replication and market uptake activities. The proposal is expected to be submitted to the CBE JU 2026 call (Research and Innovation Action). The planned project duration is 48 months and the expected total project budget is approximately €3 million. Potential target sectors include: •	Cosmetics and personal care packaging •	Healthcare and medical packaging •	Retail packaging •	Consumer goods packaging
candidate.technical_problem_evidence_text: The consortium is looking for: End-users / Brand Owners Companies interested in validating packaging solutions for commercial products. Packaging Users Manufacturers, retailers and companies using primary, secondary or tertiary packaging. Sector-specific Industrial Partners Preferably active in: •	Cosmetics and personal care •	Healthcare and medical products •	Retail and consumer products Expected contribution: •	Definition of technical and market requirements (e.g. barrier properties, mechanical performance, shelf-life, regulatory constraints). •	Validation of packaging demonstrators under real operating conditions. •	Assessment of user acceptance, recyclability and market readiness. •	Participation in exploitation, replication and dissemination activities. Previous participation in European projects is considered an advantage but is not mandatory.

candidate.description_text: A Spanish SME developing innovative floating photovoltaic tracking solutions is preparing an international R&D project proposal under the Transnational Eureka Lightweighting Call 2026. The company has successfully developed a single-axis floating solar tracker capable of increasing electricity generation by approximately 18-25% compared with conventional fixed floating photovoltaic systems. To support future commercial deployment and improve sustainability performance, a new generation of the technology is being designed with a strong focus on lightweight structures, circularity and environmental resilience. The proposed project aims to develop and validate an innovative structural platform for floating solar trackers operating in reservoirs, irrigation ponds, ports and other sheltered water environments, including potentially saline conditions. Main technical activities include: •	Development of sustainable lightweight structural materials based on recycled HDPE and advanced polymers. •	Substitution and optimisation of conventional structural materials. •	Design and validation of innovative components and manufacturing processes. •	Development of joining technologies and interface protection systems. •	Evaluation of durability under UV radiation, corrosion, saline water exposure, fatigue and biofouling conditions. •	Life cycle assessment, traceability, repairability and end-of-life disassembly studies. •	Design, manufacture and validation of a demonstration pilot installation. The project is planned as a bilateral collaboration between Spain and Germany, with a total duration of 24 months. The consortium currently seeks a German industrial partner capable of contributing to both technological development and industrial implementation.
candidate.technical_problem_evidence_text: The sought partner should preferably be a German SME or industrial company with expertise in one or more of the following areas: •	Recycled and sustainable HDPE materials. •	Advanced polymers. •	Sustainable plastics manufacturing. •	Material formulation and optimisation. •	Extrusion, injection moulding or related processing technologies. •	Structural components for outdoor applications. •	Corrosion and environmental resistance. •	Industrial prototyping and pilot production. •	Scale-up and industrialisation of innovative materials. The partner is expected to participate actively in the R&D activities and apply for funding through the appropriate German funding scheme (ZIM).

candidate.description_text: A reputed Spanish University Research Institute is exploring opportunities to join an EDF 2026 consortium with a patented technology based on a titanium-iron MOF material capable of degrading organophosphorus compounds, including laboratory simulants used to assess technologies against chemical threats. The technology could be developed as a functional self-decontaminating material for integration into technical textiles, coatings, paints or polymers, with potential application in CBRN protection, protective equipment, technical surfaces and defence-related materials. The technology is based on a titanium-iron metal-organic framework — MUV-17 / TiFe₂ — designed for the degradation of organophosphorus compounds, and it is protected under patent MOFs are highly porous crystalline materials that can interact with specific molecules inside their pores. In this case, the patented material has shown experimental activity at laboratory scale against organophosphorus compounds, including simulants commonly used in research to evaluate detoxification technologies for chemical threat scenarios. The current development status is laboratory validation. Further work would be required to integrate the material into relevant supports and validate its performance under operationally relevant conditions. Potential application routes include: - technical textiles with detoxifying functionality; - protective coatings; - paints and surface treatments; - polymer-based materials; - functional materials for CBRN protection of personnel, equipment or technical surfaces. The Institute would be interested in joining a consortium as a research and technology partner, contributing expertise in MOF materials, material synthesis, characterisation and laboratory validation of detoxification activity. A possible project approach could be the development and validation of MOF-based self-decontaminating materials for protection against chemical threats, including material integration, stability assessment, activity validation and a roadmap towards demonstrator-level prototypes. Potential European Defence Fund 2026 call topics: - EDF-2026-RA-MCBRN-DST — CBRN decontamination systems and technologies This appears to be the strongest fit, particularly regarding CBRN decontamination technologies and self-decontaminating materials for protection of personnel, equipment or surfaces. - EDF-2026-DA-MATCOMP-SMT — Smart and multifunctional textiles This could be a secondary fit if the technology is oriented towards integration into technical or multifunctional textiles for defence applications.

candidate.description_text: The project focuses on developing advanced structural damping and vibroacoustic technologies for next-generation aircraft and defense systems. Its main objective is to reduce airframe and cabin noise, mitigate engine noise sources and installation effects, and improve structural fatigue resistance, fully aligned with the expected outcomes of HORIZON-CL5-2027-04: reduction of airframe and cabin noise, mitigation of engine noise sources and installation effects, and the development of methodologies to manage noise perception and annoyance. The partner is a French SME specialized in vibroacoustics, headquartered in Toulouse France. Our highly responsive team is able to identify problems and then define solutions and developments up to the industrial stage. In its day-to-day operations, the company addresses issues within its area of expertise, ranging from those faced by SMEs to those of large industrial groups across all sectors: aerospace, transportation, defense, capital goods, and more. It offers solutions to problems based on its existing technologies, but also dedicates a significant portion of its activity to developing new ones to address emerging needs. R&D thus constitutes a substantial part of its business. With over 30 years of experience, the company has a proven track record in developing high-performance passive damping solutions for aerospace and defense systems and has participated in European collaborative projects. The company is currently a candidate as a partner in a European sustainable wind turbine development project, which brings together 17 partners in 4 EU countries. In the past, it coordinated two European projects focused on the development of vibroacoustic technologies. Methodology: the company uses an integrated "From Simulation to Industrialization" workflow: •	Software Tools: Utilization of industry-standard codes (NASTRAN, DYTRAN, MARC) alongside proprietary Python-based software. •	Integrated Process: Development begins with advanced simulation, followed by prototype construction and testing at ARTEC’s internal facilities to ensure industrial readiness. •	Custom Methodology: The Intelligent Damping Design® approach allows for targeted problem analysis and the creation of customized noise reduction technologies. Key Technological Building Blocks the company offers a proven portfolio of anti-vibration solutions, specifically validated for high-noise environments such as aircraft powered by counter- rotating open rotors: •	Fuselage Damping: Lightweight damping patches for fuselage skin (certified for fire/smoke) and specialized damping concepts for stringers and frames. •	Interior Comfort: Advanced damping floor technologies designed to mitigate engine harmonics. •	Developed in collaboration with the French Defence Procurement Agency (DGA), this structural damping connecting rod reduces vibrations at the source. candidate.description_text: French deep-tech company developing the first Large Vision Language Model (LVLM) for precision radiology. Our expertise lies in transforming massive 3D medical datasets into actionable diagnostic or predictive insights through an AI-native PACS (Picture Archiving and Communication System) viewer or through API integration designed to assist radiologists and researchers in a pathology-agnostic manner. technical expertise is broad and centered on three pillars: developing state-of-the-art open-source Foundation Models (FM) for radiology, fostering accessibility and adoption of AI in the medical world through AI as a Service approaches, and tackling real medical use cases through applied AI models integrated into multiscale workflows. (i) Developing state-of-the-art open-source Foundation Models (FM) for radiology: Our R&D team is heavily centered on building "frontier" AI, having already developed several large multimodal models trained on a massive corpus of over 200 million CT and MRI images. This provides an unparalleled baseline for anatomical understanding and feature extraction across diverse populations, accounting for age, sex, and gender differences. Our current efforts are focused on developing sovereign LVLMs for radiology which are open-source models trained on massive proprietary datasets and designed to understand both medical imaging and clinical text simultaneously. These models represent a paradigm shift, moving beyond simple image recognition to a sophisticated understanding of patient context, which is essential for the future of personalized medicine and European digital sovereignty, thus contributing to the development of dynamic Virtual Human Twins (VHTs) and bridging the gap to make advanced in-silico models accessible. (ii) Fostering accessibility and adoption through AI as a Service (AIaaS): We bridge the gap between the AI and medical worlds through AIaaS approaches. Indeed, we notably distribute our models through a native PACS viewer developed in-house as a SaaS platform or through advanced interoperable integration with existing PACS providers. We ensure that AI is not just powerful, but also resilient, easily deployable, and aligned with FAIR data principles to support clinical uptake within the European Health Data Space. (iii) Applying expertise to clinical-centric issues: As a specialized medical AI provider with an active footprint in clinical centers across Europe and the United States, translates theoretical breakthroughs into operational value. We integrate AI directly into the diagnostic loop for high-impact specialties such as Oncology, Cardiology, and Neurology. This applied AI approach is key to validating VHTs with longitudinal patient data, bringing real value to healthcare providers and precision medicine initiatives targeting cancers with limited treatment options or low survival rates. Company seeks to join Consortium Coordinators or Lead Partners that aim at answering to the HORIZON-MISS-2026-02-CANCER-03 European program as a technical partner in charge of a WP or associated to it.
candidate.technical_problem_evidence_text: We are looking for Consortium Coordinators or Lead Partners who require a specialized deep-tech SME to lead or be part of AI and Healthcare centered Work Packages. What we provide to the Consortium: The Foundation Model Brick: State-of-the-art, pre-trained 3D medical LVLMs; The Product & Biomarker Brick: An AI-native PACS viewer designed for immediate clinical integration. This tool enables the automated extraction of a vast spectrum of complex biomarkers, transforming every examination into a flow of structured, comprehensive, and actionable biological data for precision medicine. Expertise: Beyond standard AI, we bridge the "clinical last mile." We bring high-level R&D combined with a deep mastery of medical workflows and international regulatory standards

candidate.description_text: A French AgriTech DeepTech startup (Toulouse, founded in 2025) built on 3 years of R&D validated within a Tunisian agritech company with 522 ha of field-validated deployments). The platform is the first full-stack digital twin for precision irrigation and smart fertigation combining LoRaWAN IoT, FAO-56 agronomic AI, and XAI/SHAP explainability, currently assessed at TRL 6. THE TECHNOLOGY (Technical part) The Cloud-Edge-IoT architecture consists of 5 layers: (1) 15 AgroSense/SenseCAP LoRaWAN sensors (soil moisture, EC, pH, temperature, leaf moisture, flow, pressure, CO₂, PAR light, microclimate) — all IP67/68, CE/RoHS, LoRaWAN V1.0.3 OTAA EU868; (2) SenseCAP M2 SX1302 shared gateway covering multiple farms simultaneously, reducing per-farm cost by 70–85%; (3) AWS IoT Core/Lambda backend; (4) Java Spring Boot API; (5) Angular SaaS dashboard The core algorithm computes ETc = ET0 × Kc (FAO-56 Penman-Monteith), integrates soil water balance, and generates automated precision irrigation and fertigation schedules. The platform adds three simultaneous agronomic models (hydraulic, nutritional NPK, physiological phenology) with experimental protocol management and SHAP/XGBoost explainability that isolates the exact contribution of each variable to recommendations. VALIDATED RESULTS (field pilots, 522 ha, 2022–2025): 15–25% water savings, +8–15% yield improvement, 15–30% fertilizer reduction. Active commercial pipeline: >2,300 ha in Occitanie cooperatives, viticultural estates, and arboricultural farms. INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY: 2 INPI patents pending (synchronised fertigation algorithm; hydraulic leak and anomaly detection). GATE 5.0 CONTEXT: The company seeks an Agrifood SME partner (farmer, cooperative, or food processor) to co-submit a joint proposal under Topic 1 (Water Management) or Topic 4 (Soil Health & Crop Optimisation). The technology French SME contributes to the full IoT/AI technology stack, deployment expertise, and agronomic modelling. The agrifood partner contributes an operational irrigated field site, sector-specific knowledge, and real-world validation context. Total funding : up to 118 500€ per consortium (59,250€ per SME). Programme start : August 2026. Submission deadline : 30 April 2026.
candidate.technical_problem_evidence_text: No specific technical expertise is required from the agrifood partner. The only prerequisites are an operational irrigated site equipped with a standard irrigation network (pump, valves, and flowmeter) and the ability to share historical data on water consumption and yields — in any standard format — to support project KPI measurement. The platform is designed for seamless integration with the vast majority of existing European irrigation systems via Modbus RS485, a standard industrial communication protocol, eliminating any need to replace or upgrade existing infrastructure.

candidate.description_text: EMDF addresses the structural disadvantage faced by European media SMEs (99.8% of companies, yet under 50% of sector revenues) by providing a turnkey distribution infrastructure connecting rights holders with editorial resellers across multiple EU territories. The platform, NSeven_V2, integrates AI-powered metadata tooling (Holli/HOLLM + PRODO) for automated content enrichment, rights verification, and environmental impact measurement; green streaming technology (Quanteec) reducing CDN bandwidth consumption; and a transparent AVOD trust layer combating ad fraud. The cross-sectoral dimension is delivered through WTPL, a music rights manager with a 30-country sub-publisher network, enabling the distribution of live music content alongside audiovisual works. The project will be validated through a proof-of-concept deployment with BFM Grand Lille, France (regional media) and scaled across 5 European territories additionally to France ( Seweden, Poland, Germany, Italy, Spain, etc)
candidate.technical_problem_evidence_text: The consortium seeks additional partners with expertise in: (1) European audience analytics and recommendation systems for editorial platforms; (2) Cross-border rights clearance automation, particularly for music synchronisation and multi-territory licensing; (3) Regional media networks, cultural institutions, press editors, …, in targeted EU territories (Germany, Benelux, Iberian Peninsula, Nordics) willing to act as pilot resellers or content owners for the platform.

candidate.description_text: A French deep-tech company developing autonomous drone systems based on neuromorphic computing is seeking to join a consortium for the Horizon Europe call HORIZON-CL3-2026-01-BM-01 – Advanced border surveillance and situational awareness. The company is  part of the EUDIS Business Accelerator cohort 2, being selected top20 among more than 400 applicants. This call addresses the need for enhanced real-time situational awareness at European borders, where current UAV-based solutions remain limited by high latency, heavy onboard systems, and high energy consumption. The French company develops embedded neuromorphic vision systems enabling ultra-fast and energy-efficient perception and decision-making directly onboard drones. In line with the call objectives, the company aims to: •	Provide real-time drone detection and tracking capabilities for border surveillance •	Enable distributed and autonomous situational awareness systems •	Contribute to rapid response mechanisms, including drone interception •	Improve UAV autonomy and operational range beyond current supervision constraints. Current UAV-based border surveillance solutions are often limited by high latency, heavy onboard processing units, and high energy consumption, which restricts mission autonomy and real-time response capabilities. •	Provide real-time detection and tracking of threats for border surveillance. •	Enable distributed and autonomous situational awareness. •	Contribute to rapid response mechanisms, including drone-on-drone interception. •	Extend the operational range and autonomy of UAVs beyond current supervision constraints. The company wishes to join an existing consortium or one in formation. The Expression of Interest (EOI) deadline is the 5th of September and call deadline is the 5th of November 2026. Expected Role of the Partner: Partners are sought to facilitate system integration, provide expertise in robotics or sensor fusion, or act as end-users (border management authorities) to provide an operational validation framework. Activities are expected to achieve TRL 6-7 by the end of the project.

candidate.description_text: A French Technology Transfer Office (TTO) dedicated to innovation and technology transfer subsidiary of a French university supports innovative projects through TRL maturation, funding strategy, IP management, licensing and spinout creation. The French TTO also incubates and accelerates deep-tech startups, while facilitating the transfer and commercialization of academic research results to industry. For the Horizon EIE call, the project could focus on university-linked TTO models, with three operational pillars: 1.	Startup-friendly licensing and technology transfer: simplified negotiation pathways, model clauses, clearer decision processes and licensing approaches better adapted to spinouts and early-stage deep-tech startups. 2.	Value-sharing and incentive mechanisms: practical models for revenue sharing, royalties, equity participation and incentives for researchers, students and academic teams involved in valorization. 3.	Intellectual asset portfolio strategies: approaches to make intellectual assets more readable, attractive and marketable, including package deals for licensing or transfer to companies and startups. Expected activities could include mapping and sharing best practices, developing a common European toolbox, designing templates and decision frameworks, and testing these tools through concrete commercialization pilot cases. The final objective would be to produce a European blueprint for more efficient, fair and startup-compatible technology transfer. The French office is particularly interested in partnering with TTOs or university innovation structures that can have a transformative impact within their institutions and are ready to test new tools in real operational settings. Experience in researcher/student incentive schemes, revenue-sharing models, equity mechanisms, or intellectual asset portfolio packaging would be a strong added value.

candidate.description_text: A Bordeaux-based French cluster dedicated to the vine, wines and spirits sector, bringing together winegrowers, supplier companies, technical centers, research organizations, and public institutions that view innovation as a key driver of sustainable economic performance, is looking for partners to participate to call HORIZON-CL6-2026-01-CIRCBIO-09: Balancing food security, bioeconomy, climate and biodiversity objectives to unlock sustainable value chains (deadline: 17/09/2026). The French wine sector faces significant economic pressures, climate-related challenges, and a growing need to diversify farm revenues while improving environmental performance. Viticulture generates substantial volumes of by-products including grape pomace, wine lees, grape seeds, and vine pruning residues. These biomass streams can feed circular bio-based value chains such as polyphenols, functional food ingredients, cosmetics, biochar, soil amendments, and renewable energy. The key challenge is not solely technological — it is about designing fair, sustainable, and replicable value chains that avoid resource-use conflicts and ensure primary producers capture a fair share of the value generated. The French cluster is already collaborating with other European clusters and technology transfer organisations in the wine sector in Spain, Portugal, and Italy, with which they are currently implementing several European projects. The French wine innovation cluster's role in the project will be to lead a dedicated wine-sector case study. Their added value lies in direct access to winegrowers and sector stakeholders, practical knowledge of biomass logistics during harvest, and experience in collaborative innovation involving industry, research, and public actors. The case study would assess biomass availability, economic incentives, value distribution, business models, environmental trade-offs, soil health implications, and replication potential across European wine regions. Activities could include stakeholder workshops with winegrowers, cooperatives, distilleries, SMEs, and downstream users, with synergies explored with existing initiatives such as C4B and GRAPPA. The objective is to develop practical recommendations for policymakers and value-chain actors on how circular bioeconomy models can support income diversification, climate and biodiversity goals, and long-term resilience of food and farming systems. Specifically, the French cluster's role within the project could be as follows: •	lead or co-lead the viticulture case study; •	mobilise winegrowers and value chain actors; •	organise interviews and workshops; •	provide practical knowledge on grape pomace, wine lees, and pruning residues; •	contribute to the analysis of business and governance models; •	support the dissemination of results to the wine sector; •	help translate project findings into concrete recommendations for farmers, SMEs, and public decision-makers. Other competences in the consortium already include: •	expertise on new areas of valorisation and business models in the wine sector •	dissemination of results
candidate.technical_problem_evidence_text: Expertise sought within the consortium: •	life cycle assessment and environmental evaluation; •	biodiversity indicators; •	natural capital accounting; •	agricultural economics; •	nature markets, carbon or biodiversity credits; •	assessment of bio-based value chains. They are particularly interested in partnering with companies or research organisations working on agricultural residues, circular bioeconomy, agricultural business models, and fair value distribution.

candidate.description_text: Most drug discovery processes today rely on whole-cell or cell-free assays, which fail to capture the complexity of intracellular biology. Organelles such as lysosomes, mitochondria and the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) are small compartments located inside the cells and are central to cell function. A dysfunctioning organelle can trigger lysosomal storage disorders, rare diseases, neurodegeneration, metabolic diseases, immunology, cancer and others. Yet, these organelles remain largely inaccessible to standard screening platforms. This gap results in poor target validation, low assay reproducibility, and high attrition rates in early drug discovery. Company has developed a patented microfluidic process to isolate functional organelles at scale, stable for months, in preparations fully compatible with high-throughput screening (HTS) platforms. Our products, LYSO-Prep™ and MITO-Prep™, enable pharmaceutical and biotech companies to run drug discovery assays directly on isolated organelles, delivering improved biological relevance, precision and reproducibility. This shifts drug discovery from a cell-based vision to an organelle-based new paradigm. The proposed project aims to expand the scope and impact of organelle-based research across four dimensions. First, extending organelle extraction capabilities across lysosomes, mitochondria and the ER to new and underexplored cell types, including primary cells, iPSC-derived models, tissue-specific models and patient tissues. Second, developing and validating organelle-based assays spanning the full drug discovery value chain — from target pharmacology to safety assessment. Isolated organelles offer a uniquely direct and relevant system to evaluate how compounds interact with specific intracellular compartments: assessing lysosomal membrane permeabilisation, mitochondrial toxicity, or ER stress responses at the organelle level, earlier and with greater precision than current cell-based methods allow. This opens a new field of intracellular toxicology with direct implications for preclinical safety profiling and attrition reduction. Third, generating large-scale organelle-resolved molecular datasets — including proteomics, metabolomics, and lipidomics — on isolated organelle fractions derived from disease-relevant models. This organelle-level omics layer will provide unprecedented resolution into compartment-specific biology, enabling the identification of new drug targets and mechanistic biomarkers inaccessible through whole-cell approaches. Fourth, establishing organelle extraction directly from patient-derived tissues, creating a translational bridge between preclinical models and human disease. Organelle preparations from biopsies or surgical specimens will be profiled to identify disease-associated signatures, with direct applications in biomarker discovery and, longer term, in companion diagnostics or patient stratification tools. The enterprise will contribute its core expertise in organelle membrane physiology, extraction technology and scale-up capabilities across all partner activities, ensuring high-quality, functional organelle preparations at the throughput required by each workpackage. The consortium could bring together: academic laboratories with expertise in cell or organelle biology; industrial partners from the pharmaceutical or biotech sector, contributing compound libraries or assay development expertise; omics and bioinformatics specialists to generate and interpret organelle-resolved molecular datasets; clinical or public partners with access to patient tissues and expertise in translational biomarker research; toxicology specialists from academic institutions or CROs. Other profiles relevant to the project scope are welcome. Target programmes: Horizon Europe, Eurostars, EIC Pathfinder. Expected project start: Q4 2026. Call deadlines vary by programme and will be confirmed upon expression of interest. Typical project duration: 2-3 years.
candidate.technical_problem_evidence_text: Company is seeking partners whose expertise complements its core capabilities in organelle extraction, membrane physiology and scale-up, and who can contribute to one or more of the project's research dimensions. Academic laboratories are sought for their expertise in cell or organelle biology, particularly those working with primary cells, iPSC-derived models, tissue-specific cell lines or patient-derived specimens. Their role would be to provide access to new cell types, support biological validation of organelle preparations, contribute to functional characterisation workflows, and where relevant, facilitate access to clinical samples in collaboration with anatomopathology or biobank infrastructure. Industrial partners from the pharmaceutical or biotech sector are sought for their expertise in drug discovery, assay development or compound screening. Their role would be to benchmark organelle-based pharmacology and toxicology assays against existing platforms, contribute compound libraries or active pipelines, and validate the applicability of company's preparations within real drug discovery and preclinical safety contexts. Toxicology specialists, from academic institutions or CROs, are sought for their expertise in in vitro toxicology, safety pharmacology or regulatory sciences. Their role would be to co-develop organelle-based toxicology assays — including mitochondrial liability, lysosomal disruption or ER stress profiling — define biologically meaningful readouts, and assess regulatory applicability. Omics and bioinformatics specialists are sought to generate, process and interpret large-scale organelle-resolved molecular datasets. Their role would be to apply proteomics, metabolomics or lipidomics workflows to isolated organelle fractions and contribute to biomarker identification pipelines. Clinical and anatomopathology partners with access to patient tissues and translational research expertise are sought to support organelle extraction from biopsies or surgical specimens, and to co-develop disease-associated molecular signatures with diagnostic or patient stratification potential.
candidate.title: French start up look for partners under Horizon Europe program (extraction and purification of stable and functionnal organelles as a NAM)

candidate.description_text: The French biotech SME is preparing to join an EIC Pathfinder consortium under the "Biotechnology for Healthy Ageing" challenge. The company specializes in the development of a versatile ligand platform designed to address the "therapeutic drug delivery" work package. This technology focuses on innovative preventive or therapeutic interventions acting on the hallmarks of ageing. The platform addresses a critical scientific gap: in many current therapies, only 1% to 3% of the agent reaches its intracellular target due to limited permeability or systemic toxicity. The company's glyco-engineered ligands enhance receptor-mediated uptake and intracellular trafficking, specifically targeting the mannose 6-phosphate receptor (M6PR). This approach enables precise targeting of tissues beyond the liver, such as bone, muscle, heart, prostate, or colon. The technology is highly modular and can be grafted onto various therapeutic compounds, including enzymes, antibodies, ASOs, or gene-editing tools. With over 10 years of expertise in glyco-chemistry and a solid intellectual property portfolio, the SME provides precise control over the conjugation and characterization process. The company seeks to integrate its expertise into a high-risk, high-gain project for the October 2026 deadline.

candidate.description_text: A French technological center is coordinating a Horizon Europe project to develop innovative lead-free brass alloys for the energy sector. Leaded brass is widely used in fluid distribution, automotive and electrical applications due to its excellent machinability, corrosion resistance and sealing properties. However, growing regulatory pressure in Europe, including the Drinking Water Directive, ELV (End-of-Life Vehicles), RoHS and REACH frameworks, is accelerating the replacement of lead-containing alloys with safer and more sustainable alternatives. While several low-lead and lead-free brass grades have already been developed for drinking water applications, significant challenges remain in the energy sector, which operate under more demanding conditions such as higher temperatures, thermal cycling, pressure fluctuations and stringent long-term tightness requirements. The project aims to develop and validate innovative lead-free brass grades capable of meeting these technical requirements while complying with Safe and Sustainable by Design (SSbD) principles. A key objective is to demonstrate their industrial feasibility and performance through pilot-scale validation in representative use cases, paving the way for future market uptake and supporting the transition towards lead-free components in strategic European industrial sectors. The methodology developed will be transferable to other sectors (automotive, medical, process industries). Industrial partner (end-user), active in the brass value chain and target application markets, capable of leading the validation of the developed lead-free brass within a relevant use case at TRL 7 are searched in the frame of a Research agreement and/or technological agreement
candidate.technical_problem_evidence_text: Industrial partner (end-user), active in the brass value chain and target application markets (fluid distribution, automotive and electrical applications, ...), energy sector, capable of leading the validation of the developed lead-free brass within a relevant use case at TRL 7 are searched. The partner should have access to pilot-scale and/or semi-industrial manufacturing facilities for brass component production, enabling the integration, demonstration and validation of the developed material under representative operational conditions. * Other technology partners and tech contribution may be considered for future developments and areas of application

candidate.description_text: A French company is developing a multi-index biomarker panel for the detection of age-related pathology, including cancer and chronic inflammatory conditions. The panel has been designed (TRL 1) and now requires validation in a retrospective clinical study, together with a route to clinical adoption. Within a proposal to Objective 2 of the Healthy Ageing Challenge — a biomarker-based tool to enable the responsible deployment of ageing-related interventions — the company is seeking three complementary partners: 1. Biobanks and research groups with suitable sample collections They are looking for banked material from patients with cancer, from patients with chronic inflammatory or metabolic conditions (Crohn's disease, cardiovascular disease, diabetes, arthritis and similar), and from healthy controls, in one or both of the following forms: – leukocytes or PBMCs, viably cryopreserved in at least 10% DMSO – plasma Longitudinal collections, with repeat samples from the same individuals over time, are of particular interest, as they allow the effect of ageing to be assessed directly. Samples must be accompanied by clinical annotation (age, sex, diagnosis, stage or disease activity, treatment status) and be transferable under an MTA with appropriate consent. 2. Regulatory expertise Diagnostic tools for the assessment of ageing-related risk do not yet exist as a regulated category, so neither the regulatory strategy nor the deployment pathway has been established. One of the expected outcomes of this Challenge is the development of approaches to the shared regulatory hurdles and societal questions linked to ageing-related interventions, in order to facilitate their adoption. They are therefore seeking regulatory experts to define the regulatory strategy and assess deployment feasibility for their technology, and to work with other projects in the Challenge portfolio on these common roadmaps. 3. Scientific communication The adoption of new ageing-related tools depends on their uptake by clinical partners and on public understanding of what they do and do not measure. They are therefore seeking professionals experienced in scientific communication with both medical and public audiences.

candidate.description_text: Space safety has become a critical challenge due to the exponential increase of active satellites and space debris in Low Earth Orbit (LEO). To address this, a French SME specializing in space situational awareness is currently deploying a global network of advanced space surveillance radars, as well as the digital infrastructure required to build a real-time picture of space events. The main objective of this collaborative project is to improve the capability of the company's digital infrastructure to understand the behaviors of space objects. This will be achieved through the integration of advanced modeling techniques combined with artificial intelligence (AI). Within this framework, the sought German partner will focus on bringing its specialized expertise to the development of innovative AI algorithms to enhance overall knowledge of the orbital environment. The project is prepared under the framework conditions of the bilateral French-German joint R&D call (Bpifrance / ZIM). The collaborative project has a planned duration of 24 months (96 weeks), with an expression of interest and proposal submission deadline in November 2026.
candidate.technical_problem_evidence_text: The sought partner should be an innovative company (SME) or a research organization with strong, proven expertise in Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML). Specifically, the partner is expected to bring know-how in: •	Algorithm Development: Designing and training advanced machine learning algorithms (such as deep learning, neural networks, or pattern recognition) capable of processing and analyzing large, noisy, or complex physical datasets. •	Predictive Modeling: Developing models to analyze behaviors, detect anomalies or maneuvers, and predict future states or trajectories. No prior specialization or experience in the space domain is required. The French SME will provide all necessary domain-specific background, physical parameters, and labeled radar tracking data.
candidate.title: A French space technology SME seeks a German partner specialized in artificial intelligence and machine learning algorithms under the Bpifrance/ZIM bilateral call.

candidate.description_text: The coordinator is a multidisciplinary research laboratory combining biomechanics, assistive robotics, artificial intelligence and human factors, operating experimental platforms dedicated to mobility and rehabilitation. the core group is preparing a proposal for the Horizon Europe topic HORIZON-HLTH-2027-01-STAYHLTH-01 ("Addressing disabilities through the life course to support independent living and inclusion"). The project adopts a life-course approach to disability. It combines AI/deep learning, biomechanical modelling and an intelligent, sensor-based assistive device, together with multi-site clinical/human-factors validation, to support functional autonomy and participation. The consortium (target: 6-7 countries, up to 12 partners, EUR 6-8 million EU contribution) already gathers expertise in biomechanics/engineering , AI/deep learning. To complete the consortium ahead of the call's expected opening (10/02/2027), they are looking for: - a partner (research organisation, SSH institute, or disability representative organisation) able to lead a named co-design/SSH task ensuring effective, active involvement of people with disabilities in the research ( which is a call requirement); - additional clinical sites able to contribute to multi-site longitudinal validation across the three life-course profiles (paediatric, adult/trauma, geriatric/neurodegenerative); - a regulatory affairs partner with expertise in EU MDR and AI Act, to support the classification pathway of the assistive device and its AI-based software component. Cooperation type sought: Research and development cooperation agreement, i.e. joint preparation and, if the proposal is successful, joint delivery of the Horizon Europe project as consortium partners (not a commercial or licensing relationship).

candidate.description_text: The proposed Research and Development Request addresses the need for reliable and interpretable AI agents capable of performing complex scientific tasks in real-world environments, as defined in the Horizon Europe call HORIZON-CL4-2026-05-DIGITAL-EMERGING-02. Current AI-driven discovery workflows often rely on data-intensive approaches that lack physical consistency and limited adaptability when applied to experimental research settings. The requesting entities consist of a university pharmaceutical laboratory and a physics and artificial intelligence research centre. The collaboration focuses on the integration of physics-informed artificial intelligence with experimental biophysical and pharmaceutical research. The objective is to contribute to the development of autonomous AI agents that can decompose complex scientific problems into structured sub-tasks, operate within known physical laws, and adapt their behaviour based on continuous feedback from simulations and experimental data. The physics and AI research centre contributes expertise in applied mathematics, numerical modelling and high-fidelity simulations, including fluid, particle and magnetohydrodynamic models originally developed for astrophysical research. These methods are combined with physics-informed neural networks to accelerate simulations and reduce computational cost while preserving physical consistency. The university pharmaceutical laboratory provides application-driven use cases, experimental workflows and high-quality datasets. Its activities include computational drug design with a focus on G protein-coupled receptors and antimicrobial compounds, molecular dynamics simulations of biomolecular systems, and experimental validation in pharmaceutical and theranostic research. The laboratory enables the validation and benchmarking of AI agent outputs through real experimental feedback. Within a Horizon Europe Research and Innovation Action, the partners aim to support the design, testing and validation of AI agents that operate across simulation and experimental environments. The consortium is expected to submit a single-stage proposal by the call deadline of 15 April 2026, with an expression of interest deadline of 25 March 2026. The partners are seeking a coordinator to lead the consortium and integrate their contributions into a coherent multi-agent research framework under a research and development cooperation agreement.

candidate.description_text: AI systems increasingly shape critical life outcomes—educational grading, employment screening, social media curation—yet operate as opaque "black boxes" that perpetuate social biases. Marginalized students are disproportionately affected but lack the literacy to challenge these systems, creating a "democratic deficit" where critical technology understanding remains an elite privilege. FAIR-PATH (Fostering AI Inclusion & Responsibility through Partnerships for Academic Transitions and Human-centricity) addresses this gap through a strategic research-to-classroom bridge. Led by InsightBrains, a Greek independent AI advisory and education organization specializing in responsible AI implementation, the project transforms students from passive technology consumers into "Responsible AI Practitioners." The consortium's current structure includes InsightBrains (Greece) as coordinator providing technical and scientific leadership, two secondary schools (one from Greece and one from abroad) and -potentially- a fourth, NGO, partner. The core innovation shifts from traditional digital literacy (tool usage) to "Responsible AI Literacy" (ethical interrogation). Using a signature gamified pedagogical methodology designed to deconstruct algorithmic decision-making through experiential auditing, students conduct hands-on audits of real-world systems—generative AI platforms, search algorithms—visualizing how data practices perpetuate inequalities based on race, gender, or socioeconomic status. Primary objectives: (1) co-design a trilingual "Responsible AI Playbook" (English, Greek, Partner Language) with a structured sequence of proprietary pedagogical modules that bridge high-level AI research with secondary education utilizing a proprietary ethical framework based on international AI auditing standards; (2) train 20+ "Ethical AI Mentors" across two countries for interdisciplinary AI ethics integration in Math, Science, Social Studies; (3) empower 100+ marginalized students (identified via local NGOs) to increase digital self-efficacy and career readiness; (4) introduce "Green AI" concepts on the environmental footprint of data centers and algorithmic efficiency, aligning with EU Green Deal. Work program: Activity 1 (Responsible AI Framework Lab) - InsightBrains leads co-creation with teachers from Greek and EU partner schools, utilizing eTwinning TwinSpace for virtual collaboration before physical meetings. Activity 2 (Training Ethical AI Mentors) - intensive transnational training event where InsightBrains equips educators to facilitate AI audits and manage ethical classroom debates, with emphasis on green travel practices. Activity 3 (Responsible AI Showcase & Policy Lab) - students present AI Audit Reports to local stakeholders, receiving FAIR-PATH Responsible AI Badges as digital credentials. Budget: €60,000 (Erasmus+ KA210-SCH lump sum). Schools serving diverse populations and committed to digital inclusion and environmental responsibility are invited to join this cross-border "Research-to-Classroom" initiative.
candidate.technical_problem_evidence_text: The consortium seeks a secondary school partner from an EU Member State meeting the following criteria: Essential institutional characteristics: - Accredited secondary education institution (general or vocational) serving students aged 12-18 (ISCED levels 2-3) - Location in EU Member State with Erasmus+ national agency access (priority: Spain, Italy, Portugal; also open: France, Germany, other EU countries) - Demonstrated commitment to educational equity, with significant proportion of students from socio-economically disadvantaged backgrounds, migrant or refugee populations, or other marginalized communities - Administrative capacity to serve as formal Erasmus+ KA210-SCH partner, managing lump-sum funding and reporting requirements through national agency - Institutional commitment to digital inclusion and environmental responsibility in education Pedagogical expertise and commitment: - Teaching staff with interest in digital ethics, critical thinking, social justice education, or STEM innovation - Openness to interdisciplinary curriculum integration connecting AI ethics to mathematics, science, social studies, and civic education - Experience with or willingness to adopt gamified, project-based, or inquiry-based learning methodologies - Capacity to facilitate student-centered learning requiring critical analysis rather than passive consumption Implementation capabilities: - Ability to recruit and engage 40-50 secondary students for pilot implementation, with particular attention to inclusion of marginalized learners through partnerships with local NGOs or community organizations - Access to basic digital infrastructure (computers, tablets, internet) for students to conduct AI system audits - Institutional support for organizing community showcase events, inviting local stakeholders including parents, industry representatives, and policymakers - Willingness to participate in eTwinning TwinSpace virtual collaboration before and after physical mobility activities Language and collaboration: - Staff members with working proficiency in English for consortium collaboration (trilingual Playbook will be produced in English, Greek, and partner country language) - Commitment to virtual meetings, online co-design workshops, and collaborative digital documentation - Readiness to send 3-5 teachers to Greece for intensive Ethical AI Mentors training (travel costs covered by project budget) Sustainability and values alignment: - Commitment to environmental sustainability in education, including willingness to explore "Green AI" concepts with students and utilize low-carbon transport for mobility activities where feasible - Institutional values aligned with democratic resilience, algorithmic accountability, and youth empowerment - Interest in long-term integration of responsible AI education into curriculum beyond project period

candidate.description_text: GENIA (Genomic Pharmacy & Personalised Medicine Skills Innovation Alliance) is an Erasmus+ Alliances for Innovation project (Lot 1: ERASMUS-EDU-2026-PI-ALL-INNO-EDU-ENTERP) addressing the critical pharmacogenomics skills gap across Europe. Despite growing policy momentum and infrastructure investment in precision medicine, fewer than 10% of pharmacy professionals feel adequately prepared to interpret and apply pharmacogenomic test results. GENIA establishes a Nordic-Mediterranean skills corridor connecting Europe’s most advanced genomic medicine ecosystems with its largest implementation frontiers. The project will design, develop and pilot: (1) an HE curriculum module on clinical pharmacogenomics for pharmacy and medical students (EQF 6-7); (2) a VET curriculum for genomic laboratory technicians (EQF 5); (3) a micro-credential programme for practising pharmacists and physicians; and (4) two ESCO-compliant occupational profiles. Curricula will be co-designed with enterprise partners through skills needs analysis, then piloted with at least 300 learners. The project directly supports the EU Deep Tech Talent Initiative, building workforce capacity in genomics and AI-enabled healthcare. A clinical decision support simulator will enable learners to practise integrating genomic information into prescribing workflows. All resources will be available as Open Educational Resources. The consortium seeks partners with expertise in pharmacy/medical education, VET curriculum development, clinical pharmacogenomics, bioinformatics and genomic laboratory practice.
candidate.technical_problem_evidence_text: Partners should have expertise in one or more of: pharmacy or medical education (HE); vocational education and training curriculum development; clinical pharmacogenomics or genomic medicine; bioinformatics and genomic data analysis; clinical genetics laboratory management; hospital pharmacy management; pharmaceutical R&D; digital health and electronic health records; AI-enabled clinical decision support systems; ESCO occupational profile development; micro-credential design and quality assurance.

Curricula will be co-designed with enterprise partners through skills needs analysis, then piloted with at least 300 learners. The project directly supports the EU Deep Tech Talent Initiative, building workforce capacity in genomics and AI-enabled healthcare. A clinical decision support simulator will enable learners to practise integrating genomic information into prescribing workflows. All resources will be available as Open Educational Resources. The consortium seeks partners with expertise in pharmacy/medical education, VET curriculum development, clinical pharmacogenomics, bioinformatics and genomic laboratory practice.
technical_problem_evidence_text: Partners should have expertise in one or more of: pharmacy or medical education (HE); vocational education and training curriculum development; clinical pharmacogenomics or genomic medicine; bioinformatics and genomic data analysis; clinical genetics laboratory management; hospital pharmacy management; pharmaceutical R&D; digital health and electronic health records; AI-enabled clinical decision support systems; ESCO occupational profile development; micro-credential design and quality assurance.
title: Erasmus+ Alliances for Innovation partner sought for genomic pharmacy and personalised medicine skills curriculum development

candidate.description_text: A Greek university is preparing a proposal for submission to the Creative Europe Programme – CREA-CULT-2026-COOP-2: European Cooperation Projects (Medium Scale). The project will address the call objective of strengthening transnational creation and circulation of European cultural works and artists.The initiative focuses on the cultural heritage and artistic traditions of historically multicultural cities in the Black Sea region. These cities have long functioned as hubs of cultural exchange, hosting diverse communities and artistic influences. However, many local cultural expressions and community traditions remain under-documented and insufficiently represented in contemporary cultural cooperation initiatives. The project aims to explore how these cultural traditions can inspire new forms of artistic creation, collaboration and community engagement across the region. The consortium will develop activities that connect cultural heritage with contemporary artistic practices and support the transnational circulation of cultural content. Planned activities may include: •	research and documentation of cultural traditions and community practices in selected port cities •	collaborative artistic experimentation and co-creation involving artists and cultural practitioners from different countries •	development of cultural events, exhibitions or artistic productions inspired by the documented traditions •	cross-border exchange activities promoting cultural dialogue and artistic mobility •	dissemination activities designed to share project outcomes with wider cultural audiences. The project will be implemented through a consortium of cultural and research organisations from the Black Sea region, combining expertise in cultural heritage, artistic production and community engagement. The expected project duration is approximately 36 months, in line with the framework conditions of the Creative Europe programme. Additional partners are sought to strengthen the consortium with complementary expertise and to contribute to the transnational development, co-creation and circulation of cultural works and artistic practices.

candidate.description_text: The Interreg VI-A Greece-Italy cooperation program under the objective RSO 2.4 (climate change adaptation) and intervention category 60 focuses on the adaptation to climate change measures and prevention and management of climate related risks: such as natural events, e.g. storms and drought. The cooperation at the cross-border level is expected to raise awareness, maximize civil protection and broaden disaster management systems, infrastructures and ecosystem-based approaches, increase capacities, contributing to greater ecological resilience and reduced negative impacts from climate change. Furthermore, adaptation to climate change measures and prevention measures and management of risks are anticipated to improve, with solutions emerging from pilot actions, joint efforts, agreements and plans. These efforts will complement the EUSAIR macroregional strategy and offer opportunities for capitalizing on previous and ongoing initiatives. The proposal to be submitted will focus on the development of a drone-enabled rapid environmental picture Toolkit with integrated coastal stress indicators and consequent pilot runs on Greek territory. The Italian university beneficiary is expected to implement the Italian mirror pilot in an eligible Italian province and co-develop the joint solution and joint action plan on selected Italian Geographical areas.

candidate.description_text: A Greek research center is preparing a proposal for the Horizon Europe call HORIZON-CL4-2026-01-MAT-PROD-31 (Research and Innovation Action), focusing on optimising resource use within a circular economy. The project aims to develop an innovative catalytic platform capable of converting industrial carbon dioxide streams, particularly from biogas and energy-intensive sectors, into high-value chemicals by promoting CO₂ activation and carbon–carbon coupling reactions leading to multi-carbon products such as acetic acid. The concept combines graphene-based catalytic nanoarchitectures with membrane-intensified reactors designed to continuously remove reaction by-products, thereby improving CO₂ conversion efficiency. The project will advance the technology from TRL 3 to TRL 5 through catalyst development, advanced membrane technologies, and laboratory-scale reactor demonstrations. The research will explore nanostructured catalytic materials, integrated reaction–separation systems, and process optimisation strategies aimed at enabling efficient carbon utilisation in industrial environments. To strengthen the industrial relevance and future deployment potential of the technology, the consortium seeks industrial partners interested in providing practical insights into biogas production, cement manufacturing, acetic acid production, and industrial process engineering. Industrial partners will mainly contribute by defining industrial performance targets, providing process insights and operational constraints, supporting techno-economic and life-cycle assessments, evaluating scalability and integration potential, and contributing to the exploitation and scale-up roadmap. Their participation focuses on industrial validation and strategic input and does not require laboratory experimentation. The proposal will be submitted under Horizon Europe, with a call deadline of 21 April 2026, while the deadline for Expressions of Interest (EoIs) is 31 March 2026.
candidate.technical_problem_evidence_text: The consortium is seeking industrial partners from the biogas, cement, and acetic acid sectors. Relevant expertise includes industrial process operation, CO₂ emissions management, chemical production processes, and process engineering. Partners are expected to provide process data, operational insights, and input for techno-economic and sustainability assessments. Experience in industrial decarbonisation or CO₂ utilisation technologies will be considered an advantage.

candidate.description_text: An innovative Greek startup specializing in the development of AI-driven decision support systems and data analytics solutions for workforce management is preparing a proposal under the Eurostars 3 call 11. The company has strong experience in developing data-driven solutions that leverage machine learning and behavioural insights to support task allocation and organisational decision-making. The aim of the Eurostars project is to develop an innovative AI-powered software solution designed to integrate seamlessly into existing Human Capital Management (HCM) systems, enabling organizations to make more objective and meritocratic decisions in job task assignment, team formation, hiring and promotions, based on psychocognitive profiles of individuals. By combining validated psychological and cognitive assessment methodologies with predictive machine learning models, the system will identify which individuals are best suited for specific tasks or projects. The approach promotes inclusivity, especially for neurodivergent individuals, by recognizing diverse cognitive strengths that traditional human resources (HR) tools often overlook, while always prioritizing data security and GDPR compliance. The solution will incorporate real-time analytics, explainable AI modules, and an interoperability toolkit for HCM platforms (e.g., SAP, Oracle, Dynamics). The overall objective is to develop a scalable and powerful data-driven tool, that supports fair, transparent, efficient and future-proof workforce management. The Greek company will act as the project coordinator and will lead the development of the core AI-based HCM solution, including the psychocognitive profiling framework and machine learning algorithms. It will oversee data strategy and ethics, ensuring GDPR compliance, and coordinate the consortium's scientific and project management activities. The company will also lead end-user piloting and validation to test and refine the solution in real-world settings. To complete the consortium, the company is seeking two additional partners from Eurostars-eligible countries. Ideal partners are an AI/software company that will contribute to the development of the machine learning and system architecture components, and an industry partner that will provide access to workforce data and support pilot testing and validation in real organisational environments. The proposal is currently under development, with a deadline for expression of interest set for 01/07/2026.
candidate.technical_problem_evidence_text: The Greek start-up is looking for one to two partners from Eurostars-eligible countries, active in the technology and engineering sectors, with complementary expertise in the following areas. In particular, the company is looking for an industry or end-user partner, such as a private company, capable of providing access to relevant workforce data and organisational environments. This partner should be able to support the secure and anonymised collection of employee data, contribute to data processing activities, and participate in testing and validation of the solution in real-world conditions. In parallel, a technology partner is sought, preferable an SME with experience in software development and machine learning, particularly in data-driven applications. Expertise in predictive analytics and AI-based systems will be considered an asset, supporting the development and optimisation of the machine learning components. Experience in survey implementation, data analysis workflows, and/or the integration of psychological or cognitive assessment methodologies will be considered an advantage.

candidate.description_text: A Greek university is preparing an Erasmus+ proposal under the call ERASMUS-EDU-2026-PEX-COVE, aiming to strengthen vocational skills for the use of digital water and ocean technologies in the Danube River–Delta–Black Sea area. The project will focus on making advanced tools such as earth observation, geographic information systems, artificial intelligence, big data and digital twin approaches easier to understand and use in vocational education, work-based learning and operational environments. The proposal addresses the gap between fast-developing environmental and blue-economy technologies and the practical skills available among learners, teachers, trainers, workers, SMEs, ports, waterway operators, environmental actors and public authorities. The objective is to create training pathways and practical learning activities that help these groups apply digital tools to real water, river, coastal, port and marine challenges. The emerging consortium is currently built around Greek expertise in higher education, geospatial and environmental applications, and project development. It is now seeking complementary partners from Danube-region countries in order to complete the transnational partnership. More specifically, partners are sought from countries connected to the Danube–Black Sea area, with priority given to Bulgaria, Romania, Austria and Serbia. The main need is for vocational education and training providers and universities with expertise in water management, environmental sciences, geoinformatics and blue economy. Additional partners are sought from the technology/data field, operational actors such as ports, waterway operators and environmental organisations, as well as public-sector bodies able to support regional uptake and long-term use of the project results. The selected partners will join the Erasmus+ proposal consortium and contribute to the preparation and implementation of the project under a research and development cooperation agreement.
candidate.technical_problem_evidence_text: The consortium is looking for partners from Bulgaria, Romania, Austria and Serbia, with a strong preference for organisations connected to the Danube River, Danube Delta, Black Sea, inland waterways, coastal areas, water management or blue economy. The main partners sought are: Vocational education and training providers and adult learning providers: organisations able to develop, adapt and test vocational training activities for learners, teachers, trainers or workers in fields such as water management, environmental monitoring, geoinformatics, blue economy, ports, logistics, sustainability or digital skills. Universities and applied research organisations: partners able to provide scientific and methodological input on digital water and environmental applications, including earth observation, geographic information systems, artificial intelligence, big data, environmental monitoring, coastal/marine systems or blue-economy innovation. Technology and data actors: SMEs, research institutes or other organisations working with earth observation, geographic information systems, artificial intelligence, environmental data, water data, digital tools or decision-support systems. Their role will be to help translate technical tools into practical training examples and learning tasks. Operational actors: ports, waterway operators, utilities, SMEs, environmental organisations or protected-area managers that can provide real operational challenges, pilot cases and feedback on the usefulness of the skills and training activities for workplace needs. Public-sector and uptake actors: municipalities, regional authorities, qualification bodies or sector organisations that can support stakeholder engagement, policy uptake, skills recognition, dissemination and long-term use of the project results.

candidate.description_text: A Greek consortium is preparing proposal under ERASMUS-EDU-2026-PEX-COVE, aiming to create a transnational vocational excellence ecosystem for wine tourism, bringing together education providers, wine associations, regional actors, tourism organisations and innovation support organisations. The project responds to a clear need in European wine regions. Wine tourism is growing, but training remains fragmented and often does not fully address the practical skills required by wineries and tourism businesses. The proposal will focus on competences related to visitor experience design, storytelling of place and terroir, sustainable wine tourism, digital tools, service quality, pricing, visitor data, regional cooperation and business-oriented innovation. The project will develop a European competence framework for wine tourism professionals, modular vocational training content, micro-credentials, digital learning resources and practical work-based learning activities. Learners and professionals will work with wineries, wine routes and tourism SMEs on practical outputs, such as visitor journey maps, wine tourism experience blueprints, storytelling scripts, sustainability interpretation plans, digital visitor management plans and simple performance dashboards. A key part of the project will be the establishment of Regional Wine Tourism Excellence Labs in the participating countries. These labs will connect vocational education and training providers with wineries, tourism SMEs, wine associations, regional authorities and other local actors, in order to identify skills needs, test training material, support pilot actions and promote long-term cooperation between education, business and regional development stakeholders. The emerging consortium is currently built around Greek expertise, combining academic and applied research expertise with experience in skills development, lifelong learning, sustainable regional and international development. It is now seeking complementary partners from Hungary and France. For each of these countries, the consortium needs at least one vocational education and training provider and at least one enterprise, industry or sector representative organisation. The aim is to complete the required country-level structure of the Erasmus+ Centres of Vocational Excellence proposal and to ensure that the project is strongly connected to the real needs of wine tourism regions. The cooperation will be developed under a research and development cooperation agreement. The selected partners will join the consortium and contribute to the preparation and implementation of the Erasmus+ proposal. The deadline for Expressions of Interest is 15 July 2026.
candidate.technical_problem_evidence_text: The consortium is looking for partners from Hungary and France that can cover the required Erasmus+ Centres of Vocational Excellence country structure. For each country, the consortium is seeking: a) at least one vocational education and training provider, at secondary and/or tertiary level, active in tourism, hospitality, wine, agri-food, rural development, sustainability, digital skills or visitor experience. b) at least one enterprise, industry or sector representative organisation, such as a wine association, wine route, chamber, wine tourism organisation, winery network, tourism SME association or other professional/sector body connected to wine tourism. The ideal partners should have a clear link with the wine tourism ecosystem and be able to contribute to skills mapping, training design, micro-credentials, work-based learning activities and regional pilot actions. Experience in Erasmus+ projects, vocational excellence, wine tourism, sustainable tourism, digital transformation or regional cooperation will be considered an asset.

candidate.description_text: The rapid adoption of artificial intelligence and edge computing across critical infrastructure and commercial space systems has significantly expanded the cyberattack surface. At the same time, new European regulations, including the NIS2 Directive, the Cyber Resilience Act (CRA) and the EU AI Act, require operators not only to detect cyber incidents but also to provide transparent, explainable and auditable evidence supporting their response. To address this challenge, a Greek innovative SME specialised in edge AI cybersecurity is preparing a Eurostars proposal entitled EDGE-SENTRY, aiming to develop a software-defined cybersecurity layer for AI-enabled edge devices operating in regulated industrial and space environments. The project will develop a lightweight three-layer architecture capable of operating entirely on edge devices. The solution combines deterministic anomaly detection with an on-device Small Language Model (SLM) that automatically explains every detected anomaly using recognised threat intelligence frameworks such as MITRE ATT&CK for ICS and ESA SPACE-SHIELD. The generated outputs will support both security operators and compliance officers by providing regulator-ready evidence aligned with the requirements of NIS2, the Cyber Resilience Act and the EU AI Act. The solution will be deployed as hardware-agnostic software capable of running on existing industrial edge devices without dependence on proprietary hardware. Validation activities will include laboratory testing followed by field pilots in representative industrial IoT and space-related operational environments, targeting technology maturation from TRL4 to TRL6. The consortium is coordinated by the Greek SME and currently includes a research University in Brussels contributing expertise in explainable AI and edge computing. The consortium is now seeking an additional SME from a Eurostars country to strengthen the industrial validation and commercialisation activities. The sought partner should be eligible for Eurostars funding in its own country and willing to actively participate in proposal preparation and project implementation. The deadline for Expressions of Interest is 10 August 2026, allowing sufficient time for consortium finalisation and preparation of the national funding applications before the Eurostars Call 11 deadline of 10 September 2026. The consortium welcomes expressions of interest from experienced organisations wishing to contribute to the development of next-generation trustworthy cybersecurity solutions for critical infrastructure and space applications.
candidate.technical_problem_evidence_text: The consortium is seeking an SME established in a Eurostars country (with allocated funded for the call 11) with experience in industrial IoT, critical infrastructure or space-sector technologies. The ideal partner should have practical expertise in the deployment and integration of edge computing solutions and industrial communication technologies or equivalent industrial connectivity platforms, as well as experience in deploying cybersecurity solutions/pilot deployment in operational environments. The ideal partner should also have an interest to align the outcome of EDGE-SENTRY project to their roadmap and plans for exploitation and commercialization activities. Access to representative pilot sites or established relationships with industrial end users in sectors such as energy, transport, manufacturing, water utilities or satellite ground-segment operations would be considered particularly valuable. Previous participation in collaborative R&D projects, including Eurostars or Horizon Europe, would be an advantage but is not a mandatory requirement.

candidate.description_text: The project will address the need for practical digital solutions that help farms, producer groups, agri-food companies, advisors and public stakeholders improve circular resource management. The proposed solution will support the monitoring and optimisation of resource flows, including agricultural inputs, by-products, waste streams, water, energy and environmental performance indicators. The objective is to demonstrate how digital tools can support circular economy decisions in agri-food systems, reduce inefficiencies, improve traceability and facilitate the adoption of more sustainable production and advisory models. The consortium intends to develop and demonstrate a digital solution at TRL 6–8, in line with the RIVCircular call requirements. The solution may combine data analytics, artificial intelligence, IoT-enabled monitoring, interoperability mechanisms and user-oriented decision-support functionalities. The project will include pilot and validation activities in relevant operational environments, with the aim of testing the technical performance, usability, transferability and circular economy impact of the proposed approach.
candidate.technical_problem_evidence_text: The consortium seeks a partner with expertise in one or more of the following areas: Digital circular economy platforms; AI and machine learning for resource optimisation; IoT monitoring systems; data interoperability; blockchain or other traceability technologies; environmental footprint assessment; life-cycle thinking; circular economy indicators; agri-food waste and by-product valorisation; digital product or resource passports; cybersecurity for data platforms; pilot testing and validation in agricultural, agri-food or circular economy environments. The partner should be able to contribute to a TRL 6–8 innovation project and provide technical knowledge, pilot access, datasets, user communities, validation methodology, replication capacity or exploitation support.
