candidate.description_text: A Greek deep-tech medtech SME specialising in microwave medical imaging and diagnostics is preparing a proposal for Eurostars Call 11. The company has developed a microwave breast imaging technology that uses low-power electromagnetic waves to produce three-dimensional (3D) breast images without ionising radiation or breast compression. The project aims to develop a compact next-generation microwave breast imaging scanner for early breast cancer detection. It will build on an existing TRL 5 system that has already been evaluated through two exploratory clinical investigations. The objective is to deliver a fully functional prototype for initiating subsequent clinical validation studies at TRL 6. The clinical study itself will not be conducted within the project. The project will address technical and usability limitations that have restricted the wider clinical adoption of microwave breast imaging. The planned developments include a more compact scanner architecture, a miniaturised radio-frequency scanning subsystem, faster scanning, improved mechanical stability and a tailored breast-to-scanner interface for more standardised and repeatable patient positioning. The Greek SME will coordinate the proposal and contribute its expertise in microwave engineering, electromagnetic medical sensing and imaging, image processing, clinical strategy and preparation of the prototype for testing and validation. The company is now seeking complementary partners with expertise in industrial product and medical device development, compact and modular scanner design, mechanical support engineering, patient ergonomics and imaging scanner usability. The selected partners will join the Eurostars proposal consortium and contribute to the development and integration of the next-generation scanner under a research and development cooperation agreement. Expressions of interest are welcomed until 14 of August 2026.
candidate.technical_problem_evidence_text: The company is looking for one or more industrial partners from Eurostars participating countries, preferably SMEs or larger companies. Suitable partners may include industrial product development and engineering companies, medical device design and manufacturing companies, developers or manufacturers of medical imaging and other compact medical equipment, and industrial design companies specialising in medical device ergonomics and usability. More specifically, the partners should have expertise in at least one of the following areas: Industrial product development, ideally including certified medical device design and manufacturing expertise. Modular and compact scanner design, including the optimal reallocation of scanner submodules based on key multiphysics specifications, such as thermal and mechanical constraints, electromagnetic compatibility and radio-frequency coupling between modules. Patient ergonomics and imaging scanner usability, to assure: scan repeatability, streamlined patient positioning and ultimately standardised imaging in challenging configurations of deformable soft-tissue organs such as the breast.

candidate.description_text: A Greek SME specialising in the design, development and manufacturing of specialty materials and surface coatings is coordinating an international consortium preparing a proposal under Eurostars 3 Call 11. The project aims to develop durable, non-leaching antimicrobial coatings for filtration media and high-touch surfaces. Conventional antimicrobial surface treatments may lose effectiveness within one to three months of normal cleaning and use. The project targets sustained antimicrobial action for 6–12 months through three technological routes: a contact-killing coating based on quaternary ammonium silanes, doped titania photocatalysts active under normal indoor visible light and a novel hybrid bilayer combining both mechanisms. The project aims to produce two tangible prototypes. The first will involve an antimicrobial coating formulation applied to surfaces and heating, ventilation and air-conditioning filter media, tested for self-disinfection capacity and air-purification performance in relevant operational environments. The second will be a modular point-of-use water dispensing and disinfection system, validated for high-sterility filtered water in laboratory and healthcare settings. The existing consortium includes a Greek SME responsible for coating chemistry and scale-up, a Greek research organisation with expertise in visible-light photocatalysts and advanced materials characterisation, and a German SME specialising in engineering, prototyping and accredited testing. One industrial end-user is sought, preferably a manufacturer active in air or water filtration or a manufacturer of equipment with high-touch surfaces. The partner will participate in the validation of one or both prototypes and is expected to lead commercial exploitation. Cooperation is foreseen under a research and development cooperation agreement. Expressions of interest are welcomed until 20 August 2026.
candidate.technical_problem_evidence_text: The consortium is looking for one industrial end-user from a Eurostars participating country, preferably an SME or a larger company with relevant product development, manufacturing or validation capabilities. More specifically, suitable partners may include: Air filtration product manufacturers, such as manufacturers of heating, ventilation and air-conditioning filters, filter elements, air-handling equipment or air-purification units for hospitals, laboratories, cleanrooms, buildings or transport. Water filtration product manufacturers, such as manufacturers of point-of-use filters, cartridges, ceramic or polymeric membranes, water dispensers or medical and laboratory water systems. Manufacturers of equipment incorporating high-touch surfaces, including hospital furniture and fittings, medical device housings, touch panels, screens or interior components used in public or hygiene-sensitive environments. Professional end-users, such as hospital groups, hygiene service providers or facility-management organisations, may also be considered where they have the capacity to host validation activities under real operating conditions. The ideal partner should have access to representative substrates, filter media, components or equipment and should be interested in integrating the developed coating into a specific product and supporting its subsequent commercial exploitation.

candidate.description_text: A Greek technology SME with expertise in cybersecurity, data analytics, cloud computing and Internet of Things (IoT) solutions is preparing a proposal for EUDOROS Open Call 2, funded under the Digital Europe Programme. The company will participate as the Cybersecurity Services Provider (CSP) and is seeking an additional partner to act as the Cybersecurity Services Recipient (CSR). The proposed project addresses one of the main challenges faced by Security Operations Centres (SOCs): although modern Security Information and Event Management (SIEM) platforms generate alerts when suspicious activity is detected, cybersecurity analysts still spend considerable time manually correlating events from multiple data sources before they can understand the scope and origin of an incident. The project will develop an Incident Investigation Module that extends existing SIEM capabilities by automatically collecting, correlating and presenting related security events in a chronological investigation timeline. From a single alert, analysts will be able to initiate an investigation that links relevant logs, highlights suspicious activities and provides direct access to the original evidence. Rather than replacing digital forensic tools, the solution aims to accelerate the initial investigation phase, enabling faster and more informed incident response. The consortium is seeking an organisation eligible to participate as a Cybersecurity Services Recipient (CSR) under the EUDOROS Open Call. The selected partner will deploy the solution within its operational ICT environment, participate in pilot testing, validate its performance using realistic cybersecurity scenarios and provide operational feedback to support further development and optimisation. Potential partners include medium-sized or large organisations, public authorities, healthcare providers, universities, research organisations or operators of critical infrastructure with established ICT environments and a genuine need to strengthen cybersecurity preparedness. The proposal will be submitted to EUDOROS Open Call 2 (DIGITAL-ECCC-2023-DEPLOY-CYBER-04). The deadline for Expressions of Interest is 31 July 2026, while the call deadline is 7 August 2026. The anticipated project budget is approximately €90,000, with funding allocated to both the technology provider and the pilot organisation.

candidate.description_text: A Greek innovative SME is preparing an international research and development project under Eurostars Call 11. The project, provisionally titled PULSE-EU, will advance a pilot-validated media-intelligence pipeline for audio, video and text from technology readiness level (TRL) 6 to TRL 8 over 24 months. Media organisations process large volumes of unstructured audiovisual content, but existing tools are often fragmented: transcription, content identification, semantic analysis, visual analysis and rights metadata are handled separately. Outputs are frequently generic, difficult to adapt to each organisation and not ready for editorial, monitoring, licensing or rights-management workflows. The project will research and develop a scalable European platform that converts audiovisual content into configurable, machine-readable intelligence. It will extend client-defined templates, controlled vocabularies and taxonomies; multilingual extraction and cross-language rendering; distributed worker orchestration; privately deployed or self-hosted artificial intelligence; and editorial-grade structured outputs. Research may also cover direct visual-stream analysis, including optical character recognition, scene and shot detection, logo or product recognition and temporal correlation of visual findings with speech, sound, transcripts and content-identification results. A rights-aware workstream will investigate interoperability between detected recordings, musical works, rightsholders, publishers and identifiers such as ISRC, ISWC and IPI. This may support metadata validation, recording-to-work matching and future cue-sheet workflows without replacing partners' existing rights or royalty systems. The Greek SME will contribute its existing configurable platform, audio fingerprinting and broadcast-monitoring technology, self-hosted AI and owned computing infrastructure, Greek-language media-intelligence know-how, APIs, template and vocabulary architecture, and pilot-validation capacity. Its pre-existing platform and related technology will remain background intellectual property; project access rights and ownership of jointly developed results will be defined in the consortium agreement. Partners are sought from Eurostars countries, particularly organisations active in media, broadcasting, publishing, music technology, rights management, multilingual AI, computer vision, scalable software or audiovisual data. They will undertake complementary R&D and/or provide datasets, integration environments, pilots, validation and routes to market. The consortium will be led by an innovative SME and will include at least two independent organisations from at least two Eurostars countries. Expressions of interest are requested by 20 August 2026. The Eurostars Call 11 deadline is 10 September 2026 at 14:00 CEST.
candidate.technical_problem_evidence_text: Relevant partners should contribute at least one of the following: 1. Media, broadcast, publishing, record-label, music-library or rights-management pilot environments, including representative audiovisual content, metadata, workflow requirements, validation criteria and end-user feedback. 2. Multilingual speech and language technologies for speech-to-text, diarisation, transcript correction, translation, entity extraction, semantic classification and cross-language rendering, with measurable performance in Greek and/or other European languages. API, licensed or self-hosted deployment should be possible. 3. Computer-vision or multimodal expertise for scene and shot detection, optical character recognition, on-screen text, logo/product detection, visual context and timestamped fusion of image, speech, sound and transcript results. 4. Scalable software and data-engineering expertise for distributed processing, worker orchestration, secure APIs, metadata interchange, quality assurance and deployment at European scale. 5. Music-rights, repertoire, publishing, royalty-accounting or cue-sheet expertise, with documented data models or interfaces for recordings, works, rightsholders, territories, ownership shares and identifiers including ISRC, ISWC and IPI. Recording-to-work matching and the handling of incomplete or conflicting metadata are particularly relevant. Proposed work must complement the existing platform and provide high reuse. The project does not seek a replacement audio-fingerprinting, monitoring or generic analysis platform, nor unrelated product development.

candidate.description_text: A Greek technology SME active in data-driven software and cybersecurity is preparing an application for the TRUNSPORT Open Call 1, “Strengthening Cybersecurity Resilience and Innovation in the Transport Sector”, funded under the European Union’s Digital Europe Programme. The proposed project will adapt and validate a security incident investigation solution for use in a real transport environment. The solution is currently under development and is intended to help security teams investigate incidents by bringing together alerts, findings and related evidence from different cybersecurity tools in a common investigation workflow. It links evidence to affected assets and reconstructs events into a chronological incident timeline, supporting the analysis of suspicious activity, possible attack paths and response priorities. An artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted component is also being explored to summarise evidence, identify relationships between events and support analyst prioritisation while keeping the human analyst in control. The TRUNSPORT project will investigate how these capabilities can be adapted to the complex and heterogeneous cybersecurity environments found in connected transport systems, where vehicles, infrastructure, sensors, operational platforms and digital services may generate information from multiple sources. A concrete transport use case will be defined jointly with the selected partner. candidate.description_text: The company is an established manufacturer and service provider located in Croatia, deeply embedded in the Adriatic nautical market. Their core expertise lies in working with glass-reinforced plastic (GRP/fiberglass), delivering both structural hull laminations and high-gloss gelcoat finishes. Distinct from pure laminating shops, the company offers a comprehensive "turnkey" manufacturing process. Their facility is equipped to handle the entire production cycle: GRP/fiberglass molding and lamination according to partner specifications; assembly and installation of mechanical parts, inboard/outboard propulsion systems; and integration of electrical networks, navigation equipment, and advanced marine electronics. The company is currently spearheading a project proposal named "Green & Smart Adriatic Fleet." The objective is to finalize technical development, integrate advanced eco-friendly propulsion (hybrid/electric), and complete full CE certification for two highly market-relevant GRP boat models: (1.) Betina 700 R: A robust, traditionally-inspired 7-meter vessel designed for professional use, water taxi services, and tourist transport in environmentally protected areas (such as National Parks). (2.) Phoenix f75: A brand new, modern 7.5-meter cabin cruiser boat optimized for long-term family cruising, multi-day charters, and premium nautical tourism. To support this initiative, the company offers existing, high-quality production molds and expert GRP/fiberglass laminating capabilities in Croatia, direct access to the Adriatic nautical market (the world's largest charter fleet location), and ready-to-build hulls waiting for advanced technological integration. The strategic location on the Croatian coast also enables them to serve as an ideal logistical and maintenance hub for international partners looking to deploy or maintain vessels in Southern Europe and the Mediterranean.
candidate.technical_problem_evidence_text: The partner must possess specialized technical expertise in designing, manufacturing, or supplying marine electric/hybrid propulsion systems, advanced battery management systems (BMS), or smart marine electronics/IoT monitoring setups. The partner is required to co-develop the technical integration layout, supply the necessary propulsion/electronic kits, and handle the engineering alignment required for the eco-modernization of 7 to 7.5-meter GRP hulls.

candidate.description_text: European disaster management suffers from data overload and dangerous latency caused by operators needing to manually search 2,000+ page PDF safety manuals during a crisis. The SMARDES project addresses this by creating a 100% European sovereign AI Operational Decision-Support Assistant, directly aligning with the CITADEL Open Call 1. The CITADEL Open Call 1 is a funding initiative designed to support innovative digital solutions that strengthen cybersecurity and digital resilience across Europe. It enables solution providers to collaborate with partner organizations that can test and validate their technologies in real-world environments. Deadline for call: 5 May 2026 Deadline for EOI 4 May 2026 The Hungarian SME as coordinator will handle the technical execution (WP1 & WP2), bridging live Copernicus/GloFAS satellite data with text-based rules using a secure, EU-hosted LLM. Role of the Partner: Hungarian SME is looking for an operational partner (such as an emergency response NGO, municipal civil protection agency, or government body) to collaborate on Work Package 3 (TRL 7 Operational Pilot). The partner will: •	Provide their existing localized disaster/vulnerability manuals to shape the AI's knowledge base. •	Participate in a 48-hour live simulated stress-test (e.g., flood scenario) using their senior emergency operators to validate the system's effectiveness and measure the reduction in response time.
candidate.technical_problem_evidence_text: The sought partner does not require software development expertise. The Hungarian company is looking for Domain Expertise in Disaster/Emergency Management. The partner should possess: •	Established disaster management workflows, protocols, and written vulnerability manuals (PDFs, docs). •	Active emergency operators, crisis response staff, or civil protection personnel capable of evaluating a software platform during a simulated crisis scenario. •	(Optional but beneficial) Existing use cases involving flood response or municipal security.

candidate.description_text: Spine surgery increasingly relies on technologies that can improve precision, reproducibility and workflow safety. Robotic assistance and image-guided surgical solutions can support surgeons in performing complex procedures in a more standardised way, potentially improving access to high-quality specialised care. A Hungarian medical robotics small and medium-sized enterprise is developing Lumbotix, a robotic assistance system for endoscopic lumbar spine surgery. The project is based on proprietary surgical know-how and aims to translate selected surgical steps into measurable spatial directions, controlled movements and quantitative parameters. The technology is currently at laboratory-tested prototype stage, estimated at Technology Readiness Level 4. The next development phase aims to advance the system towards Technology Readiness Level 6 through further technical development, navigation and imaging integration, robot-compatible precision surgical instruments, safety and usability testing, and cadaver-based demonstration in an anatomically relevant environment. The current project team combines clinical spine surgery expertise, proprietary surgical know-how and robotic system development experience. A working laboratory prototype has been developed and tested, and technical documentation and test results are available for confidential partner discussions. The planned cooperation is intended to be submitted as an international research and development project under the Eurostars / Eureka framework, subject to final consortium structure and partner eligibility. Eurostars / Eureka supports international market-oriented research and development cooperation involving innovative small and medium-sized enterprises. The project is currently in the partner search and concept development phase. The expected project duration is approximately 24–36 months. The target submission is the next suitable Eurostars / Eureka call, to be confirmed after partner selection. The consortium is seeking partners with expertise in one or more of the following areas: •	surgical navigation, neuronavigation, image-guided surgery, image fusion, three-dimensional patient registration or intraoperative imaging; •	precision medical device development, robot-compatible surgical instruments, minimally invasive or endoscopic surgical tools; •	cadaver-based validation, preclinical testing, clinical workflow assessment, usability feedback or surgical training environments. •	The selected partner is expected to contribute to the technical development, integration, testing or validation of the robotic assistance system, depending on its area of expertise. Detailed technical information can be shared under appropriate confidentiality arrangements. •	Expressions of interest are welcome until 31/July/2026 Demonstration video: https://youtu.be/eZsykeyMHKw
candidate.technical_problem_evidence_text: The project is seeking partners with technical and/or clinical expertise in one or more of the following areas: Surgical navigation and imaging integration Partners with experience in surgical navigation, neuronavigation, image-guided surgery, image fusion, three-dimensional patient registration, magnetic resonance imaging / computed tomography-based planning, intraoperative imaging or fluoroscopy-supported workflows. The partner is expected to support the development or adaptation of the navigation component and its integration into the robotic surgical workflow. Precision medical device and surgical instrument development Partners experienced in the design, development and testing of precision medical devices, minimally invasive surgical instruments, endoscopic tools, robotic surgical tools, mechatronic systems or robot-compatible instrument interfaces. The partner may contribute to the development of dedicated tools for robot-assisted endoscopic lumbar spine surgery. Preclinical and cadaver-based validation Clinical, academic or specialised validation partners with access to cadaver laboratories, surgical training environments or preclinical testing infrastructure. The partner is expected to support cadaver-based demonstration, usability assessment, workflow feedback and preliminary technical validation. Regulatory and medical device development expertise Partners with expertise in Medical Device Regulation, conformity assessment preparation, clinical evidence planning, risk management, usability engineering and preparation for later CE marking may also be relevant. The exact role of the partner will be defined jointly during consortium development, depending on its expertise and funding eligibility.

candidate.description_text: Social Dance Official (SDO) is an early-stage cultural and creative industries initiative based in Budapest, Hungary. The founder is developing SDO as a repeatable social-dance participation model that connects offline cultural and community experiences with a practical bilingual digital layer for discovery, registration, communication and privacy-conscious learning from pilot delivery. The founder's engagement with the social dance community began in 2006, bringing nearly two decades of first-hand experience with its music, culture, participant needs, and community dynamics. Alongside the development of SDO, the founder has also worked part-time as a DJ and social dance event organiser. Between 2022 and 2024, the founder regularly organised social dance events and parties at Budapest Park. This practice-based background is central to the initiative, providing a deep understanding of both the participant journey and the operational realities of building a safe, welcoming, and sustainable local community around music and dance. SDO addresses a common challenge for local cultural and community formats: how to convert initial interest into regular participation, maintain meaningful contact between events, and learn systematically from delivery. Social dance serves as a valuable practice-based test case because it combines learning, social interaction, cultural expression, and recurring local participation. Through this initiative, the founder aims to make these experiences more accessible, inclusive, and repeatable without reducing them to a transactional event service. The initiative is currently in the pre-launch and pilot-preparation stage. Its digital foundation supports participant discovery, registration, communication, and operational learning, with Budapest identified as the intended first pilot market. The founder does not claim completed pilot outcomes, market validation, or a scaled service. Instead, the founder is seeking a suitable collaboration in which the pilot design, baselines, target values, consent procedures, data minimisation principles, and evaluation methodology are jointly agreed. Within a suitable European consortium, the founder can contribute as a practice-based pilot partner or work package contributor. The founder's potential contribution includes: - local pilot design and delivery in a Hungarian cultural-community setting; - audience development, bilingual outreach, and participant onboarding; - community activation and participant communication; - practical digital participation processes and consent-aware feedback collection; - privacy-conscious measurement of registrations, confirmed participation, attendance, repeat participation, and participant feedback; - documentation of operational lessons and a transferable playbook for partner locations or other cities. The founder is particularly interested in collaborating with cultural and creative organisations, research and technology partners, public bodies, innovation hubs, and community organisations working on cultural participation, audience engagement, participatory formats, digital inclusion, creative entrepreneurship, or real-world pilot testing. The founder has not previously participated in Horizon Europe and is open to joining a consortium led by an experienced coordinator, contributing to a clearly defined work package, or co-designing a realistic pilot with partners that bring complementary research, technology, or local-delivery expertise.
candidate.technical_problem_evidence_text: An experienced Horizon Europe Innovation Action coordinator and consortium partners are sought to jointly develop a competitive proposal under HORIZON-CL2-2026-01-HERITAGE-02. Relevant expertise includes creative and cultural industries innovation, startup and scale-up support, Horizon consortium coordination, research design and impact evaluation, participatory cultural formats, audience engagement, pilot methodology, digital participation, responsible data and ethics, dissemination, and replication across locations. Particular interest is placed on partners capable of leading the research and innovation framework, recruiting or connecting relevant creative startups, and designing the required real-world pilot trials. Universities, R&D organisations, innovation hubs, cultural networks, and experienced SMEs are all considered highly relevant partners.

candidate.description_text: School of Engineering of University of Galway (Ireland) is currently joining an EU consortium to applying for Eurostars grant call. The proposal is planning to research activities in the field of design, manufacture, test, and demonstration of polymer membranes for the applications in hydrogen fuel cells or electrolyzers. The target material of this project is proton conducting ionomer or anion conducting ionomer. The applications include proton exchange membrane or anion exchange membrane, for hydrogen fuel cells or water splitting using electrolyzer. Looking for an Irish SME to join the consortium. The expected company is to take at least one of the following tasks. • Synthesis of precursor including upscaling • Polymerization of ionomers from the precursor • Membrane preparation/processing from the ionomers • Preparation of sub-scale test cells via CCM or GDE path • Testing: mechanical, electrochemical, aging testing etc. The SME is more than welcome to propose other tasks of the project according to their interests. The SME will apply for funding from the project according to the guidelines of EuroStars programme. The sme will directly benefit from the project’s outputs regarding such as the design, manufacture, processing, testing and application of novel ionomer membranes.
candidate.technical_problem_evidence_text: We are seeking an SME that is able to take at least one of the following tasks. The SME can either do related manufacturing or processing in a pilot scale or upscale the techniques to a larger scale. The SME is more than welcome to propose tasks in other fields according to its interests. • Synthesis of precursor including upscaling • Polymerization of ionomers from the precursor • Membrane preparation/processing from the ionomers • Preparation of sub-scale test cells via CCM or GDE path • Testing: mechanical, electrochemical, aging testing etc. The SME will mainly lead the tasks of the project regarding the processing, manufacturing and testing of a demonstrator. The related tasks can be complete either in a laboratory scale, or pilot scale, or large industrial scale. If possible, it would be ideal if the SME can upscale the related techniques in the project.

candidate.description_text: An Irish organic gourmet mushroom producer and circular bioeconomy demonstration farm is seeking to build a multidisciplinary consortium for a Horizon Europe research project focused on fungal bio-based innovation for more sustainable ways of living. The project would investigate how cultivated fungal biomass, mycelium and mushroom cultivation residues can be developed into practical, user-friendly bio-based products and services with clear societal and environmental benefits. The proposed research would examine fungal-derived ingredients and cosmetic applications, mycelium-based biomaterials, circular use of spent mushroom substrate and alternative local biomass feedstocks, and product or process routes that reduce resource use and waste. Scientific partners would characterise relevant compounds and materials, evaluate extraction or processing methods, undertake safety and performance testing and support formulation and prototype development. Potential skin, wellness or functional benefits would be investigated scientifically; no benefit or health claim is assumed in advance. The farm would contribute organic mushroom cultivation capability, controlled production facilities and a real-world demonstration environment for cultivation, substrate, circularity and end-user trials. The project would also assess life-cycle impacts, resource efficiency, market potential, consumer understanding and acceptance, and social factors influencing adoption of bio-based products. The target programme is Horizon Europe Cluster 6, call HORIZON-CL6-2026-01-CIRCBIO-10, “Bio-based innovation in society: supporting the sustainable way of living”. It is a single-stage Research and Innovation Action using lump-sum funding. The European Commission indicates an EU contribution of around EUR 4 million per project, with activities expected to achieve technology readiness level 4-5 by project end. Expressions of interest are requested by 4 September 2026. The call deadline is 17 September 2026 at 17:00 Central European Summer Time. A project duration of approximately 208 weeks is proposed. The Irish enterprise intends to participate as a small enterprise, end-user and farm-scale demonstration partner and is particularly seeking an experienced Horizon Europe coordinator together with research, technology, product-development and social-science partners.
candidate.technical_problem_evidence_text: Partners are sought with complementary expertise in fungal biotechnology and mycology, analytical chemistry and metabolomics, extraction and purification of fungal compounds, cosmetic science and formulation, food or functional ingredient development, mycelium biomaterials and materials characterisation, toxicology and product safety, regulatory science, life-cycle and techno-economic assessment, circular bioeconomy, consumer behaviour, social science and public engagement, and data or bioinformatics. An experienced Horizon Europe coordinator is particularly sought to lead proposal development, consortium management and project governance. Research organisations and universities should be able to design and conduct laboratory studies, characterisation and validation and translate results toward technology readiness level 4-5. Industry partners should contribute product requirements, formulation, processing, scale-up, regulatory and market knowledge. Social-science partners should lead consumer perception, acceptance, inclusion and socio-economic assessment. description_text: An Irish organic gourmet mushroom producer and circular bioeconomy demonstration farm is seeking to build a multidisciplinary consortium for a Horizon Europe research project focused on fungal bio-based innovation for more sustainable ways of living. The project would investigate how cultivated fungal biomass, mycelium and mushroom cultivation residues can be developed into practical, user-friendly bio-based products and services with clear societal and environmental benefits. The proposed research would examine fungal-derived ingredients and cosmetic applications, mycelium-based biomaterials, circular use of spent mushroom substrate and alternative local biomass feedstocks, and product or process routes that reduce resource use and waste. Scientific partners would characterise relevant compounds and materials, evaluate extraction or processing methods, undertake safety and performance testing and support formulation and prototype development. Potential skin, wellness or functional benefits would be investigated scientifically; no benefit or health claim is assumed in advance. The farm would contribute organic mushroom cultivation capability, controlled production facilities and a real-world demonstration environment for cultivation, substrate, circularity and end-user trials. The project would also assess life-cycle impacts, resource efficiency, market potential, consumer understanding and acceptance, and social factors influencing adoption of bio-based products. The target programme is Horizon Europe Cluster 6, call HORIZON-CL6-2026-01-CIRCBIO-10, “Bio-based innovation in society: supporting the sustainable way of living”. It is a single-stage Research and Innovation Action using lump-sum funding. The European Commission indicates an EU contribution of around EUR 4 million per project, with activities expected to achieve technology readiness level 4-5 by project end. Expressions of interest are requested by 4 September 2026. The call deadline is 17 September 2026 at 17:00 Central European Summer Time. A project duration of approximately 208 weeks is proposed. The Irish enterprise intends to participate as a small enterprise, end-user and farm-scale demonstration partner and is particularly seeking an experienced Horizon Europe coordinator together with research, technology, product-development and social-science partners.
technical_problem_evidence_text: Partners are sought with complementary expertise in fungal biotechnology and mycology, analytical chemistry and metabolomics, extraction and purification of fungal compounds, cosmetic science and formulation, food or functional ingredient development, mycelium biomaterials and materials characterisation, toxicology and product safety, regulatory science, life-cycle and techno-economic assessment, circular bioeconomy, consumer behaviour, social science and public engagement, and data or bioinformatics. An experienced Horizon Europe coordinator is particularly sought to lead proposal development, consortium management and project governance. Research organisations and universities should be able to design and conduct laboratory studies, characterisation and validation and translate results toward technology readiness level 4-5. Industry partners should contribute product requirements, formulation, processing, scale-up, regulatory and market knowledge. Social-science partners should lead consumer perception, acceptance, inclusion and socio-economic assessment. Partners should be willing to integrate laboratory work with farm-scale trials and demonstration in Ireland and to contribute to shared exploitation, communication and dissemination activities.

candidate.description_text: Voiceitt is an accessibility-focused AI company that has developed the first and only commercial speech recognition solution specifically designed for people with non-standard speech patterns caused by disabilities and neurological conditions. Traditional speech recognition systems are trained primarily on standard speech and often fail when used by individuals with speech impairments. Voiceitt addresses this challenge through proprietary AI technology that learns and adapts to each user’s unique speech patterns, enabling people with speech disabilities to communicate and interact more independently. The solution currently supports English and is commercially deployed across accessibility and communication use cases. Voiceitt is seeking strategic partners for collaborative R&D and international innovation projects, including the development of support for additional European languages. Voiceitt’s technology supports people with conditions such as cerebral palsy, ALS, Parkinson’s disease, stroke-related impairments, and other neurological disorders. The platform integrates with smartphones, healthcare platforms, mobility technologies, smart glasses, wearables, and enterprise accessibility solutions. The solution is already integrated with widely used platforms and tools including Zoom, Microsoft Teams, Google Chrome, Amazon Alexa, and ChatGPT, enabling users with speech disabilities to access mainstream communication and digital services more independently. Voiceitt is already impacting thousands of users with speech disabilities worldwide by breaking communication barriers and enabling greater independence, accessibility, and quality of life. Voiceitt is backed by strategic collaborations with Microsoft, Amazon, Cisco, and Intel, and has successfully secured multiple European Commission grants and innovation awards. The company is currently seeking R&D, healthcare, rehabilitation, mobility, wearable technology, distribution, and commercialization partners.

candidate.description_text: The project aims to strengthen cross-border cooperation between Italy and France in the management of water resources and the prevention of hydrogeological risks by introducing innovative environmental monitoring technologies. The overall objective is to improve the capacity to observe and forecast soil moisture and the snow water equivalent (SWE), key factors for understanding hydrological processes, water resource availability, and the vulnerability of the territory to extreme phenomena such as droughts, floods, and landslides. The specific objectives are structured along several lines. First, a network of probes will be installed and validated in cross-border pilot areas, with particular attention to mountainous and snowy contexts. This phase will be accompanied by calibration campaigns and comparisons with traditional methods to ensure data reliability. The use of specific sensors will make it possible to obtain non-invasive, continuous measurements on a wide spatial scale, providing a more realistic and representative framework than traditional point sensors. At the same time, the acquired data will be collected and integrated with other sources - meteorological and hydrological stations, satellite data, climate models, and geological information - in order to create a comprehensive and interoperable information base. On this basis, the project will develop predictive models and analytical tools capable of estimating soil moisture evolution, identifying critical situations of drought or saturation, forecasting the contribution of snow to water flows, and detecting areas potentially exposed to hydrogeological risk, also using artificial intelligence tools. The final stage will consist of translating this complex data into interactive dashboards, alert systems, and user-friendly interfaces that allow operators, local authorities, and public decision-makers to access clear, operational, and timely information.
candidate.technical_problem_evidence_text: Specific technical requirements/know-how from the potential partner: •	Water and land Management and water resources management •	Hydrogeology know how and knowledge •	Hydrogeological risk monitoring and prevention

candidate.description_text: The Italian medtech start-up is developing a digital platform to standardize and scale personalization of orthopedic immobilization devices. The platform will support clinicians and technicians in designing patient-specific devices through a guided workflow: data capture (measurements/parameters), automated model selection and customization (rules/parametric design), validation checks, generation of manufacturing-ready files and traceability for certified use. They have already developed an initial PoC demonstrating the core workflow and the feasibility of automated customization. They are now entering the MVP phase through the I.Magister program, with the objective to deliver a production-grade platform suitable for early pilots with selected clinics and partners. They are looking for a technology partner to co-develop the platform end-to-end, bringing strong software engineering capabilities (cloud architecture, web application development, APIs, DevOps, cybersecurity and data management). Experience in regulated/medical environments is a plus to align development with documentation, traceability and quality requirements. The project has a clear roadmap toward a scalable SaaS business model, leveraging BioLibrary’s IP and a growing library of validated models. The partner should support both product development and the longer-term evolution toward an industrial-grade platform that can serve EU/US markets.

candidate.description_text: The University of Calabria is a public university located in southern Italy and the biggest campus-based university in Italy. It combines basic and applied research with technological innovation, carried out through numerous laboratories, research groups, and interdisciplinary infrastructure. Indeed, UNICAL promotes the transfer of research results to public institutions and industries through patents, spin-offs, and innovative startups. This research group is specialized in image processing and signal analysis from IoT sensing systems. The team focuses on intelligent data processing and real-time decision-support systems to support monitoring, diagnostics, and prognostics, collaborating with academic institutions and industrial partners on interdisciplinary and applied research projects. The research group intends to develop a project proposal under the AI Continent call (DIGITAL-2026-AI-PILOTING-10-SCREENING) of the Digital Europe Programme (DIGITAL). For the establishment of the consortium, it is seeking partners with the following expertise: - at least one partner with IT expertise aimed at the development of the cloud-based platform required by the project, including competencies in data protection and cybersecurity (to be assessed whether these competences should be covered by two separate partners); - at least one partner with IT expertise in the processing and management of medical data and images; - at least two partners (such as hospitals, medical centers, or similar institutions) able to provide data related to oncological diseases; - at least two partners (such as hospitals, medical centers, or similar institutions) able to provide data related to cardiovascular diseases. The project will aim to develop and implement a scalable cloud-based AI/GenAI system based on trustworthy and secure European algorithms trained and validated on large datasets of patient data. The project will establish a secure and privacy-preserving cloud environment for health data analysis, equipped with appropriate access and identification tools for authorised users, and will integrate the solution into the clinical workflows of the healthcare settings involved, ensuring interoperability with major health IT infrastructures (e.g., EHR, PACS, RIS). The system will undergo large-scale integration and validation in real clinical environments, with a particular focus on oncological and cardiovascular diseases, through testing on a large number of clinical cases. The project will also include technical and clinical validation, performance and usability assessment, post-deployment monitoring, and cost-efficiency analysis, in line with regulatory requirements and Health Technology Assessment (HTA) procedures. Collaboration with the R&D partners will be carried out within the framework of research and development (R&D) agreements.
candidate.technical_problem_evidence_text: The consortium seeks complementary expertise from several key partners. In particular, clinical partners specialised in cardiovascular and oncological care are required to provide access to medical imaging data and associated clinical information (e.g., MRI, CT, X-ray, PET, ultrasound) necessary for the development, training, and validation of AI/GenAI models. An industrial partner with expertise in secure cloud infrastructures will support the design and deployment of the cloud-based platform, ensuring scalability, interoperability with clinical systems (e.g., PACS, RIS, EHR), and full compliance with data protection and cybersecurity regulations. candidate.description_text: The proposing company is the Italian subsidiary of an international group leading in industrial engineering and technologies for the energy transition. This project focuses on the development and demonstration of an innovative system for ammonia (NH₃) combustion, characterized by significantly reduced nitrogen oxide (NOx) emissions, aligning with European Zero Pollution objectives and Industrial Emissions Directive (IED) regulations. Ammonia is a strategic, carbon-free energy carrier essential for the decarbonization of hard-to-abate industrial sectors; however, its combustion presents technical challenges due to low reactivity and the high potential for NOx formation. To overcome these limitations, the proposed solution employs an integrated approach combining advanced NOx reduction strategies such as staged combustion, MILD (Moderate or Intense Low-oxygen Dilution) technology, RQL (Rich-burn, Quick-mix, Lean-burn) systems, and optimized swirl. The design process utilizes advanced CFD modelling specifically dedicated to NH₃ flame chemistry and integrates primary combustion with optimized after-treatment systems, including Selective Catalytic Reduction (SCR) and adaptive Selective Non-Catalytic Reduction (SNCR). This scalable and replicable design aims to achieve a NOx emission reduction of 60–80% compared to conventional ammonia combustion while maintaining compatibility with existing energy-intensive industrial infrastructures. In preparation for the LIFE 2026 call (Sub-programme Environment – Zero Pollution), the company is looking for an industrial partner operating in sectors such as cement plants, steel mills, energy utilities, or fertilizer production interested in testing alternative fuels. The selected partner will serve as a demonstration end-user and must be available to host the pilot plant at their facility, providing a gas withdrawal point. Beyond hosting the demonstration combustion unit and measurement systems, the partner will provide operational support during the testing phase and contribute to the validation of emission results, including NOx and NH₃ slip measurements. Furthermore, the partner is expected to collaborate in the demonstration, replicability, and dissemination activities required by the LIFE program framework.
candidate.technical_problem_evidence_text: The sought partner must be an industrial energy-intensive end-user. Essential technical requirements include: •	Availability of a stable ammonia (NH₃) supply or a gas withdrawal point for the pilot unit •	Physical space and technical readiness to integrate a TRL 6-7 demonstration combustion unit into the operational line •	On-site personnel to provide operational support and facilitate access to continuous emission monitoring systems •	A clear commitment to decarbonization strategies and/or interest in validating alternative, carbon-free fuels
candidate.title: Italian engineering firm seeks an industrial end-user for pilot demonstration of low-NOx ammonia combustion technology LIFE 2026 project

candidate.description_text: Lookin is an Italian SME providing technology consulting services across four interconnected domains: cybersecurity, custom software development, artificial intelligence (AI), and data intelligence. Lookin supports SMEs and startups in designing, building and securing digital solutions tailored to their operational needs. The company combines hands-on engineering capability with strategic advisory, enabling clients to navigate digital transformation with concrete, measurable results. Lookin’s service portfolio includes: (1) secure-by-design software architecture and development; (2) AI integration into business processes (automation, prediction, NLP-based tools); (3) data intelligence pipelines and dashboards for operational decision-making; (4) cybersecurity assessments, hardening and compliance support. The company operates as a lean, agile unit capable of acting as a technical partner in consortium-based R&D projects, contributing software development, AI expertise and data engineering capabilities. Lookin is fully operational with active paying clients. The primary strategic objective is to participate in co-funded European and national R&D projects — including Horizon Europe, Digital Europe, Eurostars, and Italian PNRR and regional programmes — as a technical partner within multi-stakeholder consortia. Lookin is looking for partners to form or join project consortia in the areas of cybersecurity, AI, data intelligence and digital transformation.
candidate.technical_problem_evidence_text: We welcome contact from: technology SMEs or system integrators looking for a technical partner (software, AI, cybersecurity) to complete a consortium for a funded project; public bodies or agencies seeking a technology partner for digital innovation projects under PNRR or regional programmes; universities and R&D centres that need an industry partner with applied engineering capabilities for Horizon Europe or Eurostars applications; international companies (non-Italian) seeking an Italian SME partner for European project consortia. We are not looking for subcontracting arrangements without a co-development or funded project dimension.
candidate.title: Italian SME Offers Software, AI and Cybersecurity Expertise as Technical Partner for EU‑Funded R&I Projects (Horizon Europe, Digital Europe, Eurostars, others.)

candidate.description_text: A consortium composed of the Municipality of Rende, an Italian university, a startup, a social cooperative, and a municipal utility company is preparing a project aimed at establishing an open-air urban laboratory dedicated to the development and testing of innovative solutions for smart cities, under the  Fourth Call for Proposals of the EUI – Innovative Actions initiative. The project envisages the integration of IoT technologies, embedded systems, cloud platforms, and data-driven management tools, together with energy recovery technologies and renewable energy sources, with the aim of reducing energy consumption, emissions, and dependence on traditional infrastructure. The solutions will be designed according to the principles of multifunctionality and modular scalability, enabling them to adapt to different urban and environmental contexts. The initiative aims to create a real-world experimental environment in which the functionality, integration, and scalability of the developed technologies can be directly tested in urban settings, addressing the concrete needs of local communities. The project is based on the principles of:sustainable mobility, universal accessibility, social inclusion, and energy efficiency. The technologies and infrastructures developed will be conceived as enabling systems for advanced and sustainable urban services, contributing to the transformation of cities into smarter, more inclusive, accessible, and resilient environments. Each solution will be designed to: - be fully or partially energy self-sufficient; - use energy recovery systems powered by renewable sources; - employ innovative low-maintenance materials with photocatalytic properties; - interact digitally through integrated technological infrastructures. The project has a total budget of €2.5 million, with a maximum European contribution covering up to 80% of the total cost, and an expected duration of 30 months, divided into: - 3 months for project initiation; - 24 months for implementation; - 3 months for closure activities. As the initiative also foresees the involvement of European patner cities interested in replicating the developed solutions within their respective urban contexts, the Italian municipality is looking for EU municipalities interested in joining the project consortium for the Fourth Call for Proposals of the EUI – Innovative Actions initiative. The cooperation will be carried out under R&D agreements.

candidate.description_text: An Italian private company specialised in European project development and territorial cooperation is building a consortium under the Interreg VI-A Italy-France Maritime 2021–2027 Programme (Priority 1 – Specific Objective 1.3). The project aims to strengthen the competitiveness and internationalisation capacity of SMEs operating in rural and territorial value chains across the eligible cooperation area, including Sardinia, Liguria, Tuscany, Corsica, VAR and Maritime Alps. The initiative seeks to improve market access opportunities for SMEs active in agri-food production, rural crafts, experiential tourism and green bioeconomy sectors by fostering cross-border cooperation, joint promotion, innovation and international outreach. The project will support the development of common quality and territorial identity tools, digital solutions, business support services and cooperation mechanisms capable of generating long-term benefits for rural territories and local economies. The consortium is seeking organisations interested in contributing to territorial development, SME competitiveness, internationalisation and innovation through a collaborative Mediterranean approach. Detailed project information will be shared with organisations expressing interest in joining the partnership.
candidate.technical_problem_evidence_text: The consortium is seeking partners from Corsica, VAR and Maritime Alps, as well as other eligible territories of the Interreg Italy-France Maritime Programme, with experience in SME support, rural development, internationalisation, territorial promotion, innovation and cross-border cooperation. Target organisations include GAL/LAGs, Chambers of Commerce, local and regional authorities, development agencies, business support organisations, sector associations, innovation clusters, universities and research centres. The consortium is also interested in technical partners specialised in digital solutions for SMEs, including the development and management of digital platforms, online marketplaces, business matching tools, e-commerce solutions, digital marketing and internationalisation services. Experience in supporting territorial value chains, local products and SME access to international markets will be considered an asset. Target regions / departments: - Regions / departments of Programme area: France (Corse, VAR and Alpes-Maritimes), Italy (Liguria, Tuscany). - In addition to the eligible territories mentioned above, the call exceptionally allows participation from entities located outside the Programme area that possess the specific competencies required for the proposed actions. Public bodies, private entities, and international organizations that, although not located in the Programme area, are based in France are also eligible, provided they guarantee a direct impact on the Programme area.

candidate.description_text: The company is looking for an eastern european sme able to provide YSZ coating service upon space frame requirement (generally ECSS). The objective of the Call is to develop an engine for European Mars entry, descent and landing capability. The activity specifically focuses on chemical propulsion engines that use storable propellants. The output of this activity will reach TRL 5 at throttleable engine assembly level by developing and verifying key performance characteristics of a full-scale throttleable engine assembly model. The activity will also identify technology gaps and prepare a development plan for TRL 6. candidate.description_text: The company developed a pilot model that combines green management, destination development and digital communication to create sustainable and economically viable territorial ecosystems. The model starts by defining a geographical area and mapping local businesses, organisations and initiatives adopting low-impact, circular or environmentally responsible practices. These may include sustainable accommodation, restaurants, farms, local producers, sustainable mobility providers, cultural organisations, nature-based activities, renewable energy initiatives, circular economy projects and community enterprises. The objective is not to create a conventional tourism directory, but to build a Green Destination ecosystem, connecting local actors of the same area,  around shared sustainability values and transforming their individual activities into a recognisable territorial offer. The ecosystem is supported by a system of connected web sites, conceived as an SEO-driven website prototype. They organize a digital ecosystem and communicates local resources through business profiles, green experiences, itineraries, geolocated content, destination storytelling and editorial content designed around users' search intentions. A key element is the use of Search Engine Optimisation (SEO) as a long-term distribution strategy. Instead of relying primarily on paid advertising or Online Travel Agencies (OTAs), the digital web sites ecosystem aims to generate organic visibility and direct traffic for destinations and local operators. The websites  are supported by social media channels including Instagram and LinkedIn, creating a coordinated Green Communication ecosystem. Content focuses on sustainability practices, local communities, circular economy, low-impact activities, local production and measurable territorial impact. The model therefore connects: territory → green actors → impact → storytelling → organic visibility → direct demand → local economic value. The Sardinian company represents the initial proof of concept. Starting from its role as an eco-sustainable hospitality facility, it has progressively developed territorial communication, networking and projects. The R&D objective is to transform this experience into a replicable European methodology and digital framework, capable of being tested in different territories and adapted to different governance models, including private DMOs and public-private partnerships. The project will investigate green classification criteria, impact indicators, territorial data structures, SEO-based destination architecture, digital engagement, direct distribution models and the economic sustainability of the platform. The long-term ambition is to create a European model in which sustainability is not only communicated, but becomes a measurable criterion for destination development and a competitive asset for local businesses.
candidate.technical_problem_evidence_text: The project seeks R&D and technology partners with expertise in: •	destination management platforms and tourism technology; •	GIS, geolocation and territorial data management; •	sustainable tourism and circular economy; •	environmental and social impact measurement; •	ESG and sustainability indicators; •	database architecture and interoperable data systems; •	SEO and large-scale content architecture; •	AI-assisted content creation and semantic search; •	recommendation and personalisation systems; •	digital marketing and social media analytics; •	SaaS platform development; •	APIs and integration with third-party systems; •	data visualisation and dashboards. Technical development may include a territorial mapping system, green business classification, impact scoring, structured destination data, automated content generation, SEO optimisation, analytics and dashboards. Partners should contribute to the definition and validation of Green Destination criteria and impact indicators, technological architecture, pilot implementation and performance measurement. The preferred approach is modular and scalable, allowing deployment across territories of different sizes and integration with existing public and private digital infrastructures.

candidate.description_text: A consortium led by European industrial and research partners is preparing the Horizon Europe proposal CIRCUIT-PACK under HORIZON-CL6-2026-01-CIRCBIO-01. The project aims to demonstrate a circular value chain for food-contact flexible PET packaging, enabling effective collection, sorting, recycling and closed-loop reuse into new food-contact packaging applications. The consortium brings together packaging manufacturers, recyclers, technology providers, food companies and retailers to validate innovative circular packaging solutions under real market conditions. To strengthen the value chain and ensure the demonstration of industrial-scale circularity, the consortium is seeking an experienced waste management organisation active in the collection, sorting and treatment of post-consumer packaging waste. The consortium is looking for a waste management company in Spain to: - Operate the collection of used food-contact PET packages during the project demonstrations. - Organise and support the transfer of collected materials to sorting and recycling facilities. - Provide data and statistics on the quantities and quality of packaging waste collected. - Contribute to the assessment and optimisation of the collection system, identifying opportunities to improve efficiency, participation rates and material recovery. - Support the validation of a circular value chain enabling the recycling and reuse of PET into new food-contact packaging applications.

candidate.description_text: The Lithuanian company has developed a mobile application that bridges the "Actionability Gap" for health-conscious consumers. While the current MVP utilizes a database of 30,000+ cosmetic ingredients and 1M+ cosmetic products, the R&D objective is to transition from a binary "safe/unsafe" presence model to a sophisticated dosage-based assessment. The project will focus on: Dosage-aware logic: Developing a model to estimate ingredient concentration based on label position (INCI order) and typical industry formulations. Impact modeling: Assessing each ingredient for both human health (toxicological risk) and environmental sustainability (aquatic toxicity, biodegradability). Cross-sector expansion: Adapting the validated cosmetic logic for household cleaning products and the food industry in a second phase. The project duration is around 24 months. The lead SME has already validated the market gap with 300+ users and finalized the brand identity.
candidate.technical_problem_evidence_text: The partner should provide the following technical capabilities: Toxicological mapping: Data or expertise in mapping INCI ingredients to specific health risk thresholds. Environmental data: Expertise in ecotoxicology to score the environmental footprint of household and cosmetic chemicals. Algorithm development: Experience in building complex scoring engines or processing large-scale chemical databases. Food/Household regulatory knowledge: Expertise in EU labeling and safety regulations for both household cleaning products (e.g., Detergents regulation, CLP regulation) and food to assist in adapting the dosage-aware scoring logic and ingredient risk assessment.

candidate.description_text: This project addresses a critical gap in healthy ageing biology: the lack of early-lifespan human models that can predict long-term physiological decline before chronic, age-related diseases appear. Standard ageing clocks measure slow-drift biological degradation in post-reproductive populations. Recent literature, by contrast, shows that human pregnancy acts as a naturally occurring, time-compressed and hormonally amplified stress test of the core hallmarks of ageing. The project aims to build an investigational, low-maturity machine learning engine, at Technology Readiness Level 1 to 3 (TRL 1-3), to map this stress window. Rather than deploying a commercial app or consumer intervention, it establishes a non-interventional, multi-modal biological screening platform. The central data-processing engine uses a late-fusion neural network with gated attention, designed to ingest asynchronous digital and multi-omic data streams. These fall into two complementary types. - The first is high-frequency edge data: vocal biomarkers, actigraphy-based sleep patterns, physical activity, self-reported food logs and stress metrics. - The second is discrete biological data: shotgun gut metagenomics, serum inflammaging panels and plasma epigenetic clocks, sampled every three months. The algorithm will then evaluate cross-talk across six hallmarks of ageing defined by López-Otín and colleagues (2023): dysbiosis (#12), chronic inflammation or inflammaging (#11), epigenetic alteration (#3), deregulated nutrient sensing (#6), mitochondrial dysfunction (#7) and cellular senescence (#8).
candidate.technical_problem_evidence_text: We are seeking clinical research institutions, university hospital networks or maternal-foetal medicine centres with access to first-trimester cohorts and the capacity to run longitudinal observational perinatal protocols.
candidate.title: EIC Pathfinder Challenge: Clinical partners sought to collect multimodal datasets for machine-learning models tracking maternal and infant healthy ageing trajectories

candidate.description_text: A Latvian non-profit innovation and technology organisation is coordinating the preparation of a project proposal under the I3-2026-INV2a – Financial and advisory support for investments in interregional innovation projects for the development of value chains in less developed regions call. The planned project will establish an interregional European value chain for the development and production of large rotationally moulded products intended primarily for demanding marine applications. The investment concept includes the development and demonstration of rotational moulding processes for large components, using high-density polyethylene in granulate and powder form. An important project objective is to increase the use of recycled materials while maintaining the mechanical properties, processability, durability and product safety required for demanding industrial applications. The project will therefore investigate the technically and economically viable integration of post-industrial and post-consumer recycled HDPE into rotational moulding production. The project is expected to address the complete pathway from material preparation and formulation to processing, prototype production, testing and industrial demonstration. Potential activities include: * selection and characterisation of virgin and recycled HDPE feedstock; * evaluation of HDPE granulate and powder suitable for rotational moulding; * preparation and modification of recycled-HDPE formulations; * optimisation of particle size, powder flow, melt behaviour and sintering performance; * assessment of material contamination, degradation and batch variability; * optimisation of blends containing virgin and recycled HDPE; * investigation of additives, pigments, antioxidants and UV stabilisers; * development of single-layer and multilayer rotational moulding solutions; * process optimisation for large and geometrically complex moulded components; * mechanical, impact, creep, fatigue and environmental durability testing; * evaluation of UV exposure, temperature variation, moisture and saltwater resistance; * analysis of weldability, repairability, recyclability and end-of-life options; * development of quality-control procedures and specifications for recycled-HDPE feedstock; * demonstration of selected formulations in full-scale or near-full-scale rotationally moulded components. The project will not focus only on laboratory research. The selected materials and formulations should be suitable for validation in an industrial environment and should support progression towards commercial production. The planned applications include large, durable and potentially buoyant structures for marine environments. Nevertheless, the developed recycled-HDPE formulations and manufacturing methods may also be transferable to other sectors using large rotationally moulded products, including infrastructure, transport, aquaculture, energy, agriculture and environmental technologies. The project is being prepared under the I3 Strand 2a programme, which supports interregional investments, innovation diffusion, demonstration, industrial deployment and market uptake. Projects are expected to begin at a minimum of TRL 6 and progress towards demonstration, commercialisation and scale-up. The programme applies a 70% EU funding rate for standard eligible project costs, while the remaining 30% must be provided as the partner’s own contribution or through other eligible non-EU resources. The planned project duration is expected to be approximately 36 months. The call deadline is 12 November 2026, and the consortium is currently being developed.
candidate.technical_problem_evidence_text: The consortium is seeking a partner with demonstrated expertise in one or more of the following areas: * recycled HDPE material development; * post-consumer or post-industrial HDPE recycling; * preparation of polyethylene powder for rotational moulding; * grinding, pulverisation, compounding or pellet-to-powder conversion; * characterisation of recycled polymer feedstock; * rotational moulding of HDPE granulate or powder; * formulation of virgin/recycled HDPE blends; * polymer additives, antioxidants, pigments and UV stabilisers; * prevention of oxidation, embrittlement and environmental stress cracking; * melt-flow, rheological and sintering behaviour of polyethylene powders; * multilayer rotational moulding; * mechanical, impact, creep and fatigue testing of HDPE; * industrial scale-up and validation of recycled polymer formulations. The most important selection criterion is practical and research-based knowledge of recycled HDPE, particularly its preparation, formulation and use in rotational moulding. General expertise in plastics or composites without demonstrated experience in recycled polyethylene would be considered less relevant.
candidate.title: I3 Strand 2a: European Union-based coordinator seeks research partner with expertise in recycled HDPE granulate and powder for rotational moulding

candidate.description_text: The project aims to establish sustainable collaborative relationships among partners, with the goal of developing joint research, facilitating the exchange of experience, and supporting academic mobility. By creating strategic partnerships, the project will encourage interdisciplinary and transnational cooperation, enabling the transfer of knowledge and best practices between higher education institutions and research centers. Academic mobility will include exchanges of students, doctoral candidates, and teaching staff, contributing to the development of research skills and the professional growth of participants. Furthermore, the project will support the strengthening of international networks, fostering innovation through the integration of diverse expertise and promoting a collaborative academic environment focused on concrete results in both scientific and educational domains. The research will focus on current issues, such as: •Developing strategies for implementing research results into student-centered learning within biology lessons. •Designing STE(A)M projects to stimulate creativity, critical thinking, and active-participatory learning skills in students. •Applying STE(A)M projects to develop research skills in students through the study of plant organisms. •Developing strategies for organizing and conducting extracurricular activities in the educational process of biology. •Promoting health education among students by leveraging knowledge of pathogen handling and safety. •Developing a representative collection of plant organisms with broad applicability in biotechnology, approached from the perspective of biodiversity conservation, ecological education, and sustainable use of biological resources. •Elucidating the interactions between host genotype × pathogenic microorganism × environment in the development of plant resistance. •Determining growth, development, and application characteristics of microorganisms (micromycetes, algae, etc.) in various biotechnological processes.
candidate.technical_problem_evidence_text: •Fundamental and applied research in biology, including biotechnology and ecology; •Development and implementation of innovative methodologies for teaching and learning in biology; •Use of digital technologies and IT tools for the analysis of biological data; •Analysis of biological flows and natural resources in sustainable contexts; •Evaluation and quality assurance in biology education programs and teacher training; •Interdisciplinary collaborations between biology, educational sciences, and other STEM fields.

candidate.description_text: PMSI Institute of Oncology is a public tertiary cancer centre in the Republic of Moldova, operating under the Ministry of Health. It is the country’s leading institution for cancer diagnosis, treatment, rehabilitation and palliative care, and it runs the national cancer registry. The institute has participated as an affiliated entity or partner in Horizon Europe projects (CCI4EU, EUonQoL) and is involved in EU4Health Joint Actions and OECI. Older cancer patients often face multiple chronic conditions, reduced functional reserve, frailty and social vulnerability. Standard oncology pathways do not always address their specific needs regarding quality of life (QoL), symptom burden, psychological support, nutritional status, mobility and continuity of care after treatment. Call HORIZON‑MISS‑2026‑02‑CANCER‑07 specifically targets interventions to improve QoL in this growing population. The institute offers direct access to a large cohort of older cancer patients as a nationwide referral centre, a multidisciplinary care model covering surgery, chemotherapy, radiotherapy, nutritional and psychological support, palliative care and rehabilitation, and the national cancer registry to provide real‑world data and follow‑up on QoL indicators. Clinical research infrastructure includes immunologic and molecular genetic laboratory, endoscopy, nuclear medicine, radiology, cytology and early detection programmes. The institute has proven ability to collect patient‑reported outcomes and participate in multi‑centre studies through its experience in EUonQoL, as well as strong links with the University of Medicine and Pharmacy and national health authorities. The institute offers to act as a partner, work package leader or task leader – for example in work packages related to patient recruitment, clinical data collection, QoL assessment, dissemination of results at national level, or adaptation of interventions to resource‑limited settings. The institute is currently in advanced discussions with a partner from Romania to form a consortium for this call. The institute aims to learn from and contribute to European best practices in QoL‑focused cancer care. It brings under‑represented patient populations (Eastern European, older, mixed urban/rural) into consortia, which strengthens the external validity of project outcomes.
candidate.technical_problem_evidence_text: The institute is looking for partners with proven expertise in designing and implementing quality‑of‑life interventions for older cancer patients, including validated assessment tools, patient‑reported outcome measures, and psychosocial support programmes. Experience in multi‑centre clinical studies, health economics analysis, and dissemination of results to policy makers would be particularly valuable.
