candidate.description_text: The clinical partner is a tertiary referral hospital in the Republic of Moldova, serving as one of the largest healthcare institutions in the country with over 772 beds and around 30 clinical departments, including specialised intensive care units, cardiovascular surgery, multidisciplinary surgery, and internal medicine wards. The hospital hosts an advanced clinical microbiology laboratory that performs pathogen identification and antimicrobial susceptibility testing according to European Committee on Antimicrobial Susceptibility Testing (EUCAST) standards. The laboratory maintains cumulative antibiogram databases and routinely processes clinical isolates from critically ill and surgical patients, generating antimicrobial resistance data for institutional surveillance. This profile addresses Horizon Europe call HORIZON-HLTH-2027-01-DISEASE-08, which supports the development of innovative antimicrobials against pathogens resistant to current therapies. The call responds to the urgent global threat of antimicrobial resistance, particularly concerning WHO-priority pathogens. Recent institutional surveillance data confirm the presence of clinically significant carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii, carbapenem-resistant Enterobacterales, carbapenem-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa, and methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus — pathogen groups explicitly targeted by this call. The hospital can provide well-characterised clinical isolates, minimum inhibitory concentration data, resistance profiles, and epidemiological information suitable for translational research, antimicrobial testing, and preclinical validation studies. The institution manages large cohorts of surgical and intensive care patients from across Moldova, creating opportunities for future observational cohorts, translational research, and early clinical studies. A dedicated sanitary-epidemiological service oversees infection prevention and control, healthcare-associated infection surveillance, and antimicrobial stewardship activities. Institutional data on infection rates, resistance trends, and stewardship outcomes can contribute to epidemiological, implementation, and health-system work packages within a consortium. As the Republic of Moldova is a Horizon Europe Associated Country, the clinical partner ensures full eligibility for EU funding participation, contributing to geographic diversity, inclusiveness, and the external validity of clinical research — all of which align with Horizon Europe evaluation criteria. The call is a single-stage Research and Innovation Action, with approximately five projects expected to be funded. The call opens on 10 February 2027 and closes on 13 April 2027 at 17:00 Brussels time. The anticipated project duration is up to 60 months. Expressions of interest are sought as soon as possible to allow sufficient time for consortium building and proposal preparation. The clinical partner is currently in preliminary discussions with several potential partners, but no formal consortium agreement has been signed at this stage. The hospital is seeking to join a consortium as a partner, not as coordinator. Specifically, it seeks collaborations with academic research institutions, universities, pharmaceutical companies, or biotechnology small and medium-sized enterprises from EU Member States and Horizon Europe Associated Countries. The hospital will contribute clinical microbiology expertise, characterised isolate provision, patient cohort access, infection prevention and control data, and support for clinical study work packages. candidate.description_text: IMSP Republican Clinical Hospital “Timofei Moșneaga” is Moldova’s national republican clinical hospital, operating under the Ministry of Health. The hospital provides tertiary-level care across 30+ specialties to approximately 42,000 inpatients and 180,000 outpatient visits annually, drawing patients from all regions of the country. In the context of HORIZON-HLTH-2027-01-STAYHLTH-01, the hospital proposes to contribute as a clinical research and focus group site within a multidisciplinary European consortium addressing disability, rehabilitation and independent living through the life course. Hospital's main clinical expertise lies in musculoskeletal disabilities associated with degenerative and inflammatory rheumatic diseases, conditions that significantly affect functional independence, quality of life and social participation. The hospital has access to a well-established institutional clinical database and routinely follows a large population of patients with chronic rheumatic diseases, providing an excellent setting for patient recruitment, longitudinal follow-up and evaluation of interventions aimed at improving functional outcomes and independent living. IMSP Republican Clinical Hospital “Timofei Moșneaga” can contribute to: recruitment of patients with chronic musculoskeletal disabilities; clinical assessment of pain, disability and functional status; collection of real-world clinical data and patient-reported outcomes; implementation and evaluation of person-centred interventions; dissemination of evidence-based practices in rehabilitation and chronic disease management. A particular strength of the hosipital is its capacity to organize and facilitate structured focus groups and co-creation activities involving persons with disabilities, rheumatologists, physiotherapists, occupational therapists, psychologists, social workers and patient representatives. These activities will support the development of person-centred, community-based solutions aligned with the objectives of the call. Potential research activities include identifying barriers to independent living, assessing unmet rehabilitation and psychosocial needs, exploring chronic pain self-management strategies, evaluating experiences with community-based care, and co-designing integrated models of care that promote autonomy and participation in society. IMSP Republican Clinical Hospital “Timofei Moșneaga” welcomes discussions with prospective coordinators and consortium partners interested in HORIZON-HLTH-2027-01-STAYHLTH-01 (Addressing disabilities through the life course to support independent living and inclusion), deadline: 13 April 2027. The institute is currently in discussions with Fundación Descúbreme (Spain–Chile) regarding potential participation in the consortium. specializes in improving the quality of life, inclusion and participation of people with disabilities, bringing valuable expertise in disability-inclusive and person-centred approaches.
candidate.technical_problem_evidence_text: IMSP Republican Clinical Hospital “Timofei Moșneaga” is seeking a consortium coordinator and complementary partners for HORIZON-HLTH-2027-01-STAYHLTH-01, focused on addressing disabilities through the life course to support independent living and inclusion, with a specific contribution in musculoskeletal and rheumatological disability rehabilitation and chronic pain management. IMSP Republican Clinical Hospital “Timofei Moșneaga” can contribute: (1) clinical patient cohorts with degenerative and inflammatory musculoskeletal diseases; (2) structured multidisciplinary focus groups (3) qualitative and mixed-methods research (4) institutional rehabilitation pathway data for community transition modelling; (5) policy context data from a country. Letters of Intent, institutional information, and additional documentation can be provided upon request. The hospital additionally offers: (6) structured chronic pain management training programmes within a multidisciplinary framework to deliver evidence-based pain education, self-management strategies, and functional rehabilitation for patients with inflammatory and degenerative musculoskeletal conditions; (7) a multifunctional rehabilitation approach combining pharmacological, physical, psychological, and social interventions tailored to individual patient profiles - directly aligned with the call’s emphasis on person-centred, multimodal care models supporting independent living. Letters of Intent, institutional information, and additional documentation can be provided upon request. We welcome discussions with interested organizations to explore potential collaboration opportunities.

candidate.description_text: A Montenegrin licensed research institution specialized in finance, institutional economics, governance analysis and applied research is seeking international partners for research and development cooperation within European projects. The organisation provides expertise in institutional quality assessment, governance indicators, environmental, social and governance (ESG) assessment, macroeconomic analysis and quantitative modelling. Its research activities include the application of advanced econometric methods, including vector error correction models (VECM), panel data analysis and cointegration techniques, to support evidence-based policy development and decision-making. The organisation contributes to projects related to sustainable finance, digital transformation, innovation ecosystems, financial technologies and economic resilience. Its expertise supports the development of analytical frameworks, policy recommendations and research methodologies addressing challenges faced by businesses, public institutions and financial stakeholders. The organisation can provide regional macroeconomic, institutional and ESG-related data, conduct policy analysis and contribute to the development and validation of innovative solutions. Its expertise is particularly relevant for initiatives involving artificial intelligence applications, digital modelling, business resilience, financial risk assessment and the development of tools supporting sustainable investment and financing decisions. The organisation is interested in joining international consortia and collaborating with universities, research institutions, companies, public authorities, financial institutions and other innovation stakeholders involved in European research and innovation programmes. Through research and development cooperation, the organisation aims to contribute its expertise in economic modelling, institutional analysis and sustainability assessment while benefiting from complementary knowledge, technologies and international networks. Cooperation may include participation in EU-funded research projects, joint development of methodologies and analytical tools, contribution to pilot activities, data analysis, policy evaluation and dissemination of research results. The organisation is particularly interested in partnerships addressing sustainable finance, digital transformation of financial services, ESG integration, SME financing mechanisms, economic resilience and evidence-based policymaking in South-East Europe and beyond.

candidate.description_text: Anxiety-related disorders represent a significant public health challenge in Europe and are increasingly associated with biological factors beyond psychosocial determinants. Growing scientific evidence suggests that microbiome composition, host genetic variability, and microbiota-derived metabolites are involved in neuroimmune and metabolic pathways relevant to anxiety-related traits. The central hypothesis is that inter-individual differences in microbiome composition and function, together with host genetic variants (SNPs) and urinary metabolic signatures, are associated with anxiety-related phenotypes. The project follows a clear, stepwise workflow: 1.	Recruitment of participants by clinical or research partners; 2.	Collection of non-invasive biological samples (saliva, stool, urine); 3.	Laboratory and computational analysis of microbiome, genetic, and metabolic data; 4.	Bioinformatic correlation analysis linking biological data with phenotypic or questionnaire-based information. The study is exploratory and intended to generate high-quality, reproducible datasets to support future validation studies and larger collaborative projects. It does not aim to diagnose or treat anxiety disorders. At this stage, collaborators are expected to apply for support through national or local funding mechanisms. Depending on consortium development and results generated, future EU funding applications may be explored.
candidate.technical_problem_evidence_text: Depending on partner expertise, collaborators may be responsible for: •	Participant recruitment and informed consent; •	Ethical approvals at local sites; •	Collection of saliva, stool, and/or urine samples; •	Administration of validated anxiety-related questionnaires or assessments; •	Generation of complementary datasets (e.g. SNP genotyping or metabolomics), where applicable; •	Contribution to interpretation and dissemination of results.

candidate.description_text: Eliar develops integrated hardware, software, and data-driven solutions for industrial plants, with a strong focus on textile dyeing and finishing processes, and growing applications in other industrial sectors. In recent years, Eliar has been expanding its portfolio by integrating advanced analytics, data engineering, and artificial intelligence technologies into existing automation systems. These solutions leverage real industrial data collected from sensors, PLCs, machine controllers, and mechatronic systems to enable predictive maintenance, anomaly detection, digital twins, and adaptive process control. candidate.description_text: A partner is sought for Eurostars R&D project concept to improve early detection of patient deterioration on general wards and during step-down / recovery at home. The idea is to combine continuous, medical-grade multi-parameter wearable monitoring with a risk-stratification layer that supports tiered escalation (advisory vs urgent) and integrates into existing hospital workflows rather than creating a separate “IT island”. The project’s novelty is the translation of continuous physiological monitoring into an operational early-warning workflow that is practical for hospitals: reliable ingestion of high-frequency wearable data, robust handling of artefacts and dropouts, and standards-based interoperability so that summarised observations/alerts can be written back into the hospital EHR. A clinical partner in Sweden (University/Hospital environment) supports real-world validation and usability/evidence generation. IPR conditions for the development: Each consortium party retains ownership of its background IP and will contribute only assets it is entitled to use for the project. Foreground IP will be generated by the respective contributors according to standard Eurostars collaboration practice; interfaces will be defined contractually for project execution, and commercial licensing arrangements (if any) will be agreed after a positive grant decision. A targeted freedom-to-operate check will be performed prior to market launch.
candidate.technical_problem_evidence_text: An innovative software SME with proven experience in hospital interoperability and deployment engineering, ideally including: •	HL7 v2 and/or FHIR implementation, specifically EHR write-back of observations/alerts/annotations (not only data ingestion). •	Experience with hospital integration constraints: interface engines, mapping, testing, identity/SSO patterns, routing to clinical channels. •	Security-by-design for healthcare: encryption in transit/at rest, RBAC/SSO, audit logging, operational monitoring, GDPR-aligned processing patterns (ISO 27001 / NEN 7510 experience is a plus). •	Capability to deliver a repeatable “site integration kit” (templates, mapping guides, test scripts, acceptance criteria) to reduce site-specific engineering and speed deployments. •	Ability to work as a genuine R&D co-development partner in Eurostars (not supplier-only), contributing to WP delivery, validation activities and dissemination where appropriate.
candidate.title: Dutch company is looking for a SME experienced in the medical/clinic area to develop together in a Eurostars project for early detection of patient deterioration.

candidate.description_text: The Dutch agro-ecological research coordinator Wageningen University & Research (WUR) is looking for European innovative small and medium-sized enterprises and startups to collaborate in an ERDF-funded Kansen voor West III project focused on future-proof agriculture. The project aims to increase the innovation capacity of the agricultural and horticultural sector and support a smarter and more sustainable economic transition in Europe. The opportunity is open on a rolling basis for expressions of interest, with the call remaining open until December 2027. Projects can run for up to 24 months. The project offers two support routes: - The first is an R&D voucher, which helps applicants cover external costs for developing and testing a prototype in a laboratory or other relevant controlled environment. This voucher reimburses 100% of accepted Wageningen Research costs, excluding VAT, up to 90,000 euros, and up to 50% of other accepted external costs, excluding VAT, up to 30,000 euros. - The second is a practical test voucher, which supports the use of experts and facilities at the Farm of the Future and connected practice-oriented companies to test and demonstrate an innovation in a real operational environment. This voucher reimburses 100% of accepted Wageningen Research costs, excluding VAT, up to 30,000 euros. The initiative is aimed at innovations that contribute to sustainable agriculture in Flevoland, especially in arable farming and vegetable cultivation. Main crops include potatoes, onions and carrots, supported by crop rotations with grass clover, winter wheat, summer faba bean and cover crops. Relevant innovation themes are agro-ecology, data and technology, energy, residual flows and circularity, and transition management. Links with other crop-related sectors may be possible when the focus remains on soil, cultivation and the farming system. Innovations in animal housing systems and indoor cultivation are not within scope.
candidate.technical_problem_evidence_text: 1. Agro-ecology 2. Data & Technology 3. Energy 4. Residual Flows & Circularity 5. Transition Management
candidate.title: European regional development fund (ERDF) opportunity for innovative SMEs and startups to test and validate future-proof arable farming solutions

candidate.description_text: The Dutch company has developed smart energy software products that help design and manage operations of energy installations. Next to that, they are able to install and integrate with these Solar Energy (PV), Battery Energy Storage System (BESS), e-Heat, lighting and EV chargers. Through their smart Energy Hub EMS platform they orchestrate the components and enable congestion relief for SMEs, so they can continue to expand and grow their business despite severe challenges in the energy landscape. The Dutch company has subsidiaries in Poland and Spain, and commercial activities in Germany. The company offers to partners in a Eurostars consortium to participate in shared development of their Energy HUB EMS platform, further enhancing how it helps electrify an decongest through the three pillars of 1 social, 2 technical, and 3 legal processes involved in Energy HUBs. The platform will help streamline this across the European landscape. What is the company looking for? The company has developed a project that nearly received Eurostars funding in the call mentioned below, and they are now urgently looking for a new partner to further develop this project and get it funded in the next round of EUROSTARS. This means that a new consortium partner that fits the goals does not have to provide enormous writing skills for the proposal, as the proposal is already written. However, finetuning and adding valuable skills and plans is highly appreciated. The main goal within the Eurostars call is to have Exchange of knowledge across European contexts and sharing of necessary expertise and development resources to, in the end, develop and deliver a highly functional platform for developing Energy HUBs in large companies, or in a co-operation of companies located all nearby eachother, on the 3 pillars explained above. The company is aiming to enable electrification and decentralisation of energy for organisational and national resilience, in a context where security of supply and energy costs are increasingly uncertain and unaffordable. In this way, the company is helping to relieve energy congestion and enable business growth where none is possible now due to long waiting times for grid expansion. The company has all software components for an Energy Hub: Asset monitoring product for monitoring, machine learning-driven forecasting, building comfort for building controls, and an asset dashboard for client-side interfaces. The Energy Hub brings these together, together with the social and legal knowledge required to navigate congestion issues. This Dutch company is looking for partners to do co-development of their Energy Hub platform and proposition, extending it to other European countries, all this to start within a cooperation as consortiumpartners in the mentioned EUROSTARS 11 Call. The company is looking for: 1: Innovative partners that are active in the energy landscape, that have complementary skills to theirs. For instance companies that can be described as Energy Consulting companies, supporting companies with advisory services on energy use, energy infrastructie investments,  having good knowledge of the grid in their own country, are in close contact with Network operators, TSO's and DSO and have knowledge of their national energy market and playfield. 2: Companies that install PV panels and Batteries, who would like to offer their clients an integral software system so clients an effectively manage their energie use and sources, are also interesting companies to participate in the proposed Eurostars 11 call. 3: Manufacturers of EV charging, e-boilers, lighting, inverters that like to offer their products within an Energy Hub to increase attractiveness. All companies located in European countries that are supported by their national innovation fund, part of Eurostars, are invited to make an expression of Interest. For instance companies from Germany, France, Sweden and Norway but also other countries based in Europe.
candidate.technical_problem_evidence_text: As stated above, the company is looking for consortiumpartners with complementary energy knowledge to their software development core business, also in the field of decongestion and electrification. Partners should have seen as Grid Partners or Energy consulting companies, with national&regional grid knowledge, valuable contacts with their network operators and national market knowledge.

candidate.description_text: Peripartum depression is a common and serious complication during and after pregnancy. The consequences not only affect the mother, but can also affect the child's emotional, cognitive, and social development. A significant number of cases are never recognized in regular care. Current detection mostly relies on questionnaires and what a woman dares to disclose herself. Shame, stigma, and fear of being seen as a bad or inadequate mother can lead women to not fully express their complaints, even when asked. A biological approach can help lower this barrier by making risks objectively visible. Previous research shows that hormonal, immune, and other biological processes can play a role for some women. The company has developed a novel AI-based algorithm that combines various biological and clinical signals from a simple blood test in combination with a user-friendly app into a personal risk assessment for peripartum depression. By analysing biological signals during pregnancy, the risk of peripartum depression can become visible earlier. In addition, participants receive explanations through the app about hormones and mental health during pregnancy, as well as information on when it is wise to contact their own healthcare provider. In this way, women can receive appropriate support in a timely manner and a healthy start for mother and child can be promoted. The ultimate vision is a completely innovative type of mental health diagnostic paired with precision medicine. The algorithm has been validated in retrospective studies and is currently being evaluated in a prospective Dutch cohort. The company is now seeking international collaborators with complementary expertise, technologies, or resources to advance women's health. Areas of collaboration may include, but are not limited to, the following: •	Validation and/or implementation in markets beyond the Netherlands •	Novel approaches for collecting blood biomarker data •	Provision of resources and support following diagnosis •	Integration into established digital health platforms and mobile applications •	Expansion beyond peripartum depression to other conditions affecting women's health A Eurostars Call 11proposal is currently under development, with a deadline for expression of interest set for July 10, 2026.

candidate.description_text: A Dutch university research group specialised in computer vision and video representation learning is coordinating an emerging consortium for the next round of the Sustainable Blue Economy Partnership (SBEP) joint transnational call. The project concept centres on AI World Models for Unmanned Underwater Vehicles (UUVs): learned latent-dynamics models that allow underwater robots to build internal predictive representations of their environment from video and sensor data, and to use these representations for robust perception, prediction and planning in turbid, dynamic and communication-limited marine conditions. Applications include autonomous ecosystem monitoring, habitat mapping, and biodiversity observation. The emerging consortium already covers a strong technological core across three countries and two European sea basins: video representation learning and model interpretability (Netherlands, coordinator), multimodal video understanding (Italy), 3D perception and autonomous exploration (Netherlands), and resilient underwater robot autonomy and field deployment (Denmark/Norway). To complete the consortium, two partner profiles are sought: 1.	Marine biology / marine ecology research partners able to define ecologically meaningful monitoring objectives, ground-truth and interpret UUV-collected observations, and connect the technology to ecosystem-assessment and policy needs (e.g. biodiversity indicators, habitat status, MSFD-relevant descriptors). 2.	Blue-economy industry partners (SMEs or larger) active in marine monitoring, aquaculture technology, offshore inspection, or ocean data services, to provide operational use cases, contribute to piloting and validation at sea, and drive exploitation of results. Partners joining now will co-shape the scientific objectives, use cases and work plans.
candidate.technical_problem_evidence_text: Marine biology / ecology research organisations with expertise in one or more of: •	Marine ecosystem monitoring and assessment •	Biodiversity observation, species identification, habitat mapping •	Ecological indicator frameworks and marine environmental policy (e.g. MSFD, ecosystem-based management) •	Field campaigns and ground-truthing of observational data; experience with imagery/video-based marine data is an asset Industry / SME partners in the blue economy with activities in: •	Marine monitoring and inspection services •	Aquaculture technology and operations •	Ocean data services, marine sensors or autonomous platforms •	Offshore operations requiring underwater situational awareness Optionally: public authorities or agencies responsible for marine environmental monitoring, as use-case providers and uptake actors.
candidate.title: A Dutch university seeks marine ecology and blue-economy partners for a Sustainable Blue Economy Partnership (SBEP) proposal on AI world models for underwater vehicles and marine ecosystem monitoring

candidate.description_text: The Dutch SME has expertise in developing AI models, AI-based tools, sustainable AI, and privacy-first AI. Their core competency lies in creating domain-agnostic AI agentic workflows. They create end-to-end, full-stack web and desktop applications that implement their AI models and services, with a strong focus on data security and GDPR compliance. The rapid adoption of Large Language Models (LLMs) in daily life presents a significant challenge for the education sector: students increasingly use these tools for schoolwork, while schools lack suitable instruments to guide that use. Simple prohibition is ineffective and fails to prepare students for a future in which AI interaction is a fundamental skill. This project develops a new generation of novel AI-powered pedagogical tools that foster critical thinking in primary and secondary education, addressing that gap. The underlying concept, functional design and technical architecture are proprietary. The technical and pedagogical work is covered within the existing consortium, so only one partner is still sought, in a commercial, marketing and dissemination role (see below). Programme call: Eurostars – Call 11 (2026). Estimated timeline: • Call opens: 09.07.2026 • Eurostars call deadline: 10.09.2026, 14:00 CET • Expression of Interest (EoI) deadline: 21.08.2026 • Project duration: 36 months
candidate.technical_problem_evidence_text: Only one partner is sought, with the following profile: - Sector: active in the education sector, primarily primary and secondary education (K-12). - Role: supporting the development of the tool from marketing perspective, marketing, dissemination, market introduction and commercial exploitation of the final product within the K-12 market. - Market access: established relationships with schools, school boards, teacher networks, educational publishers or distributors, and the ability to reach them at scale. - Capabilities: marketing and communication capacity, market and end-user insight, and the ability to support pilot activities and go-to-market planning. - Market knowledge: familiarity with procurement, budgeting and decision-making processes in K-12 education, ideally in more than one European country.

candidate.description_text: This expression of interest comes from a university department of family medicine in the Netherlands, active in medication safety, implementation science and primary care research. The organisation is seeking to join an existing or forming consortium under the Horizon Europe topic HORIZON-HLTH-2027-01-CARE-02: Personalised Approaches to Reduce Risks from Adverse Drug Reactions due to Administration of Multiple Medications, as a project partner or, depending on the consortium's needs, as a work package leader. The project it wishes to contribute to addresses adverse drug reactions (ADRs) linked to taking multiple medications at once (polypharmacy), a growing patient-safety concern, especially among older adults and people with complex medication regimens. The call seeks more personalised, evidence- and biomarker-guided prescribing decisions, safer deprescribing, and better integration of clinical decision-support tools into everyday primary care. The organisation can contribute expertise in medication optimisation and safety in primary care, pragmatic clinical trials, implementation science, and the use of real-world data, including electronic health records, to evaluate and scale up personalised prescribing and deprescribing interventions. It can help generate real-world evidence on the clinical utility and cost-effectiveness of biomarker-guided prescribing, support integration of clinical decision-support systems into primary care workflows, and help address behavioural and organisational barriers to adopting personalised medicine among healthcare professionals.

candidate.description_text: This university department of family medicine and public health research in the Netherlands, active in preventive intervention research, implementation science, and behavioural health in primary care, is seeking to join one or more existing or forming consortium under the Horizon Europe topic HORIZON-HLTH-2027-01-DISEASE-10: Prevention and management of chronic non-communicable diseases in children and young people (GACD), as a project partner or, depending on the consortium's needs, as work package leader — particularly for work packages on intervention development, implementation strategy, process evaluation, stakeholder engagement, real-world evaluation, or dissemination. The project it wishes to contribute to addresses the rising burden of chronic non-communicable diseases (NCDs) among children and young people, such as those linked to tobacco and nicotine use and unhealthy lifestyle behaviours. The call seeks to develop, adapt, and scale up evidence-based prevention and management strategies that reach the young people who need them most, including in under-resourced and underserved communities, and to demonstrate that these strategies remain effective and sustainable beyond the life of the project. The organisation brings two complementary strands of expertise. First, broader primary-care implementation research: developing, implementing and evaluating preventive interventions in routine primary care in both European and low- and middle-income settings (e.g. Ethiopia), including digital health innovations, self-management support for chronic conditions, and pragmatic or platform trial methods. Second, a specific focus on tobacco and nicotine prevention and cessation among adolescents and young adults, including behavioural counselling, digital and AI-supported support tools, financial incentives, and policy-level approaches, alongside strong methodological expertise in evaluation design (including randomised and quasi-experimental studies) and equitable implementation among disadvantaged groups.

candidate.description_text: This research institute seeks a partner to join their consortium application for the Horizon Europe European Innovation Council (EIC) Pathfinder Challenge "Biotechnology for Healthy Ageingt" (deadline: 28 October 2026), specifically its non-animal model (NAM) track, an approach aimed at reducing reliance on live-animal testing. The Dutch institute are coordinator in this consortium. The project aims to build a laboratory model of brain ageing that uses induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC)-derived models of the brain and gut, artificially aged through a process called replicative exhaustion (repeated cell division until cells reach their natural limit), to create a human-specific screening platform for studying ageing and testing potential treatments. To confirm that this new laboratory model accurately reflects real biological ageing, the project needs to compare it, or benchmark it, against a recognised in vivo (animal) model of natural ageing, such as aged rats. A partner is sought with a documented track record in in vivo models of natural ageing, such as aged rats, and with such an animal model readily available in-house for use in the project. The partner should also be able to analyse senescence-associated markers - biological indicators of cellular ageing - in brain and gut tissue from the animal model. The partner is expected to join as a full consortium member and active research collaborator, rather than as a subcontracted service provider.
candidate.technical_problem_evidence_text: A full consortium partner is sought with expertise in in vivo natural ageing animal models (e.g. rats) and senescence marker analysis to benchmark the new platform.

candidate.description_text: The Institute's research is focused on ecological technologies based on reduction of VOC (waterborne, UV-cured), using sustainable and renewable raw materials (binders, fillers, additives) and innovative additives such as nanopowders, nanoadditives. Their works are also focused on materials which use waste as a raw materials and design for recycling and life-time extension of materials. They can implement innovative materials (synthesized, prepared by other collaborators) into a paint or composite formulation and test it for specific application or in which we could test a formulated by us coating materials as a part of bigger element /system used in different industries (mechanical testing, artificial aging tests, protective and optical properties). The Institute is interested in participating in projects regarding the development and use of advanced materials and technologies for organic coatings and polymer composites that: • meet the assumptions of the Green Deal (bio-renewable, sustainable, circular) for building industry, agriculture, defence, electromobility, smart, zero emission cities, • reduce the impact and carbon footprint of materials and technologies, • are designed for recycling and life-time extension of materials, • use advanced materials to achieve sustainable development goals, especially clean and accessible energy, economic growth and decent work, industrial innovation, infrastructure, less inequality, sustainable cities and communities, responsible consumption and production, climate action, life under water, life on land. They are able to: 1.	Develop new formulations of paints and coatings for various substrates, considering renewable raw materials. 2.	Impart and modify their properties with appropriate additives and study the impact of these additives on: o	Application properties o	Usability o	Durability o	Aging under various laboratory conditions o	Produce semi-industrial batches of coating products for larger-scale tests, e.g., on demonstrators. Their tasks could include: 1.	Developing formulations based on raw materials (resins, additives, fillers) for obtaining customer requirements to the final application. 2.	Selecting other raw materials that impart specific properties (they can use experimental raw materials provided by other consortium partners). 3.	Developing paint or coating formulations and producing trial batches for laboratory-scale tests on infrastructure used in the paint and coatings industry. 4.	Testing the properties of coating products in a liquid state as well as their mechanical, aging (long term exposure to humidity, temperature, UV, salinity), application, and protective properties, functional properties (microbiological, mechanical, thermal, anticorrosion, conductivity). 5.	Comparing the properties with traditional commercial systems or those developed for the project. 6.	Scaling up the production of coating products by ensuring the appropriate amount of raw materials and producing trial batches, e.g., for application on specific objects up to 150 l/month. 7.	Transferring products for further tests by other consortium partners.
candidate.technical_problem_evidence_text: The sought partner is a German SME operating in the field of production and development of raw materials for the paints and coatings industry, with particular emphasis on sustainable, bio-based raw materials or highly specialised, niche applications in paint and coating technologies. The partner should possess: •	technological and manufacturing capabilities enabling scaling of solutions and their industrial implementation, •	experience or a demonstrable potential in the commercialisation of developed solutions, •	market knowledge and the ability to provide information on market needs, technological trends, and customer requirements, •	facilities and expertise to carry out industrial and development activities focused on specific application-driven solutions. Scope of work within the project The project is expected to include: •	development of new additives, binders, or raw materials for use in paints and coatings, or modification of existing raw materials, •	implementation of the developed raw materials into paint formulations, formulation of coating systems, and their laboratory testing (application, physicochemical, and performance properties), •	assessment of the technological suitability and implementation potential of the developed solutions.

candidate.description_text: The Polish company operates in the fields of creative industries, digital media and emerging technologies. Its activities focus on digital content production, personal brand development, social media communication and the implementation of innovative solutions supporting content creators and professionals operating in the creator economy. The company combines expertise in content marketing, audiovisual production, creative project management and the development of digital products tailored to the rapidly evolving digital economy. The owner and founder has extensive experience in the media, entertainment and digital sectors. Through cooperation with artists, influencers, experts, cultural institutions and digital entrepreneurs, the company has gained practical knowledge regarding the challenges faced by content creators, including audience engagement, content monetisation, digital visibility, career sustainability and skills development in an increasingly AI-driven environment. The organisation is actively involved in content creation, digital communication and community-building projects and continuously tests innovative communication formats, audience engagement strategies and digital business models. Project idea The project addresses the growing need to support professionals working in digital creative professions, including content creators, influencers, online educators, creative freelancers, digital artists, media professionals and emerging creator-economy entrepreneurs. While AI technologies are increasingly used in content production, communication and business development, there is currently a lack of comprehensive methodologies ensuring that AI serves human development, wellbeing and sustainable career growth. The DIGITAL CREATIVE FUTURES project aims to: develop a European Human-Centered AI framework for digital creative professions; identify future competencies required in the creator economy and digital labour market; create tools supporting professional resilience, wellbeing and career sustainability; develop AI-assisted learning and career development methodologies; explore ethical, social and economic implications of AI adoption in creative industries; design pilot programmes and training solutions for creators and digital professionals; support inclusive and sustainable growth of Europe's digital creative ecosystem.
candidate.technical_problem_evidence_text: The consortium is seeking Norwegian partners with expertise in one or more of the following areas: Human-Centered Artificial Intelligence (HCAI); AI ethics, responsible AI and trustworthy AI implementation; digital transformation and future workforce development; creator economy, digital entrepreneurship and platform-based business models; labour market research and future skills analysis; psychology, wellbeing, resilience and mental health in digital work environments; education, lifelong learning and innovative training methodologies; social innovation and digital inclusion; data analytics and AI-driven competency assessment tools; policy development related to digitalisation, employment and emerging professions. Potential partners may include universities, research institutes, innovation centres, technology companies, public organisations, NGOs and industry associations. Experience in international R&D projects and participation in European funding programmes would be considered an advantage. Partners are expected to contribute to research activities, methodology development, pilot implementation, validation, dissemination and stakeholder engagement.

candidate.description_text: Mountain trails located within forest ecosystems are increasingly affected by forestry operations, erosion, drainage failures, extreme weather events and growing tourist pressure. Information regarding trail conditions, closures and risks is often fragmented, delayed and unavailable in real time. At the same time, trail managers lack integrated tools enabling evidence-based maintenance planning and prioritisation of interventions. The project seeks to address these challenges through the development of an integrated methodology capable of reliably assessing the current technical condition, accessibility and resilience of mountain trails using multiple data sources. Project Objective is to develop an integrated methodology that combines field observations, satellite imagery, meteorological information, administrative datasets and community-generated data to provide reliable assessments of the technical condition, accessibility and resilience of mountain tourist trails. Pilot Area-research and pilot activities will be conducted in the Beskid Żywiecki mountain region in southern Poland, focusing on trails: located within State Forest areas, periodically used by heavy forestry machinery, vulnerable to erosion, rutting, mud accumulation and drainage damage, temporarily closed to visitors, situated in areas with limited internet connectivity, intensively used by hikers and cyclists. Partner Sought- the company is seeking a Norwegian partner to join the consortium and contribute expertise in: mountain trail management, sustainable tourism, climate adaptation, forest ecosystem management, environmental monitoring, GIS and remote sensing, nature-based solutions, resilience of recreational infrastructure.
candidate.technical_problem_evidence_text: Expected Role of the Norwegian Partner- a leader of Research on Trail Resilience, Adaptive Management and European Transferability.

candidate.description_text: A Polish research organisation is preparing a project proposal under the POLNORIS Call for Proposals, implemented within the Applied Research and Innovation Programme and financed by the EEA Financial Mechanism 2021–2028. The Programme Operator is the National Centre for Research and Development in Poland. The POLNORIS Call aims to enhance the quality of research in Poland and strengthen international cooperation in research and innovation through projects implemented jointly by Polish organisations and partners from the Donor States: Norway, Iceland and Liechtenstein. The call is open to different thematic areas, but proposals must contribute to at least one of the three priorities of the EEA Grants: the European green transition; democracy, rule of law and human rights; or social inclusion and resilience. The proposed project directly contributes to the European green transition and circular-economy objectives. The research organisation intends to develop biodegradable biocomposites based on recycled cotton fibres and biodegradable polymer matrices, including modified PLA, to address the environmental impact of textile waste and the need for more sustainable materials. The concept builds on previous research in fibre-matrix interface engineering and polymer modification. It aims to improve compatibility between hydrophilic natural fibres and biodegradable polymers. Waste cotton fibres obtained from post-consumer or post-industrial textile streams will be used as reinforcement in place of conventional natural fibres. The planned work will focus on targeted modification of the polymer matrix and optimisation of fibre-matrix interactions. The objective is to develop materials with improved mechanical performance, durability and controlled biodegradability, while reducing environmental impact and supporting circular-economy principles. The project will valorise textile waste by converting it into higher-value materials. It will assess environmental performance through life cycle assessment and biodegradability testing and will evaluate scalability, market potential and applicability in selected industrial sectors. The project consortium must include at least one entity established in Poland acting as the Project Promoter and at least one research organisation from Norway, Iceland or Liechtenstein. The Polish Project Promoter may be a research organisation or an enterprise. Additional project partners may include public or private entities, commercial or non-commercial organisations, enterprises, non-governmental organisations and industrial end users established in Poland or in one of the Donor States. The POLNORIS Call supports industrial research and experimental development. Interdisciplinary and cross-sectoral cooperation, research valorisation and the involvement of early-stage researchers are encouraged. Applications may be submitted from 17 September 2026, 10:00 CEST, until 17 December 2026, 15:00 CET. Applications must be prepared in English and submitted electronically.
candidate.technical_problem_evidence_text: The research organisation seeks partners with complementary expertise for the development, testing, validation and future application of the biocomposites. The following partner profiles are sought: - textile recycling companies experienced in collecting, processing and supplying waste cotton textile materials; - research institutions or specialised organisations with expertise in life cycle assessment, environmental impact assessment and biodegradation testing of materials; - industrial end users interested in testing the developed materials under application conditions, validating their performance and supporting market-oriented activities. The partners should be interested in a research and development project focused on scaling, testing and validation of innovative material solutions.
candidate.title: POLNORIS – Applied Research and Innovation Programme: Polish research organisation seeks partners to develop biodegradable biocomposites from recycled cotton textile waste and modified PLA

The concept builds on previous research in fibre-matrix interface engineering and polymer modification. It aims to improve compatibility between hydrophilic natural fibres and biodegradable polymers. Waste cotton fibres obtained from post-consumer or post-industrial textile streams will be used as reinforcement in place of conventional natural fibres. The planned work will focus on targeted modification of the polymer matrix and optimisation of fibre-matrix interactions. The objective is to develop materials with improved mechanical performance, durability and controlled biodegradability, while reducing environmental impact and supporting circular-economy principles. The project will valorise textile waste by converting it into higher-value materials. It will assess environmental performance through life cycle assessment and biodegradability testing and will evaluate scalability, market potential and applicability in selected industrial sectors. The project consortium must include at least one entity established in Poland acting as the Project Promoter and at least one research organisation from Norway, Iceland or Liechtenstein. The Polish Project Promoter may be a research organisation or an enterprise. Additional project partners may include public or private entities, commercial or non-commercial organisations, enterprises, non-governmental organisations and industrial end users established in Poland or in one of the Donor States. The POLNORIS Call supports industrial research and experimental development. Interdisciplinary and cross-sectoral cooperation, research valorisation and the involvement of early-stage researchers are encouraged. Applications may be submitted from 17 September 2026, 10:00 CEST, until 17 December 2026, 15:00 CET. Applications must be prepared in English and submitted electronically.
technical_problem_evidence_text: The research organisation seeks partners with complementary expertise for the development, testing, validation and future application of the biocomposites. The following partner profiles are sought: - textile recycling companies experienced in collecting, processing and supplying waste cotton textile materials; - research institutions or specialised organisations with expertise in life cycle assessment, environmental impact assessment and biodegradation testing of materials; - industrial end users interested in testing the developed materials under application conditions, validating their performance and supporting market-oriented activities. The partners should be interested in a research and development project focused on scaling, testing and validation of innovative material solutions.
title: POLNORIS – Applied Research and Innovation Programme: Polish research organisation seeks partners to develop biodegradable biocomposites from recycled cotton textile waste and modified PLA

candidate.description_text: Polish enterprise operating in the electric power and infrastructure sectors seeks a Norwegian research partner for the POLNORIS programme.  The company possesses extensive technical capabilities and resources for implementing energy infrastructure projects and developing innovative technological solutions. WPE combines engineering and execution competencies with a growing focus on research and development, digital transformation, and energy transition initiatives. Its strategic development areas include power infrastructure solutions, energy-related prefabricated structures, and technologies enhancing infrastructure safety, durability, and operational efficiency. Validation procedures for AI models in international and cross-border environments.

candidate.description_text: A Polish company conducting R&D activities related to the development of innovative AI-based platforms for automated analysis of public procurement documentation seeks a Norwegian partner to join a consortium. The company also provides institutional consulting services concerning public procurement systems, inter-institutional cooperation frameworks, and support mechanisms for SME participation in public markets. Its expertise combines artificial intelligence, digital transformation, regulatory compliance, and innovation management. The growing volume of post-consumer textile waste in Europe creates significant environmental and economic challenges. At the same time, many textile products collected from second-hand markets retain valuable properties that could be utilized in new industrial applications. However, the effective identification, classification, and valorisation of these materials remain limited due to the complexity and diversity of textile waste streams. The TEXTILE SECOND LIFE project aims to develop a novel Human-Centered AI framework enabling the automated recognition, assessment, and processing of selectively collected textile waste, particularly knitted and textile products originating from second-hand markets. The project will support circular economy objectives by transforming waste streams into high-value functional materials for construction and industrial applications. AI-based tools for automated identification and classification of textile waste. Decision-support systems for selecting optimal valorisation pathways. Trustworthy, transparent, and explainable AI models aligned with European regulations and ethical standards. International validation procedures for AI-supported circular economy solutions.
candidate.technical_problem_evidence_text: The Norwegian partner will: Develop scientific foundations for AI-supported textile circular economy solutions. Contribute to the design of Human-Centered AI methodologies. Support the development of classification and valorisation models. Conduct scientific validation of developed AI models. Participate in pilot testing and international evaluation activities. Support dissemination and exploitation of project results.
candidate.title: Human-Centered AI Framework for Circular Valorisation of Selectively Collected Textile Waste -TEXTILE SECOND LIFE.

candidate.description_text: An independent Serbian game studio is seeking partners to form a research and development consortium around AI-assisted game prototyping, educational virtual environments and gamified learning. The proposed project direction addresses a common problem in game and interactive media development: early-stage ideas require significant time and cost before they become usable prototypes or fundable proposals. Small studios, universities and educational organizations often need to prepare design documents, prototype concepts, integrate feedback and assess feasibility before committing months of work. The envisioned solution is a modular AI-assisted toolkit and methodology that helps transform an idea into a structured project proposal, early game design document, prototype plan and interactive demonstration. It would support user feedback integration, documentation workflows, learning objectives, gamification mechanics, narrative/game structure and rapid Unreal/UEFN or Unity/Godot-based prototyping. Potential application areas include video game prototyping, serious games, educational escape rooms, virtual classrooms, cultural heritage experiences, game jams, university-industry cooperation and training environments. Alkonost Team can contribute game development practice, Unreal Engine experience, Slavic mythology/cultural IP experience, gamification research and practical knowledge from releasing a commercial game. Partners sought should contribute AI/ML expertise, learning science, HCI/UX evaluation, educational methodology, data/privacy expertise, user testing, academic coordination and access to pilots with students, teachers, game developers or creative industry users. A dedicated research strand could examine trustworthy LLM-supported creative workflows: maintaining reusable project context, producing structured and traceable outputs, connecting models to approved tools and data sources, preserving human decision-making, evaluating consistency and usefulness, and protecting confidential or copyrighted project material. Claude technologies or comparable LLM platforms may be evaluated depending on the selected call, partner requirements and data-governance constraints
candidate.technical_problem_evidence_text: Expertise sought: AI/ML, generative AI for design support, learning analytics, HCI/UX, educational technology, serious games, game-based learning, Unreal Engine/UEFN, Unity/Godot, web platforms, data protection, user testing, evaluation methodology, project coordination and EU funding experience. Additional expertise sought: LLM engineering, agentic systems, tool/MCP integration, evaluations and observability, AI safety, data governance, IP protection and human-in-the-loop workflow design.
candidate.title: R&D consortium partners sought: AI-assisted game prototyping, educational virtual environments and gamified interactive learning

candidate.description_text: Slovenian technology company is developing an innovative system for non-contact foam detection in single-use bioreactors. The machine will incorporate a non-contact sensor system for continuous detection and quantification of foam levels during the process, together with an adaptive foam elimination system based on controlled dosing of an anti-foam agent. The system will be designed for integration into existing bioreactors and will operate via an independent, standalone control unit. The control architecture will include an adaptive regulation algorithm that dynamically adjusts the system response according to real-time foam measurements. Based on the detected foam volume and its rate of change, the algorithm will calculate the optimal quantity of anti-foam agent required and determine the appropriate depletion time to achieve the target foam level. This closed-loop control strategy ensures efficient foam suppression, minimized chemical consumption, and stable process conditions without unnecessary disturbance to the bioprocess. The company has already developed an initial proof of concept (PoC) that demonstrates the foam detection principle and anti-foam dosing principle. The company is looking for a technology partner to co-develop the platform from start to finish.
candidate.technical_problem_evidence_text: •	Access to laboratory/pilot-scale single-use bioreactors, enabling controlled fermentation trials and foam-generation testing under realistic bioprocess conditions •	Bioprocess engineering expertise (aeration, agitation, gas–liquid mass transfer, foam formation dynamics, batch/fed-batch operation) •	Foam characterization and anti-foam strategy knowledge, including evaluation of anti-foam impact on cell culture performance, oxygen transfer (volumetric oxygen mass transfer coefficient kLa), and product quality •	Process validation and experimental design capability, including structured trial planning, data acquisition, statistical analysis, and benchmarking against conventional foam control methods •	Regulated bioprocess environment experience (Good manufacturing practice (GMP)-aware), including documentation practices, traceability, validation protocols, and process risk assessment •	Co-development support for industrial integration, including defining user requirements, integration constraints with existing bioreactor control systems, and biotechnology-driven input for final product industrialization
candidate.title: EUREKA - Eurostars 3 - Call 10 - Slovenian company that produces equipment for biotech companies is looking for a research and development cooperation agreement to test&validate an innovative system for non-contact foam detection in single-use bioreactors.

candidate.description_text: The organisation is a UK-based higher education institution with expertise in sustainable urban development, the built environment, social economy, climate innovation, and spatial analysis. The research team has extensive experience in participating in Horizon Europe and other international collaborative projects involving public authorities, research organisations, industry, and civil society. The organisation is preparing a proposal for the Horizon Europe call HORIZON-CL2-2027-01-TRANSFO-03, focusing on sustainable competitiveness through the concept of "Lived Sustainability". The project will examine how social economy actors, place-based interventions, and sustainable built environment solutions contribute to inclusive urban transition. Activities include the development of living labs, comparative policy analysis, stakeholder engagement, spatial mapping of green inequality hotspots, and evaluation of social, environmental, and economic impacts. The consortium is seeking partners to jointly develop and implement the proposal. Cooperation is envisaged with universities, research and technology organisations, public authorities, social economy organisations, industry, and civil society organisations able to contribute complementary expertise, case studies, data, stakeholder networks, pilot activities, or policy evaluation. International collaboration will support comparative research across different European regions and the co-creation, testing, and validation of practical approaches for sustainable and inclusive urban development.
candidate.technical_problem_evidence_text: The consortium is seeking partners with expertise in one or more of the following areas: sustainable urban development, social economy, sustainable competitiveness, urban governance, spatial analysis and GIS, energy justice, environmental and social inequalities, living labs, citizen and stakeholder engagement, public policy analysis, and impact assessment. Experience in Horizon Europe or other international collaborative research projects is desirable. Partners should be able to contribute comparative case studies, access to local stakeholders and data, policy and governance expertise, or pilot activities in different European contexts. We particularly welcome organisations with experience in co-creation methodologies, place-based innovation, and the evaluation of social, environmental, and economic impacts of sustainable urban transition initiatives.
candidate.title: Reframing Sustainable Competitiveness Through “Lived Sustainability” in the Sustainable Built Environment and Urban Transition

candidate.description_text: The research is developed at the Slovak University of Technology in Bratislava (STU), Slovakia, within an academic environment focused on architecture, building design and sustainability. The expertise addresses climate-responsive and energy-efficient architecture, with particular emphasis on improving building performance through passive and low-tech architectural strategies before additional technical systems are introduced. The approach has been developed and tested in research on the renovation of the post-war housing stock, including representative family-house types and a prefabricated apartment building. It evaluates how architectural decisions influence energy performance, environmental impact, spatial quality and the architectural character of existing buildings. Investigated strategies include buffer zones and winter gardens, orientation and optimisation of transparent surfaces for passive solar gains, improvement of building compactness/form factor, and integration with terrain/earth to moderate heat transfer and thermal fluctuations. The research combines architectural design and case studies with calculation-based energy-performance assessment and comparative evaluation of variants. Results demonstrate that orientation, exposed glazing, buffer zones and building geometry can significantly influence energy demand and associated CO2 emissions without relying solely on thicker insulation or more powerful building technologies. The team seeks international research partners to extend the methodology beyond the Slovak context, validate it under different European climatic conditions and complement it with dynamic building simulation, indoor thermal-comfort assessment, real-building monitoring and life-cycle/whole-life-carbon assessment. The cooperation may lead to joint research projects, publications, comparative case studies and grant proposals.
candidate.technical_problem_evidence_text: Universities, R&D institutions and specialised industry partners are sought in the fields of building physics, sustainable architecture, building-performance simulation, façade systems, environmental assessment and building monitoring. Academic and research partners should contribute expertise in dynamic energy simulation, thermal comfort, experimental monitoring, LCA/whole-life carbon or climate-specific building performance. Partners from industry may contribute demonstrators, façade/building-system expertise, monitoring technologies or access to suitable case-study buildings. The expected role is to jointly validate and extend the methodology across different European climatic conditions, develop comparative case studies and prepare joint publications and international R&D proposals.
candidate.title: Passive architectural strategies for climate-responsive and energy-efficient buildings

candidate.description_text: Airlines struggle with generic recommendation engines because passengers on the same route can have different motivations (business, leisure, visiting friends & family). The project addresses this by estimating travel purpose at ticket/client/destination level and turning it into actionable “Passenger DNA”. The solution incorporates the temporal dimension of travel demand: time between successive trips, booking-to-flight horizon, national/school holidays, weather and seasonal appeal, and events/festivals. Therefore, recommendations propose a timeline together with the destination (“where & when”). Core analytics layer: An LLM-enhanced hybrid model for travel purpose estimation that combines probabilistic intent scoring, sequential travel-pattern learning, business-rule constraints and latent interaction modelling across customer–destination relationships. Outputs include travel purpose distributions for clients, destinations and individual tickets. Business value layer: -CRM / Loyalty & lifecycle management: intent-driven micro-segmentation enables personalized channel, timing and language plus tailored destination recommendations. -Ancillary services upsell: matching persona and booked-flight intent supports personalized timing and pricing of ancillary offerings during the book-to-flight window. -Revenue management: when temporal demand slowdown is detected, high-intent customers can be targeted to promote low load-factor flights via destination recommendations. R&D collaboration scope: -Data & feature co-design: define data contracts and feature sets from booking/PNR, loyalty/CRM and ancillary signals; privacy-preserving processing and evaluation datasets. -Model co-development: improve intent inference and time-aware recommendation quality; incorporate airline-specific constraints (network, seasonality, commercial rules). -Experimentation & validation: design offline metrics and A/B testing methodology for engagement, conversion and revenue uplift; bias/robustness checks. -Pilot-to-production design: define deployment architecture (batch/near-real-time), monitoring, retraining and governance. Additional capability: demographic and intent-based archetypes and personalized content generation for customer engagement workflows.
candidate.technical_problem_evidence_text: The company is seeking R&D partners who can provide access to representative airline PNR and booking datasets as the foundation for collaborative development and validation of an intent-aware, time-aware next-trip recommendation solution. This is an early-stage R&D project. Success depends on establishing data partnerships that enable: Intent inference model training and validation Development of data-driven recommendation algorithms Pilot evaluation with real airline operational data Core Data Partnership Requirements: Partners should be able to provide access to: PNR-level booking data (origin, destination, booking date, flight date, passenger demographics, advance purchase window, duration of stay) Historical flight records (past travel patterns, frequency, seasonal behavior) Optional but valuable: loyalty/CRM signals, ancillary service purchase data All data collaboration will use privacy-preserving and fully compliant mechanisms.
candidate.title: AI-Powered Passenger DNA & Next-Trip Recommendation Engine for Airlines – Developed by a Turkish R&D Company

candidate.description_text: A Turkish-based SME (Small and Medium-sized Enterprise) applies to international project calls. Currently, it has received support from the 2024 Eureka Network program. The evaluation process for the 2025 Eureka Network program is ongoing. The Turkish SME is interested in the IraSME call. The Turkish SME focuses on developing application-oriented alloys using computational materials engineering technology. It also conducts R&D studies in additive manufacturing (powder bed systems, solid-state deposition, powder deposition systems) through EU-funded projects within the scope of advanced manufacturing technologies. The company also conducts R&D activities aimed at improving surface properties in cermets. In this context, it is working on the WC-xCo alloy. Improving wear properties is also an area of ​​interest. It is considering submitting a project under the 37th IraSME Call, which includes Turkey. In this context, it wishes to focus on alloy development, production, and characterization within a jointly agreed alloy group. The alloy groups he wishes to work on are: nickel, aluminum, cast iron, titanium, iron-based materials, or WC-xCo. The project proposals he wishes to present are as follows: 1- Development, production (casting or additive manufacturing), and characterization of new generation nickel/aluminum-based alloys. Turkish SME conducts alloy development studies. Depending on the expertise of the international partner, the focus could be on casting or powder production. For partners with additive manufacturing equipment, Turkish SME could include a Turkish Higher Education Institution in the project consortium. 2- A project proposal focusing on improving surface properties of cast iron, iron-based materials, or cermets (WC) could be submitted. The Turkish partner could undertake alloy development and WC production. The international partner could be an organization with expertise in surface coating equipment. Thus, work could focus on materials and surface enhancement for wear resistance.
candidate.technical_problem_evidence_text: Technical specifications or expertise sought: A Turkish SME is seeking a project partner who will actively participate in production or characterization activities. In this context, priority will be given to partners with infrastructure for casting or laboratory-scale powder production. (Turkish SMEs may include Turkish Higher Education institutions in the project consortium for production via gas atomization). However, in the absence of such production capacities, cooperation can be established with partners who can carry out comprehensive characterization studies, including: - Chemical composition analysis - Microstructural studies (optical and scanning electron microscopy) - Mechanical tests (hardness, tensile strength, wear resistance) - Corrosion tests - The partnership will contribute to the advancement of alloy development through joint R&D studies within the scope of international cooperation.

The system must be able to scan across a defined field of view, to detect the direction and location of rising heat, and identify anomalies in a spatial context, not just at a fixed point. The project is being prepared under the Eurostars Programme, which supports market-oriented R&D cooperation between innovative SMEs and their partners. candidate.description_text: Targeted Call: HORIZON-MISS-2026-02-CANCER-04: Earlier and more precise palliative care The project aims to develop an AI-supported, integrated model that enables the early start and personalized management of palliative care for cancer patients. The model combines clinical data, patient-reported outcomes (PROs), measurements from digital monitoring devices, and healthcare staff assessments to predict care needs in advance. The model works through four main components: 1.	Early Identification: From the moment of diagnosis, all patient-related data—including electronic health records, patient-reported outcomes (PROs), data from wearable devices (if available), clinician assessments…—are collected and integrated into the system. The model analyzes this data stream in real time to automatically determine whether the patient needs palliative care. Based on the analysis, the system generates risk scores and alerts the clinical team when early intervention is needed, making it easier to monitor critical changes in the patient’s condition. 2.	Predictive Care Planner: AI algorithms recommend the most appropriate care plan based on the patient’s clinical condition, lifestyle, and personal preferences. This information is collected through questionnaires, patient-reported outcomes (PROs), and discussions with caregivers. The system analyzes these inputs together with clinical data to create a personalized plan. The plan includes home- and hospital-based interventions, medication management, psychosocial support, and follow-up schedules, ensuring that care fits the patient’s daily routines. For home-based interventions, families are informed, making care coordination and process management easier. 3.	Digital Coordination Platform: Patients, family members, clinicians, and care staff are all connected through one platform. Real-time communication, symptom reporting, video consultations, and emergency alerts work seamlessly together. This ensures continuity of care and smooth information flow among all parties. It also allows patients and doctors to easily reach each other, giving patients and their families a greater sense of trust throughout the process. 4.	Workforce Management: The workload and patient volume of clinical teams are analyzed to dynamically plan resources. This approach helps maintain care quality and strengthens staff sustainability. The model will be tested in real-world conditions across some (according to final consortium) countries. Its results will be evaluated in terms of clinical effectiveness, patient satisfaction, cost-efficiency, and workforce performance. Separate work package dedicated to training will be included and cover: Entering collected patient data into the system by relevant staff. Training and guidance on using digital tools, tailored separately for clinical staff, patients, and caregivers.  Finally, based on the findings, standardized European guidelines will be developed and disseminated through the ECPDC (European Cancer Patient Digital Centre).

candidate.description_text: A university from Türkiye, specialized in the convergence of immersive technologies, data science, and pedagogical innovation, is preparing a proposal under the ERASMUS-EDU-2026-POL-EXP call. The project positions itself as a European policy experimentation laboratory designed to bridge the widening gap in basic skills (literacy, science, and digital) through the deployment of AI-powered Personalised Learning Pathways (PLPs) within immersive environments. It focuses on initial Vocational Education and Training (iVET) students (EQF levels 1-4), targeting those at risk of falling behind due to the decline in traditional basic skills achievement. By capturing behavioral data in VR and utilizing ML for predictive modeling, they aim to deliver an adaptive, data-driven framework that bridges the gap in literacy, science, and digital competencies. A central feature of the initiative is the creation of VR-based Learning & Assessment Ecosystems that simulate realistic vocational tasks. While the primary engagement is driven by digital skill acquisition, the environments are strategically engineered to integrate and measure literacy and scientific inquiry as "embedded outcomes." The project’s core innovation lies in its Predictive Analytics Engine: by capturing multidimensional behavioral data within VR, it utilizes machine learning models to map individual learning curves, identify specific skill gaps, and autonomously generate adaptive, ethical, and transparent learning plans tailored to each student’s pace. By fostering this data-driven educational environment, the project aims to address the urgent need for inclusive and scalable evidence-based models that enhance student motivation and performance without replacing the vital role of the educator. The initiative will contribute to the definition of a European framework for AI-integrated basic skills education, providing actionable policy recommendations supported by real-world data from international, multi-lingual pilots.
