candidate.description_text: Project concept (VAI‑TriNCD): Create clinically actionable, privacy‑preserving AI models that extract digital biomarkers from structured voice tasks, and fuse them with clinical variables and (where available) wearable/physiological signals. The platform targets three NCD domains: cardiometabolic (e.g., hypertension/heart‑failure risk), neurodegenerative (Parkinson’s disease), and respiratory (COPD), focusing on longitudinal monitoring and treatment response. Technical scope: (i) harmonisation of multimodal datasets across sites; (ii) development of robust, explainable multimodal models (optional wearables/clinical data) with calibration and uncertainty; (iii) validation of predictive biomarkers for disease progression and treatment response; (iv) deployment‑ready pipelines aligned with GDPR and clinical AI quality requirements. Detailed algorithmic and dataset specifics can be shared under NDA. Expected outputs: validated biomarker panels, reference pipelines for multi‑site deployment, and evidence packages supporting future regulatory and reimbursement pathways (including HTA‑relevant endpoints).

candidate.description_text: The institute has a long-standing record in the research, conservation, and management of biodiversity in wetlands and marine ecosystems. Its scientific expertise spans several core areas, including: •	Waterbirds and their ecology •	Identification of benthic organisms •	Identification of algae and plankton •	Ichthyology, including species identification and stock size management •	Identification of plants, habitats, vegetation The institute has direct access to the Gediz Delta, the largest river delta on Türkiye’s Aegean coast. The region includes Türkiye’s largest saltworks (5,500 ha, producing ~800,000 tons of sea salt annually), 700 ha of dry freshwater reedbeds, and three coastal lagoons totaling 2,200 ha. The delta is a RAMSAR site, an Important Bird Area (IBA), and a national Wildlife Reserve. It supports breeding populations of tens of thousands of waterbirds, including 15,000–20,000 pairs of Greater Flamingos, Dalmatian Pelicans, various tern species, and many others. The lagoons also host globally endangered species such as the Critically Endangered Common guitarfish (Rhinobatos rhinobatos) and the European eel (Anguilla anguilla). The flamingo is an important species in the target study area, and approximately 30–40% of the Mediterranean population is found there. Because flamingos feed through filtration, they are negatively affected by poor environmental conditions. Therefore, we are also interested in ensuring that one of the project’s research themes focuses on flamingo habitats — such as lagoons, saltpans, and saline marshes. The Delta is currently facing severe drought due to declining freshwater inputs and increasing water demand from agriculture, urbanization, and industry. Parts of the wetland dried out in recent years, and rainwater alone is no longer sufficient to sustain the ecosystem. Therefore, alternative external water sources are needed. Potential options include agricultural drainage water or treated effluent from a wastewater treatment plant. Once a source is selected, comprehensive monitoring of habitat conditions, bird populations, fish stocks, and other biological communities will be necessary. Additional challenges include rising salinity levels in the lagoons — which are progressively reducing fish and aquaculture productivity — as well as pressures from macro and microplastics coming through rivers and city, and legacy pollution from the leather industry. Addressing these complex issues requires innovative solutions and advanced expertise beyond the institute’s current capacity.
candidate.technical_problem_evidence_text: Prospective partners should bring innovation capacity, advanced methodological expertise, and demonstrated experience in policy-relevant environmental research. The consortium prioritises organisations capable of contributing to: •	The development of scalable monitoring solutions •	Policy-relevant environmental assessments •	Multi-stakeholder engagement •	Cross-country demonstration activities •	Effective dissemination and exploitation of results across Europe and neighbouring regions In open words: 1.	Environmental monitoring and remediation, covering marine, coastal, soil, and freshwater systems. 2.	Water-quality assessment, particularly for evaluating and improving water supplied to reedbeds, lagoons and river outlets. 3.	Training and capacity-building for local stakeholders, including public authorities and private operators. 4.	Automated and online monitoring systems for continuous water‑quality measurement. 5.	Microclimate monitoring and climate‑impact assessment in wetland ecosystems. 6.	Groundwater quality assessment, including spatial and temporal analyses. 7.	Remote sensing and GIS, with a focus on primary productivity, land cover, and habitat change detection. 8.	Replication activities, with partners conducting comparable monitoring at representative sites in their own countries. 9.	SSH contributions, such as stakeholder mapping, socio-economic analysis, behavioural studies, and governance aspects. 10.	Dissemination and communication, including international outreach, training materials, and knowledge transfer. Partners from all EU Member States and Horizon-associated countries are welcome. Preference is given to organisations located in the Mediterranean basin, where findings can be directly demonstrated and replicated.

candidate.description_text: For this call, the proposed thematic area is related to the advanced Diagnostics & Data Technologies (on-site molecular diagnostics, biosensor technologies) / Next-Generation Therapies (innovative cancer approaches – early detection). Regarding innovation and technological level, current methods (MRI, CT, biopsy) often detect cancer late or are invasive. This project offers a novel approach including the following innovations: -Innovation 1: Extracting biomechanical properties (stiffness, viscoelasticity) from acoustic wave data of cellular structures. -Innovation 2: Detecting micro-scale thermal emission from acoustic-induced vibration using quantum sensors for thermal microscopic imaging. -Innovation 3: Creating a database of biomechanical and thermal signatures for cancerous vs. healthy cells. - Regarding TRL levels: It will start from TRL 2-3 (concept, experimental proof), end at TRL 4-5 (prototype validation in lab). Project Objectives: 1.	Model acoustic wave interaction (specific frequency ranges) with healthy and cancerous cells. 2.	Develop algorithms to derive cellular biomechanical properties from acoustic scattering/transmission data. 3.	Integrate a thermal microscope and quantum sensor to detect acoustic-induced thermal (IR) emission at microscopic level. 4.	Build a prototype of the quantum-enhanced thermal-acoustic imaging system. 5.	Validate the prototype using intestinal epithelial cells (preclinical tests).
candidate.technical_problem_evidence_text: The Turkish SME/R&D company will act as project coordinator. They seek at least two partners from EUREKA member countries (one must be an EU or Horizon Europe associated country) with the following expertise: -Thermal microscopy modeling, simulation, design; micro-scale thermal emission detection (Germany, Netherlands, Switzerland, Israel, UK) -Quantum sensors/detectors (e.g., superconducting, NV-center) integration for biomedical applications (Nordic countries, Germany and France) -Surface acoustic wave (SAW) microfluidics for live cell analysis; cellular biomechanical characterization (any Eureka member countries) Note: Desired partner qualifications: Previous participation in EUREKA or Horizon Europe projects; experience in biomedical imaging, photonics, quantum technologies; capability to advance from TRL 3-4 to TRL 5-6.

candidate.description_text: Project Context: The project is designed within the framework of the BlueActionAA initiative supporting the European Union mission to restore oceans and waters. The SME develops modular electrochemical water treatment systems based on electrochemical advanced oxidation processes (EAOP) using boron-doped diamond (BDD) electrodes. Problem Addressed: Persistent micropollutants such as perfluoroalkyl and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS, also referred to as “forever chemicals”), pharmaceuticals and pesticides are difficult to eliminate using conventional water treatment technologies. This challenge is particularly significant in complex and saline environments such as ports, marinas, aquaculture systems and coastal waters. Technology Description: The SME provides a treatment system utilizing in-house developed boron-doped diamond electrodes. These electrodes offer a wide electrochemical potential window, enabling strong oxidation capability for the degradation of persistent micropollutants. The system is designed to operate with reduced chemical dosing and is suitable for complex water matrices, including saline environments. description_text: Project Context: The project is designed within the framework of the BlueActionAA initiative supporting the European Union mission to restore oceans and waters. The SME develops modular electrochemical water treatment systems based on electrochemical advanced oxidation processes (EAOP) using boron-doped diamond (BDD) electrodes. Problem Addressed: Persistent micropollutants such as perfluoroalkyl and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS, also referred to as “forever chemicals”), pharmaceuticals and pesticides are difficult to eliminate using conventional water treatment technologies. This challenge is particularly significant in complex and saline environments such as ports, marinas, aquaculture systems and coastal waters. Technology Description: The SME provides a treatment system utilizing in-house developed boron-doped diamond electrodes. These electrodes offer a wide electrochemical potential window, enabling strong oxidation capability for the degradation of persistent micropollutants. The system is designed to operate with reduced chemical dosing and is suitable for complex water matrices, including saline environments. candidate.description_text: What we bring to your consortium; Biodiversity modelling and scenario frameworks depend on continuous, spatially distributed ground-truth observations from ecosystems that are difficult or impossible to access with conventional monitoring infrastructure. ForestGuard provides exactly this: a self-contained, field-deployable sensor system that generates structured environmental data streams from remote terrain, dense vegetation, and infrastructure-free zones. Each node monitors 30+ parameters including particulate matter LPM1.0, PM2.5, PM4, PM10M, temperature, relative humidity, VOC, NOx, pressure, and microclimate indicators. Nodes operate on solar power with supercapacitor backup, providing 5+ years of autonomous field operation with no mains power, trenching, or gateway infrastructure required. Communication runs on dualmode: LoRa as primary network with S-band satellite fallback, enabling realtime data transmission from any location globally. On-device edge AI performs two-step anomaly detection and false positive filtering before data reaches the cloud, where structured outputs are generated in GIS-compatible, API-ready formats suitable for integration with biodiversity modelling frameworks, Earth observation platforms, and policy dashboards. The system is validated at TRL 6 through field deployment across multiple operational environments. EU-level validation was conducted in June 2025 through partnership with a French national public research institution, producing structured environmental datasets from a European forest environment. Field data is available for consortium reference under NDA. Contribution to HORIZON-CL6-2026-01-BIODIV-05 objectives; HORIZON-CL6-2026-01-BIODIV-05 targets advancing integrated scenarios and redictive models for the transition to a nature-positive society. ForestGuard contributes the in-situ observational infrastructure that feeds these models: continuous, calibrated, hyper-local environmental data from ecosystems that satellite and remote sensing systems cannot adequately monitor at ground level. Our data layer directly supports model validation, scenario calibration, and evidence-based policy outputs. Our role; We are available as a technology partner contributing a defined monitoring work package. We do not seek consortium coordination. Our system is selfcontained, field-ready within days of agreement, and generates minimal operational burden for the consortium coordinator. Deployment, operation, and data delivery are handled entirely by our team.

Ideal coordinators include research institutions, environmental modelling groups, or RIA-experienced organisations with an identified gap in ground-truth data from hard-to-reach ecosystems.

candidate.description_text: The DEEP-MED project introduces a decentralized, community-led marine monitoring paradigm to address severe sub-mesophotic biodiversity loss in the Mediterranean. The initiative upgrades and deploys Edge-AI powered ROV/BRUV systems capable of functioning as static, long-term baited cameras at depths up to 1000 meters. Rather than relying on expensive research vessels, local NGOs, fishery cooperatives, and diver networks will independently deploy these systems from small artisanal boats. The integrated AI automatically processes massive deep-sea video datasets locally on the device. It filters hours of footage to generate Marine Strategy Framework Directive (MSFD)-compliant biodiversity metrics and track invasive species in near real-time. The verified ecological data feeds directly into a "Biodiversity Dialogue Platform," empowering local authorities to convert grassroots data into officially signed Evidence-Based Action Plans and Marine Protected Area (MPA) expansions. The core consortium currently includes Karadeniz Technical University (Coordinator), Degz Robotik (Technology Provider), Akdeniz Koruma Derneği (Community Mobilization), Democritus University of Thrace (Regional Scale-up), and FORENSOFT (an Ankara-based SME bringing deep expertise in Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, large-scale data processing, and IoT integration).
candidate.technical_problem_evidence_text: To meet the large-scale demonstration requirements of the Mission Ocean 2026 calls, the consortium is seeking partners with the following profiles: Flagship Marine Research Institute: Top-tier deep-sea or marine-biodiversity institutes from high-R&D Mediterranean states (e.g., France, Italy, Spain) to add scientific weight and operate a Western/Central-Med pilot site. Small-Scale & Recreational Fisher Organisations: Fisher associations and cooperatives in additional Mediterranean countries to co-design and operate the AI-BRUVs on the ground. Coastal Municipalities & Regional Environmental Authorities: Public authorities functioning as end-users who will utilize the data for MSFD reporting and sign Evidence-Based Action Plans. South-Mediterranean Partner: Entities from Tunisia or Egypt to prove basin-wide, cross-border replication for North-South diffusion. Blue-Economy SME / Port Operator: Early adopters for underwater infrastructure inspection and predictive maintenance to validate OPEX savings. Data/Digital-Twin-Ocean Partner: Experts capable of connecting localized Edge-AI datasets to the EU Digital Twin of the Ocean (DTO), Copernicus, and EMODnet under FAIR data principles.
candidate.title: A Turkish-led consortium seeks partners for AI-supported deep-sea biodiversity monitoring and community-based marine conservation

candidate.description_text: The company is a Turkish software SME, is preparing an IraSME R&D project around a Windows desktop application for privacy-preserving PC performance optimization. The product addresses a common and measurable problem for consumers, SMEs and managed device fleets: Windows PCs gradually lose performance and energy efficiency because of unnecessary startup processes, redundant background activity, fragmented workloads, temporary/cache accumulation, resource-heavy update loops and heterogeneous hardware/software behaviour. Existing clean-up and tune-up tools are often static, generic, cloud-dependent or insufficiently transparent, which creates safety and trust concerns. The planned R&D project aims to move the product from a mature local optimization prototype towards an experimentally validated, energy-aware AI optimization system. The technical work will focus on local system-health interpretation, anomaly/deviation detection, safe action scoring, human-in-the-loop recommendations, rollback-aware optimization and repeatable before/after measurement of performance and resource indicators. The software is designed to process device health and performance signals locally, without requiring user files or personal content to be sent to the cloud. Optional telemetry, if used in pilots, will be aggregated and anonymized. The project will include experimental development up to prototype/pilot level. Main R&D activities are expected to include: (1) definition of a cross-device benchmark protocol for startup time, CPU/RAM pressure, disk I/O, freeze/crash indicators, optimization duration and energy/resource indicators; (2) improvement of the local AI decision layer for contextual scoring of safe optimization actions; (3) development of an energy-aware evaluation model that links reduced redundant background activity to measurable or estimated kWh/CO2 indicators; (4) implementation of safer policy boundaries, exclusion lists, quarantine/restore logic and signed update/model bundle validation; and (5) real-world validation on Windows 10/11 devices in SME or comparable operational environments. The work involves significant technical risks. Windows environments vary widely by hardware, installed software, user behavior, security policies and administrator rights. It is technically challenging to distinguish optimization opportunities from actions that could affect stability, user workflows or device security. Energy/resource savings must also be measured or estimated in a defensible way, avoiding exaggerated claims. The project will therefore use constrained safe actions, transparent recommendations, rollback mechanisms and repeatable tests to validate technical feasibility. We are seeking one R&D partner from an IraSME participating country/region to form the minimum transnational consortium with the company in Türkiye. The partner should complement with technical validation capacity, endpoint management expertise, AI/software engineering, energy-efficiency measurement, SME pilot access or applied research capability. The exact workshare can be adapted to national funding rules and partner strengths. The intended result is a validated prototype and pilot evidence package for a privacy-first, energy-aware AI PC optimization product that can later scale through direct software licensing, SME support channels and managed fleet deployments.
candidate.technical_problem_evidence_text: We are seeking one R&D partner from Austria, Brazil, Czech Republic, Flanders (Belgium), Germany, Luxembourg, or Wallonia (Belgium) for the IraSME 38th call. The planned project budget is EUR 325,000. The preferred partner role is independent validation, benchmarking and pilot deployment. The Turkish company will remain responsible for the core product’s AI optimization engine, product runtime, licensing layer and main product integration. The partner will complement this with an external R&D validation layer that makes the project technically stronger and commercially more credible. Expected partner tasks may include: defining a Windows endpoint benchmark protocol; testing CPU, RAM, disk I/O, startup time, freeze/crash indicators and optimization duration; developing or validating the kWh/CO2 measurement model; checking safety constraints, rollback logic and exclusion policies; running SME or institutional pilot tests; collecting structured user/admin feedback; and preparing an independent validation report. This work is technically meaningful because Windows devices differ widely by hardware, installed software, security policies and user behaviour. The partner will help prove that the product can optimize safely across heterogeneous environments without exposing personal data or destabilizing critical workflows. We are also open to complementary ideas from the partner, provided they fit the project scope and national funding rules. Possible additions include endpoint security validation, managed-service-provider deployment scenarios, fleet dashboard benchmarking, energy-efficiency methodology, on-premise deployment testing, or sector-specific pilots in SMEs, education, healthcare, public sector or industrial environments. The ideal partner is not only a dissemination or sales partner, but an active R&D contributor with expertise in software testing, endpoint management, energy/resource-efficiency measurement, AI/software validation, cybersecurity, managed IT services or applied research. The final workshare can be adapted to the partner’s strengths, but the intended outcome is clear: The Turkish company delivers the core AI optimization product, while the partner delivers independent validation, benchmark evidence and pilot credibility.

candidate.description_text: Pomegranate processing generates large volumes of by-products (peel, seeds, membranes) that are rich in bioactive compounds polyphenols, punicalagins, ellagic acid, and anthocyanins with proven antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and skin-health properties. Conventional extraction methods (solvent-based, thermal) are often energy-intensive, environmentally burdensome, and can degrade sensitive bioactives. Our project proposes a hydrodynamic cavitation-based extraction process as a green, scalable alternative for recovering high-value bioactives from pomegranate waste streams. The technology has been tested at lab scale, demonstrating high potential for enhanced extraction performance and reduced solvent/energy use compared to conventional methods. The applicant SME is preparing a Eurostars application (Call deadline: March 2027) and is looking to build an international consortium to: ● Scale up and optimize the hydrodynamic cavitation process for industrial application; ● Validate extracted bioactives for formulation in food (functional ingredients, natural antioxidants/preservatives) and cosmetic (skincare, anti-aging actives) end-products; ● Support regulatory, safety, and stability assessment of the extracts; ● Pilot/demonstrate the process at a relevant scale with industrial partners.
candidate.technical_problem_evidence_text: 1. Industrial partners (food and/or cosmetic manufacturers) interested in incorporating natural pomegranate-derived bioactive ingredients into their product lines, and able to support formulation, testing, and market validation. 2. Academic / R&D institutions with expertise in extraction technologies, phytochemical characterization, bioactive compound analysis, or food/cosmetic formulation science. 3. Equipment / technology providers in cavitation, extraction, or process engineering equipment, able to support process scale-up.

candidate.description_text: 1. Project Context & ObjectivesWe are forming a consortium to submit a proposal for the upcoming Horizon Europe (BATT4EU Partnership) call. Our objective is to revolutionize Sodium-Ion Battery (SIB) technology by shifting from fossil-based materials to sustainable, circular, and high-performance bio-based alternatives.The project aims to develop high-performance electrode architectures by synergizing three key pillars: Fungal Mycelium & Hemp Applications: 1-Transforming fungal mycelium and industrial hemp residues into high-performance hierarchical porous carbon skeletons.  Quinone-based Redox-Active Materials: Integrating these carbon matrices with bio-sourced redox-active molecules (specifically quinone derivatives).  Interface Engineering: Utilizing covalent "grafting" (aşılanma) methodologies to anchor quinone molecules onto bio-carbon, thereby addressing fundamental limitations such as low electrical conductivity and electrolyte solubility. 2. Technical InnovationThe project circumvents common degradation pathways (such as dimerization or Michael addition) often found in organic battery materials. By using a covalently functionalized bio-carbon approach, we ensure long-term cyclability and energy density comparable to state-of-the-art organic systems. We provide a circular economy solution that aligns with the EU Green Deal by utilizing low-cost bio-precursors (hemp, mycelium) and sustainable, green processing techniques. 3. Seeking PartnersWe are actively seeking consortium partners (universities, research centers, or industrial SMEs) with specific expertise in:Bio-Carbon Processing: Expertise in carbonization/activation of hemp and mycelium-based precursors for energy applications.  Quinone Electrochemistry: Deep knowledge of quinone-based redox-active molecules and their practical application as electrode materials in Na-ion batteries.  Electrochemical Interface & Stability: Researchers skilled in characterizing quinone-carbon interfaces, managing degradation pathways (e.g., disproportionation, tautomerization), and long-term cycling stability validation.  Battery Prototyping & Sustainability: Partners capable of full-cell assembly, high-rate performance testing, and Life Cycle Assessment (LCA). 4. Expertise/Assets OfferedExpertise in the valorization of hemp and mycelium into advanced energy storage materials.  Methodology for covalent surface modification of bio-carbon with quinone derivatives.  Strong background in SIB electrochemistry and aqueous electrolyte optimization.  International project coordination and industrial network support
candidate.technical_problem_evidence_text: We are seeking partners (R&D centers, universities, and industrial SMEs) with specific expertise to collaborate on the development of next-generation bio-based Sodium-Ion Battery (SIB) materials for the Horizon Europe (BATT4EU) call. The ideal partner should contribute expertise in the following domains:Bio-Carbon Processing: Expertise in sustainable carbonization, activation, and structural characterization of bio-precursors (industrial hemp, fungal mycelium, seaweed) to engineer hierarchical porous carbon skeletons with high surface area and optimal pore-size distribution.  Quinone Electrochemistry: Technical mastery of the redox chemistry of quinone-based pendant groups. Expertise in tuning the redox potential of quinones to match the conducting region of the carbon matrix, and managing pH-dependent PCET (Proton-Coupled Electron Transfer) processes.  Interface Engineering & Degradation Mitigation: Proven capability in characterizing and stabilizing the carbon-electrolyte interface. Expertise is required to mitigate specific degradation pathways such as disproportionation, nucleophilic substitution, Michael addition, and tautomerization that currently limit the lifespan of anthraquinone-based electrodes.  Battery Prototyping & Validation: Capability to perform full-cell assembly, high-rate electrochemical performance testing (e.g., GCD, CV, EIS), and long-term cycling stability assessments in aqueous alkaline/acidic electrolytes.  LCA & Sustainability: Industrial partners or research groups capable of performing Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) to validate the "environmentally benign" footprint of our production process, from biomass refining to end-of-life recycling.  We prioritize partners who can demonstrate a TRL (Technology Readiness Level) advancement potential, aiming to bridge the gap between bench-scale bio-material development and scalable, industrial battery-grade electrode production

candidate.description_text: Established in Gaziantep, Xloop Interactive is a technology studio that transforms complex data into high-interaction digital experiences. The company has a proven track record in developing proprietary B2B solutions, including map-based spatial management systems and real-time digital twin platforms tailored for heavy industry and machinery manufacturers.Building on its extensive expertise in 3D visualization and industrial digitization, Xloop is initiating a new R&D project named "SafeGuard". In heavy industry, traditional OSH training heavily relies on static physical or digital sign-off sheets. During workplace accident litigations, these sheets fail to provide non-repudiation in court, as workers often claim a lack of cognitive comprehension regarding the hazards. To solve this, SafeGuard replaces standard training with interactive 3D simulations running directly on blue-collar workers' personal smartphones via a BYOD architecture. Xloop provides the optimized Unity-based industrial hazard environments and the domain content, which already includes 47 verified heavy-industry hazard scenarios validated through a pilot phase. To finalize the product for the European market, Xloop is seeking a specialized SME partner to handle the digital forensics/cybersecurity aspects or the EU legal compliance algorithms.
candidate.technical_problem_evidence_text: We are seeking an SME with expertise in either Cybersecurity/Digital Forensics to develop a zero-trust, automated verification pipeline for high-volume dynamic video telemetry, OR an SME specializing in European OSH Compliance & Risk Engineering to create an automated legal-compliance translation engine for spatial training data.

candidate.description_text: The client is a Turkish deep-tech small and medium-sized enterprise (SME) specialised in teleradiology and medical-imaging software. The purpose of the proposed project is applied research and development (R&D) to create three novel technologies that do not yet exist on the market and are currently at concept / early-prototype stage. Innovation 1 — voice/audio analysis for radiology reporting: an automatic transcription and intelligent-reporting engine that converts a radiologist’s dictated speech into a structured report. The research aims to adapt speech-to-text to medical and radiological terminology (with strong Turkish-language performance), map spoken findings to structured report templates, correctly capture measurements and values (e.g. Hounsfield units, millimetres), and support a human-in-the-loop review and correction loop. It is currently at early-prototype stage. Innovation 2 — a federated, privacy-preserving artificial-intelligence method for medicalimage reading. The research aims to develop models that learn the normal appearance of studies per examination type with very high sensitivity, so that normal studies can be safely de-prioritised and scarce radiologist time is focused on suspect cases. Training would be distributed across institutions (cross-silo federated learning): each hospital’s data remains a local silo and only model parameters are exchanged, so no images or patient records ever leave the institution (aligned with the General Data Protection Regulation, GDPR, and the European Health Data Space, EHDS). Innovation 3 — a native medical-image compression codec written in a single modern programming language, without dependence on legacy third-party libraries, to improve cost, performance and cross-platform (edge) deployment. No production-ready native equivalent currently exists on the market; this involves genuine technical uncertainty and research. Foundation for the research (not the object of funding): the client already operates a teleradiology platform deployed across a network of more than 70 hospitals. This deployment is the real-world validation environment for the new technologies and provides the potential to build an extensive, weakly-labelled clinical dataset (radiology reports linked to imaging studies and examination codes) for training and validation. The funded work is the development of the new technologies above, not the existing platform. The client seeks consortium partners for European collaborative R&D programmes Eureka eurostars, Ira SME. Cooperation is envisaged as a research and development cooperation agreement within a multi-partner consortium.

candidate.description_text: KAF Dynamics is an R&D-focused technology company located in the Istanbul Technopark region of Türkiye. The company develops high-power unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), avionics architectures, embedded software, flight control solutions, sensor integration, and mission systems. DUHAN Project, to be applied to Eureka, will develop and operationally validate a hose-fed aerial firefighting system for high-rise buildings, industrial facilities, refineries, ports and other hard-to-access fire scenarios. The UAV will be supplied from a fire engine or fixed firefighting infrastructure, eliminating the need to carry extinguishing water on board. The system is intended to operate under hose tension, water-jet recoil, gusts, thermal updrafts, smoke and degraded GNSS conditions. The proposed international project builds on an ongoing nationally supported R&D programme and will constitute a clearly separated scaling, validation and commercial deployment phase. The Eureka project is planned to start at TRL 6 and reach TRL 9 through integrated prototype maturation, operational field demonstrations, European validation, product safety engineering, manufacturability improvements and pre-commercial deployment. Core technical workstreams: • Active compensation of hose tension, oscillation, whipping and water-jet recoil through adaptive and feed-forward flight control. • Intelligent ground-based hose management unit with controlled hose payout/retrieval, tension monitoring and emergency shut-off. • Smart nozzle, flow and pressure control integrated with UAV attitude and target-point control. • Thermal/RGB/LiDAR or radar sensor fusion, fire-scene mapping and AI-supported target prioritisation. • Safe navigation near façades and in smoke or degraded-GNSS environments, including fail-safe mission logic. • Operational demonstration with fire brigades or industrial emergency-response users and preparation for market deployment. KAF Dynamics will lead • Heavy-lift UAV architecture, avionics and power distribution • Flight dynamics, hose-force estimation and adaptive stabilisation • Mechanical, electronic and software system integration • Prototype manufacturing and flight-test programme in Türkiye • Commercial product architecture and international market entry
candidate.technical_problem_evidence_text: We seek an R&D-performing company from a Eureka participating country, preferably Austria, Belgium (Flanders) or Spain, with one or more of the following capabilities: Firefighting equipment and hose systems: Develop the intelligent hose-management unit, high-pressure interfaces, emergency shut-off and field integration. Remote-controlled monitors / smart nozzles: Develop controllable nozzle geometry, flow/pressure regulation and recoil-aware targeting interfaces. Thermal imaging, LiDAR/radar or perception AI: Develop and integrate robust fire-scene perception, 3D mapping, hotspot detection or target prioritisation. Emergency-response robotics and field validation: Contribute hazardous-environment know-how, safety engineering, pilot demonstrations and access to end users.
candidate.title: Partner Search for the Eureka Disaster Resilience Call 2026: AI-Assisted Hose-Fed Aerial Firefighting System for High-Rise and Industrial Fires Project

candidate.description_text: Traditional call center and voice customer service platforms heavily rely on complex cloud infrastructures, internet-based call routing, and high operating costs. This creates a significant barrier for Small and Medium-sized Enterprises (SMEs) seeking to automate customer interaction efficiently. To bridge this gap, this project aims to develop an innovative, accessible, and highly scalable customer support platform that integrates custom embedded hardware directly with telecommunication networks and real-time Artificial Intelligence (AI). Project Scope & Coordinator's Role: Under the targeted Eureka Network Projects call, our company will act as the project coordinator and lead partner. Leveraging our dual expertise in software development, AI, and electronics engineering, our primary responsibilities include: Hardware & Electronics: Designing electronic hardware, developing custom PCBs, and manufacturing prototypes for a dedicated GSM communication module. Architecture & Infrastructure: Engineering the overall hardware-software system architecture and establishing robust telecommunication protocols. Core Software Development: Developing the primary software platform for the AI-driven virtual customer representative. Integration & Testing: Performing full system integration, optimizing hardware-software interactions, executing prototype validation, and managing technical preparations for pilot deployments. Role & Requirements for the Sought Partner: We are seeking an international R&D partner (University, Research Institute, or SME) with deep expertise in speech processing and conversational AI to take ownership of the advanced natural language work packages. The partner will be responsible for: Developing, fine-tuning, and optimizing Speech-to-Text (STT), Large Language Models (LLM), Natural Language Processing (NLP), and Text-to-Speech (TTS) models tailored for real-time voice scenarios. Collaborating closely on integrating these AI modules into the GSM-based hardware and core software ecosystem. Providing technical support during laboratory testing, performance benchmark analysis, and real-world pilot applications across various SME use cases.
candidate.technical_problem_evidence_text: Required Expertise & Technical Profile: The sought partner (University, R&D Institution, or SME) should possess strong technical capabilities and proven R&D experience in the following domains:  Speech & Language AI Technologies: Core expertise in Speech-to-Text (STT), Large Language Models (LLM), Natural Language Processing (NLP), and Text-to-Speech (TTS) systems.  Model Optimization & Fine-Tuning: Demonstrated ability in fine-tuning, compressing, and optimizing generative AI/LLM models for low-latency, real-time voice communication applications.  System Integration Support: Technical capacity to integrate conversational AI software components into custom-designed hardware and core backend frameworks.  Validation & Testing Capabilities: Infrastructure and technical expertise to conduct laboratory testing, performance benchmarking, model evaluation, and technical support during pilot deployments across diverse SME operational scenarios.

candidate.description_text: Established in 2019 and based in Mersin Technopark, the Turkish SME develops scalable solutions in web and mobile applications, artificial intelligence, machine learning, cybersecurity, data processing and system integration. The company is developing Lipyum – Autonomous Service Intelligence Platform, an AI-based solution that understands customer service requests expressed in natural language, identifies the likely type and scope of the required service, determines the necessary skills and recommends the most suitable service provider by considering operational constraints and the probability of successful service delivery. The platform integrates several AI-driven components within a common data architecture: AI Diagnosis: Extracting the likely service/repair type, scope and required skills from customer requests expressed in everyday language. Intelligent Matching: Matching customers with suitable service providers based on problem type, location, skills, historical performance, price, availability, capacity, cancellation probability and user behaviour. Demand Prediction: Forecasting service demand according to geographical area and time. Learning Decision Engine: Optimising supply-demand-capacity balance and the number of candidates presented to users. AI User Assistant: Asking complementary questions to clarify incomplete service requests and improve the quality of matching. The company will act as the project coordinator and technology provider, responsible for the common data model and system architecture, web/mobile applications, integration of AI services, cybersecurity and traceability layers, pilot implementations and productisation of the results. A preliminary application, mobile concept, sector-specific question sets and initial architecture have already been prepared. The international R&D cooperation will focus on further model development, comparative experiments, validation and testing across multiple sectors and countries. Partner Sought The consortium is looking for: Universities and research institutions R&D centres and research institutes Innovative SMEs with relevant AI/R&D expertise Potential partners should have strong expertise in at least one of the following areas: Applied Artificial Intelligence Multilingual Natural Language Processing (NLP) Information extraction Recommendation and ranking systems Time-series based demand forecasting Safe offline reinforcement learning Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) Partners are expected to contribute to the development of anonymised field-service datasets and data-labeling methodologies, development of reference models, comparative experiments, and validation of performance, fairness and safety criteria. Partners with access to real users, service-provider networks or pilot environments in technical services, maintenance and repair, home services or other professional service sectors are particularly welcome. The selected partner will contribute to the model development and validation work package and work closely with the Turkish company's platform team on system integration and field pilots.
candidate.technical_problem_evidence_text: Expertise in applied artificial intelligence, multilingual natural language processing (NLP), information extraction, recommendation and ranking systems, time-series based demand forecasting, safe offline reinforcement learning and/or explainable AI (XAI). Experience in developing and validating AI/ML models, dataset preparation and labelling, comparative experiments, and evaluation of model performance, fairness, safety and explainability is sought. Experience with field service, maintenance, repair, home services or professional service applications and access to relevant real-world data or pilot environments would be an advantage
candidate.title: R&D partners sought for an AI-powered autonomous service intelligence platform for field service management

candidate.description_text: A Turkish technology-oriented SME established in 2021 and based in Mersin Technopark is developing Beatify – AI Song Generation and Audio Intelligence, an innovative platform for controllable AI-based music and song generation. The project aims to develop an end-to-end artificial intelligence system capable of generating original songs based on natural-language prompts, lyrics, genre, mood, tempo, key, instrumentation and reference style inputs. The proposed system will integrate lyric and theme analysis, melody, harmony, rhythm and arrangement generation, singing voice synthesis, instrumental audio generation, style and voice-character control, and source separation within a unified generative music workflow. The Turkish SME will act as project coordinator and technology provider, leading the development of the common data and rights management architecture, Turkish lyric/text processing layer, cloud and GPU integration of generative models, web-based platform, APIs, security and traceability components, and pilot applications. A particular research focus will be placed on Turkish lyrics, syllable-stress-prosody alignment and the rhythmic and modal characteristics of local music genres. Users will be able to control genre, mood, tempo, key, duration, instrumentation and vocal characteristics, while generated musical layers can be regenerated and edited. Rights-cleared data, explicit permissions for reference audio, data/output provenance and AI-generated content labelling will be incorporated into the system design.
candidate.technical_problem_evidence_text: The project is seeking a university, research institute or innovative SME with strong R&D expertise in one or more of the following areas: Generative music and audio AI Music Information Retrieval (MIR) and computational musicology Audio tokenisation and neural audio codecs Transformer- or diffusion-based text-to-music and text-to-song generation Symbolic music modelling Singing voice synthesis and vocal transformation Melody, harmony, rhythm and arrangement generation Lyric-melody-prosody alignment, particularly for multilingual music generation The partner should have experience in developing, testing or validating AI-based music and audio models and be able to contribute to rights-cleared datasets, data annotation, benchmarking and comparative experiments. Expertise in evaluating musical coherence, prompt adherence, originality, audio quality and copyright/permission compliance is also sought. Partners with access to music studios, professional musicians, record labels, digital content platforms or other creative-industry networks are particularly welcome to support international pilot activities.

candidate.description_text: A Turkish SME is seeking international R&D partners for Horizon Europe, Eureka, Eurostars and similar collaborative funding programmes in the field of advanced additive manufacturing and industrial product development. The company aims to contribute to R&D projects as an industrial additive manufacturing, demonstrator production and process development partner. Its capabilities include Large-Format Additive Manufacturing (LFAM), HP Multi Jet Fusion (MJF), Fused Deposition Modelling (FDM), SLA, reverse engineering, design optimisation, Design for Additive Manufacturing (DfAM), post-processing coordination, CNC finishing coordination through its partner network, and prototype-to-pilot production workflows. One key R&D focus is LFAM-based production of large-scale tooling, moulds, plugs, patterns, fixtures and demonstrators for composite and polymer applications. Possible products or demonstrators may include wind turbine blade moulds or plugs, composite tooling for large shell structures, unmanned aerial or marine vehicle body components, simulator and cabin components, automotive or mobility panels, architectural or public-use elements, large industrial models, jigs and fixtures, and selected end-use polymer or composite parts where material and process requirements are suitable. LFAM may be combined with CNC finishing, surface preparation, coating or sealing strategies to achieve the required dimensional accuracy and surface quality. A second focus is the development of functional polymer components using HP Multi Jet Fusion, FDM and related additive manufacturing technologies. Potential R&D topics may include lightweight drone and UAV components, mobility parts, housings, brackets, assembly components, low-volume end-use parts, functional prototypes, design iterations and validation parts. The SME is particularly interested in projects where additive manufacturing can reduce development time, enable part consolidation, support lightweight design or provide a scalable route from prototype to small- or medium-volume production. A third focus is the integration of sustainable materials, DfAM, testing and validation into additive manufacturing workflows. The company is open to projects involving recycled or bio-based polymer materials, fibre-reinforced compounds, material-process trials, mechanical testing, durability assessment, life cycle assessment (LCA), circularity, digital traceability and industrial validation. The SME can also facilitate access to local material development and compounding partners in Turkey, as well as academic expertise, testing facilities and laboratory infrastructure. The Turkish SME is looking for partners with complementary expertise in materials, design, simulation, testing, end-user applications, system integration, certification, LCA, circular economy and market deployment. Expected outcomes of such collaborations may include validated demonstrators, improved manufacturing processes, application-specific additive manufacturing workflows, new lightweight or functional components, and project results suitable for further industrial adoption.

candidate.description_text: A Turkey-based consortium is currently preparing a project proposal in response to the DIGITAL-2026-AI-PILOTING-10-SCREENING call for proposals, launched under the European Union’s Digital Europe Program. The project aims to implement and validate, across multiple centers throughout Europe, an AI-based dermatology screening and patient monitoring platform developed to support the early diagnosis of dermatological diseases, particularly skin cancers. The proposed solution consists of an integrated digital health platform that includes: •    A portable dermoscopic imaging device, •    A cloud-based artificial intelligence analysis infrastructure, •    A clinical decision support system, •    Patient follow-up and long-term monitoring modules, •    Integration layers with hospital information systems. The platform has already reached the prototype stage, and as part of the project, multicenter validation and roll-out activities will be conducted in real clinical settings. Current Consortium Expertise The following areas of expertise are represented within the consortium: •    Development of artificial intelligence and digital health technologies •    Medical image analysis •    Dermatology expertise •    Clinical research and validation •    Hospital pilot programs •    Health economics and cost-effectiveness analysis •    Commercialization and impact assessment Expected Impact The project aims to contribute to the following objectives: •    Early diagnosis of skin cancers and dermatological diseases •    Increasing efficiency in dermatology services •    Widespread adoption of AI-supported clinical decision-making

candidate.description_text: The Austrian SME, founded in 2012, develops innovative technologies for surface functionalization, with a particular focus on the metallization of technical substrates. Together with their partners, they can draw on many years of experience in plasma technology, systems engineering and production automation. A key area of application is the functionalization of aluminum surfaces to make them suitable for subsequent soldering processes, such as those used in the electronics and printed circuit board industries. This makes it possible to replace the conventionally used copper with aluminum, which is cheaper and much lighter. The Austrian company already has established market access to the electronics industry and specifically targets applications in the fields of printed circuit boards, electronic assemblies, and innovative connection technologies. As part of the further development of this technology, the SME is now seeking industrial partners with experience in etching aluminum structures, such as those typically found in printed circuit boards and electronic assemblies.
candidate.technical_problem_evidence_text: Potential partners could include, for example: •    manufacturers of chemicals for aluminum etching •    chemical processors or process service providers for aluminum etching •    equipment manufacturers with expertise in etching and inline processing Ideally, partners should come from the following fields: •    etching of formed parts, •    spray etching of fine metal structures, •    or continuous inline etching processes for metallic materials. The Austrian SME is looking for partners who: •    can provide suitable etching chemicals and process chemicals, •    possess in-depth expertise in etching processes and integration into industrial manufacturing processes, •    actively support joint technological development, •    and are interested in the subsequent joint marketing of the technology in the printed circuit board and electronics markets. Of particular importance is a process chemistry that can be implemented as simply, reliably, and cost-effectively as possible on existing etching lines in the electronics industry or on lines modified with minimal effort.
candidate.title: Austrian SME is seeking industrial partners in the field of aluminum etching

Together with their partners, they can draw on many years of experience in plasma technology, systems engineering and production automation. A key area of application is the functionalization of aluminum surfaces to make them suitable for subsequent soldering processes, such as those used in the electronics and printed circuit board industries. This makes it possible to replace the conventionally used copper with aluminum, which is cheaper and much lighter. The Austrian company already has established market access to the electronics industry and specifically targets applications in the fields of printed circuit boards, electronic assemblies, and innovative connection technologies. As part of the further development of this technology, the SME is now seeking industrial partners with experience in etching aluminum structures, such as those typically found in printed circuit boards and electronic assemblies.
technical_problem_evidence_text: Potential partners could include, for example: •    manufacturers of chemicals for aluminum etching •    chemical processors or process service providers for aluminum etching •    equipment manufacturers with expertise in etching and inline processing Ideally, partners should come from the following fields: •    etching of formed parts, •    spray etching of fine metal structures, •    or continuous inline etching processes for metallic materials. The Austrian SME is looking for partners who: •    can provide suitable etching chemicals and process chemicals, •    possess in-depth expertise in etching processes and integration into industrial manufacturing processes, •    actively support joint technological development, •    and are interested in the subsequent joint marketing of the technology in the printed circuit board and electronics markets. Of particular importance is a process chemistry that can be implemented as simply, reliably, and cost-effectively as possible on existing etching lines in the electronics industry or on lines modified with minimal effort.
title: Austrian SME is seeking industrial partners in the field of aluminum etching

candidate.description_text: An Austrian company operating in the field of sustainable timber construction is developing next-generation building systems based on prefabricated timber panels. To further improve the environmental performance, circularity and adaptability of its construction solutions, the company is seeking an innovative connection technology for joining structural timber elements. Current fastening and connection solutions often require compromises between structural performance, ease of assembly, material health and circularity. The company is therefore looking for a novel connection concept that can simultaneously address these requirements while remaining suitable for industrial production and large-scale construction applications. The requested technology should enable the connection of timber wall, roof and floor elements in load-bearing applications. The solution should support modern industrial prefabrication processes and facilitate efficient on-site assembly, maintenance and future building modifications. The company is particularly interested in technologies that support circular construction principles through reversible and non-destructive disassembly, enabling multiple use cycles and preserving the value of building components and materials throughout their lifecycle. Potential cooperation may involve adaptation of an existing technology, co-development of a new connection system, testing and validation activities, material optimisation or industrial implementation. The company is open to commercial agreements with technical assistance as well as research and development cooperation agreements.
candidate.technical_problem_evidence_text: The company seeks a future-proof connection system designed according to open-building and circular-construction principles, ensuring long-term adaptability, interoperability and material innovation readiness. The sought technology should fulfil the following functional requirements: •	Suitable for structural timber construction applications. •	Enables connections between wall, roof and floor elements. •	Capable of transferring vertical, horizontal and dynamic loads. •	High mechanical strength and long-term durability. •	Suitable for repeated assembly and disassembly cycles. •	Compatible with industrial prefabrication processes. •	Facilitates rapid installation, maintenance and replacement. •	Supports future extensions, modifications and adaptive reuse of buildings. Material-related requirements include: •	Use of recyclable materials. •	Preference for PFAS-free solutions. •	Compliance with REACH regulations. •	Absence of substances of very high concern (SVHC). •	Efficient material use with low material intensity. •	High corrosion resistance. •	Long service life. •	Possibility to integrate bio-based materials or components. •	Low-emission materials supporting indoor air quality. •	Low VOC emissions and minimisation of hazardous substances. •	Consideration of human health criteria aligned with sustainability certification systems such as DGNB, Cradle-to-Cradle and LEED. Circular economy requirements include: •	Non-destructive disassembly. •	Multiple reuse cycles without significant performance loss. •	Easy separation of materials at end-of-life. •	Support for pure material streams and high-quality recycling. •	Preservation of material value throughout the lifecycle. •	Compatibility with cradle-to-cradle design principles. •	Potential integration into take-back systems. •	Facilitation of secondary markets and remanufacturing of building components. System-level requirements: •	Enable compatibility across multiple generations of building systems, from existing solutions (Generation 1) to future developments (Generation X). •	Ensure backward compatibility with previously deployed panel systems and connection concepts. •	Support standardized and interoperable interfaces to facilitate integration across different manufacturers, suppliers and construction systems. •	Enable modular extensions and upgrades throughout the building lifecycle. •	Allow integration of future material innovations, including emerging bio-based, recycled or advanced engineered materials. •	Accommodate different panel configurations, dimensions and assembly concepts without requiring fundamental redesign of the connection system. •	Support adaptable building designs and evolving construction requirements over time. •	Facilitate long-term system scalability while maintaining structural integrity and ease of assembly.
candidate.title: Austrian construction company seeks circular and demountable connection technology for load-bearing timber panel systems

candidate.description_text: The Austrian deep-tech startup (a university spin-off) builds on more than 25 years of expertise in electrolysers and fuel cells. The company specialises in developing and manufacturing cutting-edge Membrane Electrode Assembly (MEA) technology that powers the hydrogen economy. In line with its activities in the development and production of electrochemical energy components, the startup is looking for European partners with roll-to-roll manufacturing capacity. The company develops membrane electrode components used in anion exchange membrane water electrolysis and proton exchange membrane fuel cells. These components include catalyst-coated membranes, catalyst-coated substrates and membrane electrode assemblies. The company currently builds its processes at laboratory and pilot scale and has access to a roll-to-roll pilot line for process validation and medium-volume production. After this validation step, external manufacturing capacity will be needed for larger and more regular production volumes. The purpose of this partner search is therefore to assess the availability of suitable European manufacturing capacity, including which capabilities are available, what technical limitations apply, and how cooperation could be structured. The external manufacturing need is expected from 2028 onwards. The required technology is roll-to-roll slot-die coating and related downstream processing for thin functional catalyst layers on flexible and, where possible, porous substrates. The preferred partner should be able to support not only coating but also drying, web handling, lamination, cutting or stamping, integration of gasket or subgasket materials, quality control, documentation and packaging. The expected production capacity is up to around 5,000 m² per year, depending on product mix and successful process transfer. The company is seeking cooperation with European industrial partners that already operate suitable roll-to-roll coating or converting lines, ideally with experience in functional coatings, electrochemical components, membranes, catalyst inks, fuel cells, electrolysers, batteries, sensors, printed electronics or comparable thin-film products. The minimum useful coating width is 300 mm; a width up to 800 mm would be ideal. Detailed coating formulations, layer structures, product drawings, process windows and customer-related specifications are confidential and would only be shared under a non-disclosure agreement and after an initial technical fit assessment. Cooperation could start with capability discussions and non-confidential process mapping, continue with feasibility trials and pilot campaigns, and later move into recurring manufacturing. The preferred cooperation types are an outsourcing agreement, a supplier agreement and, where process transfer or adaptation is needed, a commercial agreement with technical assistance.
candidate.technical_problem_evidence_text: The partner should be a European company, contract manufacturer or coating specialist operating roll-to-roll slot-die coating and converting equipment. The partner should first provide a non-confidential overview of its available line widths, coating technologies, compatible substrates, drying and lamination options, quality control methods, typical campaign sizes, available capacity and experience with functional coatings.
candidate.title: Seeking roll-to-roll slot-die manufacturing capacity for electrochemical membrane electrode components

candidate.description_text: Brussels-based energy technology company providing modular first-life LFP BESS together with a proprietary EMS and cloud analytics platform. The solution combines an integrated battery-and-energy management architecture with continuous monitoring and digital-twin-based analytics to optimize performance, reliability, and lifetime. Up to February 2026, 80 MW of smart-controlled flexible assets and manages 150 MWh of battery storage capacity, reflecting strong growth and a rapidly expanding position in the flexibility and storage market were operated by the company. Research is a core pillar of their activities to stay aligned with state-of-the-art methods and to shape future products based on market needs and emerging technologies. They are active in European (e.g., Horizon) and national R&D projects and focus on State-of-X topics (SoC/SoH), lifetime and Remaining Useful Life modelling and advanced EMS control for more efficient multi-asset power flow. Main products & services offered: • Hardware product: Modular Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS) for the C&I segment ranging from 100 kWh to 5 MWh. •	Services o	Battery Care 	Detailed remote monitoring and automated alerting 	Troubleshooting in case of issues with the Battery System 	Warranty management o	Energy Management System (EMS) 	Self-consumption optimization 	Peak shaving 	Market arbitrage (day-ahead and imbalance markets) 	Grid services 	Value stacking of different applications
candidate.technical_problem_evidence_text: Seeking industry partners and research centers to collaborate on its R&D roadmap and accelerate next-generation BESS and EMS innovation. Collaboration topics include improved State-of-X (SoC/SoH) estimation accuracy, lifetime and Remaining Useful Life modelling, and integration of these models into EMS optimization algorithms. The SME also aims to co-develop forecasting and smart control capabilities, including weather-condition–based forecasting, household consumption mapping, and AI-based control to optimize multi-asset power flow more efficiently.
candidate.title: Belgian energy technology company developing advanced BESS and intelligent EMS is seeking industry and research partners to advance next-generation battery management and control systems.

candidate.description_text: This Belgian chocolate manufacturer has a long history behind its today's production, with longstanding expertise and craftmanship in every stage of chocolate making. They produce high-quality fine chocolates for branded manufacturers and for private labels and have built their reputation and the collaboration with their clients on a blended mix of creativity, innovation and quality. This results in a variety of fillings, shapes, molds, decorations. While wishing to keep all these characteristics  - which combine traditional skills and modern techniques - to deliver excellent products, they are confronted with the increasing of the production costs. Among the others, costs linked to the cocoa.
candidate.technical_problem_evidence_text: In order to limit the impact of raw material prices, and notably cocoa, this Belgian company is actively looking for vegetable fat to be used as an alternative to cocoa in the filling of their large range of chocolates, chocolate bars, pralines, truffles etc. The vegetable fat alternative will be used in the filling of the chocolate pralines and has to guarantee the same density and easiness to work the product as for traditional pralines stuffed with cocoa. The cocoa would then be used only for the external coating. The vegetable fat alternative sought needs to: - be used directly in production, without melting step, - ideally come in 20kg (max 25kg) for proper handling - be easily combined with the coating, which can be of simple chocolate or eg a praline powdered or enrobed with nuts, fruits - easily embrace the shape, moulds selected for the production The filling with vegetable fat alternative must be : -	close the density of the pralines with a traditional cocoa filling -	FSSC 22000 certified: Guaranteed food safety and quality standards -	from sourced ingredients produced in Europe by suppliers located in Europe The potential partner must have track records in the manufacturing of the vegetable fat alternative sought
candidate.title: Looking for vegetable fat to be used as an alternative to cocoa in the manufacturing of a large range of chocolates, chocolate bars, pralines, truffles etc

candidate.description_text: The organisation is currently assessing the feasibility of using online sensors and continuous monitoring technologies for the compliance monitoring of treated wastewater discharged from wastewater treatment plants. The parameters of interest mainly include: - Total Suspended Solids (TSS) - Chemical Oxygen Demand (COD) - Total Organic Carbon (TOC) - Nitrates The objective is to evaluate whether online measurements could partially substitute or complement conventional laboratory analyses while maintaining regulatory reliability and compliance. They are particularly interested in: - Types of sensors and technologies currently in use; - Operational constraints and field experience (maintenance, cleaning, recalibration, fouling, sensor drift, robustness, etc.); - Methodologies used to demonstrate equivalence, correlation or regulatory acceptance compared with standard laboratory analyses; - Existing pilot projects, case studies or operational deployments; - Partnerships for technical exchanges, benchmarking activities or collaborative projects.
candidate.technical_problem_evidence_text: They are seeking contacts with organisations that have already developed or tested such solutions in operational environments.
candidate.title: Seeking partners and feedback on online sensor technologies for wastewater treatment plant effluent compliance monitoring.

candidate.description_text: A Bulgarian deep-tech SME with long-standing expertise in geospatial technologies, surveying and infrastructure monitoring has developed a protected software-led autonomous air-water inspection and mapping technology. The technology is designed to bridge the operational gap between above-water and underwater surveying by combining observations from both environments into a single georeferenced operational model. Potential applications include dams and hydraulic structures, ports and harbour infrastructure, bridges, underwater pipelines and cables, coastal erosion and sediment monitoring, marine environmental monitoring, and underwater cultural heritage documentation. The software architecture, data-processing environment and artificial intelligence perception layer have already been developed. The current stage focuses on integration with real underwater hardware and validation in operational missions. The company is seeking European technology and industrial partners capable of providing, adapting or integrating an open and customisable underwater robotic platform. Relevant capabilities include payload capacity, onboard electrical power and thermal management for edge computing, access to vehicle telemetry and raw sensor data, documented software interfaces, and integration of customer-selected navigation, sonar, bathymetric and environmental sensors. Cooperation may involve integration with an existing commercially available underwater vehicle, adaptation of a platform for customer-supplied onboard computing and sensing equipment, physical and electrical integration, prototype manufacturing, laboratory and field testing, pilot validation and preparation for commercial deployment. The Bulgarian company retains ownership of its protected software, artificial intelligence, algorithms, system architecture and integration know-how. The expected partner contribution concerns complementary underwater hardware, manufacturing, physical integration, testing, validation and/or investment supporting market deployment.
candidate.technical_problem_evidence_text: The company is seeking partners with expertise in underwater robotics, autonomous or remotely operated underwater vehicles, marine electronics, subsea sensor integration, advanced manufacturing, mechanical and electrical integration, or field validation. Depending on its capabilities, the partner may: •	provide a commercially available open and customisable underwater robotic platform; •	adapt an existing platform for customer-supplied onboard computing and sensors; •	provide sufficient electrical power, payload capacity and thermal management for edge computing; •	provide documented access to telemetry, navigation data, raw sensor data and vehicle interfaces; •	integrate customer-selected sonar, navigation, bathymetric or environmental sensors; •	perform physical, mechanical and electrical integration; •	manufacture prototype mechanical or pressure-resistant components; •	support laboratory, field and pilot validation; •	participate in preparation for commercial deployment; •	or provide strategic investment supporting hardware integration, validation and market entry. The Bulgarian company will retain responsibility for its proprietary software, artificial intelligence, data-processing and system-level integration technology.
candidate.title: Bulgarian deep-tech SME seeks partners for integration and validation of an autonomous air-water inspection and mapping technology.

candidate.description_text: Founded with the mission to accelerate the transition to a circular economy, a Swiss startup specializing in sustainable industrial chemistry and eco-friendly additive development leverages advanced material science to transform industrial waste streams into valuable manufacturing inputs. Operating with a lean structure and cutting-edge vision, the organization focuses on developing scalable, green chemical solutions that mitigate the environmental footprint of traditional manufacturing materials. The company seeks manufacturers of rubber goods or industrial organization to co-develop and scale up rubber recycling through a more sustainable devulcanization process. The global vulcanized rubber industry faces a severe waste management challenge. Traditional vulcanization creates permanent, crosslinked sulfur bonds within the rubber matrix. These bonds make the material durable but also difficult to recycle. Standard mechanical grinding merely downgrades the material into low-value filler, while incineration and landfilling create significant environmental liabilities. To solve this problem, the startup offers a high-performance eco-friendly chemical additive for rubber devulcanization. The product functions via a gentle chemical-mechanical process that targets and breaks down the sulfur-sulfur crosslinks while preserving the integrity of the main polymer chains. The resulting material acts as a functional secondary raw material that retains the inherent elastomeric or abrasion properties of the original feedstock. While not all recovered rubber is highly formulated, preserving the original compound's existing additives in highly compounded inputs - like tires - allows manufacturers to optimize formulations and reduce the volume of new chemical inputs. While the chemical formulation is available, the core problem to be solved lies in its end-user application. The startup requires advanced end-user technical manufacturing know-how and material testing capabilities. Specifically, the technology requested involves the practical application, compounding, and performance validation of the devulcanized material when it is blended back into new product lines. Collaboration with manufacturers of technical rubber goods, consumer rubber products or industrial organization seeking sustainable technologies to recycle their rubber waste would allow to determine how the treated rubber behaves during industrial molding and production, ensuring it seamlessly integrates into new technical rubber goods or consumer products without compromising final structural integrity. Transitioning a chemical formulation into a successful, commercial-grade end product requires a collaborative feedback loop between the chemical developer and the material manufacturer. Technical cooperation or joint venture with manufacturers of technical rubber goods, consumer rubber products or industrial organization is thought: to co-develop optimized blending guidelines and successful manufacture market-ready consumer or technical rubber goods containing high percentages of recycled material. Unlike conventional high-temperature devulcanization methods, our chemical-mechanical process operates efficiently under reduced thermal requirements without demanding high-heat inputs, lowering energy consumption. By providing a substitute for resource-intensive virgin materials, this method inherently drives a substantial reduction in the overall process carbon footprint. Cooperation throught: commercial agreements, or joint development projects (Eurostars or Horizon Europe) if mutually beneficial. Partners are expected to provide industrial testing environments, product compounding expertise, and quality assurance evaluation for the final rubber products. The start up is also open to joint venture or partnership that support both the validation of the innovation and the integration of recycled  rubber materials into new goods or consumer products.
candidate.technical_problem_evidence_text: Performance, Ease of Use, and Quality Required The startup offers a high-performance chemical additive that transforms scrap rubber into a reusable asset. We require technical partners to test the product and evaluate the devulcanized material to optimize blending ratios within their product lines. The primary technical objective is verifying how the material behaves during industrial molding and production, ensuring it integrates into new technical rubber goods or consumer products without compromising final mechanical properties. Capability and Equipment Requirements End-user partners must have operational facilities utilizing conventional, standard rubber processing equipment (such as standard extruders, open mills, or internal mixers). The partner must possess internal material testing capabilities, compound formulation expertise, and final product quality validation workflows. The partner will be responsible for evaluating the mechanical tolerances, durability, and dimensional stability of the final rubber products containing the recycled material. Sustainability and Compliance Standards Because the additive and its supply chains are fully compliant with the European Union Regulation on Deforestation-free Products (EUDR), partners must be capable of maintaining matching environmental tracking and quality assurance standards throughout their compounding trials. Sustainability and Compliance Standards A key environmental capability of this process is that the resulting recycled rubber produced by the partner can fully comply with the European Union Regulation on Deforestation-free Products (EUDR). While not strictly mandatory for initial testing, it would be an advantage if partners possess the quality assurance tracking and environmental standards necessary to maintain this regulatory compliance throughout their compounding and manufacturing trials. Stage of Development Needed Partners at the prototype, pilot, or commercial stage are welcome. Ideally, the partner has the flexibility to perform pilot-scale compounding runs or help translate initial test results into commercial-grade production logic, though we are open to discussing different scales of cooperation. The ideal partner is an end-user manufacturer or sustainability-driven organization looking to test the startup's chemical additive within standard rubber processing setups to achieve devulcanization. They will collaborate with the startup to evaluate how the additive integrates, optimize compounding mixtures for their specific products, and provide feedback on the final product's performance.
