description_text: Founded with the mission to accelerate the transition to a circular economy, a Swiss startup specializing in sustainable industrial chemistry and eco-friendly additive development leverages advanced material science to transform industrial waste streams into valuable manufacturing inputs. Operating with a lean structure and cutting-edge vision, the organization focuses on developing scalable, green chemical solutions that mitigate the environmental footprint of traditional manufacturing materials. The company seeks manufacturers of rubber goods or industrial organization to co-develop and scale up rubber recycling through a more sustainable devulcanization process. The global vulcanized rubber industry faces a severe waste management challenge. Traditional vulcanization creates permanent, crosslinked sulfur bonds within the rubber matrix. These bonds make the material durable but also difficult to recycle. Standard mechanical grinding merely downgrades the material into low-value filler, while incineration and landfilling create significant environmental liabilities. To solve this problem, the startup offers a high-performance eco-friendly chemical additive for rubber devulcanization. The product functions via a gentle chemical-mechanical process that targets and breaks down the sulfur-sulfur crosslinks while preserving the integrity of the main polymer chains. The resulting material acts as a functional secondary raw material that retains the inherent elastomeric or abrasion properties of the original feedstock. While not all recovered rubber is highly formulated, preserving the original compound's existing additives in highly compounded inputs - like tires - allows manufacturers to optimize formulations and reduce the volume of new chemical inputs. While the chemical formulation is available, the core problem to be solved lies in its end-user application. The startup requires advanced end-user technical manufacturing know-how and material testing capabilities. Specifically, the technology requested involves the practical application, compounding, and performance validation of the devulcanized material when it is blended back into new product lines. Collaboration with manufacturers of technical rubber goods, consumer rubber products or industrial organization seeking sustainable technologies to recycle their rubber waste would allow to determine how the treated rubber behaves during industrial molding and production, ensuring it seamlessly integrates into new technical rubber goods or consumer products without compromising final structural integrity. Transitioning a chemical formulation into a successful, commercial-grade end product requires a collaborative feedback loop between the chemical developer and the material manufacturer. Technical cooperation or joint venture with manufacturers of technical rubber goods, consumer rubber products or industrial organization is thought: to co-develop optimized blending guidelines and successful manufacture market-ready consumer or technical rubber goods containing high percentages of recycled material. Unlike conventional high-temperature devulcanization methods, our chemical-mechanical process operates efficiently under reduced thermal requirements without demanding high-heat inputs, lowering energy consumption. By providing a substitute for resource-intensive virgin materials, this method inherently drives a substantial reduction in the overall process carbon footprint. Cooperation throught: commercial agreements, or joint development projects (Eurostars or Horizon Europe) if mutually beneficial. Partners are expected to provide industrial testing environments, product compounding expertise, and quality assurance evaluation for the final rubber products. The start up is also open to joint venture or partnership that support both the validation of the innovation and the integration of recycled  rubber materials into new goods or consumer products.
technical_problem_evidence_text: Performance, Ease of Use, and Quality Required The startup offers a high-performance chemical additive that transforms scrap rubber into a reusable asset. We require technical partners to test the product and evaluate the devulcanized material to optimize blending ratios within their product lines. The primary technical objective is verifying how the material behaves during industrial molding and production, ensuring it integrates into new technical rubber goods or consumer products without compromising final mechanical properties. Capability and Equipment Requirements End-user partners must have operational facilities utilizing conventional, standard rubber processing equipment (such as standard extruders, open mills, or internal mixers). The partner must possess internal material testing capabilities, compound formulation expertise, and final product quality validation workflows. The partner will be responsible for evaluating the mechanical tolerances, durability, and dimensional stability of the final rubber products containing the recycled material. Sustainability and Compliance Standards Because the additive and its supply chains are fully compliant with the European Union Regulation on Deforestation-free Products (EUDR), partners must be capable of maintaining matching environmental tracking and quality assurance standards throughout their compounding trials. Sustainability and Compliance Standards A key environmental capability of this process is that the resulting recycled rubber produced by the partner can fully comply with the European Union Regulation on Deforestation-free Products (EUDR). While not strictly mandatory for initial testing, it would be an advantage if partners possess the quality assurance tracking and environmental standards necessary to maintain this regulatory compliance throughout their compounding and manufacturing trials. Stage of Development Needed Partners at the prototype, pilot, or commercial stage are welcome. Ideally, the partner has the flexibility to perform pilot-scale compounding runs or help translate initial test results into commercial-grade production logic, though we are open to discussing different scales of cooperation. The ideal partner is an end-user manufacturer or sustainability-driven organization looking to test the startup's chemical additive within standard rubber processing setups to achieve devulcanization. They will collaborate with the startup to evaluate how the additive integrates, optimize compounding mixtures for their specific products, and provide feedback on the final product's performance.
title: Manufacturers of rubber products sought for co-development of sustainable and circular devulcanization of waste materials

candidate.description_text: A Swiss organisation linked to the Geneva Forum and the Geneva Foundation for the Future is seeking user organisations worldwide to test, use and deploy the impact finance evaluation framework AGILE within real decision-making processes. The request concerns practical integration to further evaluate both its usage methodology and its effectiveness in project assessment, not the development of a new tool. AGILE is an impact finance evaluation framework designed to help users identify, assess, mentor, monitor and scale impact-driven initiatives. It provides a shared grammar between philanthropy, investment, public institutions, project leaders and academic actors, and can be applied to project pipelines, grantmaking, impact investment selection, public funding schemes, blended finance, CSR/ESG (Corporate Social Responsibility/ Environmental, Social, and Governance) transition, incubation, portfolio review, education and training. The framework is structured around five functional pillars: - Alignment with values, SDGs (Sustainable Development Goals), ESG/GRI (Global Reporting Initiative) standards and local realities; - Governance based on participation, transparency and accountability; - Intention focused on deep, structural and systemic impact; - Leadership able to mobilise and sustain change; - Efficiency in resource use, economic viability and scalability. The sought partners are organisations willing to pilot AGILE on real cases, compare it with their existing criteria and explore its deployment in their own processes. The collaboration may start with a limited pilot, workshop or use case, then progress to internal training, portfolio integration, platform adaptation or broader deployment. AGILE is a methodological and decision-support framework. Its use does not replace financial, legal or investment advice.
candidate.technical_problem_evidence_text: The partners sought should be organisations able to test or deploy AGILE in at least one real operational process. Expected capabilities: - Existing activity in impact finance, philanthropy, public funding, development cooperation, CSR/ESG transition, incubation, academic training, project evaluation or portfolio management. - Ability to provide one or more anonymised use cases, project pipelines or evaluation workflows. - Internal capacity to involve relevant teams: finance, impact, programme, due diligence, sustainability, innovation, legal/compliance, IT or platform teams when relevant. - Interest in testing the AGILE five-pillar methodology, scoring logic, project profiles, evaluation sheets, dashboards or collaborative review process. - Capacity to provide structured feedback on usability, sector relevance, workflow integration and deployment conditions. - Interest in staff training, local adaptation, co-design of templates or integration with existing digital platforms where appropriate. No specific technology stack is required for a first pilot. Digital integration, API connection, data import/export or dashboard adaptation can be discussed after the initial use case.
candidate.title: Seeking organisations worldwide to test, use and deploy an agile and simple impact finance tool in their evaluation and funding processes acting as a common benchmark to provide transparent framework

candidate.description_text: The company develops charging infrastructure for electric vehicles and e-bikes that combines industrial design, embedded hardware and software, and a digital platform for charge point operation and user management. To support further innovation, the company is seeking research and industrial partners for collaborative projects related to electromobility, energy management, digital platforms and user applications, smart-city applications of charging infrastructure, and sustainable or circular product design, including materials and packaging. Cooperation could take the form of applied research, joint technology validation, prototype development, pilot testing in real operating conditions, or joint participation in national or European research and innovation funding programmes. The company has previously been selected for support under a national programme for technology-oriented development companies and has received several design and sustainability awards, reflecting an established practice of combining product development with external evaluation and recognition. The expected outcome of the cooperation is joint research leading to new or improved products, services or technological solutions in the field of charging infrastructure and sustainable mobility.
candidate.technical_problem_evidence_text: Partners are expected to contribute research capacity, specialised knowledge, testing or laboratory facilities, or complementary technological expertise, and to participate in the joint definition and execution of research activities, including potential joint funding applications.

candidate.description_text: The initiative is structured as an integrated platform combining infrastructure systems, economic clusters, and institutional components within a unified development framework. The project requires the development of a fully integrated energy system forming the technical backbone of a large-scale urban platform. The system combines multiple renewable generation sources with storage and backup solutions to ensure reliable, scalable, and resilient energy supply. While the initiator is situated in Germany, the project itself is located in the Republic of Moldova and is positioned as an integrated economic development platform within an emerging European growth market. The requested partner is expected to assume a system-level integration role, including overall architecture design, interface definition across subsystems, and optimization of energy flows. This includes load balancing, seasonal storage considerations, and integration of digital energy management systems. The role may extend into long-term system optimization and operational models, positioning the partner as a key infrastructure orchestrator. The project is currently in a pre-feasibility stage. No fixed procurement budget or tender structure is defined at this stage. The objective of this cooperation request is to identify qualified partners for early-stage technical alignment and system design. Depending on project progression, the cooperation may evolve into structured participation models, including system integrator roles within EPC+ (Energy Performance Contracting Plus), ESCo (Energy Service Company), or asset-level Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV) structures. The partner may participate as technical lead, co-developer, or long-term operator within the energy infrastructure segment. Subject to project progression, the cooperation may evolve into a joint venture participation at asset or SPV level.
candidate.technical_problem_evidence_text: The solution should integrate solar, wind, and biogas generation with battery storage and hydrogen-based backup systems. Advanced energy management systems, digital control, and experience in district-scale or city-scale integrated energy systems are strongly preferred.
candidate.title: Partner sought for system-level integration of a multi-source renewable energy infrastructure at district scale

candidate.description_text: The SME, located in South Korea and Germany is specializing in EV and ESS battery technologies. Their primary service is remanufacturing EV or ESS batteries but they also provide a wide range of services relating to batteries, leveraging deep and comprehensive data obtained through their remanufacturing activities. Seamless evaluation and diagnostics conducted by the company provide precise SOH (State of Health) and a performance grading as well as information on defects exist in each part of EV or ESS batteries. The company is committed to advancing sustainability and circularity by maximising the lifespan of batteries that contain rare and valuable materials. Their approach focuses on extending battery value through longevity enhancement and replacement of end-of-life components with reusable parts. To further these objectives, the company is collaborating with an R&D institute on a Eureka project and intends to pursue additional funding opportunities to realise their innovative ideas. They are therefore looking for partners active in remanufacturing, automation or evaluation in terms of HV batteries who are interested in forming a project consortium and applying for funding. They would like to meet interested partners for ideation on potential project directions. As a remanufacturer the company is also looking for a supplier for used EV traction batteries for their production activities. The partner would need to be able to provide used or defective battery packs which haven't entered into waste phase.
candidate.technical_problem_evidence_text: Suitable partners should have expertise in one or more of the following areas: EV battery remanufacturing, automation of dismantling or refurbishment processes, diagnostics and technical evaluation of HV batteries, battery testing, process engineering, BMS development, Battery Passport Solution or related R&D. For supplier cooperation, the company is specifically looking for used or defective EV traction battery packs that remain outside waste status. Batteries already classified, registered or handled as waste are not suitable.
candidate.title: German SME seeks research and supplier partnerships for electric vehicle (EV) traction battery remanufacturing, automation and high-voltage (HV) battery evaluation

candidate.description_text: The City of Excellence is a private greenfield smart city initiative in the Republic of Moldova. The project is currently at pre-feasibility stage and is conceived as an integrated urban system combining education, innovation, housing, industry, healthcare, emergency services, and critical infrastructure. The city is designed for a future population of approximately 100,000 residents. Its central Education & Innovation Hub is planned to include universities, a business school, an innovation hub, a convention centre, and emergency response facilities. The healthcare component is a digital teaching hospital intended to provide high-quality medical services, support medical education, and contribute to healthcare workforce development in Moldova. According to the pre-feasibility concept, the hospital is planned with a capacity of 500 beds, corresponding to 5 beds per 1,000 residents. The hospital is expected to comprise approximately 150,000 sqm of building space on approximately 60,000 sqm of land. It is intended to be fully digitalized to improve patient management, operational efficiency, and quality of service. The hospital is also intended to cooperate closely with doctors’ offices in the city. This cooperation should include digital patient files, efficient referral processes, and coordinated resource allocation. Patients suitable for treatment in doctors’ offices should be referred accordingly, while patients requiring hospital-level services should be directed to the hospital. The teaching hospital is intended to take a leading role in knowledge dissemination and exchange of experience in Moldova. It should include facilities for training doctors, nurses, hospital staff, and other healthcare professionals. The concept also foresees modern medical equipment, digital teaching, robot-based surgical techniques, and access to international specialists. The project initiator is seeking experienced partners for an initial non-binding exchange. Relevant partners may include hospital operators, university hospitals, medical faculties, healthcare infrastructure planners, digital health providers, MedTech companies, medical training institutions, or consortia with experience in teaching hospitals and smart healthcare systems. The cooperation sought at this stage is exploratory. Possible cooperation may include concept validation, feasibility-stage input, technical advice, digital health architecture, hospital planning, medical equipment strategy, teaching hospital operating models, or later participation as operator, co-developer, technology provider, academic partner, or specialist advisor.
candidate.technical_problem_evidence_text: The project is seeking partners with expertise in one or more of the following areas: ● Hospital planning and development: experience in the design, development, commissioning, or operational preparation of general hospitals, teaching hospitals, university hospitals, or integrated healthcare facilities. ● Hospital operation: experience in operating hospitals, healthcare networks, teaching hospitals, or clinical service platforms with strong quality, efficiency, and training standards. ● Digital health infrastructure: solutions for electronic patient records, hospital information systems, digital referral processes, patient management, clinical workflow systems, telemedicine, and healthcare data integration. ● Medical training and teaching hospital models: experience in training doctors, nurses, clinical staff, hospital administrators, or healthcare professionals according to international standards. ● MedTech and advanced medical infrastructure: experience with modern diagnostic systems, surgical technologies, robotic surgery, simulation-based training, digital teaching equipment, and advanced clinical infrastructure. The requested technologies and expertise should preferably be proven, scalable, and suitable for implementation in a future full-feasibility and development phase. At this stage, the project does not seek a final procurement offer, but qualified input and potential cooperation partners for further concept development.
candidate.title: Partners sought for digital teaching hospital and smart healthcare infrastructure in a greenfield smart city project in the Republic of Moldova

candidate.description_text: The applicant is a German SME operating in structured content production and multi-format publishing. Over the last four years the company has developed a semantic anchoring system that gives every relevant text element in an editable office-format document a persistent identifier. References stay attached to their content when documents are restructured, edited under change tracking or export-ed to several output channels in parallel. Per document the system handles between 3,000 and 9,000 anchored references. The system has been in productive use in the company's own editorial domain since late 2024. The intended cooperation moves the technology into a different field: regulated technical documentation for medical devices under MDR 2017/745. References in that field are not editorial. A symbol, a warning, a product identifier or a clinical claim carries regulatory weight, and it has to stay consistent through the whole product life cycle, through up to 24 language versions, and through every audit a Notified Body decides to run. Tools used today in this market rely either on rigid component content management, on manual reference maintenance, or on layout workflows that lose semantic links somewhere between a translation round and a release approval. The company has seen no toolchain that solves this without trade-offs. The project builds on the existing anchoring technology but requires substantial experimental development. Unresolved technical challenges concern the preservation of regulatory meaning across structural edits, multilingual transformations, terminology changes, redlining and controlled release processes. On top of this sit integration with translation memory and controlled terminology; audit trails that satisfy ISO 13485 change-control duties and MDR Annex II documentation requirements; mechanisms that carry the regulatory weight of a reference through translation, redlining and release; and validation methods that generate evidence suitable for review during quality-management and conformity-assessment audits. The cooperation delivers a demonstrator validated against real cases from the partner, plus an evaluation framework for regulatory fit. The cooperation is designed for the German ZIM cooperative project track. Each side runs its own work packages and holds its own grant share. The company brings running technology, software-side R&D capacity and document-structure expertise. The partner brings the regulated domain and contributes its own regulatory-methodological R&D work packages — among them the development of a formal regulatory reference model, risk-based validation criteria, multilingual compliance rules, and methods for verifying reference integrity across document revisions, translations and release processes. The parties intend to conclude a research and development cooperation agreement for the planned project. Rights to pre-existing technology, jointly developed results and subsequent exploitation will be regulated in a project-specific cooperation agreement.
candidate.technical_problem_evidence_text: Sought is a partner with operational responsibility for MDR-regulated documentation. The partner brings the regulated domain the applicant does not have in-house. Required: •	active responsibility for medical device documentation under MDR 2017/745 (instructions for use, technical documentation, labelling, clinical content); •	working knowledge of ISO 13485 quality management, in particular document and change control; •	practical experience with multilingual release, translation memory and controlled terminology; •	practical experience with audits and conformity-assessment procedures involving Notified Bodies (an institutional link to a Notified Body is not required); •	own R&D capacity to define regulatory acceptance criteria, co-develop the regulatory reference model and validation methodology, and run its own work packages; •	ability to name concrete validation scenarios, document structures and bottlenecks from current practice; •	willingness to provide realistic sample content (anonymised where required) for demonstrator validation; •	readiness to enter a formal cooperation under the German ZIM cooperative project track. The semantic anchoring base technology is in production in the applicant's own domain. For the MedTech application the work is at concept stage: the regulatory extension, the terminology integration and the audit-trail validation are the subject of the cooperation. A working demonstration of the base mechanism is available under NDA.

candidate.description_text: A company in northern Germany has identified knowledge management as a key area for innovation. In operational settings, valuable experiential knowledge is generated directly in day-to-day work, but it is often not systematically recorded, is tied to specific individuals, or is difficult to locate. This creates risks of knowledge loss, for example due to employees retiring or changing jobs. Therefore, the goal is to find a practical, AI-supported solution for capturing, structuring, and making implicit domain knowledge available. The focus is on the audiovisual documentation of systems and processes, as well as ease of use in day-to-day work to support onboarding, problem documentation, and knowledge retention. Solutions already implemented: - Use of existing knowledge management solutions, e.g., documents, training materials, file repositories, and Office and collaboration systems. - Partial use of isolated knowledge platforms and multiple databases with limited interconnectivity. - Debriefing and interview formats to capture the knowledge of experienced employees (e.g., prior to retirement or offboarding). - Ongoing or completed projects for documenting facilities, the findings of which should be taken into account. - Previous approaches in the field of augmented reality (AR), the lessons learned from which can be incorporated into solution development. - Low-code applications for documenting events with visual material. Limitations of previous approaches: - Existing solutions are not sufficiently field-ready; in particular, they lack hands-free functionality. - There is a lack of uniform standards and a consistent structure for documenting knowledge. - Knowledge is difficult to find and can only be used to a limited extent because it is scattered across various systems. - Implicit experiential knowledge has not yet been systematically recorded and preserved. - An intelligent, user-friendly solution for capturing, structuring, and providing experiential knowledge is currently lacking. ------ Please note: Since this request is part of an innovation challenge, kindly answer the questions below within your EoI or write me an email. 1. candidate.description_text: The Danish SME develops reusable container solutions for catering and takeaway with the objective of reducing single‑use packaging and improving circular return systems. To support efficient return logistics, the company is seeking a technology capable of reliable single‑item identification of reusable food containers (e.g. bowls, plates, trays). The containers are manufactured from a wood‑plastic composite (WPC) material and are designed for repeated reuse under demanding operational conditions. They must withstand industrial dishwashing, microwave heating, oven exposure and freezing without degradation. Any identification solution must tolerate the same conditions over the product lifetime. The purpose of the identification technology is to enable operational tracking and identification during use and return cycles (e.g. in catering kitchens and return facilities). The solution is not consumer‑facing and does not require anti‑counterfeiting or brand protection features. A key operational requirement is that containers cannot be guaranteed a fixed orientation during scanning. The requested technology must therefore be orientation‑independent, either through surface‑wide identification or through identification principles that do not rely on a predefined code position. Containers are scanned in two main environments: Small‑scale or decentralised operations using standard smartphones High‑volume kitchens using fixed or tunnel‑mounted industrial camera systems The company is not seeking a full end‑to‑end tracking platform, but rather access to the core identification technology (e.g. algorithm, SDK (Software Development Kit), or licensable method) that can be integrated into its own backend systems. Material‑intrinsic identification The container material has a naturally heterogeneous surface structure, with visible wood fibres distributed randomly. This inherent variability means that no two containers are identical, opening the possibility of identification based on the material itself. Solutions based on surface fingerprinting or material‑intrinsic identification, where the natural surface structure is captured (e.g. optically) and used as a unique identifier are therefore of strong interest, provided they can reliably identify individual containers over the full product lifetime despite normal wear and cleaning.
candidate.technical_problem_evidence_text: The requested technology should meet the following requirements: -Enables single‑item identification (each container uniquely identifiable) -Implemented as: integrated surface marking (e.g. engraving or sandblasting), or material‑intrinsic identification (e.g. surface fingerprinting) (adhesive labels and add‑on tags are out of scope) -Readable using standard smartphones and industrial camera systems -Orientation‑independent reading -Withstands: industrial dishwashing (~85 °C) microwave use (up to 1000 W) freezing (−18 °C) oven exposure up to 135 °C for at least 35 minutes -Minimum 200+ reuse cycles without loss of identification reliability -Compatible with wood‑plastic composite (WPC) materials -No dependency on proprietary platforms, closed ecosystems or mandatory cloud services -Available as a technology licence or core technology access (SDK, library, algorithm, or equivalent) -Cost structure suitable for SME‑scale deployment (initial volumes approx. 5,000–50,000 units/year) Solutions leveraging the material’s natural surface variation as identifier (e.g. surface fingerprinting) are equally welcome.

candidate.description_text: A Danish SME active in specialised clinical nutrition is seeking a German university hospital or clinical research environment to conduct a controlled pilot study involving a protein-enriched nutritional ice cream developed for patients with low appetite and risk of malnutrition. The product is classified as a Food for Special Medical Purposes (FSMP) under Regulation (EU) 609/2013 and has been notified with the German Bundesamt für Verbraucherschutz und Lebensmittelsicherheit (BVL). The product is intended as a supplementary nutritional intervention for adult patients who struggle to maintain sufficient caloric and protein intake through ordinary meals. The company has already conducted a 30-day pilot study in Denmark involving nutritionally at-risk nursing home residents. The study demonstrated complete product consumption compliance throughout the intervention period together with positive weight development among participants. To achieve a useful result, it is necessary that we are able to follow the selected patients for a continuous period. This suggests that we target the search for clinicians & nursing homes that have close daily continuous contact The company is now seeking a recognised German clinical partner capable of conducting a structured pilot study under clinically relevant conditions. Cooperation with a university hospital, clinical nutrition department or academic research group is particularly relevant, including possible involvement of PhD researchers or clinical nutrition researchers. The proposed study would compare the nutritional ice cream with conventional oral nutritional supplements used in institutional care. The target population may include: •	Oncology patients undergoing treatment •	Elderly patients with low appetite •	Patients identified as nutritionally at-risk •	Patients with poor compliance to standard oral nutritional supplements The planned intervention period is 30 days with a minimum target of 20 participants. Indicative outcome measures include: •	Change in body weight •	Product consumption compliance •	Patient acceptance and palatability •	Practical integration into clinical care routines •	Care staff observations regarding usability and acceptance •	Caregiver observations of patient mood, basic attitude and outlook on life The Danish company will provide: •	Study products free of charge during the pilot •	Study protocol and data collection tools •	Coordination support during the study period •	Logistics and product supply •	Participation in data analysis and possible scientific publication The international cooperation is envisaged as a research and development cooperation agreement supporting clinical validation and documentation of patient compliance and nutritional outcomes.

The product is intended as a supplementary nutritional intervention for adult patients who struggle to maintain sufficient caloric and protein intake through ordinary meals. The company has already conducted a 30-day pilot study in Denmark involving nutritionally at-risk nursing home residents. The study demonstrated complete product consumption compliance throughout the intervention period together with positive weight development among participants. To achieve a useful result, it is necessary that we are able to follow the selected patients for a continuous period. This suggests that we target the search for clinicians & nursing homes that have close daily continuous contact The company is now seeking a recognised German clinical partner capable of conducting a structured pilot study under clinically relevant conditions. Cooperation with a university hospital, clinical nutrition department or academic research group is particularly relevant, including possible involvement of PhD researchers or clinical nutrition researchers. The proposed study would compare the nutritional ice cream with conventional oral nutritional supplements used in institutional care. The target population may include: •	Oncology patients undergoing treatment •	Elderly patients with low appetite •	Patients identified as nutritionally at-risk •	Patients with poor compliance to standard oral nutritional supplements The planned intervention period is 30 days with a minimum target of 20 participants. Indicative outcome measures include: •	Change in body weight •	Product consumption compliance •	Patient acceptance and palatability •	Practical integration into clinical care routines •	Care staff observations regarding usability and acceptance •	Caregiver observations of patient mood, basic attitude and outlook on life The Danish company will provide: •	Study products free of charge during the pilot •	Study protocol and data collection tools •	Coordination support during the study period •	Logistics and product supply •	Participation in data analysis and possible scientific publication The international cooperation is envisaged as a research and development cooperation agreement supporting clinical validation and documentation of patient compliance and nutritional outcomes.
technical_problem_evidence_text: The company seeks a clinical partner with experience in: •	Clinical nutrition research •	Oncology nutrition •	Geriatric nutrition •	Nutritional intervention studies •	Patient compliance studies •	Oral nutritional supplementation The partner should preferably: •	Have access to eligible patient populations •	Be able to conduct a controlled 30-day intervention study •	Have experience with ethics approval procedures •	Be capable of collecting body weight and consumption compliance data •	Have clinical or academic staff interested in nutrition-related research activities University hospitals, clinical nutrition departments and academic research groups are preferred.
title: Danish SME seeks German university hospital or clinical research department for pilot study on protein-enriched nutritional ice cream for patients at risk of malnutrition

candidate.description_text: The company is a Spanish technology startup developing data infrastructure and analytics solutions for complex energy markets. The organisation focuses on improving how investment decisions are made in renewable energy systems by integrating fragmented operational and market data into decision-ready intelligence tools. Across European electricity markets, renewable energy investment decisions depend on multiple datasets that are typically fragmented across different sources. Market prices, grid connection constraints, infrastructure pipelines, weather data, regulatory developments and auction rules are often accessed through separate platforms, public portals or consultancy reports. Analysts and investment teams frequently combine these sources manually using spreadsheets and disconnected tools. This process is time-consuming, difficult to standardise across markets and can lead to incomplete or inconsistent analysis. Existing solutions in the market usually focus on specific analytical domains. Some platforms provide electricity market forecasts or price modelling tools, while others offer renewable resource datasets, grid information portals or consultancy-based market reports. However, these solutions rarely integrate all relevant intelligence layers required for renewable infrastructure investment decisions within a single analytical environment. The proposed technology addresses this gap by providing an integrated data and analytics platform designed to combine key intelligence layers for renewable energy markets. The platform aggregates structured data from multiple sources, including electricity market prices, transmission system operator data, renewable resource indicators, regulatory information and infrastructure development pipelines. Through a unified data architecture and analytical interface, users can analyse market conditions, compare investment opportunities across regions and evaluate potential project revenues and risks. The platform supports applications such as opportunity screening for solar, wind and energy storage projects, identification of attractive bidding zones, and simulation of potential revenue streams for battery energy storage systems under different market conditions. The technology is designed to support organisations operating in complex energy environments, including renewable energy developers, utilities, energy traders, infrastructure investors and energy consultancies. The company is currently in the technology validation phase and is seeking international partners for research and development cooperation. The aim is to validate and further develop the platform through pilot projects in real operational or analytical environments across European electricity markets. Partners are expected to provide access to relevant data, use cases or testing environments, and to contribute to the assessment of the platform’s performance and applicability. The cooperation would support the adaptation of the solution to different market conditions and the preparation for wider commercial deployment.
candidate.technical_problem_evidence_text: The company is seeking cooperation with organisations operating in European electricity and renewable energy markets that are interested in testing and applying the technology within real analytical, operational or investment environments. Potential partners may include renewable energy developers, utilities, energy trading organisations, infrastructure investors, asset operators, energy consultancies or research institutions working on electricity market analysis, forecasting and energy system modelling. The expected cooperation may include pilot deployments of the platform to support renewable energy investment analysis, operational optimisation and validation of analytical models using real project data. This includes joint exploration of use cases related to solar, wind or battery energy storage projects, as well as the application of the platform’s Forecast functionality. The Forecast functionality is designed to allow operators to enhance their existing forecasting models and strengthen market participation. By testing operator-provided forecasts against the data and analytical capabilities available within the platform, the tool can assess whether platform data, enhanced modelling and weather-based adjustments could improve forecasting accuracy and operational performance. This functionality is intended to help operators validate decisionmaking processes, identify potential forecast improvements and reinforce participation strategies in power markets. Partners may contribute expertise related to specific electricity markets, grid infrastructure planning, regulatory analysis, forecasting practices or energy project development. Collaboration could also involve joint development of additional analytical modules, validation of forecast optimisation approaches, or the integration of new data sources relevant to regional energy markets and asset performance. The objective of the cooperation is to validate and further develop the platform while enabling partners to improve their ability to analyse market opportunities, assess infrastructure constraints, optimise forecasting performance and evaluate potential revenue streams for renewable energy projects.
candidate.title: Spanish Startup with renewable energy analytics platform for Investment Assessment is looking for partners for European Market Validation

candidate.description_text: A Spanish company specialized in the production of ready-to-eat meals relies on a business model that involves sourcing high-quality agricultural raw materials from various suppliers across EU member states and Turkey. To guarantee the excellence of the final product, quality control must be performed directly at the source. The company is looking to establish a reliable network of local inspection and certification partners. These partners will be responsible for conducting on-site quality audits before shipment. Furthermore, they must ensure that the goods are sealed with tamper-evident packaging, guaranteeing that the raw materials arrive at the Spanish facilities in the exact same condition as inspected.
candidate.technical_problem_evidence_text: The quality criteria that products must have in accordance with the company’s specifications are as follows: -Products free from pests or diseases. -Product purity above a specified threshold. -Absence of chemicals not permitted under European legislation. -Presence of chemicals below a maximum residue limit, which varies according to the product and the raw material Partners must have access to certified laboratory testing facilities capable of chemical and physical-chemical analysis. Familiarity with EU food safety regulations and maximum residue limits (MRLs) is mandatory.
candidate.title: Auditing and quality certification services sought for plant-based raw materials procurement (EU and Turkey)

candidate.description_text: The company is building a new infrastructure layer for the impact economy, addressing one of the biggest gaps in sustainability today: the lack of verifiable, trustworthy and auditable impact data. Current ESG reporting is fragmented, declarative and difficult to validate. Organizations struggle to demonstrate that their actions generate real, measurable outcomes, creating a critical trust gap between companies, institutions and stakeholders. The company addresses this challenge by transforming real-world problems into structured, traceable and verifiable impact through a unified system. At the core of this system is Impact Graph, a structured workflow engine that enables organizations to transform ideas, decisions, projects or initiatives into verifiable processes. It supports: - the decomposition of actions into structured workflows - the attachment of real evidence (documents, links, files) - the generation of structured records - the creation of traceable timelines - the preparation of projects for external verification This approach turns intention into structured evidence. The platform combines : - A discovery layer where ideas, initiatives and projects emerge and are validated by the community - Impact Graph for structuring workflows and preparing projects for verification and funding - AI-driven analysis to guide decisions and execution - A traceability layer to record decisions, processes and evidence - A data integrity layer ensuring structured and verifiable information - A blockchain anchoring layer securing checkpoints and proofs - Proof-of-Impact mechanisms to certify and validate real-world outcomes Together, these components create a complete system in which every step—from problem identification to funding readiness—is structured, traceable and verifiable. This enables a new flow : problem → solution → initiative → structured workflow → evidence → verification → funding readiness The system is designed as a distributed infrastructure capable of operating locally (including in offline environments) and synchronizing with global networks. This architecture enables deployment across sectors such as energy, manufacturing, smart buildings, healthcare and sustainable infrastructure. Use cases include: - Impact measurement and certification for ESG and sustainability programs - Structuring projects to access grants and funding - Community-driven initiatives and crowdfunding with verifiable outcomes - Operational traceability in industrial environments - Energy monitoring and optimization - Transparent reporting for institutions, corporates and public-sector actors By bridging the gap between real-world actions and digital verification, the company enables organizations to move from declarative ESG reporting to measurable, auditable and trusted impact. The long-term vision is to establish Proof‑of‑Impact as a global standard for how impact is structured, verified and trusted. The company aims to provide a system that structures, verifies and certifies impact from end to end.
candidate.technical_problem_evidence_text: The company is seeking technical and strategic partners in the following areas: - industrial and energy infrastructure (smart grids, buildings, industrial sites) - IoT, edge computing and embedded systems - cybersecurity, data integrity and blockchain infrastructure - ESG, impact measurement and certification frameworks - AI and data analytics applied to real‑world operations The objective is to co‑develop, pilot and scale the infrastructure in real‑world environments, accelerating adoption across sectors and geographies. The french company is developing a distributed infrastructure for verifiable impact, combining AI, structured traceability systems and cryptographic integrity layers. The system is built on a modular architecture that includes: - an AI‑driven operational layer for event interpretation, decision support and automation - a traceability system capturing actions, decisions, evidence and impact signals - a data integrity and anchoring layer ensuring reliability and verification - Proof‑of‑Impact mechanisms enabling certification and validation of real‑world outcomes - Impact Graph for workflow structuring and evidence preparation The project is supported by proprietary intellectual property currently under development, including: - a patent on the transmission of signed metadata via power line communication (PLC), enabling secure data exchange through energy infrastructure - a patent on the integration of energy equipment as physical nodes of the system, supporting distributed validation and edge‑level data collection - a registered utility model related to the Proof‑of‑Impact methodology These innovations enable a hybrid infrastructure that bridges digital systems and physical environments, designed for deployment in industrial, energy and infrastructure contexts.
candidate.title: A French tech company is looking for a partner to co-develop a Proof-of-Impact infrastructure enabling verifiable sustainability outcomes

candidate.description_text: The French start-up is specializing in microalgae production and air purification since 2021. They have built a multidisciplinary in-house team covering technical expertise in mechanical engineering, embedded systems, and biotechnology, as well as commercial and communications functions. They are currently developing an innovative technology for industrial wastewater treatment. The concept and its effectiveness have already been successfully demonstrated in partnership with the CentraleSupélec laboratory. They design and manufacture their prototypes in-house. They are now seeking to collaborate with companies in the food and beverage industry—particularly breweries—to test their solution alongside their existing treatment facilities. The French startup has focused on microalgae production and air treatment since 2021. They use microalgae to purify indoor air and install their air purification systems in coworking spaces, cafeterias, open-plan offices, and entrance lobbies. Their products are already on the market, and they have equipped numerous clients. They also install sensors to monitor air quality at client sites, giving customers access to a platform where they can view their indoor air quality in real time. They are also developing a new business line focused on the biological treatment of wastewater using their microalgae. The team consists of 12 employees, with strong technical expertise in mechanical engineering, embedded systems, and biotechnology. They manufacture their wastewater treatment prototype in-house. Their solution is fully adaptable to the treatment volumes required. They install multiple photobioreactors containing microalgae next to industrial facilities, allowing them to treat effluents while simultaneously producing microalgae that can later be resold. This makes their technology a sustainable and environmentally friendly treatment solution.
candidate.technical_problem_evidence_text: The French startup is currently looking for partners to test their treatment solution. Their technology is designed for food and beverage manufacturing plants, particularly breweries that generate wastewater discharges. They are also seeking partnerships with wastewater treatment plants to test their solution alongside their existing treatment systems. In addition, they are looking to partner with organizations that provide financial support to industrial facilities implementing sustainable treatment technologies. They are also seeking calls for projects and grant opportunities to support the development of their solution. They are open to applying for collaborative projects in partnership with other companies and organizations.
candidate.title: French startup specialized in microalgae-based solutions for indoor air purification and wastewater treatment is seeking companies in the food and beverage industry—particularly breweries—to test their wastewarter solution.

candidate.description_text: A pioneer in the field of natural bee products, the French company seeks to develop a new propolis processing technology based on supercritical CO₂ extraction. The aim is to selectively recover compounds of interest, particularly polyphenols, flavonoids, Artepillin C, and Biochanin A, while separating undesirable substances such as pesticide residues, heavy metals, and PAHs. This process will make it possible to “decontaminate” propolis and obtain purer, better standardized extracts with improved quality and safety. It also will also address the need to diversify dosage forms, with the development of liquid extracts richer in active compounds or alternatives to traditional alcohol-based extracts, which are often highly concentrated in alcohol that has a negative effect on their aromatic properties. The company, therefore, is looking to identify a partner with proven expertise in supercritical extraction, selective separation of natural compounds, and process optimisation for complex matrices. The desired collaboration could take the form of a research and development partnership or commercial agreement with technical support for process development, optimisation, and validation. The ultimate objective is to enhance the value of propolis, improve its analytical quality, and develop new high value-added natural ingredients suitable for applications in dietary supplements, natural health products, or aromatic formulations.
candidate.technical_problem_evidence_text: The right partner is expected to have strong expertise in supercritical CO₂ extraction processes applied to natural raw materials, ideally oils, resins, aromatic plants, or complex matrices comparable to propolis. Expertise in separating and extracting large molecules such as pesticides, heavy metals, and PAHs would be an advantage. Strong capabilities in selective fractionation, process parameter optimisation, and contaminant reduction are required. The targeted know-how includes in particular: - Selection of pressure, temperature, and potential co-solvent parameters - Separation of target compounds from lipophilic or semi-volatile contaminants - Recovery of fractions rich in polyphenols and flavonoids - Evaluation of decontamination efficiency regarding pesticides and PAHs - Development of low-alcohol or alcohol-free extracts - Possible scale-up to pilot or pre-industrial level This would require establishing a comprehensive experimental design to minimise the cost of trials.
candidate.title: Seeking expertise in supercritical CO2 extraction to isolate bioactive compound in propolis

candidate.description_text: In the metal recycling sector in which the SME operates, the company produces non-ferrous materials with varying compositions. To do so, it sources metallic waste and end-of-life metal products from various origins, most of which are made of zinc and aluminium alloys. Many of these products have also undergone surface treatment using tin and or nickel/chromium, which improves their brightness and resistance to wear. Unfortunately, even very small quantities of tin are incompatible with the level of purity required by international standards for some of the alloys that the company produces and sells. It is therefore necessary to remove the tin, even when it is only present as a very thin layer on the batches of products to be recycled. Mechanical removal of this tin-based or Ni/Cr based layer has proven ineffective. The company is therefore seeking a chemical removal solution. To date, the company has worked with another partner that was able to develop a low-TRL experimental chemical method. However, this method has several drawbacks, notably significant heat generation, which make it difficult to scale up to an industrial level. There is no more cooperation of the company with that partner but the initial research results are owned by the SME. The SME is now looking for an industrial partner or research centre capable of either improving the existing research results in order to develop a chemical process suitable for removing tin layers from metal scrap at industrial scale, or launching a new research study from scratch with the same objective. It is looking for a research and development cooperation agreement
candidate.technical_problem_evidence_text: The partner sought should have expertise in chemical processes for metals, particularly processes used to remove metallic components from parts of alloys of different composition. The partner sought could be either a laboratory or technical centre specialized in materials or a metal processing industrial company
candidate.title: Chemical removal of unwanted metal components for a metal alloy recycling process

candidate.description_text: Founded in 1985, a French industrial confectionery company (employing 190 staff) active in the production of bubble gum and related products is facing challenges related to the management of its bubble gum paste waste generated during the manufacturing process. The company generates approximately 80 tonnes per year of bubble gum paste waste as a by-product of its manufacturing process. This waste is produced in the form of compact blocks weighing several dozen kilograms and is currently treated as general industrial waste. The material has specific characteristics that make it difficult to process using conventional waste treatment methods. It contains elastomers and resins, giving it a highly elastic and non-brittle structure. The material can become hard externally while remaining malleable internally. It softens when heated and cannot be crushed unless cooled below freezing. Due to its composition, traditional waste management methods such as incineration or anaerobic digestion are not suitable. The company is therefore seeking a technical solution capable of processing this material in order to improve recycling efficiency and reduce environmental impact. The objective is to identify a solution that is technically feasible, economically viable, and compliant with European regulations. Implementation is foreseen at two industrial sites, located approximately 300 km apart. The company is specifically interested in a commercial agreement with technical assistance, allowing the integration of the proposed technology into its industrial processes. The expected outcome is the deployment of a sustainable and economically viable recycling solution.
candidate.technical_problem_evidence_text: The company is looking for partners with technologies or expertise capable of: •	Processing or transforming elastomer-containing bubble gum waste •	Managing elastic, temperature-sensitive, and non-brittle materials •	Enabling recycling, material recovery, or alternative valorisation pathways •	Providing scalable and economically viable solutions •	Ensuring compliance with European environmental and industrial standards
candidate.title: French confectionery company seeking an innovative technology for recycling and valorisation of bubble gum production waste.

description_text: Founded in 1985, a French industrial confectionery company (employing 190 staff) active in the production of bubble gum and related products is facing challenges related to the management of its bubble gum paste waste generated during the manufacturing process. The company generates approximately 80 tonnes per year of bubble gum paste waste as a by-product of its manufacturing process. This waste is produced in the form of compact blocks weighing several dozen kilograms and is currently treated as general industrial waste. The material has specific characteristics that make it difficult to process using conventional waste treatment methods. It contains elastomers and resins, giving it a highly elastic and non-brittle structure. The material can become hard externally while remaining malleable internally. It softens when heated and cannot be crushed unless cooled below freezing. Due to its composition, traditional waste management methods such as incineration or anaerobic digestion are not suitable. The company is therefore seeking a technical solution capable of processing this material in order to improve recycling efficiency and reduce environmental impact. The objective is to identify a solution that is technically feasible, economically viable, and compliant with European regulations. Implementation is foreseen at two industrial sites, located approximately 300 km apart. The company is specifically interested in a commercial agreement with technical assistance, allowing the integration of the proposed technology into its industrial processes. The expected outcome is the deployment of a sustainable and economically viable recycling solution.
technical_problem_evidence_text: The company is looking for partners with technologies or expertise capable of: •	Processing or transforming elastomer-containing bubble gum waste •	Managing elastic, temperature-sensitive, and non-brittle materials •	Enabling recycling, material recovery, or alternative valorisation pathways •	Providing scalable and economically viable solutions •	Ensuring compliance with European environmental and industrial standards
title: French confectionery company seeking an innovative technology for recycling and valorisation of bubble gum production waste.

candidate.description_text: The French SME is a pioneer and technology leader in high-quality imaging systems, with deep expertise in designing high-performance cameras specifically engineered for underwater and industrial applications, including operations in highly turbid or low-visibility waters. As part of its strategic expansion to deliver advanced subsea inspection capabilities, the company is seeking an expert partner in software-based 3D reconstruction. The collaborative goal is to co-develop a robust 3D modeling and reconstruction software solution specifically adapted to challenging underwater optical conditions and designed to ingest the video streams produced by the French company's proprietary cameras. The ultimate ambition is to market a distinctive, non-intrusive solution enabling high-precision integrity monitoring and wear control of submerged offshore infrastructure. Targeted application areas include anchor chains, flexible joints on pipelines, immersed metallic structures, fittings, and specific corrosion or wear zones on marine assets. To successfully achieve this, the sought software solution must meet the following criteria: •	Exploit the raw video streams from the SME's cameras (with a strong technical preference for a mono-camera setup, though stereovision/dual-camera systems can be considered); •	Reconstruct highly accurate 3D models of the inspected objects or underwater zones; •	Reach millimetric accuracy, depending on water turbidity and acquisition geometry; •	Deliver clean, processed 3D data directly compatible with standard asset integrity software and inspection workflows. The project is structured around an 18-month roadmap to bring the joint solution to the commercial market. Depending on the partner's technology maturity, cooperation will be established through a Research and Development Cooperation Agreement or a Commercial Agreement with Technical Assistance.
candidate.technical_problem_evidence_text: The prospective partner must possess proven software engineering capabilities and advanced algorithmic expertise in 3D reconstruction, photogrammetry, stereovision, or SLAM (Simultaneous Localization and Mapping). Technical requirements include: •	Algorithms already adapted to, or capable of being optimized for, challenging low-visibility, low-light, and turbid aquatic environments; •	Demonstrated capability to achieve millimetric to sub-millimetric resolution from video tracking; •	Experience in integrating 3D processing pipelines with physical camera hardware and industrial video streams; •	Willingness to engage in active co-development with the French SME's R&D team to bring a collaborative product to market within 18 months.
candidate.title: French underwater imaging SME seeks 3D reconstruction software partners for subsea infrastructure integrity inspection solutions

candidate.description_text: We are a UK-based SME developing a novel immunomodulatory platform based on programmable, genome-inactivated Bacteria-Like Particles (BLiPs). Using proprietary bioinformatics and synthetic biology, the company generates fully inactivated, non-replicative bacterial cells that retain native surface antigens and pathogen-associated molecular patterns (PAMPs), enabling potent immune stimulation with an enhanced safety profile. The BLiP platform overcomes key limitations of conventional bacterial inactivation methods and subunit vaccine approaches while providing a versatile platform for prophylactic and immunomodulatory applications. The company is advancing two lead programmes. The first is an intranasal prophylactic vaccine against recurrent urinary tract infections (UTIs), targeting uropathogenic Escherichia coli (UPEC) to induce protective mucosal immunity. The second is a broad-spectrum innate immune trainer for respiratory diseases, designed to establish a pre-emptive antiviral state within the respiratory mucosa and provide pathogen-agnostic protection against emerging and seasonal respiratory viruses. In parallel, we offer genome inactivation services for custom bacterial targets, supporting the development of safe bacterial products and research tools. We seek international R&D collaborations with academic, CRO, and industrial partners possessing established in vitro and/or in vivo UTI models, human airway or immune models, and respiratory infection challenge models. Collaborations will involve joint study design, evaluation of BLiP-based candidates in partner models, and shared data generation to validate efficacy, mechanism of action, and translational potential. The desired outcome is to establish robust preclinical proof-of-concept for both lead programmes while demonstrating the broader applicability of the BLiP platform.
candidate.technical_problem_evidence_text: •	Validated preclinical models: Access to established in vitro and/or in vivo UTI, human airway, immune, and respiratory viral challenge models to evaluate BLiP-based candidates. •	Preclinical immunology expertise: Capability to assess immunogenicity, mucosal immunity, trained immunity, and protective efficacy following intranasal administration. •	Microbiology, virology, and systems immunology: Expertise in uropathogenic E. coli, respiratory viruses, host–pathogen interactions, and multi-omics, epigenetic, and cytokine profiling to characterise mechanism of action and immune responses.

candidate.description_text: Two UK SMEs are forming a European consortium for a proposed EIT Urban Mobility Strategic Innovation Open Call project. One specialises in transport R&D and project delivery; the other provides established municipal waste collection planning and optimisation technology. The project builds on a successful EIT Urban Mobility RAPTOR demonstration with a European city, where the platform was applied to service mapping, collection-zone and round design, route optimisation, vehicle management and operational visibility. The next stage is to validate the proven capability across several European locations and levels of digital maturity. Demonstrations may cover data structuring, zoning and round optimisation, route/resource balancing, performance visibility, service-redesign scenarios, integration with existing systems and, where relevant, low-emission fleet transition. European end users and project partners are sought to provide operational use cases, data and local validation. The consortium is targeting a 2027 EIT Urban Mobility submission.
candidate.technical_problem_evidence_text: Primary end-user partners sought are European municipalities, intermunicipal waste authorities and city-linked waste operators responsible for municipal waste collection planning or operations. Complementary European partners are also welcome where they add direct value in areas such as independent validation, municipal data/GIS integration, strategic waste-network planning, low-emission fleet transition, research or impact assessment. End-user partners should have a real operational or strategic challenge suitable for demonstration - for example route/round redesign, service-area planning, contractor oversight, service restructuring, decarbonisation, systems integration or future waste-network configuration - and be able to provide relevant data, staff input, local testing and a letter of commitment if selected. Both less digitally mature and advanced authorities are of interest. Existing route-planning or operational software is not a barrier where a complementary integration, benchmarking or future-service use case can be defined.
candidate.title: Two UK SMEs seek European municipal waste authorities and partners for multi-city waste collection optimisation demonstration

candidate.description_text: The Greek maritime company was established in 2006. It is an independent maritime brokerage and advisory company with two decades of operational expertise across over 250 global charterers and 50 shipowners. Currently, they want to extend into the field of maritime security and situational awareness for merchant fleets. The company is developing an advanced marine-grade multispectral situational awareness platform intended for maritime safety, surveillance, navigation support, and defense applications. The system is designed to enhance real-time operational awareness in complex maritime environments through the integration of multiple synchronized sensing technologies within a unified hardware architecture. The company has already sourced the core optical components, including camera modules and lenses, and is currently seeking a specialized technical partner or system integrator capable of undertaking the full hardware integration and industrialization process of the platform. Unlike conventional rotating surveillance systems, the fixed multisensor configuration is intended to ensure continuous monitoring, lower mechanical complexity, reduced maintenance requirements, and improved reliability under demanding operational conditions. The solution is expected to support future integration with autonomous navigation systems, maritime threat detection platforms, vessel monitoring systems, and smart surveillance applications. The final system must be suitable for installation on maritime vessels and coastal infrastructure and therefore must withstand harsh maritime operating conditions, including humidity, salt corrosion, vibration, temperature fluctuations, UV exposure, and continuous outdoor operation. Furthermore, the platform must support seamless interoperability with existing vessel systems and communication infrastructure, enabling efficient transmission of synchronized multispectral video streams and metadata to external AI-based processing environments and command systems. The company is particularly interested in collaborating with partners possessing proven expertise in multisensor hardware integration, marine-grade electronics, embedded systems, optical and thermal imaging technologies, ruggedized industrial design, and advanced manufacturing for maritime, surveillance, or defense-related applications.
candidate.technical_problem_evidence_text: The company is seeking partners with expertise in system integration and capable of developing and manufacturing the hardware platform of a marine-grade multispectral situational awareness system intended for maritime and defense applications. Experience in multisensor system integration, thermal and optical imaging systems, embedded electronics, ruggedized marine-grade hardware, industrial/mechanical enclosure design, video synchronization systems, embedded computing and communications, and defense or maritime hardware manufacturing, would be highly appreciated. Also, experience in naval systems, defense electronics, surveillance systems, or AI-enabled imaging platforms would be considered an advantage.
candidate.title: A Greek maritime company is looking for a technical partner to help build and integrate an advanced system that improves situational awareness at sea, using multispectral sensing technologies suitable for marine environments

candidate.description_text: A Greek SME develops and markets handmade cosmetic skincare products, including serums, eye creams, sunscreen products, cream bases and active ingredient-based formulations. The company’s approach focuses on personalised skincare solutions adapted to the specific needs of each skin type, avoiding unnecessarily complex skincare routines. Building on this activity, the company is developing an advanced, patent-pending dermocosmetic delivery system for topical cosmetic applications. The system is designed to support the stabilisation and synchronised, multi-phase release of sensitive active ingredients, including nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide, commonly known as NAD+, and targeted signalling peptides. The product has reached a stage where external laboratory testing is needed to assess the skin penetration and distribution profile of NAD+ as a selected marker under controlled in vitro conditions. The requested study should evaluate the penetration potential of NAD+ using a reconstructed human epidermis model under physiological conditions and provide quantitative evidence on the behaviour of the marker after topical application. The study is expected to result in a comprehensive technical report, including data analysis and statistical evaluation. The company is seeking a specialised skin penetration testing laboratory, dermal absorption laboratory, bioanalytical laboratory, contract research organisation, research institute or university laboratory able to provide the requested testing service under a commercial agreement with technical assistance. The company is expecting the final results to be delivered by 31 October 2026.
candidate.technical_problem_evidence_text: The company is seeking a specialised skin penetration testing laboratory, dermal absorption laboratory, bioanalytical laboratory, contract research organisation, research institute or university laboratory with proven experience in in vitro percutaneous penetration, dermal absorption or transdermal delivery studies. The partner should have the necessary equipment, validated methods and scientific expertise to work with reconstructed human epidermis models and topical cosmetic or dermocosmetic formulations under physiological conditions. Experience with Franz diffusion cells or equivalent in vitro penetration testing systems would be highly relevant. The partner should also have the analytical capacity to quantify NAD+ or comparable bioactive markers in biological or reconstructed tissue-based samples, preferably using enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) or another suitable validated analytical method. Experience in cosmetic, dermocosmetic, pharmaceutical, transdermal or bioanalytical testing is a prerequisite.
candidate.title: Α Greek SME developing a patent-pending dermocosmetic delivery system seeks specialised laboratories for in vitro skin penetration testing

candidate.description_text: This Hungarian SME specializes in the development of advanced wildfire prevention and mitigation systems. Based on several years of multidisciplinary research, the company has developed three patented inventions to enhance forest fire resilience. The core technology functions by coating tree trunks within a designated protection zone with a proprietary, highly viscous, water-cooling chemical formulation. This coating prevents the bark from heating to its ignition threshold, effectively creating an active firebreak to halt the spread of wildfires. While the chemical formulation and core principles have been validated in laboratory environments, the company requires external technical capabilities to transition from a "pilot-ready" status to large-scale, field-ready deployment. Specifically, the company lacks the heavy mechanical platforms and automated spray-applicators required to distribute the fluid formulation efficiently across uneven and densely forested terrain. To bridge this gap, the Hungarian company is seeking international partners to contribute specialized engineering expertise, heavy-machinery platforms, and automated sensing systems to co-develop a mobile wildfire-suppression prototype. The client seeks to establish partnerships under two distinct frameworks. Research and Development Cooperation Agreement: •	To combine the company's patented chemical concept with external engineering expertise to design, build, and test a fully functional physical prototype. •	Partners will collaborate on mechanical and hydraulic integration, fluid dynamics modeling for high-viscosity distribution, and the execution of joint field trials to validate performance in real-world environments. Commercial Agreement with Technical Assistance: •	To adapt existing high-mobility forestry machinery or agricultural mobile platforms to serve as the carrier vehicle for the distribution system. •	The partner will supply or adapt off-the-shelf machinery, integrated sensors, or control systems and provide the necessary technical documentation and operational training to the Hungarian development team.
candidate.technical_problem_evidence_text: The company seeks to collaborate with SMEs (SME <=10, 11-49, or 50-249), Big Companies, Research Institutions, or Universities active in forestry engineering, machinery manufacturing, or automation. •	Under a Research and Development Cooperation Agreement: The partner is expected to co-design the applicator system, conduct simulations, and provide independent scientific validation, laboratory modeling, or performance measurements during the pilot phases. •	Under a Commercial Agreement with Technical Assistance: Industrial partners are expected to customize and supply mobile platforms or hydraulic/sensor components, providing detailed technical documentation and training for system integration. •	Field Validation Partners: Operational forestry organizations or firefighting associations are sought to provide access to pilot forest terrains and support the logistical coordination of controlled field trials.
candidate.title: Forestry machinery and sensor automation technologies are sought for the co-development of a patented wildfire prevention system
