candidate.description_text: The company is an innovative start-up specialized in sustainable space propulsion technologies for the aerospace sector. It focuses on developing next-generation hybrid rocket engines for small satellites and advanced space applications. The company focuses on creating eco-friendly chemical propulsion systems that use a mix of liquid oxidizers and solid fuels, especially 3D-printed fuel made from natural materials and sustainable propellants like hydrogen peroxide and nitrous oxide. The company’s competences encompass propulsion system design, research on advanced materials, additive manufacturing, and numerical modeling. It is actively seeking industrial and research collaborations for joint R&D activities on innovative propellant materials and hybrid propulsion integration. Potential cooperation opportunities include technology validation, co-development, and testing in relevant environments. Through these collaborations, the start-up aims to advance cleaner and scalable propulsion solutions that will enable the next generation of sustainable space mobility
candidate.technical_problem_evidence_text: The company is particularly interested in collaborative R&D projects focused on advanced propellant materials, additive manufacturing processes for aerospace components, and the integration of green propulsion systems for small satellites. Potential cooperation may include joint research activities, technology validation, co-development of propulsion subsystems, and testing of hybrid propulsion solutions in relevant environments. Space Frontier is also interested in partnerships with satellite manufacturers, aerospace companies, and research institutions willing to explore innovative, sustainable propulsion technologies for future space missions.
candidate.title: Innovative start-up in the aerospace propulsion sector, seeking industrial partners, research organizations, and space system integrators interested in the development and application of hybrid propulsion technologies

Cost-effectiveness is a key requirement, both in terms of materials and scalability for industrial production. The technology must be inherently safe for direct or indirect human contact, with no release of harmful substances, volatile compounds, or secondary pollutants. Preference is given to solutions that are also safe for use in proximity to food or food-contact environments. Desired mechanisms may include (but are not limited to): adsorption, absorption, catalytic degradation, or other passive physicochemical or biological processes. candidate.description_text: About NEREUS Symposium 2026 Call for Solution Providers: NEREUS (Network of European Regions Using Space Technologies) is the European platform that brings together regional authorities to promote and maximise the use of space technologies. The network fosters the deployment of space-based services and Earth Observation data for territorial management, regional economic growth, and the direct benefit of citizens. The 2026 NEREUS Symposium (Bologna, Italy - October 22-23, 2026) features a dedicated Business-to-Government (B2G) in-person matchmaking session designed to connect Public Administrations with innovative international technological experts. Regional NEREUS members' PAs have launched local challenges that can be addressed through Space Data and AI and are now willing to meet potential solution providers. International business and research actors are invited to submit their technological solutions for the following regional challenge in urban energy analysis (Cluster #ENERGY): #06-BASILICATA - Energy and urban form. The growth of Basilicata's cities based on night-time brightness How can nighttime satellite brightness data help public authorities better understand and manage urban growth, land-use intensity, and energy-related territorial dynamics in Basilicata’s cities? How to apply: After creating an Expression of Interest, solution providers will be guided to the dedicated website to submit their solutions to the challenge via a dedicated form. Interested actors have the opportunity to meet the PA launching the challenge and pitch targeted solutions that leverage Earth Observation (EO) and space data to solve public needs, initiating potential pilots and collaborations with the PA. Application closes on September 15, 2026. PA challenge owners will select organisations that they would like to meet during the Symposium to discuss solution applications. Meetings will be held in person during the B2G matchmaking session in Bologna (Italy) on October 22-23, 2026. Participation is free of charge; registration and travel to Bologna are required if selected. Invited participants will engage with the Symposium programme and take advantage of its networking. Depending on the solution's maturity, cooperation may take the form of research and development agreements or commercial agreements with technical assistance.
candidate.technical_problem_evidence_text: International solution providers (companies and Research) are invited to submit their innovative solution proposals tailored to the launched challenge. The Call welcomes international solutions across various stages of technological development. Topics: Earth Observation (EO) Energy Smart Cities & Urban Planning Critical Infrastructures Climate Adaptation & Resilience AI & Data Analytics Digital Transformation of PA applied to urban night-time brightness analytics.

candidate.description_text: The company is a leading Lithuanian industrial group providing shipbuilding, ship repair, offshore engineering and industrial construction services. Sustainability and environmental responsibility are integral parts of the company's development strategy. The company is seeking innovative technologies and business cooperation aimed at reducing surface stormwater pollution within industrial territories. Particular interest is focused on preventive environmental protection measures, efficient stormwater treatment solutions, environmental monitoring systems and advanced data analysis tools that support environmental compliance and continuous improvement. In addition to surface stormwater management, the company is also interested in innovative environmental solutions supporting sustainable industrial operations in the fields of wastewater management, air pollution prevention and control, waste management, energy resource management and resource efficiency. The company is seeking technologies and solutions that help prevent pollution, reduce emissions, improve energy efficiency, promote the use of renewable energy sources and circular economy principles, support environmental monitoring, digitalise environmental and energy management, and ensure compliance with European Union and national environmental and energy regulations. Particular interest is given to practical, scalable, cost-effective and innovative solutions that can be integrated into existing industrial infrastructure and contribute to achieving the company's sustainability objectives, improving environmental and energy performance, and supporting Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) goals. The company is interested in implementing practical and scalable solutions suitable for industrial and shipyard infrastructure and welcomes cooperation with technology providers, solution developers, research organisations and industrial partners.

candidate.description_text: A Latvian organisation experienced in European innovation and research projects is composing proposals under the Horizon Europe and similar project. The planned cooperation will support the further development and market preparation of mature maritime technologies. The consortium is looking for a EU manufacturer that already owns, manufactures or has the legal right to further develop an existing sea-drone or unmanned surface platform. The proposed platform must have reached at least Technology Readiness Level 6 and should therefore already exist as a functional prototype demonstrated in a relevant environment. The project is not intended for the development of a completely new platform from the concept stage. The selected manufacturer should be interested in activities such as: * further technical development; * system improvement and adaptation; * validation and demonstration; * preparation for industrialisation; * improvement of business and investment readiness; * preparation for wider European and Third country market uptake. The exact development activities, cooperation structure and partner responsibilities will be defined jointly with the selected company. Due to the commercially sensitive nature of the planned initiative, information concerning the project concept, consortium composition, technical approach and planned investments will not be disclosed publicly. Further details will be shared only with prospective partners that demonstrate relevant technical capacity, ownership or development rights and genuine interest in active project participation.
candidate.technical_problem_evidence_text: The manufacturer should have: * an existing sea-drone or unmanned surface platform; * minimum TRL 6; * ownership of, or documented rights to develop and commercialise, the technology; * internal technical capacity to modify and improve the platform; * a credible interest in commercial scale-up; * capacity to participate in an EU-funded interregional investment project; * willingness to contribute personnel, technical resources and the required co-financing. The platform may be autonomous, semi-autonomous or remotely operated. No detailed technical specifications are requested at the public profile stage.

candidate.description_text: A Latvian organisation experienced in European innovation and technology-development projects is building cooperation opportunities for future Horizon Europe proposals and other EU-funded projects in the field of advanced marine propulsion. The organisation is looking for a manufacturer or technology owner established in the European Union that has already developed an electric marine propulsion system or a hybrid propulsion solution combining electric propulsion with another energy or power source. The proposed propulsion technology must have reached at least Technology Readiness Level 6 and should already exist as a functional prototype, integrated system or pre-commercial product demonstrated in a relevant environment. The sought solution may include: * electric motors intended for marine propulsion; * integrated electric propulsion systems; * inboard or outboard electric propulsion; * pod, shaft, waterjet or comparable propulsion configurations; * motor controllers, power electronics and energy-management systems; * battery-electric propulsion; * series or parallel hybrid propulsion; * range-extender solutions; * regenerative or energy-recovery functions; * modular propulsion systems suitable for integration into different marine platforms. The system must be designed for, tested in, or capable of being adapted to the requirements of a marine environment, including exposure to moisture, saltwater, vibration, corrosion, temperature variation and demanding operational conditions. The cooperation is not intended to support the creation of a completely new propulsion concept from the initial idea stage. The selected company should already own, manufacture or possess the legal right to develop and commercialise the proposed technology. Potential cooperation activities may include: * further development of an existing propulsion system; * improvement of efficiency, reliability, power density or operational endurance; * adaptation for additional marine configurations; * integration of motors, batteries, power electronics and control systems; * development or improvement of hybrid operating modes; * optimisation of propulsion and energy-management software; * validation and demonstration in relevant conditions; * preparation for certification, industrialisation and wider market uptake. The exact development activities and partner responsibilities will be defined jointly with the selected manufacturer under suitable Horizon Europe topics or other relevant EU funding opportunities. Due to the commercially sensitive nature of the planned initiative, details concerning the wider project concept, cooperation structure, participating organisations and planned activities will not be disclosed publicly.

candidate.description_text: A Latvian organisation experienced in European innovation and technology-development projects is building cooperation opportunities for Horizon Europe and other future EU-funded projects in the field of e-fuel-compatible marine propulsion. The organisation is seeking an engine or propulsion-system manufacturer established in an EU Member State that has already developed an engine, generator-based propulsion package or hybrid system capable of operating on one or more synthetic e-fuels. In the European Union context, the term e-fuel generally refers to a synthetic gaseous or liquid fuel produced using renewable electricity. Renewable electricity is typically used to produce renewable hydrogen through electrolysis. This hydrogen can then be combined with captured carbon dioxide or, for certain fuels, nitrogen to produce synthetic fuels. Examples may include: * e-methanol; * e-methane; * e-diesel; * e-ammonia; * other renewable hydrogen-derived synthetic fuels. In EU policy and legislation, many such fuels are classified as renewable fuels of non-biological origin, or RFNBOs, provided that they comply with the applicable requirements concerning renewable electricity, production pathways and greenhouse-gas-emission savings. For this partner search, an e-fuel-capable propulsion system means an engine or integrated powertrain that is designed, demonstrated, certified or technically adaptable to operate on a qualifying synthetic fuel produced mainly from renewable electricity rather than directly from fossil feedstocks. The proposed technology must have reached at least Technology Readiness Level 6 and should already exist as a functional prototype, integrated propulsion system or pre-commercial product demonstrated in a relevant environment. The sought solution may include: * internal-combustion engines capable of operating on e-methanol; * engines compatible with e-methane or synthetic methane; * engines capable of using synthetic diesel or e-diesel; * ammonia-capable engines where the fuel pathway is based on renewable hydrogen; * dual-fuel or multi-fuel engines; * e-fuel-electric hybrid propulsion; * generator-based propulsion systems using e-fuels; * engines combined with batteries, electric motors or energy-management systems; * conversion or retrofit technologies enabling an existing engine platform to operate on an e-fuel. The proposed propulsion system must be designed for, used in, or capable of being adapted to marine operating conditions, including exposure to moisture, saltwater, corrosion, vibration, temperature variation and demanding duty cycles. The cooperation is not intended to support the development of a new engine from the initial concept stage. The selected company should already own, manufacture or have the documented legal right to develop and commercialise the proposed technology. Potential cooperation activities may include: * adaptation of an existing engine to one or more e-fuels; * fuel-system and combustion-system optimisation; * improvement of efficiency, emissions and operational reliability; * development of dual-fuel or multi-fuel operating modes; * integration with electric propulsion, batteries or generators; * optimisation of control and energy-management systems; * adaptation to additional marine configurations; * validation and demonstration in relevant operating conditions; * preparation for certification and regulatory compliance; * industrialisation and market deployment. The exact fuel pathway, propulsion configuration and development activities will be defined jointly with the selected manufacturer under suitable Horizon Europe topics or other relevant EU funding opportunities. Due to the commercially sensitive nature of the planned initiative, details concerning the wider project concept, cooperation structure, intended applications and proposed activities will not be disclosed publicly.

candidate.description_text: A Latvian non-profit innovation and technology organisation is developing an interregional investment project proposal under the I3-2026-INV2a – Financial and advisory support for investments in interregional innovation projects for the development of value chains in less developed regions, Strand 2a call. The project aims to establish and demonstrate a new European value chain for the production of large rotationally moulded HDPE components. The envisaged products will be intended primarily for demanding outdoor and marine-related applications, although the production technology may also be used for large components in aquaculture, infrastructure, transport, agriculture, environmental technologies and other industrial sectors. The consortium is looking for a machinery manufacturer, engineering company or industrial technology developer capable of designing and delivering a large-scale rotational moulding production system. The equipment must be suitable for manufacturing components with approximate maximum dimensions of: Length: 6.5 metres Width: 2.5 metres Height: 1.5 metres A rock-and-roll rotational moulding machine is currently considered a potentially appropriate solution because of the intended component size and geometry. However, the consortium is open to other configurations, provided that the proposed machinery can reliably and economically manufacture components of the required dimensions and quality. The machinery must be designed to process virgin and recycled HDPE. Particular importance is placed on the ability to accommodate recycled HDPE feedstock, including material with greater variability in melt behaviour, particle distribution and processing characteristics than standard virgin rotational-moulding powder. The project partner should therefore be able to develop or adapt the machinery, heating system, mould movement, process controls and material-feeding concept to ensure consistent production when using: * virgin HDPE powder; * recycled HDPE powder; * blends of virgin and recycled HDPE; * potentially HDPE granulate, where a technically feasible granulate-based or in-line material-preparation solution is proposed; * multilayer structures containing different virgin and recycled-HDPE formulations. The final machinery should support the production of large components with controlled wall thickness, adequate fusion, limited porosity, repeatable mechanical properties and consistent dimensional accuracy. The selected partner will be expected to participate actively in the technical development, engineering, production, installation, commissioning and industrial validation of the machinery. The current technology stage should be at least on :  TRL 6 level and are expected to progress towards industrial deployment. The applicable funding rate is: 70% European Commission funding; 30% own contribution by the project partner. The prospective partner must therefore have sufficient financial capacity to provide its share of project co-financing and sufficient operational capacity to complete the machinery development and delivery.
candidate.technical_problem_evidence_text: The sought partner should have demonstrated expertise in the development and production of rotational moulding machinery, particularly systems intended for large or technically complex parts. Experience in processing recycled HDPE is highly desirable.

candidate.description_text: A Latvian non-profit innovation and technology organisation is developing cooperation opportunities in the field of large rotationally moulded polymer products. The organisation is interested in new materials, manufacturing approaches and structural solutions that can reduce the weight and material consumption of rotationally moulded HDPE parts without compromising their mechanical strength, durability or long-term performance. The intended applications include large components for demanding outdoor and marine-related environments. The developed solutions may also be relevant to aquaculture, transport, infrastructure, agriculture, environmental technologies, energy systems and other sectors using large rotationally moulded products. One of the principal technical challenges is the relatively high material consumption and weight of large rotationally moulded components. Reducing wall thickness alone can result in insufficient stiffness, reduced impact resistance, excessive deformation, lower creep resistance and limited long-term durability. The organisation is therefore seeking innovative technologies that improve the strength-to-weight ratio of rotationally moulded products. Potential solutions may include, but are not limited to: * new virgin or recycled HDPE blends; * modified polyethylene formulations; * lightweight mineral, organic or recycled fillers; * short- or long-fibre reinforcement; * glass, basalt, carbon, natural or recycled fibres; * internal reinforcement meshes or textile structures; * embedded structural elements compatible with rotational moulding; * multilayer rotational moulding; * foamed-core or sandwich structures; * chemical or physical foaming technologies; * local reinforcement of highly loaded areas; * structural ribs or integrated internal geometries; * hybrid polymer structures; * additives improving stiffness, impact resistance or creep performance; * compatibilisers for recycled or mixed-polymer formulations; * nanomaterials or functional additives; * technologies enabling thinner but stronger walls; * simulation and optimisation tools supporting lightweight component design. The organisation is open to solutions based on HDPE and to compatible polymer systems that can be processed by rotational moulding or integrated into rotationally moulded products. Particular interest is placed on solutions compatible with recycled HDPE, including technologies that compensate for the variability, degradation or lower mechanical performance often associated with recycled feedstock. The intended components may be exposed to prolonged outdoor use, direct sunlight, elevated temperatures, humidity, saltwater and continuous mechanical loading. The organisation is therefore is also seeking technologies that improve: * resistance to ultraviolet radiation; * retention of tensile, flexural and impact properties after UV exposure; * colour and surface stability; * resistance to oxidation and embrittlement; * dimensional stability at elevated temperatures; * creep resistance under sustained loads; * resistance to thermal cycling; * resistance to combined UV, heat, humidity and saltwater exposure; * long-term durability in Mediterranean, tropical and other hot-climate environments. The organisation is particularly interested in technologies that address the combined effects of UV radiation, elevated surface temperature, environmental exposure and mechanical loading.
candidate.technical_problem_evidence_text: he sought technology should have reached at least TRL 4, meaning that the concept has been validated in a laboratory environment. The proposed solution should address one or more of the following challenges: * reduction of component weight; * reduction of HDPE material consumption; * improvement of stiffness-to-weight ratio; * improvement of tensile, flexural or impact properties; * improved creep resistance; * reinforcement of large unsupported surfaces; * improved dimensional stability; * improved performance of recycled HDPE; * reduced deformation in hot climates; * improved UV resistance; * improved resistance to ageing and embrittlement; * improved long-term outdoor performance; * development of multilayer or sandwich structures; * development of reinforced or foamed rotationally moulded parts; * compatibility with industrial rotational moulding processes. The technology should be supported by available evidence such as: * laboratory test results; * prototype samples; * material data sheets; * accelerated ageing results; * mechanical testing results; * proof-of-concept demonstrators; * pilot applications; * patents or protected know-how; * scientific publications; * technical validation reports. Technologies existing only as theoretical concepts, without laboratory validation, are outside the scope of the request.

candidate.description_text: Malta-based company, an NVIDIA Inception member and founded by peer-reviewed AI researchers with MSc-level AI qualifications from the University of Malta, develops custom AI engineering for organisations that need a production AI system built to their specific operational requirements rather than fitted to an off-the-shelf product. The service offered to clients covers the complete delivery path from initial assessment through to production deployment. Engagements typically begin with an AI readiness assessment: identifying where AI fits in the client's workflows, evaluating data quality and structure, and scoping the build. From there, the team designs and delivers a system against those requirements, staying through stabilisation rather than handing over at go-live. Past work spans real-time camera analytics on edge devices, AI-assisted tools in educational environments, automated quantitative systems in financial contexts, and computer vision pipelines for industrial settings with all deployments sharing the same engineering standard: production-grade, compliant by architecture, and maintained on infrastructure the client controls. Compliance is embedded from the first design decision with GDPR and EU AI Act requirements addressed in architecture, not added at the end. Audit trails, access controls and human review checkpoints, are scoped into the system design, not appended before sign-off. Company can contribute on sovereign AI engineering capability including computer vision, edge inference, predictive analytics, and on-premise deployment architecture. The partner is to contribute on domain expertise, relevant datasets, sector regulatory context, and end-user relationships.

candidate.description_text: This Dutch deep-tech SME is active in the field of quantum technology and structural health monitoring, and is developing a patented surface coating that can turn everyday structures such as aircraft, bridges, wind turbines, ships and industrial equipment into continuous, contactless sensors. The technology requested is access to a laboratory with an operational setup for a specialised optical-magnetic measurement technique used to characterise microscopic defects in diamond material. This know-how and equipment is needed because the company has completed an extensive computational modelling programme, using five independent simulation tools across 22 separate studies, and the final missing step before physical proof-of-concept is a single, clearly defined laboratory measurement on coated diamond plate samples that the company will supply, together with a measurement protocol. Specifically, the technique requested is optically detected magnetic resonance (ODMR) on nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centres in diamond. The coating is diamond-based and is sensitive, at a quantum level, to temperature, mechanical strain and magnetic fields. This information can be read out simply by illuminating the surface with light — remotely and without any physical contact. In this way, the entire coated surface becomes a sensor, without the need for wiring or embedded electronics, allowing early detection of micro-damage long before it would be visible through conventional inspection. candidate.description_text: Background Biomethane injected into the natural gas grid must comply with strict gas quality specifications. One of these requirements is that the gas must have the same odor characteristics as natural gas, which is achieved through the addition of an odorant. During biomethane production, Volatile Organic Compounds (VOC) can occasionally be present in the gas stream. These compounds may mask the odorant, resulting in reduced odor perception and potentially causing the biomethane to fail grid injection requirements. To prevent this issue, Volatile Organic Compounds are typically removed using activated carbon filtration systems. However, it is often difficult to determine when an activated carbon filter is approaching saturation. As a result, Volatile Organic Compounds breakthrough can occur before filter replacement is initiated. Technical Challenge We are seeking a monitoring solution capable of detecting or predicting the breakthrough of volatile fatty acids in activated carbon filters used in biomethane production facilities. The ideal system should: Continuously or periodically monitor the gas stream downstream of the activated carbon filter. Detect the presence of volatile fatty acids at very low concentrations before they reach levels that can interfere with odor perception. Provide early warning of impending filter saturation or breakthrough. Operate reliably in biomethane production environments. Be suitable for integration into existing gas treatment installations. Expected Outcome The objective is to develop a reliable method for determining the optimal replacement moment of activated carbon filters, thereby preventing Volatile Organic Compounds breakthrough, ensuring compliance with biomethane grid injection specifications, and reducing unnecessary filter replacement costs.
candidate.technical_problem_evidence_text: The client would like to identify technology providers, research organizations, or industrial partners that can offer: Existing commercial solutions for VOC breakthrough monitoring. Sensor technologies capable of detecting Volatile Organic Compounds in biomethane streams. Online analytical instruments or monitoring systems. Innovative methods for predicting activated carbon saturation and optimizing filter replacement intervals. Expertise in gas quality monitoring for biomethane and renewable gas applications. Type of Cooperation Sought Commercial agreement with technical assistance Technical cooperation agreement Research and development cooperation Pilot or demonstration projects

candidate.description_text: The company intends to upgrade its production profile from conventional food ice to premium transparent ice products dedicated to high-end gastronomy and beverage presentation. While it possesses the facilities and expertise required for standard ice manufacturing, it lacks the research infrastructure necessary to independently develop an advanced freezing technology. The planned innovation involves the development of a proprietary process referred to as: Technology of Vibrational Directional Freezing (TVDF) The joint R&D work will include: •	design and construction of a prototype freezing station, •	development of vibrational freezing in polymer moulds, •	optimisation of crystallisation processes to eliminate air bubbles, •	production of high-density, high-transparency ice cubes and spheres, •	validation of the technology under real production conditions. The cooperation is expected to significantly improve production efficiency, product aesthetics, and service range, enabling entry into the premium hospitality market. Need for Cooperation The SME does not possess sufficient laboratory facilities, research personnel, or analytical capacity to conduct full-scale development alone. External scientific and engineering support is required to: •	analyse existing technological solutions and IP landscape, •	design and test innovative freezing methods, •	prepare the company for implementation and scale-up, •	support applications for European innovation funding. Expected Results •	Development of an innovative, energy- and process-efficient freezing method. •	Launch of a new premium product line. •	Increased competitiveness and entry into international markets. •	Readiness for implementation under EU innovation support programmes.
candidate.technical_problem_evidence_text: A Polish ice producer seeks a research and technology partner to jointly develop and implement an innovative process of vibrational directional freezing to manufacture highly transparent ice with minimal air inclusions.

candidate.description_text: A Portuguese health innovation organisation has developed an advanced surgical helmet intended for use in hospital environments and high-risk clinical contexts. The solution was created to improve protection and comfort for healthcare professionals during surgical procedures, while also enabling digital functionalities relevant for modern surgical practice, remote collaboration and medical training. The system integrates, in a single wearable platform, assisted ventilation, audio communication, video transmission, image recording, mobile connectivity and compatibility with external devices. A technology demonstrator with augmented reality glasses has also been developed and tested in a real surgical context. This demonstrator allowed procedural information to be displayed in the surgeon's field of view, reducing the need to look away from the operative field towards external monitors. The prototype has been demonstrated in a relevant clinical environment, including hospital-based demonstrations supported by real-time audiovisual transmission and advanced connectivity. These demonstrations have shown the potential of the system for surgical support, remote collaboration, medical training and future integration into connected surgical environments. The technology has reached TRL 7. Further work is ongoing regarding preparation for industrialisation, production of new prototypes, technical documentation, intellectual property protection and preparation for future certification. The organisation is not seeking to commercialise the product directly. It is therefore looking for a legal manufacturer with experience in medical devices, surgical equipment, healthcare protective equipment or connected medical technologies. The partner is expected to support the next stages of product industrialisation, certification and commercialisation. The cooperation may involve technology transfer, licensing, co-development, industrialisation, certification support and distribution. The preferred partner should have regulatory, industrial and commercial capacity to take responsibility for the product's certification and future market entry, particularly in Europe, but also potentially in other international markets.
candidate.technical_problem_evidence_text: The organisation is seeking an industrial partner capable of supporting the next stages of industrialisation, certification, market entry and distribution of the surgical protection helmet. The preferred partner should be a medical device manufacturer, healthcare protective equipment manufacturer or connected medical technology company with experience in regulated healthcare markets. The partner is expected to have one or more of the following capabilities: - Experience as legal manufacturer of medical devices and/or healthcare protective equipment; - Knowledge of EU Medical Device Regulation and/or personal protective equipment regulatory frameworks; - ISO 13485 certification or equivalent quality management experience; - Capacity to support technical documentation, risk management, usability, verification, validation and certification activities; - Industrialisation, assembly and scale-up capabilities; - Experience in wearable medical technologies, surgical equipment, protective systems, connected medical devices or hospital technologies; - Capacity to support market access and commercialisation in Europe and/or other international markets. The expected role of the partner is to act as legal manufacturer, supporting the regulatory and certification strategy, contributing to industrialisation and production scale-up, potentially supporting further technical optimisation and validation, and preparing market introduction and distribution. The cooperation may involve technology transfer, licensing, co-development, industrialisation, certification support and distribution. The organisation is particularly interested in partners based in Europe, but is also open to cooperation with experienced industrial partners from other international markets.

The company offers accelerated time-to-market, reduced development and delivery risk, and the opportunity to jointly build scalable industrial digital products with shared ownership and long-term commercial potential. The company contributes under investment agreement through: - Financial investment, depending on the scope and maturity of the joint solution - A dedicated multidisciplinary development team (software, data, and industrial domain experts) - End-to-end product development and delivery, from prototype stage, through MVP to pilot, launch, and scaling - Proven experience in industrial digitalization projects and operating solutions in real production environments - Access to a proprietary, production-proven industrial software platform - Long-term technical support and delivery capacity during scaling.

candidate.description_text: Company’s cases combine everyday mechanical protection of smartphones with integrated EMF-shielding layers based on advanced conductive and absorptive materials. The solution is designed to lower user exposure without blocking core device functions such as mobile data, Wi Fi, and Bluetooth connectivity. Compared to generic accessories, company focuses on evidence-based design, iterative testing, and clear communication of measured performance indicators to end users. The requested RF testing will enable the development of next generation products with optimised shielding characteristics, reduced interference, and documented compliance with international guidelines.
candidate.technical_problem_evidence_text: Company seeks partners with proven expertise in RF and EMF measurements, ideally accredited according to relevant ISO/IEC standards for electromagnetic testing. Required capabilities include: •	Measurement of shielding effectiveness of phone cases over common cellular, Wi Fi, and Bluetooth frequency ranges, using recognised methods (e.g. anechoic chamber, GTEM cell, or near field/far field setups). •	Assessment of specific absorption rate (SAR) or equivalent exposure metrics with and without the case, according to applicable standards. •	Analysis of the impact of the case on antenna performance, signal strength, data throughput, and connection reliability. •	Preparation of a detailed test plan, execution of measurements on multiple case variants and phone models, and delivery of structured test reports with raw data and engineering interpretation.

title: Slovenian SME is looking for an experienced manufacturing partner specialising in plastic injection moulding and the production of customised smartphone cases. They are prepared for collaboration with commercial agreement with technical assistance.

candidate.description_text: A university from Türkiye is preparing a Horizon Europe Innovation Action proposal with their patent-based technology. The current consortium comprises academic and RTO partners from Türkiye, Germany, France, Italy, and Slovenia and is being strategically expanded for industrial leadership. The project focused on the development of lightweight, flexible polymer nanocomposite layers and nanocomposite fiber-based, textile-like materials for advanced radiation shielding and decontamination in clinical and other high-reliability environments. Main targets of the project are polymer nanocomposites incorporating functional nanoparticles to enable multi-radiation attenuation (X-ray, gamma, neutron) while overcoming the weight, ergonomics, and sustainability limitations of conventional lead-based solutions. The project aims to advance the technology from TRL 5 to TRL 7, including pilot-scale manufacturing, industrial scale-up, validation in realistic operational environments, and demonstrator development, supported by AI-driven material optimization and life cycle assessment (LCA). They are seeking an industrial partner (SME or large enterprise) willing to act as project coordinator, with a central role in consortium leadership, scale-up strategy, pilot production, demonstrator manufacturing, and exploitation planning, and with proven capabilities in manufacturing and scale-up of composites, coatings, fibers and/or textile structures, process optimization, quality control, and operation in regulated industrial environments. Organizations with ambition to lead a high-impact Horizon Europe project and shape its industrial and market-oriented trajectory are invited to get in contact.
candidate.technical_problem_evidence_text: Willingness to act as project coordinator,  Pilot-scale manufacturing and scale-up capability,•  Experience with polymer-based nanocomposites, nanocomposite fibers and textiles,  Process optimization expertise, Quality control and quality assurance capability,  Support for TRL progression from 5 to 7.
candidate.title: Industrial Coordinator Sought for Horizon Europe Innovation Action (IA) Project on Advanced Nanocomposite Radiation Shielding Materials

candidate.description_text: The company is a major Ukrainian food manufacturer with two factories in Kharkiv and Cherkasy, Ukraine. The manufacturer works in a real production environment where energy continuity, efficiency and resilience are strategically important. The company is now looking for European partners that can offer practical green and clean technologies for an operating food factory. The goal is to reduce energy risks, improve sustainability, and increase autonomy during blackouts and other disruptions. The Ukrainian enterprise is especially interested in solar photovoltaic systems, large battery energy storage systems, smart energy management, industrial heat recovery, and solutions that help reduce greenhouse gas emissions from boiler and thermal processes. The company is also interested in solutions that can capture, reduce or monitor emissions from gas-based production processes, as well as technologies that can recover and reuse heat from waffle cup baking and other thermal operations. The Ukrainian manufacturer is ready to act as a pilot and demonstration site. The company would welcome technical partners that want to test, adapt and validate their solution in a real industrial setting and, where relevant, prepare a joint application for grant funding or other co-financing.
candidate.technical_problem_evidence_text: The company is seeking European partners with practical technologies and engineering expertise in industrial energy efficiency, renewable energy integration and decarbonisation for food manufacturing facilities, interested in pilot projects and grant funding: 1. Solar PV and other renewable / low-carbon energy generation: Technology developers, EPC contractors and integrators of solar PV systems and other renewable or low-carbon on-site energy generation solutions for industrial facilities. The company is interested in an initial pilot or first deployment of approximately 500 kWp–1 MWp of installed solar PV capacity, with possible further expansion up to 2 MWp or more depending on roof/land availability, grid connection conditions and project economics. Relevant solutions may include solar PV, hybrid PV + BESS systems, heat pumps, waste heat utilisation, biogas/biomass-based generation and high-efficiency cogeneration where it provides measurable energy savings and CO₂ reduction. 2. Battery energy storage systems: Suppliers and integrators of modular industrial battery energy storage systems with an initial pilot size of approximately 500 kW–1 MW AC-rated power output and 1–2 MWh usable storage capacity, scalable up to 2 MW / 4 MWh or more. The solution should be suitable for peak shaving, integration with solar PV, backup of critical refrigeration loads, and improved resilience of an operating food production facility with seasonal power demand of up to approximately 1.7 MW. The system should include PCS, BMS, EMS, thermal management, fire safety systems, monitoring software, commissioning support and scalability for future expansion. 3. Industrial waste heat recovery: Companies working with industrial waste heat recovery and thermal storage solutions for food manufacturing facilities. The company is looking for technologies to recover heat from gas-fired wafer cone baking ovens, gas boiler rooms, diesel generators used during blackouts, refrigeration systems, compressors and condensers. The recovered heat could be used for hot water, washing/CIP processes, space heating, preheating, defrosting and other factory needs. Relevant solutions may include flue gas heat recovery, generator exhaust heat recovery, economisers, heat exchangers, industrial heat pumps, thermal storage tanks, smart controls and integration with existing factory utilities. 4. Emissions reduction, flue gas treatment and carbon management: Providers of emissions reduction, flue gas treatment and carbon management solutions for industrial food production facilities. The company is interested in reducing emissions and improving energy efficiency related to gas-fired wafer cone baking ovens, gas boiler rooms, diesel generators used during blackouts and possible future cogeneration systems. Relevant solutions may include flue gas heat recovery, boiler efficiency upgrades, low-NOx burners, exhaust gas treatment where applicable, fuel switching, electrification measures, emissions monitoring, carbon footprint calculation, Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions assessment, and practical decarbonisation roadmaps with measurable reduction targets.
candidate.title: Ukrainian ice cream manufacturer seeks green energy, heat recovery and decarbonisation technologies for pilot deployment and joint grant-based projects

candidate.description_text: The Ukrainian manufacturing SME based in Poltava has practical experience in metalworking, steel structures, roofing and facade systems, woodworking and furniture production. The company operates its own production capacity and plans to expand into a new family of modular metal-and-timber products for veteran and social infrastructure. The planned project will establish a dedicated production and training facility for modular furniture, shelving and storage systems, partitions, workstations, kitchen and sanitary modules, accessibility elements, outdoor furniture and other adaptable solutions. Products are intended to be durable, repairable, easy to disassemble, relocate, reconfigure and reuse. The first practical batch is planned for a veteran centre in Poltava, while the facility will also provide practical training, internships and employment opportunities for Ukrainian veterans. The company is seeking a partner from the Netherlands able to contribute technical know-how in circular design, modular construction, standardised product architecture, design for disassembly, production methodology, quality requirements and knowledge transfer. A key cooperation option is the joint development of a modular frame and connection logic that can be manufactured locally in Ukraine and applied across several product families. The expected result of the international cooperation is a locally manufacturable, standardised and replicable modular product system, supported by technical documentation, production guidance and transfer of know-how to the Ukrainian engineering and production team. The cooperation is intended to support preparation and implementation of a partnership project under the Ukraine Partnership Facility or a comparable reconstruction-oriented cooperation framework.
candidate.technical_problem_evidence_text: The sought Dutch partner should have relevant expertise in one or more of the following areas: - modular steel and/or metal-and-timber systems; - circular product or construction design, including design for disassembly, repair and reuse; - detachable and standardised connection systems; - parametric design and standardisation of product families; - production engineering, manufacturability, assembly methodology and quality control; - preparation of technical documentation, design rules and production standards; - knowledge transfer and practical training for engineering and production teams. Experience in circular construction, modular manufacturing, social infrastructure or reconstruction projects would be an advantage. The partner should be willing to co-develop solutions that can be manufactured by the Ukrainian company rather than only supply finished imported products.
candidate.title: Ukrainian manufacturer seeks Dutch expertise in circular modular metal-and-timber systems for social infrastructure

candidate.description_text: A Vietnam-based renewable energy and engineering company aims to become a leading provider of sustainable energy solutions in the domestic and regional markets. The company supports clients in achieving their sustainability goals through technology transfer, renewable energy development, engineering consulting, green energy solutions, reliability improvement, and project management services. Established in 2018, the company brings together a team of experienced engineers and consultants delivering high-quality solutions in power system design, installation, project management, and asset management. Its services are designed to meet client requirements in terms of quality, timeliness, safety, and environmental performance, while supporting efficient and reliable energy operations. The company is committed to continuously improving its internal management systems, fostering professional development, and strengthening its position as a distinctive and reliable partner in the renewable energy sector. To further enhance its service offering, the company is seeking international partners that can provide smart-grid and advanced technological solutions for transmission, distribution, and renewable energy systems. The cooperation is expected to focus on improving operational reliability and optimising asset management for energy utilities and industrial clients. Partnerships may take the form of commercial agreements with technical assistance or technology cooperation.
candidate.technical_problem_evidence_text: The company is seeking partners with proven expertise in smart-grid and advanced energy technologies applicable to power transmission, distribution, and renewable energy systems. Solutions should support improved operational reliability, system monitoring, and asset performance optimisation. The partner is expected to provide technologies or systems such as grid automation, digital monitoring and control solutions, predictive maintenance tools, or asset management platforms. Experience in integrating solutions into existing power infrastructure and adapting them to different operational environments is required. The proposed solutions should be commercially available or close to market deployment, and partners should be able to provide technical support, knowledge transfer, and implementation assistance.
candidate.title: Vietnam-based energy company seeks smart-grid and power system technology partners to improve grid reliability and asset management

candidate.description_text: Vietnam-based high-tech company acting as a connector and integrator between international technology providers and the local market. The company focuses on technology transfer, pilot deployment, and commercialization of advanced solutions, supported by a growing ecosystem of industry partners, universities, and international experts. The company is currently seeking a technology partner (SME, research organization, or university) with expertise in solid-state battery to jointly establish a pilot application lab in Vietnam. The objective is to test and validate the technology under real operating conditions and adapt it to local applications. Following a successful pilot phase, the partnership aims to move toward commercialization, including potential exclusive distribution, co-development of application-specific solutions, and future localization of assembly or production for the Southeast Asian market.
candidate.technical_problem_evidence_text: The company is seeking a technology partner (SME, research organization, or university) with proven expertise in the research and development of solid-state battery technologies. The partner is expected to have: - Advanced know-how in solid-state battery design and development, including materials, cell architecture, and performance optimization - Experience in prototype development and testing, ideally with technologies approaching commercialization stage - Capability to support pilot deployment, including adaptation of battery solutions to real-world applications - Willingness to collaborate in establishing a pilot application lab in Vietnam, for testing and validation under real operating conditions - Interest in long-term cooperation, including co-development of application-specific solutions, technology transfer, and potential localization of assembly or production
candidate.title: Vietnam-based high-tech integrator seeking solid-state battery technology partner for pilot deployment and market expansion in Southeast Asia
